en:
[Note: From the root יתן, of the pattern אפעל, like אַכְזָב, אקדח. So most of the modern grammarians, and not according to the opinion of Radak that the nun is added or that it is of the pattern of היכל; — and in Arabic ותן وَتَن, was constant. Especially of a river that flows constantly.], (אֵתָן), 
a) masculine adjective, feminine אֵיתָנָה, plural -תָנִים -תנוֹת, — a) constant, that which does not cease, German dauernd, unaufhörl, French perpétuel, English incessant: — Especially of a river that flows constantly, in contrast to אַכְזָב, German perennierend, French qui coule continuellement, English perennial: "And the elders of that city shall bring the heifer down to an ever-flowing stream [נחל אֵיתָן] [Note: They said in the Sifre, Shoftim 27: איתן in its meaning 'hard'.]" Deuteronomy 21:4. "But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream" Amos 5:24. "You split open spring and brook; You dried up ever-flowing rivers" Psalms 74:15. — And with reference to a people, one that stands and endures a long time: "Behold, I bring upon you a nation from afar, O house of Israel, says the LORD; it is an enduring nation, it is an ancient nation" Jeremiah 5:15. — And of a dwelling, a seat, an abode: "And (Balaam) saw the Kenite, and took up his parable and said: firm is your dwelling place, and your nest is set in the rock" Numbers 24:21. "Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the thicket of the Jordan against the enduring habitation" Jeremiah 49:19. — Of strife and the like: "He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the strife of his bones is continual" Job 33:19. — And of a way: "but the way of the treacherous is איתן [Note: In explaining this word all the commentators have struggled and have not found anything acceptable to the heart. Many explained it as 'strong, hard', and the figure of the verse does not come out well with this. Joseph Halévy (REJ, 3 171) explains this איתן as meaning 'not paved', but without basis. And it is more reasonable, according to the translation of the Septuagint, to emend to אידם in place of איתן.]" Proverbs 13:15. — b) strong, German stark, French fort, English strong: "Strong sons, fit to arise from him" Genesis Rabbah 98. "The pulses of the right are strong" Immanuel, Machberot 11. "Its wood (of the cedar) does not rot; it is strong and good for building" Yehuda Leib Gordon, Goren Atad, Letters 2, 285. 
b) masculine noun, plural אֵיתָנִים, אֵת-, — a) the fixed, usual state of something, German normaler Zustand, French état normal, English normal state: "And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its normal state [לְאֵיתָנוֹ] at the turning of the morning" Exodus 14:27. "It happened with one lamb [Note: Shitah Mekubbetset and Bach emended to באחד.] that a wolf took (the whole membrane), and it returned to its normal state" Bekhorot 39b. "Rabbi Chanina, the son of Rabbi Yehoshua's brother, says: never has the left side preceded the right side, except for one woman in his neighborhood whose left side preceded the right side, and it returned to its normal state" Niddah 48b. "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Meir: that his bow (Joseph's) returned to its strength" Sotah 36b. — And this usage spread much in our language: "The holy King, like her bridegroom (of Israel, likened to a virgin), sent her many betrothal gifts as a present, and swore to bring her in when she stands in her full strength" Zulat for the third Shabbat, אז כארשת. "For after he parted from Laban's company, and the trouble of the conditions and Laban's challenges departed from him, (Jacob) returned to his former state, and the angels of God appeared to him in his prophecy" R. Isaac Abarbanel, commentary on Vayetze. "That even after the famine the land would remain so deficient that it would not easily return to its former state" ibid., Miketz, "And Pharaoh said to Joseph". "For after seventy years (Tyre) returned to its former state" Radak, Isaiah 23:12. "That they did not return to their former state" רמ"ע of Fano, אמר' טהור', תק' דין, 28. "And if there is a physician and sage there who recognizes the illness and sets right the weakened element and strengthens it, and the strong one and weakens it, the body will return to its former state" Abraham bar Hasdai, Sefer ha-Tappuach. "If we say that this happened (that the element was destroyed), we will not know a cause how that element returned to its state" Or Ammim, Sforno, folio 13a. "And his (Job's) being ready to persist if he returns to his state" the same, introduction to the commentary on Job. "(The man) took (the snake, frozen with cold) and wrapped a garment around it to warm it, and when the snake returned to its state, it began to cast its venom in the house" Fables of Aesop, in the collection Divrei ha-Yamim of Moses. "For when the signatures multiply, the decree will return to its former force" ר"י לאטש, Responsa 141. "By what shall (people) preserve their health, and by what shall they return to their state if they have departed from it" Abraham Shalom, Neveh Shalom 12, ב"ב. "For desire returned to its state; it fell into the net of imagination in ancient time" Moses Rieti, Mikdash Me'at, section Ha-Ulam. "I was healed and returned to my state and to my health" Collections of Joseph Sambari, Seder ha-Chakhamim ve-Korot ha-Ittim, Neubauer 101. "The first register exists in its original state" Pinkas Krakow, from the year 400, Otzar ha-Sifrut 4, 622. "Let (the enactments) stand in their force and original strength" Pachad Yitzchak, entry Haskamot, question קה"י, נתנו כח. "Like an arrow shot at a target, it divides the air, and in a moment it returns to its state, and one does not see in it where it passed" Naftali Hertz Wessely, Chokhmat Shelomo 5:12. "It has eased for me a great deal, and I have almost returned to my former state, as I was in the days of my youth" Letters of Yehuda Leib Gordon 1, 119. — c) something strong, enduring, and an epithet for high mountains, German hoher Berg, French haute montagne, English high mountain: "Hear, O mountains, the LORD's controversy, and you enduring ones [וְהָאֵתָנִים] [Note: All the ancients explain that it is an epithet for the high mountains, but this is somewhat difficult and does not sit well with the figure of the verse. And therefore he emended to ולה' והאזינו in place of והאֵתנים.], foundations of the earth" Micah 6:2. "The glory of kings, praise to the pure ones; from His fear the mighty ones and the rocks tremble" Kerovot, Ofan for the first day of Shavuot, ועתה בנים. And figuratively, of great, important people: "The month in which the mighty ones of the world were born" Rosh Hashanah 11a. "Who caused you to be thrust away from the mighty ones? The harshness with which you were harsh toward your mistress" Midrash Bereshit 98. "For were it not so, it would not have been said before such mighty ones of the world" Rav Hai Gaon, Responsa of the Geonim, Harkavy 66. "The mighty ones of the world" R. Judah of Barcelona, Yetzirah 104. "And the sages, the mighty ones of Israel, are careful about this" the same, Ha-Ittim, see there 1. "And know this, that the founders of the world, the mighty ones, our holy rabbis and the Geonim, have already said" Chizzuk Emunah, by R. Isaac son of Abraham, introduction by the author's student. And especially an epithet for Abraham and the other patriarchs: "May He yet remember for us the love of the mighty one, our master" Shacharit of Yom Kippur, כי מקדישיך. "And they recount Your righteous acts, to remember for them the three mighty ones" Shacharit of Yom Kippur, מי יתנה. "The sons of the mighty ones give a crown" Musaf of Yom Kippur, ליושב תהלות. "Holy seed, stock of the mighty ones" Ha-Emunot of R. Shem Tov 4:14. "Then the mighty ones, the foundations of the earth, began to oppose one another" Devir, רמא"ג, ב' חכמי חרשים. — And an epithet for the strong forces of nature: "For the elements [הָאֵיתָנִים] were overturned [Note: And Naftali Hertz Wessely himself explained there, and these are his words: 'that is to say, the elements of the earth, which are called in the Hebrew language איתנים, as comes in the commentary on the book of Genesis, from all the verses in the Bible, such as earth, water, fire and air.' Thus far.], and each one had a new form" Naftali Hertz Wessely, Chokhmat Shelomo 19. "For these elements will not be taken by the hands of a man" אד"מ, או"א, vision 10. "For the elements show no favor to any possessions and toil of the hands" Yehuda Leib Gordon, Ha-Ve'erah. — d) with ב, בְּאֵיתָן, יָשְׁבָה הַקֶּשֶׁת בְּאֵיתָן, that is, well set, German fest sein (d. Bogen), French être solide (l'arc), English be firm: "And the archers hated him; but his bow abode firm [בְּאֵיתָן] [Note: All the translators and commentators, ancient and modern, translated and explained here too in the sense of 'strong'. Targum Onkelos בתוקפא. The Septuagint קרטוּס ϰράτους. Rav Saadia Gaon: פת' בתת קוסה פי צלאבה (that is, with hardness). And so Menachem ben Saruk, R. Jonah ibn Janah, Rashi, Ibn Ezra, and likewise most of the moderns. And therefore we are certainly permitted to use this figure, ישבה הקשת באיתן. And nevertheless there is room to doubt this reading. Rev. C.J. Ball, in the English translation, PSBA, XVII 196, emended somewhat according to the Septuagint: ותשבר מיתר קשתו.], and the arms of his hands were made agile" Genesis 49:23-24. — e) the essential character of something, German Eigentümlichkeit, French caractère, English nature: — And figuratively, of the character of the language and its nature: "And some of the sages of the generation who investigate the nature of the holy tongue say that 'year' [השנה] is said of the solar year" Abraham bar Hiyya ha-Nasi, Ha-Ibbur 3:1. "And the pattern of תקופה will be תפולה, like the word תשועה, whose root meaning and essential character are one" ibid. 2. "And the sages of the nature of the language said in their language: this month is called by this name in plain language because the moon is seen in it" ibid. 2:1. — f) ירח הָאֵתָנִים [Note: In the Canaanite language ירח אתנם, CJS N 86, in the Cyprus inscription. Some hold that איתן is the name of the god of the mountains, and for this reason the month is so called (Joseph Halévy, REJ III, 171). And some say: the month of the ever-flowing streams.], a name for the month of Tishri, German Monat Tishri, French mois Tichri, English month Tishri: "And all the men of Israel assembled to King Solomon in the month of Ethanim, at the feast, which is the seventh month" 1 Kings 8:2.

he: בכנענית אל האל, ועי' אֵלָּה. ונמסר במסור' (בראש' כו ג). ח' סבירין בלשון אלה., הָאֵל, — מלת הרמז כמו אֵלֶּה:  רק לאנשים הָאֵל אל תעשו דבר (בראש' יט ח).  כי לך ולזרעך אתן את כל הארצות הָאֵל (שם כו ג).  כי את כל התועבת הָאֵל עשו אנשי הארץ אשר לפניכם (ויקר' יח כז).  ונס (הרוצח) אל אחת מן הערים הָאֵל וחי (דבר' ד מב).  ונשל ה' אלהיך את הגוים הָאֵל מפניך מעט מעט (שם ז כב). — ובלי ה הידיעה:  אֵלי"א כי היא היא המלה אלה, אלא שזו שארית מהזמן הקדום כשעוד לא כתבו אות ה לסימן תנועה בסוף הברה פתוחה בסוף המלה, כמו אמרתָ וכיוצא בזה, וכן בכנע' קראו אִלִ. נולדו להרפא בגת (דהי"א כ ח).
en: In Canaanite/Phoenician אל, האל; and see אֵלָּה. And it is recorded in the Masorah (Genesis 26:3): “Eight [places where] one would suppose the word אלה.” הָאֵל, — the demonstrative word, like אֵלֶּה: “Only to these (הָאֵל) men do nothing” (Genesis 19:8). “For to you and to your seed I will give all these (הָאֵל) lands” (Genesis 26:3). “For all these (הָאֵל) abominations have the men of the land done, who were before you” (Leviticus 18:27). “And that fleeing (the manslayer) to one of these (הָאֵל) cities he might live” (Deuteronomy 4:42). “And the LORD your God will cast out these (הָאֵל) nations before you little by little” (Deuteronomy 7:22). — And without the definite article ה: “These (אֵל) [Note: That is, it is the very same word אלה, except that this is a remnant from the ancient time when they did not yet write the letter ה as a vowel sign at the end of an open syllable at the end of a word, as in אמרתָ and the like; and likewise in Canaanite they said אִלִ.] were born to the giant in Gath” (1 Chronicles 20:8).

he: באשור' אִלֻ, — שם העקרי לאלהים. ובעברית עברה תנועת החירק לתנועת הצירה, כנהוג. וכן יוסף הלוי (REJ X 176), כי הנקוד הקדום היה אִל. וכן בכנענית. בסורית אִיל. אך לא בארמית ולא בערבית. משקל גֵר, זֵד, לֵץ, מֵץ, עֵד, שֵד. — והנה הראשונים גזרו מלה זו מן אֱיָל. אמר ר"י חיוג: ומזה השרש (איל) יש לאל ידי אין לאל ידך, בין האלף והלמד נח נעלם והיא היוד שהוא במלת אֱיָל אֱיָלותי. ע"כ. וכן ר"י בן נגאח: ומהשרש הזה והענין הזה (אֱיָל) האל י"י. וכמו"כ הרד"ק. ואמרו רוב הראשונים כי מזה גם אַיּל, אולי הארץ, וכי מקור הכל הוא השרש אול שהוא משמעתו כח ועזז. אך לגרד וקצת האחרונים מפקפקים במשמ' הכח של שרש אול, ורואים בו משמ' אַול, ראשון, כמו קדמון. אולד סבר כי זה השם נגזר מן השרש אלה, פול דלגרד (במחברת אוריינט' ב', ובמחברת .Uebers), מן אֶל, אלי, במשמ' התשוקה ל... והכונה, העצם שאליו פונה האדם בצרתו. אבל זה, כמו שכבר העירו חוקרים רבים מהאחרונים, מושג יתר מדי דק ומפשט לא בלבד להשמיים הקדמונים, אלא להאדם הקדמון בכלל. וקניג אחרי פלפול גדול החליט כמו כן כי נגזר אֵל מהשרש אלה, במשמעת כח. אחרים גזרו מן ולי وِلَىَ, במשמ' מחסה ומגן. יוסף הלוי גזרו מן יאל, כמו דע מן ידע, ופרושו אולי, כמו בעבר' הואיל או בערב' ואל, בקש מחסה, ועל כל פנים, הוא שם כללי לאלהים. אבל הכנוי אֵל גבור לילד, ומ"ר מזה אֵלי גבורים, וכמו"כ אֵל גוים, צוחים כי תחלת משמ' השם אינו אלהים, אלא עצם נעלה ונשגב בגבורה בכלל., ש"ז, מ"ר אֵלִים, כנ' אֵלִי. — א) אֱלוֹהַ,  Gott; Dieu; God : ויברכהו (מלכי צדק מלך שלם את אברהם) ויאמר ברוך אברם לאֵל עליון קנה שמים וארץ וברוך אֵל עליון אשר מגן צריך בידך (בראשית יד יט-כ). ותקרא (הגר) שם ה' הדבר אליה אתה אֵל ראי (שם יו יג). וירא ה' אל אברם ויאמר אליו אני אֵל שדי התהלך לפני והיה תמים (שם יז א). ויקרא (אברהם) שם בשם ה' אֵל עולם (שם כא לג). אנכי ה' אלהיך אֵל קנא (שמות כ ה). ה' ה' אֵל רחום וחנון (שם לד ו). ויצעק משה אל ה' לאמר אֵל נא רפא נא לה (במד' יב יג). ויפלו (ישראל) על פניהם ויאמרו אֵל אלהי הרוחת לכל בשר האיש אחד יחטא ועל כל העדה תקצף (שם יו כב). מה אקב לא קבה אֵל ומה אזעם לא זעם ה' (שם כג ח). לא איש אֵל ויכזב ובן אדם ויתנחם (שם שם יט). אֵל מוציאם ממצרים כתועפת ראם לו (שם שם כב). כי אֵל אנכי ולא איש (הוש' יא ט). מי אֵל כמוך נשא עון (מיכ' ז יח). אֵל קנוא ונקם ה' (נחו' א ב). הלא אֵל אחד בראנו (מלאכי ב י). ואתה אמרת בלבבך השמים אעלה ממעל לכוכבי אֵל ארים כסאי (ישע' יד יג). ומצרים אדם ולא אֵל וסוסיהם בשר ולא רוח (שם לא ג). למען תדעו ותאמינו לי ותבינו כי אני הוא לפני לא נוצר אֵל ואחרי לא יהיה (שם מג י). השמים מספרים כבוד אֵל ומעשי ידיו מגיד הרקיע (תהל' יט ב). ויאמרו (הרשעים) איכה ידע אֵל ויש דעה בעליון (שם עג יא). וידברו באלהים אמרו היוכל אֵל לערך שלחן במדבר (שם עח יט). אולם אני אל שדי אדבר והוכח אל אֵל אחפץ (איוב יג ג). ירעם אֵל בקולו נפלאות (שם לז ה). האזינה זאת איוב עמד והתבנן במקור נדפס 'והתבן'  נפלאות אֵל (שם שם יד). — ועם ה הידיעה: אנכי האֵל אלהי אביך (בראש' מו ג). כי ה' אלהיכם הוא אלהי האלהים ואדני האדנים הָאֵל הגדל הגבר והנורא אשר לא ישא פנים (דברי' י יז). כה אמר הָאֵל ה' בורא השמים ונוטיהם רקע הארץ וצאצאיה (ישע' מב ה). הָאֵל תמים דרכו (תהל' יח לא). הָאֵל המאזרני חיל (שם שם לג). — ובכנ' אֵלִי: זה אֵלִי ואנוהו אלהי אבי וארממנהו (שמות יה ב). הצילני כי אֵלִי אתה (ישע' מד יז). אֵלִי צורי (תהל' יח ג). אֵלִי אֵלִי למה עזבתני (שם כב ב). — ומ"ר אֵלים (אלם): מי כמכה בָּאֵלִם ה' (שמות יה יא). כי מי בשחק יערך לה' ידמה לה' בבני אֵלִים (תהל' פט ז). ועשה כרצנו המלך ויתרומם ויתגדל על כל אֵל ועל אֵל אִלִים ידבר נפלאות (דני' יא לו). — ובחבור עם הרים וכדומה, במשמעה של גדולים, עצומים, קדומים: צדקתך כהררי אֵל (תהל' לו ז). כסו הרים צלה (של הגפן) וענפיה ארזי אֵל (שם פ יא). — ודרך הדבור: יש לאל יד פלוני לעשות, ר"ל יש לו היכלת,  etw. zu tun die M|acht haben; avoir le pouvir de faire qqch.;have the power to do s.t : יש לְאַל יָדִי לעשות עמכם רע (ברא' לא כט). הוי חשבי און ופעלי רע על משכבותם באור הבקר יעשוה כי יש לְאַל יָדָם (מיכ' ב א). אל תמנע טוב מבעליו בהיות לְאֵל ידך לעשות (משלי ג כז). — °ועם פעל נתן: אלהים נתן לְאֵל יד עבדך (אהבת ציון למפו ו). — ובשלילה: אין לאל ידו, אינו יכול מאומה,   ohnmächtig, machtlos sein; être impuissant; be powerless: בניך ובנתיך נתנים לעם אחר ועיניך ראות וכו' וְאֵין לְאֵל ידך (דבר' כח לב). ויש מבנתינו נכבשות ואין לְאֵל ידנוּ (נחמ' ה ה). — ובקללה: האומר יכך האל (תוספת' שבועו' ב יה). — ובברכה: ייטיב לך אל (שם).
en: In Akkadian (Assyrian) ilu — the principal name for God. And in Hebrew the hiriq vowel passed to the tzere vowel, as is usual. And so Joseph Halévy (REJ X 176): that the ancient vocalization was אִל. And so in Canaanite/Phoenician. In Syriac אִיל. But not in Aramaic nor in Arabic. The pattern of גֵר, זֵד, לֵץ, מֵץ, עֵד, שֵד. — Now the early scholars derived this word from אֱיָל. Rabbi Yehudah Chayyuj said: “And from this root (איל) come יש לאל ידי, אין לאל ידך; between the aleph and the lamed there is a hidden quiescent letter, and it is the yod that is in the word אֱיָל, אֱיָלוּתִי.” End quote. And so Rabbi Yonah ibn Janach: “And from this root and this sense (אֱיָל) comes האל ה'.” And likewise Radak. And most of the early scholars said that from this also come אַיִל and אולי הארץ, and that the source of all of them is the root אול, whose meaning is strength and might. But Lagarde and some of the later scholars doubt the sense of strength of the root אול, and see in it the sense of awwal, first, like ancient. Ewald held that this noun is derived from the root אלה; Paul de Lagarde (in Orientalia II, and in Uebers.), from אֶל, אלי, in the sense of longing toward…, and the intention is: the being to whom a man turns in his trouble. But this, as many of the later scholars have already remarked, is a concept far too subtle and abstract, not only for the ancient Semites, but for ancient man in general. And König, after a great discussion, likewise decided that אֵל is derived from the root אלה, in the sense of strength. Others derived it from wly وِلَىَ, in the sense of refuge and protection. Joseph Halévy derived it from יאל, as דע from ידע, and its meaning is perhaps as in Hebrew הואיל or in Arabic wa'ala, sought refuge; and in any case it is a general name for God. But the epithet אֵל גבור for a child, and the plural from it אֵלי גבורים, and likewise אֵל גוים, cry out that the original meaning of the noun is not God, but a being exalted and lofty in might in general. Masculine noun, plural אֵלִים, with suffix אֵלִי. — a) God, German Gott, French Dieu, English God: “And he (Melchizedek king of Salem) blessed him (Abraham) and said: Blessed be Abram of God Most High, maker of heaven and earth; and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand” (Genesis 14:19–20). “And she (Hagar) called the name of the Lord that spoke to her: You are a God of seeing” (ibid. 16:13). “The Lord appeared to Abram and said to him: I am God Almighty; walk before me and be perfect” (ibid. 17:1). “And he (Abraham) called there on the name of the Lord, the everlasting God” (ibid. 21:33). “I the Lord your God am a jealous God” (Exodus 20:5). “The Lord, the Lord, God, merciful and gracious” (ibid. 34:6). “And Moses cried to the Lord, saying: Heal her now, O God, I pray you” (Numbers 12:13). “And they (Israel) fell upon their faces and said: O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and will you be angry with all the congregation?” (ibid. 16:22). “How shall I curse whom God has not cursed? And how shall I denounce whom the Lord has not denounced?” (ibid. 23:8). “God is not a man, that he should lie, nor the son of man, that he should repent” (ibid. ibid. 19). “God who brought them forth out of Egypt is for them like the lofty horns of the wild ox” (ibid. ibid. 22). “For I am God, and not man” (Hosea 11:9). “Who is a God like you, who pardons iniquity” (Micah 7:18). “The Lord is a jealous and avenging God” (Nahum 1:2). “Has not one God created us?” (Malachi 2:10). “And you said in your heart: I will ascend into heaven, above the stars of God will I exalt my throne” (Isaiah 14:13). “Now the Egyptians are men, and not God, and their horses flesh, and not spirit” (ibid. 31:3). “That you may know and believe me, and understand that I am he; before me there was no God formed, neither shall any be after me” (ibid. 43:10). “The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament shows his handiwork” (Psalms 19:2). “And they (the wicked) say: How does God know? And is there knowledge in the Most High?” (ibid. 73:11). “And they spoke against God; they said: Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?” (ibid. 78:19). “But I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God” (Job 13:3). “God thunders marvellously with his voice” (ibid. 37:5). “Hearken to this, O Job; stand still and consider [note: in the source printed 'והתבן'] the wondrous works of God” (ibid. ibid. 14). — And with the definite article ה: “I am God, the God of your father” (Genesis 46:3). “For the Lord your God, he is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great God, the mighty and the awesome, who does not show favour” (Deuteronomy 10:17). “Thus says God the Lord, he that created the heavens and stretched them forth, he that spread forth the earth and that which comes out of it” (Isaiah 42:5). “As for God, his way is perfect” (Psalms 18:31). “The God that girds me with strength” (ibid. ibid. 33). — And with suffix, אֵלִי: “This is my God, and I will glorify him; my father's God, and I will exalt him” (Exodus 15:2). “Deliver me, for you are my God” (Isaiah 44:17). “My God, my rock” (Psalms 18:3). “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” (ibid. 22:2). — And the plural אֵלים (אלם): “Who is like you among the gods, O Lord?” (Exodus 15:11). “For who in the skies can be compared to the Lord, who among the sons of gods can be likened to the Lord?” (Psalms 89:7). “And the king shall do according to his will; and he shall exalt himself and magnify himself above every god, and shall speak wondrous things against the God of gods” (Daniel 11:36). — And in combination with mountains and the like, in the sense of great, mighty, ancient: “Your righteousness is like the mountains of God” (Psalms 36:7). “The mountains were covered with its (the vine's) shadow, and its boughs were like the cedars of God” (ibid. 80:11). — And the idiom יש לאל יד פלוני לעשות, that is, he has the ability, German etw. zu tun die Macht haben, French avoir le pouvoir de faire qqch., English have the power to do s.t.: “It is in the power of my hand to do you harm” (Genesis 31:29). “Woe to them that devise iniquity and work evil upon their beds! When the morning is light, they execute it, because it is in the power of their hand” (Micah 2:1). “Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it” (Proverbs 3:27). — °And with the verb נתן: “God has given power to the hand of your servant” (Ahavat Zion by Mapu 6). — And in the negative: אין לאל ידו, he can do nothing, German ohnmächtig, machtlos sein, French être impuissant, English be powerless: “Your sons and your daughters shall be given to another people, and your eyes shall look etc., and there shall be no power in your hand” (Deuteronomy 28:32). “And some of our daughters are brought into bondage already, and there is no power in our hand” (Nehemiah 5:5). — And in a curse: “One who says: May God strike you” (Tosefta Shevuot 2:15). — And in a blessing: “May God do good to you” (ibid.).

en: In the Babylonian vocalization the lamed has a quiescent hataf patah, and sometimes it is without dagesh and accented on the last syllable (milra), and then the lamed has a full patah (Introduction to the Assyrian Vocalization 56). And when אלה comes joined to a small word, the lamed is vocalized with hataf patah with dagesh because of the compression (dehik), e.g. אלה לך (ibid. 109). In Arabic ulā, ulā', haulā' أُولآء, ھؤُلاء. In Aramaic אלין, הלין. Also in Akkadian (Assyrian) ullūtu (אֻלוּתֻ). The students of language have not determined the nature of this word, and in any case the reason for this form for the plural in Arabic and in Hebrew, and the reason for the dagesh of the lamed in Hebrew, has not been clarified. In Dalman's opinion זה and אלה are two ancient words each used for both singular and plural, and later זה was specialized for the singular and אלה for the plural. And it cannot be decided which of the two pronunciations of the aleph is the older, that of Arabic with the aleph with holam, or that of Hebrew and Aramaic with the aleph with hiriq and segol. — The demonstrative word for near things in the plural, masculine and feminine, like אֵל, German diese, French ces, English these [Note: in the original the English is printed 'there']: “Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the heart of his servants, that I might show these (אֵלֶּה) my signs in his midst” (Exodus 10:1). “And all these (אֵלֶּה) your servants shall come down to me and bow down to me” (ibid. 11:8). “And you shall lay up these (אֵלֶּה) my words in your heart” (Deuteronomy 11:18). “And let these (אֵלֶּה) my words, with which I have made supplication before the Lord, be near to the Lord our God day and night” (1 Kings 8:59). “Happy are these (אֵלֶּה) your servants, who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom” (ibid. 10:8). “Behold, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these (אֵלֶּה) your prophets” (ibid. 22:23). “Return, O virgin of Israel, return to these (אֵלֶּה) your cities” (Jeremiah 31:21). “Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these (אֵלֶּה) their works” (Nehemiah 6:14). — And with the definite article ה: “After these (הָאֵלֶּה) things the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision” (Genesis 15:1). “And behold a smoking furnace and a flaming torch that passed between these (הָאֵלֶּה) pieces” (ibid. ibid. 17). “These (הָאֵלֶּה) men are peaceable with us” (ibid. 34:21). “Discern, I pray you, whose are these (הָאֵלֶּה), the signet, and the cords, and the staff” (ibid. 38:25). “Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these (הָאֵלֶּה) wicked men” (Numbers 16:26). “See, I have allotted to you these (הָאֵלֶּה) nations that remain, to be an inheritance for your tribes” (Joshua 23:4). “And Saul and all Israel heard these (הָאֵלֶּה) words of the Philistine” (1 Samuel 17:11). “And these (הָאֵלֶּה) ten cheeses” (ibid. ibid. 18). “Fear not, neither let your heart be faint, because of these (הָאֵלֶּה) two tails of smoking firebrands” (Isaiah 7:4). — And for the feminine: “And you shall not do any of these (הָאֵלֶּה) abominations” (Leviticus 18:26). “But if you will not hearken to me and will not do all these (הָאֵלֶה) commandments” (ibid. 26:14). “And the priest shall write these (הָאֵלֶּה) curses in a book” (Numbers 5:23). “What cities are these (הָאֵלֶּה) which you have given me” (1 Kings 9:13). “Like these (הָאֵלֶּה) good figs, so will I regard the captives of Judah” (Jeremiah 24:5). “These (הָאֵלֶּה) bones are the whole house of Israel” (Ezekiel 37:11). — And before the noun: “I will make darkness light before them and crooked things straight; these (אֵלֶּה) are the things I have done, and I have not forsaken them” (Isaiah 42:16). “Behold, these (אֵלֶּה) are the wicked, and, being always at ease, they increase in riches” (Psalms 73:12). “And these (וְאֵלֶּה) wine-skins, which we filled, were new, and behold they are rent; and these (וְאֵלֶּה) our garments and our shoes are worn out by reason of the very long journey” (Joshua 9:13). “Behold, I have sinned and I have done perversely, but these (וְאֵלֶּה) sheep, what have they done?” (2 Samuel 24:17). — And this is very common in the style of the later writers: “And behold, we will set aside all these (אלה) things” (Ibn Ezra, Exodus 16:25). “And these (ואלה) verses are not written” (ibid. 19:25). — b) As the subject of the sentence, without the noun to which it points, whether what is pointed to comes before it or after it: “These (אֵלֶּה) (those mentioned there above) were the sons of Basemath” (Genesis 36:13). “All these (אֵלֶּה) (the kings mentioned there) joined together in the vale of Siddim” (ibid. 14:3). “These (אֵלֶּה) (Nebaioth and Kedar etc., mentioned before) are the sons of Ishmael” (ibid. 25:16). “These (אֵלֶּה) are my appointed seasons: six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day is a sabbath of solemn rest, a holy convocation” etc. (Leviticus 23:3). — And without הם: “These (אֵלֶּה) are the generations of the heaven and of the earth when they were created” (Genesis 2:4). “These (אֵלֶּה) (those counted above) are the sons of Ham, after their families, after their tongues” (ibid. 10:20). “All these (אלה) (those counted above) were the sons of Joktan” (ibid. ibid. 29). “And they said: These (אֵלֶּה) are your gods, O Israel, which brought you up out of the land of Egypt” (Exodus 32:4). “These (אֵלֶּה) are all (what is said above) the accounts of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, as they were rendered according to the commandment of Moses” (ibid. 38:21). “And these (וְאֵלֶּה) (those mentioned afterwards) are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab the first-born, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar” (Numbers 3:2). — And as the predicate of the sentence: “And she (Zilpah) bore these (אֵלֶּה) (those mentioned above) to Jacob, sixteen souls” (Genesis 46:18). “And these (אֵלֶּה) you shall detest among the fowls etc.: the eagle, and the bearded vulture” etc. (Leviticus 11:13). “A widow, or one divorced, or a profaned woman, or a harlot, these (אֵלֶּה) he shall not take” (ibid. 21:14). “Blind, or broken, or maimed, or having a wen, or scabbed, or scurvy, you shall not offer these (אֵלֶּה) to the Lord” (ibid. 22:22). — And without a noun near it before or after it, אֵלֶּה in place of “these men”, “these things”, “these deeds”, spoken of there in the passage: “If the Lord were pleased to kill us, He would not have received a burnt-offering and a meal-offering at our hand, neither would He have shown us all these (אֵלֶּה) things” (Judges 13:23), that is, all the wonders related in the passage there. “These (אֵלֶּה) things (the deeds related there) did the three mighty men” (2 Samuel 23:17). “Assemble yourselves, all of you, and hear: which among them has declared these (אֵלֶּה) things?” (Isaiah 48:14). “Then you shall say in your heart: Who has begotten me these (אֵלֶּה), seeing I have been bereaved of my children and am solitary, an exile and wandering to and fro? And who has brought up these (וְאֵלֶּה)?” (ibid. 49:21). “Even to them have you poured a drink-offering, you have offered a meal-offering. Should I be pacified for these (אֵלֶּה)?” (ibid. 57:6). “Your holy cities are become a wilderness etc., and all our pleasant things are laid waste. Will you refrain yourself for these (אֵלֶּה) things, O Lord?” (ibid. 60:4–11). “That say: Stand by yourself, come not near to me, for I am holier than you; these (אֵלֶּה) are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burns all the day” (ibid. 65:5). “Have you seen what backsliding Israel did? She went up upon every high mountain and under every leafy tree, and there played the harlot. And I said: After she has done all these (אֵלֶּה) things, she will return to me” (Jeremiah 3:6–7). “Your way and your doings have procured these (אֵלֶּה) things (the troubles mentioned there) for you” (ibid. 4:18). “Shall I not punish for these (אֵלֶּה) things (all the deeds he enumerates there before)?” (ibid. 5:9). “And if you say in your heart: Why have these (אֵלֶּה) things befallen me?” (ibid. 13:22). “Whoever is wise, let him understand these (אֵלֶּה) things, whoever is prudent, let him know them” (Hosea 14:10). “Is the spirit of the Lord straitened? Are these (אֵלֶּה) His doings?” (Micah 2:7). “These (אֵלֶּה) things I remember, and pour out my soul within me” (Psalms 42:5). “Lo, all these (אֵלֶּה) things God does, twice, three times, with a man” (Job 33:29). “For these (אֵלֶּה) things I weep; my eye, my eye runs down with water, because the comforter that should refresh my soul is far from me” (Lamentations 1:16). “For this our heart is faint, for these (אֵלֶּה) things our eyes are dim” (ibid. 5:17). — And repeated, אֵלֶּה — אֵלֶּה, אֵלֶּה — וְאֵלֶּה: “And they (Aram and Israel) encamped one (אֵלֶּה) over against the other (אֵלֶה) seven days” (1 Kings 20:29). “And the others came forth out of the city against them, so they were in the midst of Israel, some (אֵלֶּה) on this side and some (וְאֵלֶּה) on that side” (Joshua 8:22). “And they (the servants of Joab and the servants of David) sat down, the one (אֵלֶּה) on the one side of the pool and the other (וְאֵלֶּה) on the other side of the pool” (2 Samuel 2:13). — And in the sense of “some of them”: “Behold, these (אֵלֶּה) shall come from far, and lo, these (אֵלֶּה) from the north and from the west, and these (וְאֵלֶּה) from the land of Sinim” (Isaiah 49:12). “Some (אֵלֶּה) trust in chariots and some (וְאֵלֶּה) in horses, but we will make mention of the name of the Lord our God” (Psalms 20:8). — And with the prefixes ב, כ, ל, מ: “And if he be not redeemed by these (בְּאֵלֶּה) means, then he shall go out in the year of jubilee” (Leviticus 25:54). “And if in spite of these (בְּאֵלֶּה) things you will not be corrected by me” (ibid. 23). “And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made him horns of iron, and said: Thus says the Lord: With these (בְּאֵלֶּה) shall you gore the Arameans” (1 Kings 22:11). “But let him that glories glory in this, that he understands and knows me, that I am the Lord who exercises mercy, justice and righteousness in the earth; for in these (בְאֵלֶּה) things I delight, says the Lord” (Jeremiah 9:23). “They (the idols) are vanity, a work of delusion; in the time of their visitation they shall perish. The portion of Jacob is not like these (כְאֵלֶּה), for He is the former of all things” (ibid. 15–16). “Then Job answered and said: I have heard many such things (כְאֵלֶּה); sorry comforters are you all” (Job 16:1–2). “And by these (וּלְאֵלֶּה) you shall become unclean etc.: every beast which parts the hoof” (Leviticus 11:24–26). “And to the others (וּלְאֵלֶּה) He said in my hearing: Go through the city after him, and smite” (Ezekiel 9:5). “Of these (מְאֵלֶּה) were the isles of the nations divided in their lands” (Genesis 10:5). “And it shall be, when he shall be guilty in one of these (מֵאֵלֶּה) things, that he shall confess” (Leviticus 5:5). “And Balak sent yet again princes, more, and more honourable than they (מֵאֵלֶּה)” (Numbers 22:15). “And I look, but there is no man; even among them (ומֵאֵלֶה), but there is no counsellor” (Isaiah 41:28). — With a number, the word אלה comes after the number: “These (אֵלֶּה) three were the sons of Noah” (Genesis 9:19). “And if he do not these (אֵלֶּה) three things for her” (Exodus 21:11). “But these (אֵלֶּה) two things shall come to you in a moment in one day” (Isaiah 47:9). “These (אֵלֶּה) seven, they are the eyes of the Lord” (Zechariah 4:10).

he: משקל אֵבֶל, חֵפֶש וכיוצא בהם. ואעפ"י שיש ספק באמתת מציאות המלה בצורה זו לפנים, עי' הערה לקמן, אעפי"כ הואיל וכבר השתמשו בה הפיטנים והמשוררים, כנראה מהמשלים המובאים לקמן, יש לה זכות מלה בלשוננו. -, ש"ז, - המום של האִלֵּם, ובמליצה ההתאפקות מלדבר,  Stummheit; mutisme; dumbness: למנצח על יונת אֵלֶםהיתר מסתבר כדעת החדשים שזה שם כלי מכלי הנגינה, ואולי יש פה שבוש. אך הקדמונים, בעלי התלמ' והתרגום, רש"י ורדק ועוד, מפרשים אֵלֶם במשמ' שם מפשט, כמו אִלמוּת. רק רסע"ג פרש אלם קהל, מלשון מאלמים אלומים, ותרגם ג'מעא. וריב"ג פקפק ויפרש אלם זה מלשון אלמון והוא ארמון. - רחקים תהל' נו א. האמנם אֵלֶםגם פה נראים דברי הסוברים (הרמבן והחדשים) כי צריך לקרא אַלִים. אך תלמו' ותרגום ורשי מפרשים במשמ' אלמות, ורסע"ג פרש גם אלם זה קהל, וכן ריב"ג. צדק תדברון שם נח ב. - ואמר הפיטן:  אֵלֶם פיהן יה צדק ר"י בן יוסי, בשופרות. יה רם וגאה הקריבה אֵלֶם רחוק אליו אמרת ובכן קח נא את בנך את יחידך אשר אהבת אהב' לפ' ויר'. - ואמר המשורר: יונת אֵלֶם צבי לחשך ר"י הלוי, והוא כנוי לאֻמת ישראל. - וכנ': הרבו גבוהות לענות יום אלמו (ר"ל האֵלם שלו) אך נאלמו עמו רמב"ע, דברי חכמים פג.
en: [Note: The pattern of אֵבֶל, חֵפֶש and the like. And although there is doubt as to the true existence of the word in this form in former times, see the note below, nevertheless, since the liturgical poets and the poets have already used it, as appears from the examples cited below, it has the right of a word in our language.] -, masculine noun, - the defect of the אִלֵּם, and in poetic style, refraining from speech, German Stummheit; French mutisme; English dumbness: "For the Leader; on the dove of silence (אֵלֶם) [Note: Most plausible is the view of the moderns that this is the name of one of the musical instruments, and perhaps there is a corruption here. But the ancients, the masters of the Talmud and the Targum, Rashi and Radak and others, explain אֵלֶם in the sense of an abstract noun, like אִלמוּת. Only Rav Saadia Gaon explained אלם as a congregation, from the expression מאלמים אלומים, and translated ג'מעא. And Ibn Janach is doubtful, and explains this אלם from the expression אלמון, which is a palace.] - far off" (Psalms 56:1). "Do you indeed in silence (אֵלֶם) [Note: Here too the words of those who hold (Ramban and the moderns) that one should read אַלִים appear right. But the Talmud and the Targum and Rashi explain it in the sense of muteness, and Rav Saadia Gaon explained this אלם too as a congregation, and so Ibn Janach.] speak righteousness" (ibid. 58:2). - And the liturgical poet said: "The muteness (אֵלֶם) of their mouth, God is righteous" (R. Yose ben Yose, in Shofarot). "God exalted and proud, 'Bring near the mute (אֵלֶם), distant one to Him,' You said, and so, 'Take now your son, your only one, whom you love'" (Ahavah for parashat Vayera). - And the poet said: "Dove of silence (יונת אֵלֶם), צבי your whisper" (R. Judah Halevi, and it is an epithet for the nation of Israel). - And with suffix: "They multiplied haughty words to answer on the day of his silence (אלמו) (that is, his אֵלֶם), but they fell mute with him" (R. Moses ibn Ezra, Divrei Chakhamim 83).

he: ° באשורית אִלְתֻ, מ"ר אִלָתִ. בער' אִלָהַה إِلآھة., ש"נ, סמי' אֵלָת, אֵלָתִי,  — אלהות נקבה, Göttin; déesse; goddess goddes במקור המודפס — הערת פב"י: אתנה בתו היא מנרוה אֵלַת החכמה, אפרודיתה אֵלַת היפי האהבה והתענוגים ועוד אֵלִים וְאֵלוֹת וכו' מקום משכן הָאֵלִים וְהָאֵלוֹת האלה היה לפי דמיונם על אחד מהרי תסליה הוא הר הקדש אלמפוס (דה"י ב"י, היונים).
en: [Note: ° In Assyrian (Akkadian) אִלְתֻ, plural אִלָתִ. In Arabic אִלָהַה إِلآھة.], feminine noun, construct אֵלָת, אֵלָתִי, — a female deity, German Göttin; French déesse; English goddess [Note: "goddes" in the printed source — Project Ben-Yehuda note.]: "Athena his daughter, she is Minerva, goddess (אֵלַת) of wisdom; Aphrodite, goddess (אֵלַת) of beauty, love and pleasures; and other gods and goddesses (וְאֵלוֹת) etc. The dwelling place of these gods and goddesses (וְהָאֵלוֹת) was, according to their imagination, on one of the mountains of Thessaly, that is the holy mountain Olympus" (דה"י ב"י, "The Greeks").

he: אולי דומה לזה בערב' אַלַא, אַלַי أَلَا, أَلَّى, אילן מר תמיד ירוק. והסכימו קצת הראשוני' וכל האחרוני' כי זה שם היחידה לאֵיל אֵילים. אך ריב"ג ורד"ק מפקפקים בזה, וסברים כי הם אולי שני שמות שונים: אֵיל אֵילים שם כללי כמו אילן, וכן ת"י אֵילים (ישעיה א כט) אילניא, ואֵלה שם למין אחד מהאילנות, ויקבץ א"כ אֵלוֹת כמו שַׁרה שַׁרוֹת. וכן דונש בן לברט (תשוב' על רסע"ג סי' מט), אעפ"י שהוא סבר כי אֵלים הוא הקבוץ מן אֵלה, מ"מ הוא מחליט כי אפשר גם קבוץ אֵלות ומסים ואומר: ודע כי השמות האלה הנקבות שנתקבצו במם (כמו אשרה אשרים וכו') אם קבצתם בתו (ר"ל -רות) אתה על האמת. ע"כ. — ועי' למעלה ערך אֵיל. ובאשור' אַלָּנֻ לאחד ממיני האילן. בארמ' אלינא אילן בכלל. אונקלס תרגם תחת האלה (בראש' לה ד) תחות בוטמא: וכן ת"י במקומות הרשומים בפנים. וכן תרגם רס"ג בערבי' בוטמא. וכן ריב"ג: והוא הנקרא בלשון ערבי בטם. וכן רד"ק: ובוטם הוא בלעז terebinthus . והשבעים תרגמו אַלָה באילן זה ואֵלָה תרגמו פעמים בזה ופעמים באילן שקראים לו בערב בלוט. רש"י פרש אילים ואלה אולמא בלעז, אך זה כנראה רק השערה מפני דמיון שתי המלים., ש"נ, שם היחיד, מ"ר אֶלים, אֵלוֹת — שם אילן גדול מצוי, ממין הבטנה,   terebinthus: ויטמן אתם יעקב תחת הָאֵלָה אשר עם שכם (ברא' לה ד). וישב (המלאך) תחת הָאֵלָה אשר בעפרה (שופט' ו יא). ואבשלום רכב על הפרד ויבא הפרד תחת שובך הָאֵלָה הגדולה ויחזק ראשו בָאֵלָה ויֻתן בין השמים ובין הארץ (ש"ב יח ט). על ראשי ההרים יזבחו ועל הגבעות יקטרו תחת אלון ולבנה וְאֵלָה כי טוב צלה (הושע' ד יג). כי תהיו כְּאֵלָה נבלת עלה וכגנה אשר מים אין לה (ישע' א ל). אל כל גבעה רמה בכל ראשי ההרים ותחת כל עץ רענן ותחת כל אֵלָה עבתה (יחזק' ו יג). ולולבי האלהכך "חסר" בכל הנוסח'. זולתי במדב"מ האילה מלא. ונראה מפרוש הר"ש כי קרא אֵלָה, כיון שהביא הפסוק בישעי' ו כאֵלה וכאלון. וכן נקוד במשנ' המנקד' (דפ' אמש"ד ופיסא), ורמב"ם בפרוש המשנה תרגם אלה בלוט. והעיר ע"ז עמנ' לֶו (שמות הצמחים סי' מד), כי לפי פי' זה של הרמב"ם צריך לקרא פה אַלה, וראיה לזה הכתיב החסר. ע"כ. אך המלים של המקרא כתובים במשנה ובתלמוד עפי"ר "חסרים" גם אחרי צירה או חירק, ובמדב"מ הכתיב הוא אילה ולא אלה. והבטנה והאטדין (שבי' ז ה). האלהובהערה שם מראה מקום לבראש' לה ד(האֵלה אשר עם שכם) והביא התרגום בוטמא.   terebinthus P הוא עץ גדל על אי ציפרען אשר ממנו ישיגו אם יבקעו בו שמן טערפענטין (תולד' האר' מ' שינהק ב סי' רא).
en: [Note: Perhaps similar to this, in Arabic אַלַא, אַלַי أَلَا, أَلَّى, a bitter, evergreen tree. And some of the early authorities and all the later ones agreed that this is the singular of אֵיל, אֵילים. But Ibn Janah and Radak are doubtful about this, and hold that they are perhaps two different nouns: אֵיל, אֵילים a general term like אילן (tree) — and so Targum Jonathan renders אֵילים (Isaiah 1:29) as אילניא — and אֵלה the name of one species of the trees, and accordingly its plural would be אֵלוֹת, like שַׁרה, שַׁרוֹת. And so Dunash ben Labrat (Responses to Rabbi Saadia Gaon §49), although he held that אֵלים is the plural of אֵלה, nevertheless decides that a plural אֵלות is also possible, and concludes, saying: "And know that these feminine nouns that were pluralized with mem (like אשרה, אשרים etc.), if you pluralize them with tav (that is, -ות), you are correct." End quote. — And see above, the entry אֵיל. And in Akkadian אַלָּנֻ, for one of the species of tree. In Aramaic אלינא, a tree in general. Onkelos translated "under the terebinth (האלה)" (Genesis 35:4) as תחות בוטמא; and so Targum Jonathan in the places noted in the text. And so Rabbi Saadia Gaon translated in Arabic בוטמא. And so Ibn Janah: "And it is what is called in the Arabic language בטם." And so Radak: "And בוטם is in the vernacular terebinthus." And the Septuagint translated אַלָה by this tree, and אֵלָה they translated sometimes by this one and sometimes by the tree that in Arabic is called בלוט. Rashi explained אילים and אלה as אולמא in the vernacular, but this is apparently only a conjecture because of the resemblance of the two words.], feminine noun, the singular, plural אֶלים, אֵלוֹת — name of a large, common tree, of the species of the בטנה (pistachio), terebinthus: "And Jacob hid them under the terebinth that was by Shechem" (Genesis 35:4). "And he (the angel) sat under the terebinth that was in Ophrah" (Judges 6:11). "And Absalom was riding upon the mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of the great terebinth, and his head caught hold of the terebinth, and he was left hanging between heaven and earth" (2 Samuel 18:9). "They sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains, and burn incense upon the hills, under oak and poplar and terebinth, because their shade is good" (Hosea 4:13). "For you shall be as a terebinth whose leaf fades, and as a garden that has no water" (Isaiah 1:30). "upon every high hill, on all the tops of the mountains, and under every green tree, and under every thick terebinth" (Ezekiel 6:13). "And the shoots of the terebinth (האלה) [Note: So, "defective", in all the editions, except in מדב"מ, האילה plene. And it appears from the commentary of Rabbi Samson that he read אֵלָה, since he cited the verse in Isaiah 6, "like the terebinth and like the oak". And so it is vocalized in the vocalized Mishnah (editions of Amsterdam and Pisa); and Rambam in the Commentary on the Mishnah translated אלה as בלוט. And Immanuel Löw remarked on this (Plant Names §44) that according to this explanation of Rambam one must read here אַלה, and the proof of this is the defective spelling. End quote. But the words of Scripture are written in the Mishnah and the Talmud for the most part "defective" even after tzere or hiriq, and in מדב"מ the spelling is אילה and not אלה.] and the pistachio and the thornbushes" (Shevi'it 7:5). "The terebinth (האלה) [Note: And in the note there it gives a reference to Genesis 35:4 (the terebinth that was by Shechem) and cites the Targum בוטמא.] terebinthus P is a tree that grows on the island of Cyprus, from which, if they split it, they obtain turpentine oil" (Toledot ha-Aretz by M. Schoenhak 2 §201).

he: * כך הקריאה המקבלת של הספרדים, וגם האשכנזים, והתימנים, וכן במשנ' המנקדות, וכן בסדרי תפלה המנקדים., מלת הרמז לרבים ורבות, כמו אלֶּה:  אלו הן בין הפרקים בין ברכה ראשונה לשניה (ברכ' ב ב).  אלו ואלו (את שלפני המטה ואת שלאחרי המטה הנזכר שם) פטורים מן התפלה (שם ג א).  אלו דברים שבין בית שמאי ובית הלל בסעודה (שם ח א).  אלו דברים שאדם אוכל פירותיהן בעוה"ז והקרן קיימת לו לעולם הבא כבוד אב ואם וגמילות חסדים והבאת שלום בין אדם לחבירו (פאה א א).  אלו דברים שאדם יוצא בהן ידי חובתו בפסח (פסח' ב ה).  אלו מציאות שלו ואלו חייב להכריז (ב"מ ב א).  ואלו הן שמצילין אותן בנפשם הרודף אחר חבירו וכו' (סנה' ח ז).  ואלו הן הנשרפין וכו' ואלו הן הנהרגין הרוצח ואנשי עיר הנדחת (שם ט א).  ואלו נאמנין להעיד בגודלן מה שראו בקוטנן (כתוב' ב י).  אלו נערות שיש להן קנס (שם ג א).  אלו הן החרצניים ואלו הן הזגים החרצנים אלו החיצונים והזגים אלו הפנימים (נזיר ו ב).  על אלו טומאות הנזיר מגלה (שם ז ב).  אלו באו בכבודם ואלו באו בניוולם ((מד"ר קהלת בכל עת).  וקבעו שמונת ימי חנכה אֵלּוּ להודות ולהלל לשמך הגדול (תפל' שמ"ע, בימי מתתיהו).  – ועם ה הידיעה אחרי השם:  הרי הפירות האלו נתונים לך במתנה (מע"ש ד ה).  ארבעת מראות האלו מצטרפין זע"ז (נגע' ל ג).  – ובענין זה גם בלי ה ולפני השם:  מכל אלו הדברים נתבאר לך (רמב"ם, זרע' כלא' ד).  התכלית אשר התהוו אלו הדברים בעבורה (רלב"ג, מלח' א ו).  שלא השיג איוב עצת ה' על מה הביא לו אלו היסורין (ע"ח לר' אהרן הקראי).  למה באו לו אלו הצרות וכו' כל אלו המהומות (דה"י ליוסף הכהן, א ח).  – אֵלּוּ בְאֵלּוּ:  אם ראית מלכיות מתגרות אלו באלו צפה לרגלו של משיח תדע שכן שהרי בימי אברהם ע"י שנתגרו המלכיות אלו באלו באה הגאולה לאברהם (מ"ר ברא' מב).   – אֵלוּ עם אֵלוּ:  הן חולקין אלו עם אלו (שם שה"ש, אחת היא).  – מאֵלוּ: שתי חבורות שנתערבו פסחיהן וכו' אחד מאלו בא לו אצל אלו ואחד מאלו בא לו אצל אלו (פסחים ט י).   – אֵלוּ ש:  עד שאתה מביט באלו שאוכלין ושותין (מד"ר שה"ש, ברח דודי).  להטביל את אלו שעליה (רשי ביצה יח.).  – ועם אֵי, אֵי אֵלוּ, ועי' אֵי.
en: * [Note: This is the received reading of the Sephardim, and also of the Ashkenazim and the Yemenites, and likewise in the vocalized editions of the Mishnah and in the vocalized prayer books.] Demonstrative word for masculine and feminine plural, like אֵלֶּה: "These are 'between the sections': between the first blessing and the second" (Berakhot 2:2). "These and those (those before the bier and those after the bier, mentioned there) are exempt from prayer" (ibid. 3:1). "These are the matters between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel concerning a meal" (ibid. 8:1). "These are the things whose fruits a person eats in this world while the principal remains for him for the World to Come: honoring father and mother, acts of lovingkindness, and bringing peace between a person and his fellow" (Peah 1:1). "These are the things with which a person fulfills his obligation on Passover" (Pesachim 2:5). "These found objects are his, and these he must announce" (Bava Metzia 2:1). "And these are the ones whom one saves at the cost of their lives: one who pursues his fellow, etc." (Sanhedrin 8:7). "And these are the ones who are burned, etc. And these are the ones who are slain: the murderer and the people of an apostate city" (ibid. 9:1). "And these are believed when grown up to testify to what they saw when young" (Ketubot 2:10). "These are the maidens who are entitled to a fine" (ibid. 3:1). "Which are the חַרְצַנִּים and which are the זַגִּים? The חַרְצַנִּים are the outer ones and the זַגִּים are the inner ones" (Nazir 6:2). "For these impurities the nazirite shaves" (ibid. 7:2). "These came in their honor and these came in their disgrace" (Ecclesiastes Rabbah, "To every thing there is a season"). "And they established these (אֵלּוּ) eight days of Hanukkah to give thanks and praise to Your great name" (Amidah prayer, "In the days of Mattathias"). – And with the definite article ה after the noun: "Behold, these fruits are given to you as a gift" (Maaser Sheni 4:5). "These four appearances combine with one another" (Negaim 30:3). – And in this sense also without ה and before the noun: "From all these matters it has been made clear to you" (Rambam, Zeraim, Kilayim 4). "The purpose for the sake of which these things came into being" (Ralbag, Milchamot 1:6). "That Job did not grasp the counsel of the Lord as to why He brought these sufferings upon him" (Etz Chaim by Rabbi Aaron the Karaite). "Why these troubles came upon him, etc., all these tumults" (Divrei Hayamim by Joseph ha-Kohen, 1:8). – אֵלּוּ בְאֵלּוּ: "If you see kingdoms provoking one another (אלו באלו), look for the footsteps of the Messiah. Know that it is so, for in the days of Abraham, because the kingdoms provoked one another, redemption came to Abraham" (Genesis Rabbah 42). – אֵלוּ עם אֵלוּ: "They disagree with one another (אלו עם אלו)" (ibid., Song of Songs, "She is one"). – מֵאֵלוּ: "Two groups whose Passover offerings became mixed up, etc.: one of these comes over to those, and one of those comes over to these" (Pesachim 9:10). – אֵלוּ שֶׁ: "While you are looking at those who eat and drink" (Song of Songs Rabbah, "Flee, my beloved"). "To immerse those that are on it" (Rashi, Beitzah 18a). – And with אֵי: אֵי אֵלוּ, and see אֵי.

he: עי' הערה לאַלּוֹן., ש"ז, כמו אֵלָה, בשמות פרטים של מקומות:  אֵלוֹן מורה (בראש' יב ו), וכדומה, אֵלוֹנֵי ממרא (שם יג יח).  שתו ושכרו מיין אשישי כי על הָאֵלוֹן תלו את אריסַי (אמרי נועם לי' גליינו, פורים פורים).
en: [Note: See the note to אַלּוֹן.], masculine noun, like אֵלָה, in proper names of places: אֵלוֹן מורה (Genesis 12:6), and the like, אֵלוֹנֵי ממרא (ibid. 13:18). "Drink and become drunk from the wine of my flagons, for on the oak they hanged אריסַי" (Imrei No'am by י' גליינו, פורים פורים).

he: אֵמִים, — א) עי' אֵים. — ב) °כדור הירייה מנשק של אש וכדומה,   Kugel; balle; ball: שבגלל הדבר הזה (האימה הנופלת על הבריות) יקראו הכדורים (המוטלים מתוך נשק האש) אמים (שלט' הגבורים פר' מב).
en: אֵמִים, — a) see אֵים. — b) °the bullet of a firearm and the like, German Kugel; French balle; English ball: "For because of this matter (the terror that falls upon people) the balls (shot from within the firearm) are called אמים" (Shiltei ha-Gibborim, chapter 42).
