החמשי הנזר כאשר עשיתי זֶה כמה שנים (שם ז ג).  כי צמתם וספוד בחמישי ובשביעי וְזֶה שבעים שנה הצום צמתֻני אני (שם ה).  זֶה עשר פעמים תכלימוני (איוב יט ג).  ותבוא ותעמוד מאז הבקר ועד עתה זֶה שבתה הבית מעט (רות ב ז). – ה) אחרי מלת השאלה מַה, לָמָּה, מַה=זֶּה, לָמֳּה=זֶּהבערב' לִמַאדַא لمَاذَا., לחזק השאלה;  ויאמר יצחק אל בנו מַה=זֶּה מהרת למצא בני (בראש' כז כ).  וּמַה=זֶּה תאמרו אלי מה לך (שופט' יח כד).  ויאמר העם איש אל רעהו מַה=זֶּה היה לבן קיש הגם שאול בנביאים (ש"א י יא). ותבא אליו איזבל אשתו ותדבר אליו מַה=זֶּה רוחך סרה ואינך אכל לחם (מ"א כא ה). וישובו המלאכים אליו ויאמר אליהם מָה=זֶּה שבתם (מ"ב א ה).  ויאמר לי המלך על מַה=זֶּה אתה מבקש (נחמ' ב ד).  ותאמר אם כן למה זֶּה אנכי (בראש' כה כב).  הנה אנכי הולך למות ולמה=זֶּה לי בכרה (שם לב).  ויאמר למה זֶּה תשאל לשמי (שם לב ל).  ויאמר אל בנתיו ואיו למה זֶּה עזבתן את האיש (שמות ב כ).  אדני למה הרעתה לעם הזה למה זֶּה שלחתני (שם ה כב).  וילן העם על משה ויאמר למה זֶּה העליתנו ממצרים (שם יז ג).  ויאמר משה למה זֶּה אתם עברים את פי יי' (במד' יד מא).  ויאמר יי' אל יהושע קֻם לך למה זֶּה אתה נפל על פניך (יהוש' ז י).  ויחר אף אליאב בדוד ויאמר למה=זֶּה ירדת (ש"א יז כח).  הנה בא אבנר אליך למה=זֶּה שלחתו וילך הלוך (ש"ב ג כד).  ועתה מת למה זֶּה אנכי צם (שם יב כג).  ולמה זֶּה חרה לך על הדבר הזה (שם יט מג).  למה זֶּה את מתנכרה (מ"א יד ו).  למה=זֶּה לי לבונה משבא תבוא (ירמ' ו כ).  למה זֶּה מרחם יצאתי לראות עמל ויגון (שם כ יח).  הוי המתאוים את יום יי' למה=זֶּה לכם יום יי' (עמוס ה יח). למה=זֶּה מחיר ביד כסיל לקנות חכמה ולב אין (משלי יז יו).  אנכי ארשע למה=זֶּה הבל איגע (איוב ט כט). – ואחרי הִנֵּה, הֲרֵי:   וישכב ויישן תחת רתם אחד וְהִנֵּה=זֶה מלאך נגע בו ויאמר לו קום אכול (מ"א יט ה).  ועל משמרתי אנכי נצב כל הלילות וְהִנֵּה=זֶה בא רכב איש צמד פרשים (ישע' כא ח=ט). מרחץ שהוסקה בתבן או בקש של שביעית מותר לרחוץ בה ואם מתחשב הוא הרי זה לא ירחוץ (שביע' ח יא).  אמרו לו הבא עדים ואמר אין לי עדים אמרו הבא ראיה ואמר אין לי ראיה ולאחר זמן הביא ראיה ומצא עדים הרי זה אינו כלום (סנה' ג ח).  מצא כלי כסף וכלי נחושת וכו' הרי זה לא יחזיר עד שיתן אות או עד שיכוין משקלותיו (ב"מ כג:).  המוציא זבל על ראשו ותפילין בראשו הרי זה לא יסלקם לצדדים ולא יקשרם במתניו מפני שהוא נוהג בהם מנהג בזיון (שם קה:).
en: In Canaanite/Phoenician ז, אז; in Arabic dhā ﺫاٝ; in South Arabian ḏn, ḏt; in Aramaic דֵן, דנא. And behold, the segol testifies that in Hebrew too they said זה with the zayin with patach, and only at a late time did they incline to the sound of the segol; and so too in the Assyrian (Babylonian) vocalization: “And so every segol with us at the end of a word, when it is stressed, will be followed by a visible quiescent letter or a hidden quiescent letter; it is in place of a great patach, as in אש"ר אמ"ת גרז"ן כרמ"ל אמרפ"ל נגל"ה עוש"ה מקנ"ה ז"ה, and not as Radak says, that it is in place of tzere” (Introduction to the Assyrian Vocalization 54); and so the Yemenites read, and so they also say in speech: זַה, with the zayin with patach. And Fischer (ZDMG, 59, 443) has already rejected Barth's opinion that originally the word was זי, and so too Brockelmann. – The demonstrative word in place of a masculine pronoun, German dieser, French ce, celui, English this; and it comes: a) By itself: “And he called his name Noah, saying: This one shall comfort us concerning our work” (Genesis 5:29). “This one (the house-born son whom Abraham mentioned) shall not be your heir, but he that shall come forth out of your own bowels” (ibid. 15:4). “And she conceived again and bore a son, and said: Because the Lord has heard that I am hated, he has given me this one also” (ibid. 28:33). “And Jacob said when he saw them (the angels mentioned above): This is God's camp” (ibid. 32:3). “And the midwife took and bound upon his hand (the first child's) a scarlet thread, saying: This one came out first” (ibid. 38:28). “You know that my wife bore me two sons; and the one went out from me etc. And if you take this one also from me, and harm befall him” (ibid. 44:27–29). “And it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel etc., and the one came not near the other all the night” (Exodus 14:20). “Behold the man of whom I spoke to you! This one shall rule over my people” (1 Samuel 9:17). “But certain worthless fellows said: How shall this one save us? And they despised him” (ibid. 10:27). “Do I lack madmen, that you have brought this one to play the madman in my presence?” (ibid. 21:16). “For with what should this one reconcile himself to his master?” (ibid. 29:4). “Put this one in the prison” (1 Kings 22:27). “Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this one sends to me to recover a man of his leprosy?” (2 Kings 5:7). “And one called to another and said: Holy” (Isaiah 6:3). – And Ben Sira said: “Like a blossom that grows on a fresh tree, of which this one withers and another sprouts” (Ben Sira, Genizah, 18). “And this and that, which have the breath of life in them, are not like fire, which has no breath of life in it” (Bava Kamma 1:1). “This one came with his barrel and that one came with his beam; the jar of this one broke on the beam of that one — he is exempt, for this one has the right to walk and that one has the right to walk” (ibid. 3:5). “For a man stamps many coins with one seal and they are all like one another” (Sanhedrin 4:5). “This one pulls toward himself and that one pulls toward himself” (ibid. 7:2). “One who hires craftsmen and they deceived one another — they have nothing against one another but resentment” (Bava Metzia 6:1). “An armed robber is in this man's house, and we are to go in to him?” (Bava Kamma 80a). “The residents of alleys may compel one another not to settle among them a tailor, nor a tanner, nor a teacher of children” (Bava Batra 21b). “And would it enter your mind that this one walks in the market and that one is killed?” (Sanhedrin 78b). “Rabbi Yochanan said: Behold, how many years this one has grown up among us, and he did not hear this halakhah from me” (Keritot 27a). “He said to them: If this is a rabbi, may there not be many like him in Israel” (Derekh Eretz Rabbah 4). “Where is the good of this one, and where is the length of days of this one?” (Ruth Rabbah, “Lodge this night”). “These Jews are keepers of the Sabbatical year, and they have no vegetables, and they ate this man's thistles, and he mourns over them” (ibid. Lamentations, Petichta). “‘And maidens without number’ — there is no end to the students; one might think that they disagree with one another; Scripture says: ‘My dove, my undefiled, is but one’” (ibid. Song of Songs, “She is one”). – And with the interrogative ה: “Shall this one come into my house?” (1 Samuel 21:16). “For you do not know which shall prosper, whether this or that” (Ecclesiastes 11:6). – And with the noun after it and before it: “Oh that they had this heart of theirs, to fear me” (Deuteronomy 5:29). “This our son is stubborn and rebellious” (ibid. 21:20). “If you do not tell this business of ours” (Joshua 2:14). “Go in this your might, and save Israel” (Judges 6:14). “Whether I shall recover from this sickness” (2 Kings 1:2). “For as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him” (Exodus 32:1). “This our bread we took hot for our provision out of our houses” (Joshua 9:12). “Whose son is this youth?” (1 Samuel 17:55). “Behold the land of the Chaldeans; this people was not” (Isaiah 23:13). “The earth trembled, the heavens also dropped at the presence of God; this Sinai, at the presence of God, the God of Israel” (Psalms 68:9). “This sea, great and wide, wherein are creeping things innumerable” (ibid. 104:25). “When the foundation of this house was laid” (Ezra 3:12). – And it is found in the later literature: “For many years he pondered this verse and did not know its reason” (Ibn Ezra on Exodus 19:23). “And this matter is harder than all the difficulties we had” (ibid. 20:1). “And behold, this time was close to their journey” (ibid. 18:1). “And this matter was the cause of suspecting the sage of a great sin” (Introduction to Malmad ha-Talmidim). “Because of this deed, since Moses knew that he would in the future go with the spies” (Ramban on Exodus 17:9). “Since they (the ants) have no leader and they make this order and this conduct, how much more so man, who possesses a soul” (Commentary on Proverbs by Zerachiah ha-Levi 6:3). “He brought this parable to hint at the caution required of one who possesses intellect” (ibid.). “Behold, it will necessarily be like this very world” (Don Isaac Abravanel, Mif'alot Elohim 8:4). “And according to the opinion of this sage, that he (man) cannot apprehend Him (the Creator) because He is not like everything else” (Etz Chayyim by Aaron the Karaite 41). – And with the letters כ, ל, מ: “Can we find such a one as this (as Joseph), a man in whom the spirit of God is?” (Genesis 41:38). “And shall my soul not be avenged on such a nation as this?” (Jeremiah 5:9). “Is such the fast that I have chosen, the day for a man to afflict his soul?” (Isaiah 58:5). “Rabban Gamliel had images of the shapes of the moon on a tablet and on the wall of his upper chamber, with which he would show the unlearned and say: Did you see it like this, or like this?” (Rosh Hashanah 2:8). “Is not this the one (David, mentioned above) of whom they sang one to another in dances, saying: Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands?” (1 Samuel 21:12). “Now David had said: Surely in vain have I kept all that this fellow (Nabal, whom he mentioned above) has in the wilderness, so that nothing was missed of all that pertained to him” (ibid. 25:21). “Will you call this a fast?” (Isaiah 58:5). “When the market price is out, they may fix a price, for even though this one does not have it, that one has it” (Bava Metzia 5:7). “Woe to this one, whose defender became his accuser” (Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 3, 53c). “This one has more rest than the other” (Ecclesiastes 6:5). “Two houses, one inside the other” (Bava Batra 53b). “Charity collectors are not permitted to separate from one another, but this one may go off to the gate and that one to the shop” (ibid. 8b). “For the benefit that follows from this language is great and necessary for the Torah” (Ha-Ikkarim 1:11). “They estimate how much a man like this would want to be paid to suffer so” (Bava Kamma 8:1). “He saw his students looking at one another; he said to them: Is it hard in your eyes that I have pushed off my enemy with a straw?” (Chullin 27b). – b) Like an adjective after the noun, with the definite article ה: “For you have I seen righteous before me in this generation” (Genesis 7:1). “Up, get out of this place” (ibid. 19:14). “Will you go with this man?” (ibid. 24:58). “Take this child away” (Exodus 2:9). – And before the noun, in the sense of stating the proposition and determining the matter positively or negatively, with the verb הָיָה included in it: “This is the book of the generations of Adam” (Genesis 5:1). “Is not this the cup in which my lord drinks?” (ibid. 44:5). “This was the offering of Nahshon the son of Amminadab” (Numbers 7:17). “This is the offering made by fire which you shall offer to the Lord” (ibid. 28:3). “This is the portion of them that spoil us” (Isaiah 17:14). “This is your lot, the portion measured to you” (Jeremiah 13:25). “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” (Genesis 43:29). “This is the rule: anyone who slaughters or receives etc. outside its place — it is invalid” (Zevachim 2:3). “This is the rule: what is made to assist at the time of work is susceptible to impurity” (Kelim 15:4). – And with the pronouns: “Are you my very son Esau?” (Genesis 27:21). “Is it you, my lord Elijah?” (1 Kings 18:7). “Is it you, you troubler of Israel?” (ibid. 17). “For who is he that has pledged his heart to approach me?” (Jeremiah 30:21). “Who is he, this King of glory?” (Psalms 24:10). – c) Like זֹאת, in the sense of a general reference to what was mentioned or will be mentioned, in place of “this thing”: “And Pharaoh's servants said to him: How long shall this (the Jews' staying in Egypt) be a snare to us? Let the men go, that they may serve the Lord their God” (Exodus 10:7). “It is because of this which the Lord did for me when I came forth out of Egypt” (ibid. 13:8). “Seven hundred chosen men, left-handed; every one of these could sling a stone at a hair” (Judges 20:16). “For this our heart is faint; for these things our eyes are dim; for the mountain of Zion, which is desolate, the foxes walk upon it” (Lamentations 5:17–18). “And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly; I perceived that this also is a striving after wind” (Ecclesiastes 1:17). “Say not: How was it that the former days were better than these? For it is not out of wisdom that you inquire concerning this” (ibid. 7:10). “For all this I laid to my heart, even to make clear all this” (ibid. 9:1). “Yet all this (all the honour and greatness he mentioned above) avails me nothing” (Esther 5:13). “What honour and dignity has been done to Mordecai for this?” (ibid. 6:3). – וְעִם=זֶה, in the sense of nevertheless: “Now that which was prepared for one day was one ox and six choice sheep etc.; yet with this I did not demand the bread of the governor, because the service was heavy upon this people” (Nehemiah 5:18). – And in the sense of a relative word, like אֲשֶׁר: “And it shall be said in that day: Lo, this is our God, for whom we waited, that he might save us” (Isaiah 25:9). “Mount Zion, wherein you have dwelt” (Psalms 74:2). “Leviathan, whom you have formed to sport therein” (Psalms 104:26). “To the place which you had founded for them” (ibid. 8). “Hearken to your father that begot you” (Proverbs 23:22). “I will tell you, hear me; and that which I have seen I will declare” (Job 15:17). – And even for the plural: “All my intimate friends abhor me, and they whom I loved are turned against me” (Job 19:19). – And it is found in the later literature with שֶׁ or שֶׁהוּא after it: “If he saw the found object and fell upon it, and another came and seized it, the one who seized it has acquired it” (Bava Metzia 1:4). “One who sees a bad dream” (Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 5:1). “One who goes to the synagogue must make his feet light” (ibid.). “If he was reading in the Torah and became mute, the one who stands in his place should begin from where the first began” (ibid. 3). “If this one had one entrance and that one two entrances, the one who has one entrance takes four cubits and the one who has two entrances takes eight cubits” (Bava Batra 11a). “A parable of two who entered a bathhouse: the one who sweats first goes out first” (Leviticus Rabbah 14). “In the way of the world, one who crosses over a river cannot avoid drinking” (ibid. Numbers 21). “Moses said: Master of the world, one who killed a person unwittingly in the north or in the south, how does he know where the cities of refuge are, that he may flee there?” (ibid. 23). “And likewise they disgrace the one whose reputation is bad and revile the mother who bore him” (Rambam, Laws of Sanhedrin 24:5). “Will you say so of this, in which he has neither permission to eat nor permission to burn as fuel?” (Pesachim 32a). “Like one who wipes out the bowl” (Pesikta Rabbati 16). “Like one who puts vinegar on natron and dissolves it” (Lamentations Rabbah, Petichta). “Like one who shouts in his fellow's ear” (ibid.). “He (Rabban Gamliel) said to the one who was with him (to Rabbi Ila'i): Have we drunk a quarter-log of Italian wine? He said to him: Yes” (Eruvin 64b). “He said to them: Whom do you call Rabbi? They said to him: This one who walks behind you” (Tractate Derekh Eretz 4). – °And like מה שֶׁ, “that which”: “That which we do outside the Land, every festival of these, two days, is a custom” (Rambam, Laws of Festivals 2). “That which we said, that he may make two eruvs in two directions for the two days — that is when it is possible for him to reach each of the two eruvs on the first day” (he, Laws of Eruvin 8:11). – אֵי=זֶה: אֵי, אֵיזֶה. – d) Reference to the place, with ב, בָּזֶה, in this place, German hier, French ici, English here: “Then he asked the men of her place, saying: Where is the harlot that was at Enaim by the wayside? And they said: There has been no harlot here” (Genesis 38:21). “And Joseph said to his father: They are my sons, whom God has given me here” (ibid. 48:9). “And to the elders he said: Wait here for us, until we return to you” (Exodus 24:14). “Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven bullocks” (Numbers 23:1). “And they said to him: Who brought you here? And what are you doing in this place? And what have you here?” (Judges 18:3). “I am the woman that stood by you here, praying to the Lord” (1 Samuel 1:26). “And they said to them: Is the seer here?” (ibid. 9:11). “Bring me every man his ox and every man his sheep, and slay them here, and eat” (ibid. 14:34). “If you will take that, take it, for there is no other save that here [note: another reading: בַזֶּה.]” (ibid. 21:10). – And with מ, מִזֶּה, from this place: “Tell me, I pray you, where they are feeding the flock. And the man said: They have departed from here, for I heard them say: Let us go to Dothan” (Genesis 37:16–17). “As Pharaoh lives, you shall not go forth from here unless your youngest brother comes here” (ibid. 42:15). “God will surely remember you, and you shall carry up my bones from here” (ibid. 50:25). “Afterwards he will let you go from here; when he shall let you go altogether, he shall surely thrust you out from here” (Exodus 11:1). “For by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from here” (ibid. 13:3). “Depart, go up from here, you and the people that you have brought up out of the land of Egypt” (ibid. 33:1). “And the Lord said to me: Arise, get down quickly from here, for your people have dealt corruptly” (Deuteronomy 9:12). “Depart not from here, I pray you, until I come to you” (Judges 6:18). “Go from here, and turn eastward” (1 Kings 17:3). “Go not to glean in another field, neither pass from here, but stay here close by my maidens” (Ruth 2:8). – מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה, in the sense of on this side and on that side: “One cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end” (Exodus 25:19). “And the cubit on the one side, and the cubit on the other side, of that which remains in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle on this side and on that side, to cover it” (ibid. 26:13). “Tablets that were written on both their sides; on the one side and on the other were they written” (ibid. 32:15). “Then the angel of the Lord stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, a fence on this side and a fence on that side” (Numbers 22:24). “And all Israel, and their elders and officers and their judges, stood on this side of the ark and on that side” (Joshua 8:33). “So they were in the midst of Israel, these on this side and those on that side” (ibid. 22). “There was a rocky crag on the one side, and a rocky crag on the other side” (1 Samuel 14:4). “And the Philistines stood on the mountain on the one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other side, and there was a valley between them” (ibid. 17:3). “And Saul went on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain” (ibid. 23:26). “And they sat down, these on the one side of the pool, and those on the other side of the pool” (2 Samuel 2:13). “And the top of the throne was round behind, and there were arms on either side by the place of the seat” (1 Kings 10:19). “And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps” (ibid. 20). “Now behold, at the bank of the river were very many trees on the one side and on the other” (Ezekiel 47:7). “And by the river upon its bank, on this side and on that side, shall grow every tree for food” (ibid. 12). – אֵי=מִזֶּה, that is, from where, from which place: “Where did you come from, and where are you going?” (Genesis 16:8). “But I did not ask him where he was from” (Judges 13:6). “Of whom I know not where they are from” (1 Samuel 25:11). “To whom do you belong? And where are you from?” (ibid. 30:13). “From where do you come?” (2 Samuel 1:3). “Of what city are you?” (ibid. 15:2). “What is your country? And of what people are you?” (Jonah 1:8). – And it comes in combination with words of time and number, somewhat in the sense of now, already: “For he has supplanted me these two times” (Genesis 27:36). “These twenty years have I been with you” (ibid. 31:38). “These twenty years have I been in your house” (ibid. 41). “For now we would have returned these two times” (ibid. 43:10). “For these two years has the famine been in the land” (ibid. 45:6). “That you have smitten me these three times” (Numbers 22:28). “And behold, you have altogether blessed them these three times” (ibid. 24:10). “These forty years the Lord your God has been with you; you have lacked nothing” (Deuteronomy 2:7). “These forty and five years, since the Lord spoke this word to Moses” (Joshua 14:10). “You have not left your brothers these many days to this day” (ibid. 22:3). “You have mocked me these three times” (Judges 16:15). “Is not this David etc., who has been with me these days or these years?” (1 Samuel 29:3). “As a woman that has these many days mourned for the dead” (2 Samuel 14:2). “Now by this I know that you are a man of God” (1 Kings 17:24). “Behold, even now there have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim two young men” (2 Kings 5:22). “These three and twenty years the word of the Lord has come to me” (Jeremiah 25:3). “How long will you not have compassion on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, against which you have had indignation these seventy years?” (Zechariah 1:12). “Should I weep in the fifth month, separating myself, as I have done these so many years?” (ibid. 7:3). “When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and in the seventh month, even these seventy years, did you at all fast to me, even to me?” (ibid. 5). “These ten times have you reproached me” (Job 19:3). “So she came, and has continued from the morning until now; this, her sitting in the house, has been but little” (Ruth 2:7). – e) After the interrogative words מַה, לָמָּה: מַה=זֶּה, לָמָּה=זֶּה [note: in Arabic limādhā لمَاذَا.], to strengthen the question: “And Isaac said to his son: How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?” (Genesis 27:20). “And how then do you say to me: What ails you?” (Judges 18:24). “Then the people said one to another: What is this that has come to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?” (1 Samuel 10:11). “But Jezebel his wife came to him and said to him: Why is your spirit so sullen, that you eat no bread?” (1 Kings 21:5). “And the messengers returned to him, and he said to them: Why is it that you have returned?” (2 Kings 1:5). “Then the king said to me: For what do you make request?” (Nehemiah 2:4). “And she said: If it be so, why am I thus?” (Genesis 25:22). “Behold, I am at the point to die; and what is this birthright to me?” (ibid. 32). “And he said: Why is it that you ask after my name?” (ibid. 32:30). “And he said to his daughters: And where is he? Why is it that you have left the man?” (Exodus 2:20). “Lord, why have you dealt ill with this people? Why is it that you have sent me?” (ibid. 5:22). “And the people murmured against Moses and said: Why is it that you have brought us up out of Egypt?” (ibid. 17:3). “And Moses said: Why now do you transgress the commandment of the Lord?” (Numbers 14:41). “And the Lord said to Joshua: Get up; why is it that you are fallen upon your face?” (Joshua 7:10). “And Eliab's anger was kindled against David, and he said: Why is it that you have come down?” (1 Samuel 17:28). “Behold, Abner came to you; why is it that you have sent him away, and he is quite gone?” (2 Samuel 3:24). “But now he is dead; why should I fast?” (ibid. 12:23). “Why then are you angry about this matter?” (ibid. 19:43). “Why do you feign yourself to be another?” (1 Kings 14:6). “To what purpose is the frankincense to me that comes from Sheba?” (Jeremiah 6:20). “Why did I come forth out of the womb to see toil and sorrow?” (ibid. 20:18). “Woe to you that desire the day of the Lord! What is the day of the Lord to you?” (Amos 5:18). “Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, seeing he has no understanding?” (Proverbs 17:16). “I shall be condemned; why then do I labour in vain?” (Job 9:29). – And after הִנֵּה, הֲרֵי: “And he lay down and slept under a broom tree; and behold, an angel touched him and said to him: Arise and eat” (1 Kings 19:5). “And I stand upon my watch all the nights; and behold, here comes a troop of men, horsemen in pairs” (Isaiah 21:8–9). “A bathhouse that was heated with straw or stubble of the Sabbatical year — it is permitted to bathe in it; but if he is a person of standing, behold, this one should not bathe” (Shevi'it 8:11). “They said to him: Bring witnesses; and he said: I have no witnesses. They said: Bring proof; and he said: I have no proof. And after a time he brought proof and found witnesses — behold, this is nothing” (Sanhedrin 3:8). “If he found silver vessels and copper vessels etc., behold, this one should not return them until he gives a sign or until he states their weights precisely” (Bava Metzia 23b). “One who carries out manure on his head with tefillin on his head — behold, this one should not move them to the sides nor tie them on his loins, because he treats them disgracefully” (ibid. 105b).

he: *, — מצֻמצם מן זֶה הוּא: זהו שעומד ומתפלל תריך להשוות את רגליו (ירוש' ברכ' א א). כל זמן שפני מזרח מאדימות זהו יום (שם). זהו מרגילה וזו היא מרגילתו (יבמ' פה:). — ובמשמ' זה הוא הדבר: יכול אתה פודה את החיה ואת המתה וכו' זהו שנשאלה בכרם ביבנה לפני חכמים (ספרי קרח קיח).
en: *, — contracted from זֶה הוּא: "This is one who stands and prays: he must align his feet" (Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:1). "As long as the face of the east is reddening, this is day" (ibid.). "He is the one who habituates her, and she is the one habituated to him" (Yevamot 85b). — And in the sense of "this is the thing": "Might you redeem the living and the dead etc.? This is what was asked in the vineyard at Yavneh before the Sages" (Sifre Korach 118).

he: *, ש"ז, מ"ר זְלָחִים, — דבר, בפרט בריח טוב, שמזים וזורקים בבית וכדומה: לאכל ולא לעשות ממנה זלחיןבקצת נוסח' זלפין. ולא לעשות ממנה מלוגמא (ספרא בהר א א).  אין מזלחין את הבית בכל מיני זלחין (תוספת' שבת יז ג).
en: *, masculine noun, plural זְלָחִים, — something, especially of good scent, which is sprinkled and scattered in a house and the like: "To eat, and not to make of it זלחין [Note: In some versions זלפין.], and not to make of it a poultice" (Sifra, Behar 1:1). "One may not sprinkle the house with any kind of זלחין" (Tosefta Shabbat 17:3).

he: *, ש"ז, מ"ר זְמָרִים, — כמו זמרה, נגינה:  עשרה נקבים היו בה (בהמגרפה) כל אחד ואחד היה מוציא מאה מיני זמר ירוש' סוכ' ה נה ד  ארבעה לשונות נאין שישתמש בהן העולם ואלו הן לעז לזמר רומי לקרב וכו' עברי לדיבור שם מגי' א עא: ושם סוטה ז כא ג.  כל השותה בארבעה מיני זמר מביא חמש פורעניות לעולם סוט' מח..  הקורא פסוק של שיר השירים ועושה אותו כמין זמר והקורא פסוק בבתי משתאות בלא זמנו מביא רעה לעולם סנה' קא..  זמר יווני לא פסק (מפיו של אלישע אחר) חגי' טו:.  כשאדם נער אומר דברי זמר הגדיל אומר דברי משלות הזקין אומר דברי הבלים מד"ר שה"ש א א.  בן לוי בשעה שפותח פיו בשיר וכו' והיה מוציא כל מיני זמר עד שהיו כל אחיו הלוים נסקרין בבת ראש לאחוריהם שם, מי זאת עולה.  שהעופות נותנין זמר וקול ערב להולכי דרכים רש"י שה"ש ב יא. — ואמר הפיטן:  במו (בד' המינים) להלל, בְּזֶמֶר והלל, ביום ולא בליל, לאין לפניו ליל יוצר א סכות, אקחה. — ומ"ר:  אמרו ישראל מה עלינו לעשות אלא לומר שירים וזמרים מד"ר שמות כג.  אותה שעה כשתעשה לנו ניסים האלו אין אנו כפויי טובה אלא אף אנו אומרים שירים וזמרים פסיק' דר"כ כט. — ואמר הפיטן:  עלי גלות משרתי אל מנעימי שיר זְמָרֶיהָ ועל דמם אשר שֻפך כמו מימי יאוריה קינ' לת"ב, חלי ציון. — °כלי זמר,  עי' כלי
en: *, masculine noun, plural זְמָרִים, — Like זמרה, music, melody: “Ten holes were in it (in the magrefa), each one of which produced a hundred kinds of music (זמר),” Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 5, 55d. “Four languages are fitting for the world to use, and these are they: the foreign tongue (לעז) for song (לזמר), Roman for war etc., Hebrew for speech,” ibid. Megillah 1, 71b, and ibid. Sotah 7, 21c. “Whoever drinks to four kinds of music (זמר) brings five punishments upon the world,” Sotah 48a. “One who reads a verse of the Song of Songs and makes it into a kind of song (זמר), and one who reads a verse at banquets not in its proper time, brings evil upon the world,” Sanhedrin 101a. “Greek song (זמר) did not cease (from the mouth of Elisha ben Avuyah, Acher),” Chagigah 15b. “When a man is young he says words of song (זמר); when he grows up he says words of proverbs; when he grows old he says words of vanities,” Song of Songs Rabbah 1:1. “Ben Levi, when he opened his mouth in song etc., would produce all kinds of music (זמר), so that all his brethren the Levites would be thrown backward at once,” ibid., מי זאת עולה. “For the birds give song (זמר) and a pleasant voice to wayfarers,” Rashi, Song of Songs 2:11. — And the liturgical poet said: “With them (the four species) to praise, with song (בְּזֶמֶר) and praise, by day and not by night, Him before whom there is no night,” Yotzer for the first day of Sukkot, אקחה. — And plural: “Israel said: What is there for us to do but to say songs and melodies (זמרים)?” Exodus Rabbah 23. “At that hour, when You perform these miracles for us, we are not ungrateful, but we too say songs and melodies (זמרים),” Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 29. — And the liturgical poet said: “Over the exile of the ministers of God, who made sweet the song of her melodies (זְמָרֶיהָ), and over their blood that was shed like the waters of her rivers,” Kinot for Tisha B'Av, חלי ציון. — °כלי זמר, musical instrument, see כלי

he: בערב' זראפה زرافة, ולא נתברר מקורו, ועי' הערה שלקמן., ש"ז, בהפס' זָמֶר, מ"ר זְמָרִים, — חיה גבוהת קומה, ארוכת הצואר, חברבורת העור, Giraffe; girafe: איל וצבי ויחמור ואקו ודישן ותאו וָזָמֶרת"א דיצא. אך לא ידוע בדיוק לאיזו חיה קראו בארמ' דיצא. רסע"ג תרגם ואלזראפה, וכן ריב"ג. ואעפ"י שרוב החדשים אמרו כי הזמר הוא מין עז הבר, בכ"ז יותר ראוי לקבל דעת קדמונינו רבי הלשון, רסע"ג וריב"ג, שיש לה סמך וסעד גם בדמיון צרוף האותיות של שני השמות זמר וזראפה שאין הבדל ביניהם אלא שבהאחד מ ובהשני פ, אך התחלפות שתי האותיות האלה מצוי מאד בין שתי הלשונות האחיות. והנה המצבאח הביא בשם אבן דריד כי הוא פקפק אם המלה היא ערבית במקורה. אך הוא יחיד בזה, ואפילו אם נאמר כי באמת השם הערבי זראפה שאול מאיזו לשון אחרת, אפשר כי גם הלשון העבר' שאלה השם זמר מאותה הלשון, וכ"א משתי הלשונות הברה את השם הזר בקצת שנוי לפי טבעה. בעל שלטי הגבורים תרגם זמר בהשם אוריגי וכתב: ואולם הזמר הוא האוריגי שכתב אריסטוטילי בספר שני מספורי הב"ח שיש לו קרן אחד גם הוא במצחו והוא מפריס פרסה ומעלה גרה ולא החמור הבר כי הוא קלוט עם קרן אחת גם הוא במצחו ופרסתו אינה שסועה ואינו מעלה גרה ויקרא האוריגי זמר מפני שהוא אוהב מאד הזמרה ועל כי הבעל חי הזה הוא תקיף מאד ולא יוכלו הציידים לצודו כי אם ביגיעה רבה במקום העמל והטורח הם מבקשים בתולה יפה ומפשיטין אותה ערומה כי הב"ח הזה הוא אוהב הבתולות הרבה וכשהיא ערומה תזמר בזמרה רכה ונאה באופן שכשישמע הבעל חי הזה הזמרה ורואה הבתולה הערומה נגדו הוא רץ לקראתה וכורע על ברכיה ויניח ראשו על כרסה והבתולה תרדוף בזמרתה עד שהבעל חי הזה מרוב התענוג והעדון ישכב וירדם שם ואז הציידים משימים בכבל רגלו ונותנים שלשלת של ברזל על צוארו עד שנקרא זמר שהוא נצוד עם הזמרה (שלטי הגבור' נג). ויהודה הדסי הקראי חבר שני הפרושים יחד, וז"ל: חיה קטנה היא שמה זורפי עורה צבוע בכל מיני צביעות חברבורות בכל יופי תפוש כשתתפש ברשת בוכה ומתחננת ומדמעת לפני תופשיה לשלחה מן הרשת מדברת בלשונינו כלשון ששומע את תופשו אך לא בלשון צח כלשונך (האשכול מו). (דבר' יד ה).
en: [Note: In Arabic زرافة zarafa, and its origin has not been clarified; and see the note below.], masculine noun, in pause זָמֶר, plural זְמָרִים, — a tall animal, long-necked, with spotted skin, German Giraffe; French girafe: "The hart and the gazelle and the roebuck and the wild goat and the ibex and the antelope וָזָמֶר (and the giraffe) [Note: Targum Onkelos: דיצא. But it is not known exactly which animal was called דיצא in Aramaic. Saadia Gaon translated ואלזראפה (and the giraffe), and so Ibn Janah. And although most of the moderns said that the זמר is a kind of wild goat, nevertheless it is more fitting to accept the opinion of our early masters of the language, Saadia Gaon and Ibn Janah, which has support and backing also in the similarity of the combination of letters of the two names זמר and זראפה, between which there is no difference except that in the one there is מ and in the other פ, and the interchange of these two letters is very common between the two sister languages. Now the Misbah cited in the name of Ibn Durayd that he doubted whether the word is Arabic in origin. But he is alone in this, and even if we say that the Arabic name זראפה is in fact borrowed from some other language, it is possible that the Hebrew language too borrowed the name זמר from that same language, and each of the two languages pronounced the foreign name with some change according to its nature. The author of Shiltei HaGibborim translated זמר by the name אוריגי and wrote: "But the זמר is the אוריגי that Aristotle wrote about in the second book of his History of Animals, that it has one horn, it too on its forehead, and it parts the hoof and chews the cud; and not the wild ass, for that is solid-hoofed with one horn, it too on its forehead, and its hoof is not cloven and it does not chew the cud. And the אוריגי is called זמר because it loves song (זמרה) very much; and because this animal is very strong, and the hunters cannot catch it except with great toil, instead of the labour and trouble they seek a beautiful virgin and strip her naked, for this animal loves virgins greatly; and when she is naked she sings a soft and lovely song, so that when this animal hears the singing and sees the naked virgin before it, it runs toward her and kneels at her knees and lays its head on her belly, and the virgin pursues her singing until this animal, from the great pleasure and delight, lies down and falls asleep there; and then the hunters put its foot in fetters and place an iron chain on its neck; hence it is called זמר, since it is caught by song" (Shiltei HaGibborim 53). And Judah Hadassi the Karaite combined the two interpretations together, and these are his words: "It is a small animal whose name is זורפי; its skin is coloured with all kinds of colours, spotted in all beauty. When it is caught in a net it weeps and pleads and sheds tears before its captors to release it from the net; it speaks in our language like the language it hears from its captor, but not in a clear language like yours" (Eshkol HaKofer 46).]" (Deuteronomy 14:5).

he: °, ש"ז, — כמו *ג. זֵק, נאד:  אותם שיעשו הזקק וישאום על אלו האוכפות (הרמב"ם, פי' מקוא' ט ה).
en: °, masculine noun, — like *ג. זֵק, a skin bottle: “Those who make the skin bottles and carry them on these saddles” (Rambam, Commentary on Mikvaot 9:5).

he: *, ש"ז. — מין חגורה: איזהו המרכב המיוחד זרז האשקלוני ומדוכה המדית ועביט של גמל וטפיטו של סוס (ספרא מצורע, זבים ב ג). אלו טמאין משום מרכב זרזכך הערוך וכך הכתיב במשנ' עם גוף פרוש הערבי של הרמב"ם, ומנֻקד זֶרֶז. ובנוסח' זריז. — בעה"ש זָרָז בשני קמצים. האשקלוני ומדוכה המדית וכו' (כלים כג ב). והעלה (אדם הראשון) זרזי תאנים על בשרו מאה ושלשים שנה (ערוב' יח:).
en: *, masculine noun. — a kind of girdle: "What is the riding-seat proper? The Ashkelon זרז, the Median mortar, the camel's pack-saddle and the horse's saddle-cloth" (Sifra Metzora, Zavim 2:3). "These are unclean as a riding-seat: the זרז [Note: So the Arukh, and so is the spelling in the Mishnah with the Arabic commentary of Rambam itself, and it is vocalized זֶרֶז. And in the printed text זריז. — The author of the Shorashim has זָרָז with two kamatzes.] of Ashkelon, and the Median mortar etc." (Kelim 23:2). "And he (Adam) put זרזי of fig leaves upon his flesh for one hundred and thirty years" (Eruvin 18b).

he: °,  ש"ז, מ"ר זְרָמִים, — עורקים וגידים:  ואפילו אם היא (הבהמה שנגחה בהמה אחרת) עומדת ותהלך  ונמצאו הזרמיםלא נתברר מקור שמוש זה. מחותכות טרפה (אלדד הדני, הלכ' טרפ' ג יו).   — ועי' עוד °ב. זִרְמָה.
en: °, masculine noun, plural זְרָמִים, — veins and sinews: "And even if it (the animal that gored another animal) stands and walks, and the זרמים [Note: the source of this usage has not been clarified.] were found cut, it is terefah" (Eldad the Danite, Laws of Terefot 3:16). — And see further °ב. זִרְמָה.

he: ש"ז, מ"ר זְרָמִים, — שפיכת מים חזק, גשם חזק. Regenguss; verse; outpour of rain: ראוך יחילו הרים זֶרֶם מים עבר נתן תהום קולו (חבק' ג י).  והיה איש כמחבא רוח וסתר זָרֶם כפלגי מים בציון (ישע' לב ב).  נפץ וָזָרֶם ואבן ברד (שם ל ל).  כְּזֶרֶם מים כבירים שטפים (שם כח ב).  וסכה תהיה לצל יומם מחֹרב ולמחסה ולמסתור מִזֶּרֶם  וממטר (שם ד ו).  כי היית מעוז לדל מעוז לאביון בצר לו מחסה מִזֶֶּרֶם צל מחֹרב כי רוח עריצים כְּזֶרֶם קירהמליצה דחוקה, והגיהו רוב החדשים קֹר במקום קיר, ר"ל כזרם מים קרים. וגם זה דחוק. (שם כה ד),  כמו זרם המים הנשפכים מהגג ע"ג הקיר.  — זֶרֶם בָּרָד, ירידת הרבה ברד בתקף וזעם: הנה חזק ואמץ לאדני כְּזֶרֶם ברד שער קטב  (ישע' כח ב).  — זֶרֶם הָרִים, היורד ונתך מעל ההרים:  ערום ילינו מבלי לבוש ואין כסות בקרה מִזֶּרֶם הרים ירטבו ומבלי מחסה חבקו צור (איוב כד ז=ח).  — ומ"ר ;  °זְרָמִים, ואמר המשורר:  ולו רֵע יהי בוגד כנחל אזי עמו משכוהו זְרָמָיו (רשב"ג, שירי שלמה לה).  ובקר וערב, לקרח וחורב, למפנה זְרָמִים וְזַרְמֵי רויה (שבת שמעו, אשחר).  — והשתמשו הסופרים החדשים במלה זו במשמ' נזילה עזה של המים, של נחל וכדומה, ובהשאלה בדברים רוחניים, נטייה ומהלך בדעות, בספרות, וכדומה.
en: masculine noun, plural זְרָמִים, — a strong pouring of water, heavy rain. German Regenguss; French verse; English outpour of rain: "The mountains saw You and trembled; a downpour (זֶרֶם) of waters passed over; the deep uttered its voice" (Habakkuk 3:10). "And a man shall be as a hiding place from the wind and a shelter from the downpour (זָרֶם), as streams of water in a dry place" (Isaiah 32:2). "A cloudburst and a downpour (וָזָרֶם) and hailstones" (ibid. 30:30). "As a downpour (כְּזֶרֶם) of mighty overflowing waters" (ibid. 28:2). "And there shall be a booth for shade by day from the heat, and for refuge and for shelter from downpour (מִזֶּרֶם) and from rain" (ibid. 4:6). "For You have been a stronghold for the poor, a stronghold for the needy in his distress, a refuge from the downpour (מִזֶֶּרֶם), a shade from the heat; for the blast of the ruthless is as a downpour against a wall (כְּזֶרֶם קיר)[Note: A forced expression, and most of the moderns emend it to קֹר in place of קיר, that is, like a stream of cold water. And this too is forced.]" (ibid. 25:4), like the stream of water pouring from the roof onto the wall. — זֶרֶם בָּרָד, a heavy fall of hail with force and fury: "Behold, the Lord has one who is strong and mighty, like a downpour of hail (כְּזֶרֶם ברד), a storm of destruction" (Isaiah 28:2). — זֶרֶם הָרִים, that which runs down and pours from the mountains: "They lie all night naked without clothing, and have no covering in the cold; they are wet with the downpour of the mountains (מִזֶּרֶם הרים), and for want of shelter they embrace the rock" (Job 24:7=8). — And the plural ; °זְרָמִים, and the poet said: "And if a friend be treacherous like a stream, then its torrents (זְרָמָיו) have drawn him along with it" (רשב"ג, Shirei Shlomo 35). "And morning and evening, for cold and for heat, for the turning of torrents (זְרָמִים) and of saturating downpours (וְזַרְמֵי רויה)" (Shabbat Shim'u, Ashacher). — And the modern writers have used this word in the sense of a strong flow of water, of a stream and the like, and figuratively in spiritual matters, a tendency and movement in opinions, in literature, and the like.

en: [Note: See the previous note, in the previous entry.] Masculine noun, in pause זָרַע, plural זְרָעִים — a) That which is put into the ploughed ground so that the plant may grow from it, German Same, French semence, English seed: “and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh; and give us seed, that we may live and not die, and that the land be not desolate” (Genesis 47:19). “You shall carry much seed out into the field and shall gather little in, for the locust shall consume it” (Deuteronomy 28:38). “Behold, the days come, says the Lord, that the ploughman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him who sows seed; and the mountains shall drop sweet wine” (Amos 9:13). “He who goes forth weeping, bearing the bag of seed, shall come home with joy, bearing his sheaves” (Psalms 126:6). “fruit trees bearing fruit after their kind, whose seed is in itself” (Genesis 1:11). “One may not put a gourd seed into a mallow” (Kil'ayim 1:8). “Egyptian bean: if he sowed it for seed, it is tithed as before; if he sowed it for vegetables, it is tithed as in the future” (Jerusalem Talmud Shevi'it 2, 34a). “One does not test the seeds in soil in a pot, but one tests them in dung” (ibid. 4, 35b). — b) That which came up from the seed, the crop, German Saat, Getreide, French blé, English harvest: “And all the tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land or of the fruit of the tree, is the Lord's” (Leviticus 27:30). “You shall surely tithe all the increase of your seed that the field brings forth year by year” (Deuteronomy 14:22). “Will you rely on him to bring home your seed and gather it to your threshing floor?” (Job 39:12). “In the day of your planting you make it grow, and in the morning you make your seed to blossom” (Isaiah 17:11). “And he will take the tenth of your seed and of your vineyards and give to his officers and to his servants” (1 Samuel 8:15). — c) The very act of sowing, putting the seed into the ground, German d. Säen, French ensemencement, English sowing: “And at the ingatherings you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four parts shall be your own, for seed of the field and for your food” (Genesis 47:24). — d) The time of sowing, German Saatzeit, French saison de semailles, English seed time: “While the earth remains, seed time and harvest, and cold and heat” (Genesis 8:22). “And your threshing shall reach to the vintage, and the vintage shall reach to the sowing time, and you shall eat your bread to the full” (Leviticus 26:5). “Half of Tishrei, Marcheshvan and half of Kislev — sowing time; half of Kislev, Tevet and half of Shevat — winter; half of Shevat, Adar and half of Nisan — cold” (Bava Metzia 106b). “Six sowings and seven ingatherings — not six sowings and five ingatherings” (Jerusalem Talmud Shevi'it 2, 34a). — e) *Specifically זֶרַע, זְרָעִים, such as mustard, and kinds of flowers and the like, as distinguished from vegetables: “No kind of seed-plants may be sown in a garden bed” (Kil'ayim 3:2). “Iris and ivy and the lily, and all kinds of seed-plants are not kil'ayim in a vineyard” (ibid. 5:8). “Scripture excluded that which people are not accustomed to call seed-plants” (Jerusalem Talmud ibid. 8, 31b). “He piles his grain within it, and it turns out that he is tithing from his seed-plants for his vegetables and from his vegetables for his seed-plants” (ibid., Shevi'it 2, 34a). “Those who weed seed-plants and hoe vegetables” (Bava Kamma 119b). — °זֶרַע הָרֹאשׁ [Note: In Arabic habb al-ras حب الراس, which is zabib al-jabal زبيب الجبل, that is, mountain raisins.], a kind of wild grape (Labrusca): “זרע הראש is agria stafis” (Asaf ha-Rofe, Munich manuscript 20). — f) In living creatures, that which issues from the organs of the male and the female in their coupling, from which the offspring comes into being, Latin semen virile, and mostly in combination with the word שִׁכְבַת: “This is the law of him who has an issue, and of him from whom an emission of seed goes out, so that he is unclean by it” (Leviticus 15:32). “And every garment and every skin on which is the emission of seed shall be washed with water” (ibid. 17). “There are two openings in a man: one emits urine and one emits semen, and between them is only as the peel of garlic” (Bekhorot 44b). — g) Children, German Nachkommenschaft, French descendants: “And she bore a son and called his name Seth: ‘For God has appointed me another seed instead of Abel, for Cain killed him’” (Genesis 4:25). “And Abram said, ‘Behold, to me You have given no seed, and lo, one born in my house is my heir’” (ibid. 15:3). “Come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, that we may preserve seed of our father” (ibid. 19:32). “for in Isaac shall seed be called to you” (ibid. 21:12). “Go in to your brother's wife and perform the duty of a husband's brother to her, and raise up seed to your brother” (ibid. 38:8). “but will give to Your handmaid a man child, then I will give him to the Lord all the days of his life” (1 Samuel 1:11). “The Lord give you seed of this woman” (ibid. 2:20). “He shall see seed, he shall prolong his days” (Isaiah 53:10). “But if a priest's daughter is a widow or divorced and has no child, and has returned to her father's house as in her youth, she shall eat of her father's bread” (Leviticus 22:13). “And Onan knew that the seed would not be his” (ibid. 38:9). “of the seed which the Lord shall give you of this young woman” (Ruth 4:12). “Swear now therefore to me by the Lord that you will not cut off my seed after me, and that you will not destroy my name out of my father's house” (1 Samuel 24:22). “And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed” (Genesis 3:15). “And I will make your seed as the dust of the earth, so that if a man can number the dust of the earth, then shall your seed also be numbered” (ibid. 13:16). “And also of the son of the bondwoman will I make a nation, because he is your seed” (ibid. 48:11). “and they came into Egypt, Jacob and all his seed with him… brought he with him into Egypt” (ibid. 46:6–7). “Write this man childless, a man that shall not prosper in his days; for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting on the throne of David” (Jeremiah 22:30). — And descendants somewhat more remote: “that no stranger, who is not of the seed of Aaron, come near to burn incense before the Lord” (Numbers 17:15). “And I will for this afflict the seed of David” (1 Kings 11:39). “And I will cast you out of My sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, the whole seed of Ephraim” (Jeremiah 7:15). “But you, Israel, My servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham My friend” (Isaiah 41:8). “And the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel and afflicted them and delivered them into the hand of spoilers” (2 Kings 17:20). “Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, of the seed royal” (ibid. 25:25). “Hadad the Edomite; he was of the king's seed” (1 Kings 11:14). “the priests the Levites who are of the seed of Zadok” (Ezekiel 43:19). “If Mordecai is of the seed of the Jews” (Esther 6:13). “Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes” (Daniel 9:1). “that your seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them, and they shall afflict them four hundred years” (Genesis 15:13). “And your seed shall be as the dust of the earth, etc., and in you and in your seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed” (ibid. 28:14). “I will greatly multiply your seed, that it shall not be numbered for multitude” (ibid. 16:10). “Therefore do not fear, O Jacob My servant, says the Lord, neither be dismayed, O Israel; for, lo, I will save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity” (Jeremiah 30:10). “So shall their blood return upon the head of Joab and upon the head of his seed for ever; but to David and to his seed and to his house and to his throne shall there be peace for ever from the Lord” (1 Kings 2:33). “Behold, I establish My covenant with you and with your seed after you” (Genesis 9:9). “For as the new heavens and the new earth which I will make shall remain before Me, says the Lord, so shall your seed and your name remain” (Isaiah 66:22). “Go in and possess the land which the Lord swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give to them and to their seed after them” (Deuteronomy 1:8). “And their seed shall be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples” (Isaiah 61:9). “Therefore He lifted up His hand against them, to overthrow them in the wilderness, and to cast out their seed among the nations” (Psalms 106:26–27). “The Jews ordained and took upon themselves and upon their seed and upon all who joined themselves to them, so that it should not fail, that they would keep these two days, etc., and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor the memorial of them perish from their seed” (Esther 9:27–28). “For the seed of Esau is delivered only into the hand of the seed of Joseph” (Bava Batra 123b).

he: * ש"ז, — מ"ר זַבָּלִים, — מי שאומנותו לשים זבל על השדה: פעם אחת השכמתי ומצאתי הזבלים והתבנים מד"ר שה"ש א.
en: * masculine noun, — plural זַבָּלִים, — one whose craft is putting manure on the field: "Once I rose early and found the manure-spreaders and the straw-men" Song of Songs Rabbah 1.

he: *  בערב' זַגַּאג زَجَّاج ש"ז, מ"ר זַגָּגִים, — עושה זכוכית, מתקן זכוכית, Galser; vitrier; glas- maker: מביאין כלים מבית האומן כגון כד מבית הכדד וכוס מבית הזגג אבל לא צמר מבית הצבע (מו"ק יג:). משל לעירוני שהיה עובר לפני חנותו של זגג והיה לפניו קופה מלאה כוסות (מד"ר בראש' יט). לזגג שהיתה בידו קופה מלאה כוסות דיוטריטין (שם רות א). — ומ"ר: כבשן של סיידין ושל זגגין ושל יוצרים טהורה (כלים ח ט). שלש מטות הן העשויה לשכיבה טמאה מדרס של זגגין טמאה טמא מת ושל סרגין טהורה (שם כד ח). נפש מאזנים תלויה באויר שלשה טפחים וכו' ושל צמרין ושל זגגין תלויה באויר שני טפחים וגבוה מן הארץ שני טפחים (ב"ב פט.). הקדרין והזגגין שהיו מהלכין זה אחר זה נתקל הראשון ונפל ונתקל השני בראשון (ב"ק לא.). — ואמר המשורר: מה מאד חטא הזגג הארור, צפונה חטאתו ועונו צרור, אשר לא עשה הכוסות לדמיון הקדרה והפרור, כי אז יצאנו מעבדות לשחרור (עמנ', מחב' כה).
en: * [Note: In Arabic זַגַּאג زَجَّاج] masculine noun, plural זַגָּגִים, — one who makes glass, one who repairs glass, German Galser; French vitrier; English glas- maker: "One may bring vessels from the craftsman's house, such as a jug from the jug-maker's house and a cup from the glazier's house, but not wool from the dyer's house" (Moed Katan 13b). "A parable of a townsman who was passing before the shop of a glazier, and before him was a basket full of cups" (Genesis Rabbah 19). "Like a glazier who had in his hand a basket full of cups דיוטריטין" (ibid. Ruth 1). — And plural: "A kiln of lime-burners and of glaziers and of potters is clean" (Kelim 8:9). "There are three beds: the one made for lying is susceptible to midras impurity; that of glaziers is susceptible to corpse impurity; and that of net-makers is clean" (ibid. 24:8). "The hanger of scales is suspended in the air three handbreadths etc., and that of wool-dealers and of glaziers is suspended in the air two handbreadths and is two handbreadths high from the ground" (Bava Batra 89a). "The potters and the glaziers who were walking one after another; the first stumbled and fell, and the second stumbled over the first" (Bava Kamma 31a). — And the poet said: "How greatly the cursed glazier sinned; his sin is hidden away and his iniquity bound up, for he did not make the cups in the likeness of the pot and the pan, for then we would have gone out from slavery to freedom" (Immanuel, Mahbarot 25).

he: °,  — כמו הַזְהָרָה: רב עם צעיר מעשרים להספר, ראויים לענש וְזַהַר בסדר להתפר (יוצר פ' שקלים, קצובה).
en: °, — like הַזְהָרָה: "Great together with small, from twenty [years] to be counted, deserving of punishment and warning (וְזַהַר), in order to be atoned" (Yotzer for Parashat Shekalim, "Ketzuvah").

he: *  ש"ז, מ"ר זַהָבִים, — אומן בזהב, עושה מלאכת זהב, Goldschmied; orfèvre; goldsmith: שפופרת של זהבין ושל זגגין ושל נפחין ושל עושה זכוכית שנחלקה לאורכה טהורה תוספתא כלים ב"מ ג י. קורנס של זהבים שנינו שבת קכג.. ס' ריבוא בני אדם עשו אצלם רד"ו שנים מהם כספים ומהם זהבים שנוטלים בשכרן דינר ליום מד"ר בראש' סא. יצא כורש לטייל במדינה וראה המדינה שוממה אמר מה טיבה של מדינה זו שוממת איכן הם הזהבים איכן הם הכספים שם שה"ש, קמתי אני.
en: * masculine noun, plural זַהָבִים, — a craftsman in gold, one who does goldwork, German Goldschmied; French orfèvre; English goldsmith: "The tube of goldsmiths (זהבין) and of glaziers and of smiths and of glassmakers that was split lengthwise is clean" Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia 3:10. "We have learned of the hammer of goldsmiths (זהבים)" Shabbat 123a. "Six hundred thousand people worked for them for 210 years, some of them silversmiths and some of them goldsmiths (זהבים), who take as their wage a dinar a day" Genesis Rabbah 61. "Cyrus went out to stroll in the province and saw the province desolate; he said: What is the nature of this province that it is desolate? Where are the goldsmiths (הזהבים)? Where are the silversmiths?" ibid. Song of Songs, "Kamti Ani".

he: בערב' זית زَيت להשמן, ולהאילן והפרי זיתון زَيْتُون., ש"ז, בהפס' זָיִת, סמי' זֵית, מ"ר זֵיתִים, *זֵתִים, זֵיתֵי, בכנ' זֵיתֶך, זֵיתֵיכֶם, — אילן נותן פרי שממנו יעשו השמן, Oelbaum; olivier; olive tree: והנה עלה זַיִת טרף בפיה  בראש' ח יא.  הלוך הלכו העצים למשח עליהם מלך ויאמרו לַזַּיִת מלוכה עלינו ויאמר להם הַזַּיִת החדלתי את דשני אשר בי יכבדו אלהים ואנשים והלכתי לנוע על העצים שופט' ט ח-ט.  זַיִת רענן יפה פרי תאר ירמ' יא יו.  ילכו יונקותיו ויהי כַזַּיִת הודו הוש' יד ז.  כל זית שיש לו שם בשדה כזית נטופה בשעתו ושיכחו אינו שכחה תוספתא פאה ג ט.  זית אין עליו נושרין לא בימות החמה ולא בימות הגשמים מנח' נג:. — ומ"ר: זֵיתִים יהיו לך בכל גבולך ושמן לא תסוך כי ישל זֵיתֶךָ דבר' כח מ.  בניך כשתלי זֵיתִים סביב לשלחנך תהל' קכח ג.  זיתים משיכניסו רביעית לסאה פוצע ואוכל בשדה שבי' ד ט.  זה אומר זיתי גידלו וזה אומר ארצי גידלה ב"מ ח ה.  המוכר זיתיו לעצים ועשו פחות מרביעית לסאה שם.  שטף נהר זיתיו ונתנם לתוך שדה חבירו שם.  אמר הלה זיתיי אני נוטל אין שומעין לו וכו' משום ישוב גמ' שם קא.. — זֵית שֶׁמֶן דבר' ח ח.  זֵית יִצְהָר מ"ב יח לב. — ועצם הפרי, Olive: אתה תדרך זֵיִת ולא תסוך שמן מיכ' ו יה.  ויקחו אליך שמן זַיִת זך כתית למאור שמות כז כ.  זית כבוש אומר עליו בורא פרי העץ ירוש' ברכ' ו א.  זית על ידי שדרכו לאכל חי אעפ"י שכבוש בעינו הוא שם.  אני ראיתי את ר' יוחנן שאכל זית מליח בבלי שם לח:.  מהו לפצוע זיתים בשבת שבת נ:.  זיתים שמשך מהן שמן וענבים שמשך מהן יין  שם קמג:.  חבית של זיתים מגולגלים יבמ' טו:.  רוח צפונית יפה לחטין בשעה שהביאו שליש וקשה לזיתים בזמן שהן חונטין יומא כא:. מי שהפך זיתיו ואירעו אבל מו"ק ב א. — וזֵתִים: בראשונה שלא היו הזתים מצויין שבא אדריינוס הרשע והחריב את כל הארץ אבל עכשיו שהזתים מצויין ירוש' פאה ז כ.. — כַּזַּיִת, כשעור גֹדל הזית: כזית שאמרו לא גדול ולא קטן אלא בינוני כלים יז ח. — *וזֵתִים, במשמ' דבר כשעור זית: היה מחתך מבשרו זתים זתים ומאכילו לנעמיות פסיק' דר"כ, זכור. — כֶּרֶם זָיִת, שדה נטוע זיתים: ויבער מגדיש ועד קמה ועד כרם זָיִת שופט' יה ה. — וזַיִת בלבד במשמ' כֶּרֶם זַיִת: כן תעשה לכרמך לְזֵיתֶךָ שמות כג יא. כרמים וְזֵיתִים אשר לא נטעת דבר' ו יא. ואת כרמכם וְזֵיתֵיכֶם הטובים יקח ונתן לעבדיו ש"א ח יד. — חָבַט זַיִת, נָקַף זַיִת, להשיר את הגרגרים מן האילן: ונשאר בו עללת כנקף זַיִת שנים שלשה גרגרים בראש אמיר ישע' יז ו.  כי תחבט זֵיתְךָ לא תפאר אחריך דבר' כד כ. — *מָסַק זַיִת: זיתי מסיק שנתערבו עם זיתי ניקוף חלה ג ט. פועלין שהיו עודרין בתאנים וגודרין בתמרים ובוצרים בענבים ומוסקין בזיתים הרי אלו אוכלים ופטורים ב"מ פט:. — מַעֲשֵׂה- זַיִת, העסק בזית, גדוּל הזית: כי תאנה לא תפרח ואין יבול בגפנים כחש מַעֲשֵׂה-זַיִת ושדמות לא עשה אכל חבק' ג יז. — °זֵיתֵי שמן, זֵיתֵי כבש: וכן תורמין מזיתי שמן על זיתי כבש אבל לא מזיתי כבש על זיתי שמן רמב"ם תרומ' ה יח. — ומליצה, °החזיר זתיו במעטן, לאמר השתדל לתקן את המעֻות שבו: שהתורה מאור שוה להאיר לכל השב בכל לבו ומי שירצה לומר בהפך זה אומר שאין שמנו צח ויחזיר זתיו במעטן ר"י פרובינצלו, שו"ת בלמוד החכמ'.
*אוֹם.
בד, בית הבד, עי' במקומו.
°גִּלְגֵּל, זיתים מגולגלים. — גַּרְגֶּר, כל אחד ואחד מפרי הזית. — *גִּרְגֵּר לקח הגרגרים. — *גרופית, ענף של זית לשתילה ולהרכבה.
*זוּע, זֵעָה.
חבט, נקף.
*טען,  שמו במעטן.
*כופש, *כותש, סל גדול. — כמר. — *כתש. — כתת.
*לקה, התחיל להרקיב קצת, נתמעך.

*מֹהַל, היוצא מזיתים כבושים. — *מחבוא, לנקוף הזיתים. — *מֹחַל, כמו מֹהַל. —  מָלַח הזיתים, זית מלוּח. — *מָסַק, לקט הזיתים מהאילן. — מָסִיק, זמן המסיקה. — מעטן, מקום שכובשים הזיתים שיכמרו ויתרככו. — מפרכה, אחד מכלי בית הבד. — מתן, נרטב ונתרכך.
נקף הגרגרים מן האילן, חבט במקל להשירם.
*עוטן, *עטון. — *עקל.
*פג, פגים. — פצע, בקע אותם קודם הכבישה. — *פרוד, *פרודים. — *פריצי זיתים.
*קופה. — *קשקש, חפר סביב האילן.
en: [Note: In Arabic זית زَيت for the oil, and for the tree and the fruit זיתון زَيْتُون.], masculine noun, in pause זָיִת, construct זֵית, plural זֵיתִים, *זֵתִים, זֵיתֵי, with suffixes זֵיתֶך, זֵיתֵיכֶם, — a tree that bears fruit from which oil is made, German Oelbaum, French olivier, English olive tree: "And lo, in her mouth an olive (זַיִת) leaf freshly plucked" (Genesis 8:11). "The trees went forth to anoint a king over them, and they said to the olive tree (לַזַּיִת): Reign over us. But the olive tree (הַזַּיִת) said to them: Should I leave my fatness, by which God and men are honored, and go to hold sway over the trees?" (Judges 9:8-9). "A leafy olive tree (זַיִת), fair with goodly fruit" (Jeremiah 11:16). "His branches shall spread, and his beauty shall be as the olive tree (כַזַּיִת)" (Hosea 14:7). "Any olive tree that has a name in the field, like the dripping olive tree in its time, and he forgot it, is not a forgotten sheaf" (Tosefta Pe'ah 3:9). "The olive tree — its leaves do not fall, neither in the summer nor in the rainy season" (Menachot 53b). — And the plural: "You shall have olive trees (זֵיתִים) throughout all your borders, but you shall not anoint yourself with the oil, for your olives (זֵיתֶךָ) shall drop off" (Deuteronomy 28:40). "Your children like olive (זֵיתִים) plants around your table" (Psalms 128:3). "Olives, once they have taken in a revi'it per se'ah, one may crack them and eat them in the field" (Shevi'it 4:9). "This one says: My olive trees grew it, and that one says: My land grew it" (Bava Metzia 8:5). "One who sells his olive trees for wood, and they produced less than a revi'it per se'ah" (ibid.). "A river swept away his olive trees and put them into his fellow's field" (ibid.). "If that one said: I will take my olive trees — we do not listen to him etc., because of the settlement of the land" (Gemara ibid. 101a). — זֵית שֶׁמֶן (Deuteronomy 8:8). זֵית יִצְהָר (2 Kings 18:32). — And the fruit itself, German Olive: "You shall tread the olives (זֵיִת) but shall not anoint yourself with oil" (Micah 6:15). "That they bring to you pure olive (זַיִת) oil, beaten, for the light" (Exodus 27:20). "Over a pickled olive one says: Who creates the fruit of the tree" (Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6:1). "An olive, since its way is to be eaten raw, even though it is pickled, it is in its original state" (ibid.). "I saw Rabbi Yochanan eat a salted olive" (Babylonian Talmud ibid. 38b). "May one crack olives on Shabbat?" (Shabbat 50b). "Olives from which he drew oil and grapes from which he drew wine" (ibid. 143b). "A barrel of rolled olives" (Yevamot 15b). "A north wind is good for wheat when it has reached a third [of its growth], and bad for olives at the time that they bud" (Yoma 21b). "One who has turned his olives and mourning befell him" (Mo'ed Katan 2:1). — And זֵתִים: "At first, when olives were not available, for Hadrian the wicked came and destroyed the whole land; but now that olives are available" (Jerusalem Talmud Pe'ah 7, 20a). — כַּזַּיִת, the size of an olive: "The olive's bulk of which they spoke is neither large nor small but medium" (Kelim 17:8). — *And זֵתִים, in the sense of a thing the size of an olive: "He would cut from his flesh olive-sized pieces (זתים זתים) and feed them to the ostriches" (Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, Zakhor). — כֶּרֶם זָיִת, a field planted with olive trees: "And he burned up both the shocks and the standing grain, and also the olive groves (כרם זָיִת)" (Judges 15:5). — And זַיִת alone in the sense of כֶּרֶם זַיִת: "In like manner you shall deal with your vineyard and with your olive grove (לְזֵיתֶךָ)" (Exodus 23:11). "Vineyards and olive trees (וְזֵיתִים) which you did not plant" (Deuteronomy 6:11). "And he will take your vineyards and your olive groves (וְזֵיתֵיכֶם), the best of them, and give them to his servants" (1 Samuel 8:14). — חָבַט זַיִת, נָקַף זַיִת, to make the berries fall from the tree: "Yet there shall be left in it gleanings, as at the beating of an olive tree (כנקף זַיִת), two or three berries in the top of the uppermost bough" (Isaiah 17:6). "When you beat your olive tree (זֵיתְךָ), you shall not go over the boughs again" (Deuteronomy 24:20). — *מָסַק זַיִת: "Olives of picking that were mixed with olives of beating" (Challah 3:9). "Workers who were hoeing among the figs, and cutting dates, and gathering grapes, and picking olives — these may eat and are exempt" (Bava Metzia 89b). — מַעֲשֵׂה-זַיִת, the work of the olive, the growing of the olive: "For though the fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in the vines; the labor of the olive (מַעֲשֵׂה-זַיִת) shall fail, and the fields shall yield no food" (Habakkuk 3:17). — °זֵיתֵי שמן, זֵיתֵי כבש: "And likewise one may separate terumah from oil olives for pickling olives, but not from pickling olives for oil olives" (Rambam, Terumot 5:18). — And in literary style, °החזיר זתיו במעטן, that is, strove to correct what is crooked in it: "For the Torah is an equal light to illuminate everyone who returns with all his heart; and whoever wishes to say the opposite of this says that its oil is not clear, and let him return his olives to the vat" (R. Y. Provenzalo, responsum on the study of the sciences).
*אוֹם.
בד, בית הבד, see in its place.
°גִּלְגֵּל, rolled olives. — גַּרְגֶּר, each single one of the fruit of the olive. — *גִּרְגֵּר, took the berries. — *גרופית, an olive branch for planting and for grafting.
*זוּע, זֵעָה.
חבט, נקף.
*טען, put them in the vat.
*כופש, *כותש, a large basket. — כמר. — *כתש. — כתת.
*לקה, began to rot a little, was crushed.

*מֹהַל, what comes out of pressed olives. — *מחבוא, for beating the olives. — *מֹחַל, like מֹהַל. — מָלַח the olives, a salted olive. — *מָסַק, gathered the olives from the tree. — מָסִיק, the time of olive picking. — מעטן, a place where the olives are pressed so that they will warm and soften. — מפרכה, one of the implements of the olive press. — מתן, became moist and softened.
נקף the berries from the tree, beat with a stick to make them fall.
*עוטן, *עטון. — *עקל.
*פג, פגים. — פצע, cracked them before the pressing. — *פרוד, *פרודים. — *פריצי זיתים.
*קופה. — *קשקש, dug around the tree.

he: ת"ז, בהפס' זָךְ, לנק' זַכָּה, מ"ר זַכִּים, זַכּוֹת, — נקי, טהור, שאינו עכור, klar, rein; pur, clair; pure, clear: ויקחו אליך שמן זית זָךְ כתית למאור (שמות כז כ). נטף ושחלת וחלבנה סמים ולבֹנה זַכָּה (שם ל לד). —  °זַךְ כזכוכית, שנראה האור מבעד לו: ובעבור היות הגוף זך תעבור בו ראות העין (מו"נ א כז). שעצם המוח עצם דק רוצה לומר ספירי זך העצם (מ' אלדבי, ש"א ד). והראיה על זה שהמראה מזכוכית הזך אם לא היה מכוסה מצד אחד מעופרת ומן הזפת לא היו נראין בו הצורות על פניו (מ' אלדבי, ש"א ט). זכים כזכוכית וכספיר (בירת מגדל עוז, אוצ"ט נז:). —  ובהשאלה במוסריות, טהור בלי כתם מוסרי, שאין בו שום עון, lauter; innocent: אם זַךְ וישר אתה כי עתה יעיר עליך ושלם נות צדקך (איוב ח ו). ותאמר זַךְ לקחי ובר הייתי בעיניך (שם יא ד). אך אמרת באזני וקול מלין אשמע זַךְ אני בלי פשע חף אנכי ולא עון לי (שם לג ח-ט). גם במעלליו יתנכר נער אם זַךְ ואם ישר פעלו (משלי כ יא). על לא חמס בכפי ותפלתי זַכָּה (איוב יו יז). הפילוסופים אשר דק עיונם וזכה מחשבתם (כוזרי ב נד). שצורת האדם היא זכה יותר משאר בעלי חיים עד שהיא דומה לצורות הפשוטות (מלמ' התלמיד', תזריע). —  ומ"ר במשמ' הטבעית והמוסרית: שתה מן הבור הזה שמימיו זכין וצונן (מד"ר קהל', שמור רגליך). מפני שהגלגלים טהורים וזכים כזכוכית וכספיר (רמב"ם יסוה"ת ג). והדבר ידוע מהגשמים הזכים שבהקפל חלקיהם ובהתקבצם זה אל זה יתעבו וימעט ספיריותם (רמ"ע מפאנו, אם כל חי א כד). — ואמר המשורר: תבל גנת ילדי רשע על כן שאפה אל גן זַכָּיו, ודבק בירוא האל אולי תהיה נפשך תוך גנזכיו (רמב"ע, תרשיש ח).
en: masculine adjective, in pause זָךְ, feminine זַכָּה, plural זַכִּים, זַכּוֹת, — clean, pure, not turbid, German klar, rein; French pur, clair; English pure, clear: "That they bring unto thee pure (זָךְ) olive oil beaten for the light" (Exodus 27:20). "Stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; sweet spices with pure (זַכָּה) frankincense" (ibid. 30:34). — °זַךְ like glass, through which light is seen: "And because the body is clear (זך), the sight of the eye passes through it" (Guide of the Perplexed 1:27). "For the substance of the brain is a fine substance, that is to say, sapphire-like, clear (זך) of substance" (M. Aldabi, Shevilei Emunah 4). "And the proof of this is that a mirror of clear (הזך) glass, if it were not covered on one side with lead and with pitch, the forms would not be seen on its face" (M. Aldabi, Shevilei Emunah 9). "Clear (זכים) as glass and as sapphire" (Birat Migdal Oz, אוצ"ט 57b). — And figuratively in morality, pure without moral stain, in whom there is no iniquity, German lauter; French innocent: "If thou wert זַךְ and upright, surely now He would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous" (Job 8:6). "For thou sayest: My doctrine is זַךְ, and I am clean in Thine eyes" (ibid. 11:4). "Surely thou hast spoken in mine ears, and I have heard the voice of thy words: I am זַךְ, without transgression, I am innocent, neither is there iniquity in me" (ibid. 33:8-9). "Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be זַךְ, and whether it be right" (Proverbs 20:11). "Although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is זַכָּה" (Job 16:17). "The philosophers whose study is subtle and whose thought is pure (וזכה)" (Kuzari 2:54). "For the form of man is purer (זכה) than that of other living creatures, so that it resembles the simple forms" (Malmad ha-Talmidim, Tazria). — And plural, in the natural and the moral sense: "Drink from this cistern, whose waters are clear (זכין) and cool" (Ecclesiastes Rabbah, Shemor Raglekha). "Because the spheres are pure and clear (וזכים) like glass and like sapphire" (Rambam, Yesodei ha-Torah 3). "And the matter is known from the clear (הזכים) bodies, that when their parts fold together and gather to one another they thicken and their transparency lessens" (R. Menahem Azariah of Fano, Em Kol Hai 1:24). — And the poet said: "The world is a garden of children of wickedness; therefore long for the garden of its pure ones (זַכָּיו), and cleave to the fear of God; perhaps your soul will be within His treasuries" (Moses ibn Ezra, Tarshish 8).

he: *, זכאי, זכיי, ש"ז, מ"ר זַכָּיִם, זכאים, זכיים, — א) מי שהוא נקי מחטא, מי שזכה בדין: ב' אומרים זכאי וא' אומר חייב זכאי שנים אומרים חייב ואחד אומר זכאי חייב אחד אומר זכאי ואחד אומר חייב וכו' יוסיפו הדיינין (סנה' ג ו). בן סורר ומורה נידון על שם סופו אמרה תורה ימות זכאי ואל ימות חייב (שם ח ה). שלא חייבתי את הזכאי ולא זכיתי את החייב (מד"ר במד' יח). ומעיינין בדינה (של הנשמה) אם תצא זכאית בדינה מוסרין אותה לרחמיאל (עמה"מ, שעשועי המלך לג). — ומ"ר: וכשיהיו בעלי דינים עומדים לפניך יהיו בעיניך כרשעים וכשנפטרים מלפניך יהיו בעיניך כזכאין כשקבלו עליהם את הדין (אבות א ח). — ב) * זַכַּי בדבר, יש לו זכות בו, הדבר שייך לו עפ"י החק והצדק: האב זכאי בבתו בקידושיה בכסף בשטר ובביאה וזכאי במציאתה ובמעשה ידיה (כתוב' ד ד). שהמוכר זכיי בפיאה (ירוש' פאה ה ד). אם אמרתם בנשואה שכן בעלה זכאי במציאתה וכו' תאמרו בארוסה שאין בעלה זכאי לא במציאתה ולא במעשה ידיה (כתוב' עח:). — ומ"ר: ולא זה וזה זכאים לא במציאתה ולא במעשה ידיה (יבמ' י א). — וְזַכַּי לעשות דבר, רשאי, יש לו רשות לעשותו: כל שאני זכאי באמירתו רשאי אני להחשיך עליו (שבת כג ג). מאימתי קורין את שמע בערבין וכו' משעה שהכהנים זכאין לאכול בתרומתן (תוספתא ברכ' א א). — ג) נרדף עם צדיק, ישר, מי שיש לו זכות: מגלגלים זכות על ידי זכאי וחובה על ידי חייב (ספרי, פנחס קלג). יש כאן אחד שראוי שתשרה עליו שכינה [כמשה רבינו] אלא שאין דורו זכאי לכך (סנה' יא.). אין בן דוד בא אלא בדור שכולו זכאי או כולו חייב (שם צח.). ולעולם ימוד אדם עצמו חציו זכאי וחציו חייב (שם קהל', זבובי מות). — ומ"ר: כשהיו ישראל זכאים היו מעידים בעצמם (ספרי, האזינו שו). שהיו (בנות צלפחד) זכאות בנות זכאי (שם פנחס קלג).
en: *, זכאי, זכיי, masculine noun, plural זַכָּיִם, זכאים, זכיים, — a) one who is clean of sin, one who was acquitted in judgment: "If two say 'innocent' and one says 'guilty' — innocent; if two say 'guilty' and one says 'innocent' — guilty; if one says 'innocent' and one says 'guilty' etc. — the judges are to be increased" (Sanhedrin 3:6). "The stubborn and rebellious son is judged on account of his end; the Torah said: let him die innocent and let him not die guilty" (ibid. 8:5). "That I did not convict the innocent and did not acquit the guilty" (Numbers Rabbah 18). "And they examine its (the soul's) judgment; if it comes out innocent in its judgment, they hand it over to Rachmiel" (Emek ha-Melekh, Sha'ashu'ei ha-Melekh 33). — And plural: "And when the litigants stand before you, let them be in your eyes as wicked, and when they depart from before you, let them be in your eyes as innocent, when they have accepted the judgment upon themselves" (Avot 1:8). — b) * זַכַּי בדבר, has a right to it, the thing belongs to him according to law and justice: "The father has rights over his daughter in her betrothal, by money, by document and by intercourse, and has rights to what she finds and to her handiwork" (Ketubot 4:4). "For the seller has rights to the pe'ah" (Jerusalem Talmud Pe'ah 5:4). "If you said this of a married woman, whose husband has rights to what she finds etc., will you say it of a betrothed woman, whose husband has rights neither to what she finds nor to her handiwork?" (Ketubot 78b). — And plural: "And neither this one nor that one has rights, neither to what she finds nor to her handiwork" (Yevamot 10:1). — And זַכַּי לעשות דבר, is permitted, has permission to do it: "Anything that I am permitted to say, I am permitted to wait at the boundary until nightfall for it" (Shabbat 23:3). "From when does one recite the Shema in the evening etc.? From the time that the priests are permitted to eat their terumah" (Tosefta Berakhot 1:1). — c) synonymous with צדיק, upright, one who has merit: "Merit is brought about through a meritorious person and guilt through a guilty person" (Sifre, Pinchas 133). "There is one here who is worthy that the Shekhinah should rest upon him [like Moses our teacher], but his generation is not worthy of it" (Sanhedrin 11a). "The son of David comes only in a generation that is entirely meritorious or entirely guilty" (ibid. 98a). "And a person should always regard himself as half meritorious and half guilty" (ibid. Ecclesiastes, זבובי מות). — And plural: "When Israel were meritorious, they would testify against themselves" (Sifre, Ha'azinu 306). "For they (the daughters of Zelophehad) were meritorious, daughters of a meritorious man" (ibid. Pinchas 133).

he: *, ש"ז, מ"ר זַמָּרִים, —  מי שאומנותו לזמר, Sänger; chanteur; singer: זמר בכל יום זמר בכל יום סנה' צט:. אמו זנתה עם רקד שהיה זמר ונתעברה הימנו מד"ז איכה ה. פעם אחת הביא אביך זמר והיה רקד והיה לו קול ערב שם. האספו כלכם השואפים לעשות שירים ספרי עליכם יהי היום לעינים דרך ישרה לכל זמר ומליץ ושר יורה ר"ע פרנסיס, מבוא למתק שפת'. — ומ"ר: חבורה שהיתה מבקשת לומר הימננו למלך אמר להם כלכם נעימים כלכם זמרים ילק' שמעוני ש"ב כב. — ואמר המקונן: זַמָּרֵי שחק החשו מנעם, ונם מה לכם פה אין היום טעם, מה תקלסו למלך בשעת הזעם קינה על חרבן ביהמ"ק. — ומשל: כל מה שמזמר הזמר אינו נכנס באזני הרקד כל מה שמזמר הזמר הבן הטפש אינו שומעגוף המשל בארמית: כל דזמר זמרא לא עייל באדניה דרקדא כל דזמר זמרא ברא דטפשא לא שמע. מד"ר איכ', פתיח'.
en: *, masculine noun, plural זַמָּרִים, — One whose profession is singing, German Sänger, French chanteur, English singer: “Sing (זמר) every day, sing (זמר) every day” (Sanhedrin 99b). “His mother committed harlotry with a dancer who was a singer (זמר), and conceived by him” (Midrash Zuta, Lamentations 5). “Once your father brought a singer (זמר), and he was a dancer, and he had a pleasant voice” (ibid.). “Gather, all of you who aspire to make poems; let my book be today, before your eyes, a straight path for every singer (זמר) and orator, and it will teach the poet” (Rabbi Immanuel Frances, Introduction to Metek Sefatayim). — And plural: “A company that wished to recite a hymn for the king; he said to them: You are all pleasant, you are all singers (זמרים)” (Yalkut Shimoni, 2 Samuel 22). — And the lamenter said: “Singers (זַמָּרֵי) of the heavens, be silent from sweetness, and say: What have you here? Today there is no reason; why do you praise the King in the hour of wrath?” (Lament on the destruction of the Temple). — And a proverb: “Whatever the singer (הזמר) sings does not enter the ears of the dancer; whatever the singer (הזמר) sings, the foolish son does not hear” [Note: the body of the proverb in Aramaic: כל דזמר זמרא לא עייל באדניה דרקדא כל דזמר זמרא ברא דטפשא לא שמע, “whatever the singer sings does not enter the ears of the dancer; whatever the singer sings, the foolish son does not hear”.] (Lamentations Rabbah, Petihta).

he: ש"ז, בכנ' זַעְמוֹ, זַעַמְךָ, מ"ר זְעָמִים, — כעס וקצף עז וחזק, Zorn; colère; anger: כי עוד מעט מזער וכלה זַעַם ואפי על תבליתם (ישע' י כה).  לך עמי בא בחדריך וסגר דלתיך בעדך חבי כמעט רגע עד יעבור זָעַם (שם כו כ).  הנה שם יי' בא ממרחק בער אפו וכבד משאה שפתיו מלאו זַעַם ולשונו כאש אכלת (שם ל כז).  לא ישבתי בסוד משחקים ואעלז מפני ידך בדד ישבתי כי זַעַם מלאתני (ירמ' יה יז).  את ארץ לא מטהרה היא לא גשמה ביום זָעַם (יחזק' כב כד).  ישלח בם חרון אפו עברה וָזַעַם וצרה (תהל' עח מט).  בְּזַעַם תצעד ארץ באף תדוש גוים (חבק' ג יב).  שכח יי' בציון מועד ושבת וינאץ בְּזַעַם אפו מלך וכהן (איכ' ב ו).  יפלו בחרב שריהם מִזַּעַם לשונם (הוש' ז יו).  — ובכנ': הוי אשור שבט אפי ומטה הוא בידם זַעְמִי בגוי חנף אשלחנו ועל עם עברתי אצונו לשלל שלל ולבז בז (ישע' י ה-ו).  מקצפו (של אלהים) תרעש הארץ ולא יכלו גוים זַעְמוֹ (ירמ' י י).  לפני זַעְמוֹ מי יעמוד ומי יקום בחרון אפו (נחום א ו).  כי אפר כלחם אכלתי ושקוי בבכי מסכתי מפני זַעַמְךָ (שם לח ד).  באים מארץ מרחק מקצה השמים יי' וכלי זַעְמוֹ לחבל כל הארץ (ישע' יג ה).  פתח יי' את אוצרו ויוצא את כלי זַעְמוֹ כי מלאכה היא לאדני יי' צבאות בארץ כשדים (ירמ' נ כה).  — ושפך זַעְמוֹ: ושפכתי עליך זַעְמִי באש עברתי אפיח עליך (יחזק' כא לו).  כי משפטי לאסף גוים לקבצי ממלכות לשפך עליהם זַעְמִי כל חרון אפי כי באש קנאתי תאכל כל הארץ (צפנ' ג ח).  שפך עליהם זַעְמֶךָ וחרון אפך ישיגם (תהל' סט כה).  — *פנים של זעם: אמר לו הקב"ה למשה המתן לי עד שיעברו פנים של זעם ואניח לך  (ברכ' ז.).  אותם פנים של זעם שהיו ראויות לבא אליך יסירם ממך (מד"ר במד' יא).  — ומ"ר °זְעָמִים: וירד מיכאל המלאך להרגו בִּזְעָמִים, וזעק הגוי גם צדיק תהרוג ותשפוך דמים (שחר' ב ר"ה, אשר מי).  מלא רחמים, נא הפר זְעָמִים ויודוך עמים אלהים אדירים (סליח' מוס' יוה"כ, אלהי העברים).  זכור תזכור רחמים יום הדין, הפר כעס וזעמים עת תדין, ליראיך ולחושבי שמך המה יושבי על מדין (פזמ' תימנ', בת אהובת אל).  — ומשל: בעת הזעם אלף אוהבים לא יצדיקוך, ובעת הרצון אלף שונאים לא יזיקיך (מראה המוסר יג).
en: masculine noun, with suffixes זַעְמוֹ, זַעַמְךָ, plural זְעָמִים, — fierce and strong anger and wrath, German Zorn; French colère; English anger: "For yet a very little while, and the indignation shall be spent, and My anger [shall turn] to their destruction" (Isaiah 10:25). "Come, my people, enter into your chambers and shut your doors behind you; hide yourself for a little moment, until the indignation is past" (ibid. 26:20). "Behold, the name of the Lord comes from afar, burning with His anger, and in thick rising smoke; His lips are full of indignation, and His tongue is as a devouring fire" (ibid. 30:27). "I did not sit in the assembly of those who make merry, nor rejoice; I sat alone because of Your hand, for You have filled me with indignation" (Jeremiah 15:17). "You are a land that is not cleansed, nor rained upon in the day of indignation" (Ezekiel 22:24). "He sent upon them the fierceness of His anger, wrath and indignation and trouble" (Psalms 78:49). "In indignation You march through the earth; in anger You thresh the nations" (Habakkuk 3:12). "The Lord has caused festival and Sabbath to be forgotten in Zion, and has spurned in the indignation of His anger king and priest" (Lamentations 2:6). "Their princes shall fall by the sword for the rage of their tongue" (Hosea 7:16). — And with suffixes: "Woe, Assyria, rod of My anger, and the staff in their hand is My indignation! I send him against an ungodly nation, and against the people of My wrath I charge him, to take the spoil and to take the prey" (Isaiah 10:5-6). "At His (God's) wrath the earth trembles, and the nations cannot abide His indignation" (Jeremiah 10:10). "Who can stand before His indignation? And who can abide the fierceness of His anger?" (Nahum 1:6). "For I have eaten ashes like bread, and mingled my drink with weeping, because of Your indignation" (ibid. 38:4). "They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, the Lord and the weapons of His indignation, to destroy the whole land" (Isaiah 13:5). "The Lord has opened His armory and has brought out the weapons of His indignation, for it is a work that the Lord God of hosts has to do in the land of the Chaldeans" (Jeremiah 50:25). — And שפך זַעְמוֹ, poured out his indignation: "And I will pour out My indignation upon you; I will blow upon you with the fire of My wrath" (Ezekiel 21:36). "For My determination is to gather the nations, to assemble the kingdoms, to pour upon them My indignation, all the fierceness of My anger; for all the earth shall be devoured with the fire of My jealousy" (Zephaniah 3:8). "Pour out Your indignation upon them, and let the fierceness of Your anger overtake them" (Psalms 69:25). — *פנים של זעם, a countenance of wrath: "The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: Wait for Me until the countenance of wrath passes, and I will grant you [your request]" (Berakhot 7a). "That countenance of wrath which was due to come upon you — He will remove it from you" (Numbers Rabbah 11). — And plural °זְעָמִים: "And Michael the angel came down to slay him in wrath, and the nation cried out: Will You slay even the righteous and shed blood?" (Shacharit of the second day of Rosh Hashanah, אשר מי). "O full of mercy, annul, I pray, the wraths, and the peoples shall praise You, mighty God" (Selichot of Musaf of Yom Kippur, אלהי העברים). "Remember, remember mercy on the day of judgment; annul anger and wraths at the time You judge, for those who fear You and those who think upon Your name — they who sit upon judgment" (Yemenite pizmonim, בת אהובת אל). — And a proverb: "In the time of wrath a thousand friends will not justify you, and in the time of favor a thousand enemies will not harm you" (מראה המוסר 13).

he: ש"ז, כנ' זַעְפּוֹ, — כעס וקצף גדול: זַעַף יי' אשא כי חטאתי לו (מיכ' ז ט). והשמיע יי' את הוד קולו ונחת זרועו יראה בְּזַעַף אף ולהב אש אוכלה (ישע' ל ל).  נהם ככפיר זַעַף מלך וכטל על עשב רצונו (משלי יט יב). ויכעס אסא אל הראה ויתנהו בית המהפכת כי בְזַעַף עמו על זאת (דהי"ב יו י). ותהרגו בם בְּזַעַף (שם כח ט). וּבְזַעְפּוֹ עם הכהנים והצרעת זרחה במצחו (שם כו יט). — ואמר המשורר: אם ילדי יום אותך ענו בעזוז נפש אותם ענה, או לך מנו לילות עמל לבב כבד להם מנה, או ים זַעְפָּם לך יסתער לו לב רחב כחול פנה (ר"י בן סהל בשבח רמב"ע איכה). — ובהשאלה להים בהתגעש מימיו: וישאו את יונה ויטלהו אל הים ויעמד הים מִזַּעְפּוֹ (יונה א יה). ואיזהו השונית כל מקום שהים עולה בזעפו (אהל' יח ו). כשהלך ניקנור להביא דלתות מאלכסנדריא של מצרים בחזירתו עמד עליו נחשול שבים לטבעו נטלו אחת מהן והטילוה לים ועדיין לא נח הים מזעפו בקשו להטיל את חברתה (יומ' לא.). רמז הקב"ה לשר של ים ועמד מזעפו (מד"ר בראש' י). —  *ולהגשמים כשהם יורדים בחזקה, ברוח עז ונפץ: התחילו גשמים מנטפין אמר (חוני) לא כך שאלתי אלא גשמי בורות שיחין ומערות התחילו לירד בזעף אמר לא כך שאלתי אלא גשמי רצון (תענ' ג ח). —  *ולהרוחות: בשבאין (הרוחות) בזעף אבל שבאים בנחת אומר ברוך עושה בראשית (ירוש' ברכ' ט ג). — °ומ"ר: בקרבך תסתר רוח זְעָפִים (תוכח' מוסר יה).
en: masculine noun, with suffixes זַעְפּוֹ, — anger and great wrath: "I will bear the indignation (זַעַף) of the LORD, because I have sinned against Him" (Micah 7:9). "And the LORD shall cause His glorious voice to be heard, and shall show the lighting down of His arm, with the indignation (בְּזַעַף) of His anger and the flame of a devouring fire" (Isaiah 30:30).
