for who can put forth his hand (יָדוֹ) against the Lord's anointed and be guiltless?” (ibid. 26:9). “How were you not afraid to put forth your hand (יָדְךָ) to destroy the Lord's anointed?” (2 Samuel 1:14). “Though I should receive a thousand pieces of silver in my hand, yet would I not put forth my hand (יָדִי) against the king's son” (ibid. 18:12). “He has put forth his hands (יָדָיו) against those who were at peace with him; he has profaned his covenant” (Psalms 55:21). “Behold, all that he has is in your power; only upon himself put not forth your hand (יָדֶךָ)” (Job 1:12). “But put forth your hand (יָדְךָ) now and touch all that he has” (ibid. 11). “And they sought to lay hand (יָד) on the king Ahasuerus” (Esther 2:21). “But he thought scorn to lay hand (יָד) on Mordecai alone” (ibid. 3:6). “Who had sought to lay hand (יָד) on the king” (ibid. 6:2). “And him they have hanged upon the gallows, because he laid his hand (יָדוֹ) upon the Jews” (ibid. 8:7). “To lay hand (יָד) on such as sought their hurt” (ibid. 9:2). “Then I testified against them and said to them: Why do you lodge about the wall? If you do so again, I will lay hands (יָד) on you” (Nehemiah 13:21). — And also of things that are not living creatures: “Then the master of the house shall come near to God, to see whether he has not put his hand (יָדוֹ) to his neighbour's goods” (Exodus 22:7), that is, touched it, misappropriated it and lost it. “He puts forth his hand (יָדוֹ) upon the flinty rock; he overturns the mountains by the roots” (Job 28:9). “He shall stretch forth his hand (יָדוֹ) also upon the countries, and the land of Egypt shall not escape” (Daniel 11:42). — And מִשְׁלֹחַ יָדוֹ of so-and-so: so-and-so put his hand to the thing: “And they shall fly down upon the shoulder of the Philistines on the west; together shall they spoil the children of the east; they shall put forth their hand (משלוח יָדָם) upon Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon shall obey them” (Isaiah 11:14). — And in the Talmud and Midrash: “One who intends to lay a hand on a deposit etc. is not liable until he lays a hand on it” (Bava Metzia 3:12). — And likewise *פָּשַׁט ידו in so-and-so: “That they stretched out their hands against the cursed proselytes” (Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 6, 23d). “The fathers of these stretched out their hands against the proselytes” (Numbers Rabbah 8). “Go, consider the former kings who transgressed, in that they stretched out their hands against Israel — what became of them, such as Pharaoh and Sennacherib” (ibid. Esther, אם על המלך טוב). “It is hard before the Holy One, blessed be He, to stretch out His hand against a person; rather He warns him and smites his house” (Tanchuma Tazria 13). — מצאה יָדוֹ לְדָבָר, השיגה יָדוֹ, הגיעה יָדוֹ: he is able to do the thing: “But if his means (יָדוֹ) suffice not to get it back for himself” (Leviticus 25:28). “Then you may do to them as your hand (יָדֶךָ) shall find occasion” (Judges 9:33). “Do as your hand (יָדֶךָ) shall find, for God is with you” (1 Samuel 10:7). “As my hand has reached (מצאה ידי) the kingdoms of the idols, whose graven images etc., so shall I do to Jerusalem and her idols” (Isaiah 10–11). “And my hand (יָדִי) has found as a nest the riches of the peoples” (ibid. 14). “If I rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand (יָדִי) had gotten much” (Job 31:25). “Your hand (יָדְךָ) shall find out all your enemies” (Psalms 21:9). “Whatever your hand (יָדְךָ) finds to do, do it with your might” (Ecclesiastes 9:10). “And if a man have no one to redeem it, and his hand (יָדוֹ) has attained and found sufficient to redeem it” (Leviticus 25:26). “But if his means (יָדוֹ) suffice not for two turtle-doves” (ibid. 5:11). “And if he be poor, and his means (יָדוֹ) suffice not” (ibid. 14:21). “According to the means (יַד) of him that vowed shall the priest value him” (ibid. 27:8). “And for the rams an ephah, and for the lambs according as his means (יָדוֹ) suffice” (Ezekiel 46:7). — And Ben Sira said: “Give to God according to His gift to you, with a good eye and according to the reach of your hand (ובהשגת יד)” (Ben Sira, Genizah, 32:12). — And הִגִּיעָה ידו in this sense: “And if his means (ידו) suffice not for a lamb, then he shall bring for his guilt, in that he has sinned, two turtle-doves” (Leviticus 5:7). — *And הגיעה ידו in the plain sense: “A hole between a Jew and an Aramean — he searches as far as his hand reaches, and the rest he nullifies in his heart” (Pesachim 8b). And conversely, קָצְרָה יַד so-and-so, he could not do the thing: “If flocks and herds be slain for them (the people), will they suffice them? Or if all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, will they suffice them? And the Lord said to Moses: Is the Lord's hand (הֲיַד) waxed short? Now shall you see whether My word shall come to pass to you or not” (Numbers 11:22–23). “Why, when I came, was there no man? When I called, was there none to answer? Is My hand (יָדִי) shortened at all, that it cannot redeem? Or have I no power to deliver?” (Isaiah 50:2). “Therefore their inhabitants were of small power (קצרי יַד), they were dismayed and confounded” (ibid. 37:27). — יָד חֲזָקָה, great, hard force: “Now shall you see what I will do to Pharaoh; for by a strong hand (בְיָד) shall he let them go, and by a strong hand (וּבְיָד) shall he drive them out of his land” (Exodus 6:1). “For with a strong hand (בְיָד) has the Lord brought you out of Egypt” (ibid. 13:9). “And Edom came out against him with much people and with a strong hand (וּבְיָד)” (Numbers 20:20). “As I live, says the Lord God, surely with a mighty hand (בְּיָד) and with an outstretched arm and with fury poured out will I be king over you” (Ezekiel 20:33). — And the hand of so-and-so was strong upon him (וחָזְקָה ידו … עליו): he felt the power and might of so-and-so; so-and-so compelled him to do a thing: “So a spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness, in the heat of my spirit, and the hand (וְיַד) of the Lord was strong upon me” (Ezekiel 3:14). *יָדוֹ תַּקִּיפָה על so-and-so, he has dominion over him: “Rav said: They taught this (that a woman imprisoned by idolaters for money is permitted to her husband) only where the hand of Israel is powerful over the idolaters; but where the hand of the idolaters is powerful over themselves, even for money she is forbidden” (Ketubot 26b). — And conversely, רָפוּ יָדָיו, his strength to do a thing was taken away: “And when Saul's son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands (יָדָיו) became feeble, and all Israel were affrighted” (2 Samuel 4:1). “We have heard the fame of it, our hands (יָדֵינוּ) wax feeble; anguish has taken hold of us, pain as of a woman in travail” (Jeremiah 6:24). “The king of Babylon has heard the fame of them, and his hands (יָדָיו) wax feeble; anguish has taken hold of him” (ibid. 50:43). “Because of the tidings, for it comes; and every heart shall melt, and all hands (יָדַיִם) shall be feeble, and every spirit shall faint” (Ezekiel 21:12). “Therefore shall all hands (יָדַיִם) be slack, and every heart of man shall melt” (Isaiah 13:7). “In that day it shall be said to Jerusalem: Fear not; O Zion, let not your hands (יָדָיִךְ) be slack” (Zephaniah 3:16). “For they all would make us afraid, saying: Their hands (יְדֵיהֵם) shall be weakened from the work” (Nehemiah 6:9). — יָדַיִם רָפוֹת, lack of strength: “Strengthen the weak hands (יָדַיִם), and confirm the feeble knees” (Isaiah 35:3). “Behold, you have instructed many, and you have strengthened the weak hands (וְיָדַיִם)” (Job 4:3). — And Ben Sira said: “For it is hard servitude and shame, a wife who supports her husband; slackness of hands (רפיון ידים) and stumbling of knees is a wife [Note: In the original it is printed 'אשר'.] who does not make her husband happy” (Ben Sira, Genizah, 25:22–23). — And אָזְלַת יד: “For the Lord will judge His people and repent Himself for His servants, when He sees that their power (יָד) is gone, and there is none shut up or left at large” (Deuteronomy 32:36). — And the rhetorician said: “The princes of the age were dismayed at the death of their lord whom they had anointed as king, and at the failing power (ואזלת יד) of our Gaon; the chosen of God delayed, and to the age they say: Up, make us gods which shall go before us” (Rabbi Judah al-Harizi, Tachkemoni 3). — *נתרשלו יָדָיו (his hands grew slack): “Like people who go out to war: when they go out they are joyful, and the longer they toil, their hands grow slack” (Sifre Numbers 82). “Like a king's son who sinned against his father, and his friend appeased the king for him once, twice and three times; when he sinned a fourth time, the hands of the king's friend grew slack” (Numbers Rabbah 18). “Like a painter who was painting a portrait of the king; he came to finish the face, and they said: The king has died and another king has arisen. As soon as the painter heard this, his hands grew slack; he began to say: What shall I do with these paints that are in my hand?” (Tanchuma Naso 6). “In the dispute of Korah his (Moses') hands grew slack” (Rashi Numbers 16:4). — משך יָדוֹ את so-and-so: “He stretched out his hand (יָדוֹ) with scorners” (Hosea 7:5), see the entry מָשַׁךְ. — *And מָשַׁךְ ידו מן a thing: kept away from it, left it, did not do it: “After Simeon the Righteous died, the blessing was taken away from the two loaves and from the showbread, and each one of them received as much as a bean; the modest would withdraw their hands, and the gluttons would stretch out their hands” (Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 6, 43c). “If this Passover lamb is ours, your hands are withdrawn from yours and you are counted on ours; and if this Passover lamb is yours, our hands are withdrawn from ours and we are counted on yours” (Pesachim 98b). “Like a king who made a feast and invited the guests, and a creeping thing fell into the dish; had the king withdrawn his hand, all would have withdrawn their hands; the king stretched out his hand, and all stretched out their hands” (Song of Songs Rabbah, באתי לגני). — השיב יָדוֹ מעשות a thing, refrained from doing the thing: “The Lord has purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion; He has stretched out the line, He has not withdrawn His hand (יָדוֹ) from destroying” (Lamentations 2:8). — And השיב יָדוֹ from so-and-so, refrained from harming him: “Has given his bread to the hungry and has covered the naked with a garment, has withdrawn his hand (יָדוֹ) from the poor, has not taken interest nor increase, has executed My ordinances” (Ezekiel 18:16–17). — *סִלֵּק יָדָיו מן so-and-so, and his hands are removed (מסלקות) from the thing: “One who says to his fellow: I have no claim or dealing in this field, and I have no business with it, and my hands are removed from it — has said nothing” (Bava Batra 49a). — יָד רָמָה, did the thing with a high hand (בְיָד רָמָה): openly, without fear or dread: “And the children of Israel went out with a high hand (בְּיָד)” (Exodus 14:8). “On the morrow after the Passover the children of Israel went out with a high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians” (Numbers 33:3). “But the soul that does (the sin) with a high hand (בְּיָד), whether he be home-born or a stranger, the same blasphemes the Lord, and that soul shall be cut off from among his people” (ibid. 15:30). רָמָה יָדוֹ of so-and-so: he was strong, prevailed: “Lest they should say: Our hand (יָדֵנוּ) is exalted, and not the Lord has done all this” (Deuteronomy 32:27). “Lord, Your hand (יָדְךָ) is lifted up, yet they see not” (Isaiah 26:11). — And רָמָה יָדוֹ על so-and-so, prevailed over him: “Let your hand (יָדְךָ) be lifted up above your adversaries, and let all your enemies be cut off” (Micah 5:8). — And הרים יַד against so-and-so, especially against a king and the like: transgressed against him, rebelled against him: “And Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite etc., he also lifted up his hand (יָד) against the king. And this was the cause that he lifted up his hand (יָד) against the king” (1 Kings 11:26–27). — יַד לְפֶה, a call and command to be silent: “If you have done foolishly in lifting up yourself, or if you have planned evil, lay your hand (יָד) upon your mouth” (Proverbs 30:32). — שָׂם יַד על פה: “Mark me and be astonished, and lay your hand (יַד) upon your mouth” (Job 21:5). “Behold, I am of small account; what shall I answer You? I lay my hand (יָדִי) upon my mouth” (ibid. 40:4). — And ונשקה יָדוֹ לפיו, in this sense: “And my heart has been secretly enticed, and my hand (יָדִי) has kissed my mouth” (ibid. 31:27). — And Ben Sira said: “If you have it in you, answer your neighbour; and if not, your hand (ידך) upon your mouth” (Ben Sira, Genizah, 5:12). — יָדָיו על ראשׁוֹ, as a sign of mourning and grief, as a sign of despair: “From him also shall you go forth with your hands (וְיָדַיִךְ) upon your head” (Jeremiah 2:37). “And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her garment of many colours that was on her, and she laid her hand (יָדָהּ) on her head and went her way, crying aloud as she went” (2 Samuel 13:19). — And in the Talmud and Midrash: “It is demonstrated in the case of Lot that he dwelt in Sodom only because of his wealth; he too went out with his hands on his head” (Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10, 29d). — קבץ עַל יָד, little by little: “Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished, but he that gathers little by little (על יָד) shall increase” (Proverbs 13:11). — And doubled in the Talmud and Midrash, על יד על יד: “A shepherd who repented — they do not oblige him to sell all of them at once, but he sells gradually, little by little; if pigs and dogs fell to him by inheritance, they do not oblige him to sell all of them at once, but he sells gradually, little by little” (Tosefta Bava Kamma 8:15). “If produce was scattered for him in the courtyard, he gathers little by little and eats” (Shabbat 143b). “He should leave the sela in the shop, that is to say, give it to the shopkeeper and spend it little by little until he completes the sela” (Rambam's Commentary on the Mishnah, Ma'aser Sheni 2:9). — יָד לְיָד, this way or that, in whatever manner it may be: “Hand to hand (יד ליד), the evil man shall not be unpunished, but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered” (Proverbs 11:21). “Everyone that is proud in heart is an abomination to the Lord; hand to hand (יָד לְיָד), he shall not be unpunished” (ibid. 16:5). — *לקח a thing מִיַּד לְיַד, in the sense of without an intermediary and go-between between them: “Like a king who betrothed a noblewoman with two pearls from hand to hand, and then sent her eight more through his agent etc. The king said: Where are the two pearls I gave her from my hand to her hand etc.? For those two pearls that I gave her from hand to hand she has lost” (Exodus Rabbah 42). “Reuben claimed against Simeon that he took interest from him from hand to hand, and Simeon answered that he received it from the hand of a Cuthean” (Responsa of the Rosh 108:9). — מִלֵּא את ידו of so-and-so, gave him the priesthood and the like: “And you shall anoint them (Aaron and his sons), and consecrate them (ומלאת את יָדָם), and sanctify them, that they may minister to Me in the priest's office” (Exodus 28:41). “And you shall consecrate (ומלאת יַד) Aaron and his sons (וְיַד בניו), and you shall bring the bullock etc.” (ibid. 29:9–10). “For He shall consecrate you (ימלא את יֶדְכֶם) seven days” (Leviticus 8:33). “And the man Micah had a house of God, and he made an ephod and teraphim, and consecrated (וימלא את יַד) one of his sons, who became his priest” (Judges 17:5). “But (Jeroboam) made again from among all the people priests of the high places; whoever would, he consecrated him (ימלא את יָדוֹ), that there might be priests of the high places” (1 Kings 13:33). — And Ben Sira said in the chapter on the priesthood: “And Moses consecrated him (וימלא … את ידו) (Aaron) and anointed him with the holy oil, and it became for him an everlasting covenant, and for his seed as the days of heaven, to minister and to serve as priest and to bless His people in His name” (Ben Sira, Genizah, 45:15). — *יָדָיו יָפוֹת, quick and nimble at eating: “Members of a company, one of whom had fine hands (ידיו … יפות) — they may say to him: Take your share and eat by yourself” (Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 8, 36a). — *יָדָיו חֲמוּמוֹת, see חָמַם. — And in a special sense, יַד יי' in the matter of the holy spirit that rests upon the prophet and the like: “For the Lord spoke thus to me with a strong hand (הַיָּד), and instructed me that I should not walk in the way of this people” (Isaiah 8:11). “The word of the Lord came expressly to Ezekiel the son of Buzi the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar, and the hand (יַד) of the Lord was there upon him” (Ezekiel 1:3). “And the hand (יַד) of the Lord was there upon me, and He said to me: Arise, go forth into the plain, and I will speak with you there” (ibid. 3:22). “The hand (יַד) of the Lord was upon me, and the Lord carried me out in the spirit” (ibid. 37:1). — And by extension, יַד is used in the sense of dominion and authority [Note: They already said in the Jerusalem Gemara, Gittin 8, 49b: “Rabbi Ishmael taught: ‘And he had taken all his land out of his hand (מידו) unto Arnon’ — and did he take it out of his hand? Rather, what is מידו? From his domain (מרשותו).”], נתן בְּיַד so-and-so, into his dominion and authority: “And he delivered them into the hand (בְּיַד) of his servants, every drove by itself” (Genesis 32:17). “And he (Potiphar) left all that he had in Joseph's hand (בְּיַד)” (ibid. 39:6). “And the keeper of the prison committed to Joseph's hand (בְּיַד) all the prisoners that were in the prison” (ibid. 22). “And let them lay up corn under the hand (יַד) of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and let them keep it” (ibid. 41:35). “And I will bring a sword upon you etc., and you shall be delivered into the hand (בְּיַד) of the enemy” (Leviticus 26:25). “To deliver us into the hand (בְּיַד) of the Amorites, to destroy us” (Deuteronomy 1:27). “Then the elders of his (the murderer's) city shall send and fetch him from there, and deliver him into the hand (בְּיַד) of the avenger of blood, that he may die” (ibid. 19:12). “And the Lord delivered it also (the city of Libnah) into the hand (בְּיַד) of Israel” (Joshua 10:30). “And the Lord delivered them into the hand (בְּיַד) of Israel, and they smote them” (ibid. 11:8). “And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and He delivered them into the hands (בְּיַד) of spoilers that spoiled them” (Judges 2:14). “So the Lord left those nations, without driving them out hastily, neither delivered He them into the hand (בְּיַד) of Joshua” (ibid. 23). “Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand (בְּיַד) of the king of Assyria” (Isaiah 37:10). “And I will give you into the hand (בְּיַד) of them that seek your life, and into the hand (וּבְיַד) of them of whom you are afraid” (Jeremiah 22:25). “The earth is given into the hand (בְּיַד) of the wicked” (Job 9:24). “And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and He sold them into the hand (בְּיַד) of Cushan-rishathaim” (Judges 3:8). “For the Lord will give Sisera over into the hand (בְּיַד) of a woman” (ibid. 4:9). “And Saul thought to make David fall by the hand (בְּיַד) of the Philistines” (1 Samuel 18:25). “And David said: Will the men of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand (בְּיַד) of Saul?” (ibid. 23:12). “Come down, and our part shall be to deliver him into the king's hand (בְּיַד)” (ibid. 20). “And You have not given me over into the hand (בְּיַד) of the enemy” (Psalms 31:9). “And I will give over the Egyptians into the hand (בְּיַד) of a cruel lord” (Isaiah 19:4). “I shall now perish one day by the hand (בְּיַד) of Saul” (1 Samuel 27:1). “And have not delivered you into the hand (בְיַד) of David” (2 Samuel 3:8). “And the kingdom was established in the hand (בְּיַד) of Solomon” (1 Kings 2:46). “You have forsaken Me, therefore have I also left you in the hand (בְּיַד) of Shishak” (2 Chronicles 12:5). “Therefore You left them in the hand (בְּיַד) of their enemies, so that they had dominion over them” (Nehemiah 9:28). “Behold, your maid is in your hand (בְּיָדֵךְ); do to her that which is good in your eyes” (Genesis 16:6). “I was wroth with My people, I profaned My inheritance, and gave them into your hand (בְּיָדֵךְ)” (Isaiah 47:6). “For I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand (בְּיֶדְכֶם)” (Exodus 23:31). “He will also deliver Moab into your hand (בְּיֶדְכֶם)” (2 Kings 3:18). “But as for me, behold, I am in your hand (בְיֶדְכֶם); do with me as is good and right in your eyes” (Jeremiah 26:14). “And he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand (בְּיָדוֹ)” (Genesis 39:4). “They shall not deliver up the manslayer into his hand (בְּיָדוֹ), because he smote his neighbour unawares” (Joshua 20:5). “Behold, I have delivered the land into his hand (בְּיָדוֹ)” (Judges 1:2). “The Lord delivered all their enemies into their hand (בְּיָדָם)” (Joshua 21:42). “Lest they deliver me into their hand (בְּיָדָם), and they mock me” (Jeremiah 38:19). “The Lord has delivered me into their hands (בִּידֵי), against whom I am not able to stand” (Lamentations 2:14). — And of things that are not living creatures: “Death and life are in the power (בְּיַד) of the tongue” (Proverbs 18:21). “For You have hid Your face from us, and have consumed us by means (בְּיַד) of our iniquities” (Isaiah 64:6). — And in the Talmud and Midrash: “He shall not say so to his minor son and daughter, or to his Canaanite manservant and maidservant, because their hand is as his hand” (Ma'aser Sheni 4:4). “And not (shall he acquire) through his Canaanite manservant and maidservant, because their hand is as his hand” (Eruvin 7:6). “The Omnipresent said to Moses: My beloved ones are drowning in the sea, and the sea is closing in, and the enemy is pursuing, and you stand and multiply prayer! He said before Him: Master of the World, and what is in my hand (בידי) to do?” (Mekhilta Beshallach 2:5). “For he was a community administrator, and the hand of the administrator is as the hand of the poor” (Jerusalem Talmud Ma'aser Sheni 5, 56c). “The hand of a wife is as the hand of her husband” (Nedarim 88b). “Abaye said: A married woman — his hand is as her hand” (Ketubot 83a). “Since it is in his power (בידו) to declare them ownerless” (Shabbat 131b). “He took his merchandise and made it into precious stones and pearls; he set out on the road, and robbers seized him; they said to him: What is in your hand? He said to them: Glass vessels” (Exodus Rabbah 30). “A man of flesh and blood says a thing and does not do it, because it is not in his power (בידו) to do it” (Pesikta Rabbati, Parah). “My seizure is as his seizure, for my hand is as his hand in every business of the partnership” (Tur Choshen Mishpat 72:33, in the name of the Rosh). — מִיַּד so-and-so, from his domain, from his dominion and power: “Deliver me, I pray You, from the hand (מִיַּד) of my brother, from the hand (מִיַּד) of Esau” (Genesis 32:12). “And he bought the parcel of ground where he had spread his tent, at the hand (מִיַּד) of the children of Hamor, Shechem's father” (ibid. 33:19). “Moreover I have given to you one portion above your brothers, which I took out of the hand (מִיַּד) of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow” (ibid. 48:22). “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand (מִיַּד) of the shepherds” (Exodus 2:19). “And I am come down to deliver them out of the hand (מִיַּד) of the Egyptians” (ibid. 3:8). “Or buy of your neighbour's hand (מִיַּד)” (Leviticus 25:14). “And the Lord raised up judges, who saved them out of the hand (מִיַּד) of those who spoiled them” (Judges 2:16). “I will surely rend the kingdom from you etc.; I will rend it out of the hand (מִיַּד) of your son” (1 Kings 11:11–12). “Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand (מִיַּד) of Solomon” (ibid. 31). “And deliver the spoiled out of the hand (מִיַּד) of the oppressor” (Jeremiah 21:12). “Or deliver me from the adversary's hand (מִיַּד), or redeem me from the hand (וּמִיַּד) of the oppressors” (Job 6:23). “I bore the loss of it; of my hand (מִיָּדִי) did you require it” (Genesis 31:39). “Have they delivered Samaria out of my hand (מִיָּדִי)?” (2 Kings 18:34). “And none shall deliver her out of My hand (מִיָּדִי)” (Hosea 2:12). “He would not have received a burnt offering and a meal offering at our hand (מִיָּדֵנוּ)” (Judges 13:23). “And there is none that can deliver out of Your hand (מִיָּדְךָ)” (Job 10:7). “And the Lord has rent the kingdom out of your hand (מִיָּדֶךָ)” (1 Samuel 28:17). “And I will deliver My people out of your hand (מִיֶּדְכֶן)” (Ezekiel 13:21). “And you shall not escape out of his hand (מִיָּדוֹ), but shall surely be taken” (Jeremiah 34:3). “Behold, I am against the shepherds, and I will require My sheep at their hand (מִיָּדָם)” (Ezekiel 34:10). — And in the Talmud and Midrash: “It is a benefit for a slave to go out from the hand of his master to freedom” (Kiddushin 23a). — And with the verbs שָׁפַט, רָב: “Let me now run and bear the king tidings, how that the Lord has avenged him of the hand (מִיַּד) of his enemies” (2 Samuel 18:19). “The Lord therefore be judge, and judge between me and you, and see, and plead my cause, and deliver me out of your hand (מִיָּדֶךָ)” (1 Samuel 24:16). “Blessed be the Lord, who has pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand (מִיַּד) of Nabal” (ibid. 25:39). — And in this sense they also say מִיַּד of a beast and a wild animal: “The Lord who delivered me out of the paw (מִיַּד) of the lion and out of the paw (וּמִיַּד) of the bear, He will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine” (1 Samuel 17:37). “Deliver my soul from the sword, my only one from the power (מִיַּד) of the dog” (Psalms 22:21). — And also מִיַּד of things that are not living creatures: “I will ransom them from the power (מִיַּד) of the grave; I will redeem them from death” (Hosea 13:14). “They shall not deliver themselves from the power (מִיַּד) of the flame” (Isaiah 47:14). “But God will redeem my soul from the power (מִיַּד) of the grave” (Psalms 49:17). “And as a bird from the hand (מִיַּד) of the fowler” (Proverbs 6:5). “In famine He shall redeem you from death, and in war from the power (מִידֵי) of the sword” (Job 5:20). “Keep me from the snare (מִידֵי פח) which they have laid for me” (Psalms 141:9). — And in the Talmud and Midrash: “And one who comes to rescue from the fire, from the troops, from the collapse (מיד הדליקה מיד הגיים מיד המפולת)” (Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 2, 57c). — תחת יָדוֹ: was afflicted, submitted under his hand, under his dominion: “Return to your mistress, and submit yourself under her hands (יָדֶיהָ)” (Genesis 16:9). “Their enemies also oppressed them, and they were brought into subjection under their hand (יָדָם)” (Psalms 106:42). — Died under the hand (תחת יָדוֹ) of so-and-so, while he was occupied with him: “And if a man smite his bondman or his bondwoman with a rod, and he die under his hand (יָדוֹ), he shall surely be punished” (Exodus 21:20). — And also °בין יְדֵי so-and-so, in the sense of: with him: “Be a servant to men, between their hands (בין ידיהם) [Note: According to the idiom of the Arabic language.], and then you will be precious and also honoured in their mouth” (Rav Hai Gaon, Shirei Musar HaSechel). “Here I am, my lord the king, between your hands (בין ידיך)” (Ben HaMelech VeHaNazir 18). “And the place of shame is in rebelling against the One who does good to you with His goodness, before His face and between His hands (בין ידיו), when He reproves you by His witnesses, the good and the bad” (Chovot HaLevavot, Avodat Hashem 10). “The generations pass, and his friends and acquaintances part from him, from between his two hands (מבין שתי ידיו)” (Kad HaKemach of Rabbi Bachya the Judge). *And מתחת יָדוֹ: “Moses said: Master of the World, after all the miracles that You have done for them, I am to die at their hands (מתחת ידיהם)?” (Numbers Rabbah 19). — °He is under his hand (תחת יָדוֹ): he is subject to him: “That every idolater who has not accepted the commandments that the children of Noah were commanded is put to death, if he is under our hand (תחת ידינו)” (Rambam, Melakhim 8:9). — *And תחת ידו, מתחת ידו: with him, in his possession: “The injured person — how did they testify concerning him? That he came under his hand whole and went out injured” (Shevu'ot 7:3). “A chaver shall not serve at a banquet of an am ha'aretz or at a meal of an am ha'aretz, unless everything was prepared and tithed from under his hand (מתחת ידו)” (Jerusalem Talmud Demai 2, 22d). — *And יָצָא מִתַּחַת יָדָיו in this sense: “A bond that comes out from under the hands (מתחת ידי) of the lender in his own handwriting is invalid” (Jerusalem Talmud Shevu'ot 7, 38a). “A receipt (סמפון) that has witnesses on it is validated by its signatories; if it has no witnesses on it and comes out from under the hands of a trustee, or comes out after the signatures of documents, it is valid” (Bava Metzia 21a). “One of the brothers from under whose hand the bond of debt comes out must bring proof” (Bava Batra 173a). — *And לקח את שלו מתחת ידיו של so-and-so: was punished: “Like a king's son who was sleeping on a cradle, and his nurse was astonished and confounded, because she knew that she was destined to take her own from under his hands; so the earth foresaw that it was destined to take its own from under the hands of man, as it is said: ‘Cursed is the ground for your sake’” (Genesis Rabbah 2). “Whoever comes to join battle with Israel (to do them evil) ends up taking his own from under their hands” (ibid. 41). “Anyone against whom the sages stretched out a hand, even though they afterwards received him back, ends up taking his own from under their hands” (ibid. Numbers 14). “Thus said Moses: because I said to them ‘Hear now, you rebels’, I took my own from under their hands; and now I come to reprove them!” (ibid. Deuteronomy 1). “And Israel would say to them (to the men of Midian): Is it not enough for you that we took our own from under your hands?” (ibid. Song of Songs, אל תראוני). — בְּיַד so-and-so, in the sense that so-and-so is like the messenger for the thing: “And Judah sent the kid of the goats by the hand (בְּיַד) of his friend the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the woman's hand” (Genesis 38:20). “And he (Moses) said: Oh, my Lord, send, I pray You, by the hand (בְּיַד) of whom You will send” (Exodus 4:13). “To bring for all the work which the Lord had commanded to be made by the hand (בְּיַד) of Moses” (ibid. 35:29). “And Aaron and his sons did all the things which the Lord commanded by the hand (בְּיַד) of Moses” (Leviticus 8:36). “All the statutes which the Lord has spoken to them by the hand (בְּיַד) of Moses” (ibid. 10:11). “And shall send it (the goat) away by the hand (בְּיַד) of an appointed man into the wilderness” (ibid. 16:21). “These are the statutes and ordinances and laws which the Lord made between Him and the children of Israel in mount Sinai by the hand (בְּיַד) of Moses” (ibid. 26:46). “Of which I spoke to you by the hand (בְּיַד) of Moses” (Joshua 20:2). “And the children of Israel sent a present by him (בְּיָדוֹ) to Eglon the king of Moab” (Judges 3:15). “And he sent them throughout all the borders of Israel by the hand (בְּיַד) of messengers, saying” (1 Samuel 11:7). “And Jesse took an ass laden with bread, and a bottle of wine, and a kid, and sent them by the hand (בְּיַד) of David his son to Saul” (ibid. 16:20 [Note: In the original it is printed 'שם טז'.]). “And God is departed from me, and answers me no more, neither by the hand (בְּיַד) of the prophets nor by dreams” (ibid. 28:15). “For the Lord has spoken of David, saying: By the hand (בְּיַד) of My servant David I will save My people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines” (2 Samuel 3:18). “And David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand (בְּיַד) of Uriah” (ibid. 11:14). “And He sent by the hand (בְּיַד) of Nathan the prophet, and he called his name Jedidiah” (ibid. 12:25). “And by them (בְּיָדָם) you shall send to me everything that you shall hear” (ibid. 15:36). “That He might establish His word, which the Lord spoke by the hand (בְּיַד) of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat” (1 Kings 12:15). “And also by the hand (בְּיַד) of the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani came the word of the Lord against Baasha and against his house” (ibid. 16:7). “This is the word of the Lord, which He spoke by the hand (בְּיַד) of His servant Elijah the Tishbite” (2 Kings 9:36). “For the Lord has done that which He spoke by the hand (בְּיַד) of His servant Elijah” (ibid. 10:10). “At the same time the Lord spoke by the hand (בְּיַד) of Isaiah the son of Amoz” (Isaiah 20:2). “By the hand (בְּיַד) of your servants you have taunted the Lord” (ibid. 37:24). “And send them to the king of Edom etc. and to the king of Zidon, by the hand (בְּיַד) of the messengers that come to Jerusalem” (Jeremiah 27:3). “Came the word of the Lord by the hand (בְּיַד) of Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel” (Haggai 1:1). “To walk in His laws, which He set before us by the hand (בְּיַד) of His servants the prophets” (Daniel 9:10). — And in the Talmud and Midrash: “One who borrows a cow, and he (the lender) sent it to him by the hand of his son, by the hand of his slave, by the hand of his agent, or by the hand of the son, the slave or the agent of the borrower, and it died — he is exempt. If the borrower said to him: Send it to me by the hand of my son, by the hand of my slave, by the hand of my agent, or by the hand of your son, your slave, your agent; or if the lender said to him: Behold, I am sending it to you by the hand of my son, by the hand of my slave, by the hand of my agent, or by the hand of your son, your slave, your agent, and the borrower said to him: Send it” (Bava Metzia 8:3). — *And also of a thing that is not a living creature: “Were it not that you are holding me, I would already have been swept away by the hand (ביד) of the torrent and died” (Pesikta Rabbati 31). — And at a later time they used, in this sense, the expression עַל-יְדֵי: “To praise the Lord according to the direction (עַל-יְדֵי) of David king of Israel” (Ezra 3:10). “To offer the burnt offerings of the Lord, as it is written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and with singing, according to the direction (עַל-יְדֵי) of David” (2 Chronicles 23:18). — And also of things that are not living creatures, when they are the means used to do the thing: “The song of the Lord began also, with the trumpets, and by means of (וְעַל-יְדֵי) the instruments of David king of Israel” (2 Chronicles 29:27). — And this usage is very common in the Talmud and Midrash and in סהמ"א: “One who maintains his wife through (על ידי) a third party shall give her no less than two kav of wheat” (Ketubot 5:8). “Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai says: The Holy One, blessed be He, gave Israel three good gifts, and all of them He gave only through (על ידי) sufferings” (Berakhot 5a). “Perhaps he conferred the benefit on him through (על ידי) another” (Gittin 40b). “This one is used with (על ידי) hot water and this one is used with cold” (Pesachim 30b). “And then he sent her eight more (pearls) through (על ידי) his agent etc. The king said: Where are the two pearls I gave her from my hand to her hand, and I sent her eight through you (על ידך)?” (Exodus Rabbah 42). “If you are pure, drink and do not refrain, so that you may be clean for your husband through (על ידי) these waters” (ibid. Numbers 9). — And עַל יָדְךָ: because of you: “Because I have lost four hundred zuz on account of you (על ידך)” (Shabbat 31a). — *עַל יְדֵי שֶׁ, in the sense of: because of the thing: “Jacob, because (על ידי ש) he took four wives, Leah and Rachel, Zilpah and Bilhah, he says: ‘your father's sons’” (Genesis Rabbah 66). “The wicked, because (על ידי ש) their beginning is tranquillity and their end sufferings, open with a blessing etc.; but the righteous, because their beginning is sufferings and their end tranquillity, open with a curse” (ibid.). “Job said: Because my doors were wide open, everyone reaped dry stalks while I reaped fresh ears” (ibid.). “Because the way of a prince is that all his needs come from the public, and this one, because he did not benefit from the public at all, therefore he says: Let my widow not move from my house” (ibid. 100). “Because Israel fenced themselves off from unchastity in Egypt, they were redeemed” (ibid. Leviticus 32). — נתן עַל-יַד so-and-so: gave to so-and-so, that so-and-so should guard the thing, and the like: “Deliver him (Benjamin) into my hand (על-יָדִי), and I will bring him back to you” (Genesis 42:37). “And he (Rehoboam) committed them (the shields) to the hands (על-יַד) of the chief of the guard” (1 Kings 14:27). “If any of the men whom I bring into your hands (על-יְדֵיכֶם) escape, his life shall be for the life of him” (2 Kings 10:24). “And they gave the money that was weighed out into the hands (על-יַד [Note: יד is the ketiv, ידי the qeri.]) of those who did the work” (ibid. 12:12). “Even those did Cyrus king of Persia bring forth (the vessels of the Temple) by the hand (על-יַד) of Mithredath the treasurer” (Ezra 1:8). “That they may gather together every fair young virgin to Shushan the castle, to the house of the women, to the custody (אל-יַד) of Hegai the king's chamberlain” (Esther 2:3). — And אִנָּה לְיָדוֹ: caused to befall him, made it come to him: “And if a man lie not in wait, but God cause it to come to his hand (לְיָדוֹ), then I will appoint you a place whither he may flee” (Exodus 21:13). — And also of things that are not living creatures: “Therefore deliver up their children to the famine, and pour them out by the power (על-יְדֵי) of the sword” (Jeremiah 18:21). “And have delivered the children of Israel to the power (על-יְדֵי) of the sword” (Ezekiel 35:5). “Their judges are thrown down by the sides (בִידֵי) of the rock” (Psalms 141:6). — *בא לִידֵי a thing, and הביאו לידי a thing: “Consider three things and you will not come into the hands of (לידי) transgression” (Avot 3:1). “That the name that brings them to (לידי) lashes does not bring them to (לידי) payment” (Makkot 1:2). “Rice, millet, poppy, pulse and sesame, which do not come to (לידי) leavening and matzah but to (לידי) putrefaction” (Mekhilta Bo 8). “Sometimes stains bring a woman to (לידי) zivah” (Tosefta Niddah 3:5). “If it was a limb from a living creature, even from a sick one, it is forbidden, so that he should not come to (לידי) a stumbling” (Jerusalem Talmud Demai 3, 23b). “For nothing comes to (לידי) matzah and leaven except the five species alone” (ibid. Challah 1, 57a). “If he came to (לידי) illness, or entered into (לידי) old age, or into a measure of sufferings, and cannot do work, behold, he dies of hunger” (ibid. Kiddushin 4, 66d). “Things that come to (לידי) leavening — a person fulfils his obligation with them as matzah” (Pesachim 35a). “Either he buries her or she brings him to (לידי) poverty” (ibid. 49a). “Lest the windpipe precede the gullet and he come to (לידי) danger” (ibid. 108a). “A person should not have impure thoughts by day and come to (לידי) uncleanness at night” (Ketubot 46a). “When he says: The benefit that brings to (לידי) your food is forbidden to me” (Nedarim 33a). “For whoever does not conduct himself toward his teacher with all these qualities is called wicked before the Omnipresent, and his learning is forgotten and his years are shortened, and in the end he comes to (לידי) poverty” (Numbers Rabbah 15). — *יָצָא יְדֵי so-and-so: did what he is obliged to do with regard to so-and-so, so that so-and-so should not suspect him of anything: “Because a person must clear himself before (לצאת ידי) people just as he must clear himself before (לצאת ידי) the Omnipresent” (Shekalim 3:2). — And יְדֵי שמים: what he is obliged to do toward Heaven, toward God: “And they said to him: Fulfil your duty to Heaven (צא ידי שמים)” (Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 3, 28a). — יָצָא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ: did what he was obliged to do: “Dog-dough, when the shepherds eat of it, is liable to challah etc., and a person fulfils his obligation (ידי חובתו) with it on Passover” (Challah 1:8). “One who sleeps under a bed in the sukkah has not fulfilled his obligation” (Sukkah 2:1). “A deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor do not discharge the many of their obligation (ידי חובתן); this is the rule: whoever is not obligated in a thing does not discharge the many of their obligation” (Rosh Hashanah 3:8). “One who says: Behold, I take upon myself a meal offering in a pan, and brought one in a deep pan etc. — what he brought, he brought, but he has not fulfilled his obligation” (Menachot 12:2). “Even if you make for them (the workers) a meal like Solomon's in his time, you have not fulfilled your obligation toward them” (Bava Metzia 7:1). “Women, slaves and minors do not discharge the many of their obligation” (Tosefta Berakhot 5:15). “One who reads before this has not fulfilled his obligation. If so, why do they read it in the synagogue? Rabbi Yose said: They do not read it in the synagogue in order to fulfil one's obligation, but in order to stand in prayer out of a word of Torah” (Jerusalem Talmud ibid. 1, 2a). “Abbahu said to him: My son, if you interrupt for the length of time needed to read all of it, you have not fulfilled your obligation” (ibid. 2, 4b). “For all the commandments from which a person is exempt, a person discharges the many of their obligation, except for the Grace after Meals” (ibid. 3, 6b). “And whoever does not say ‘covenant’ and ‘Torah’ in the blessing of the land, and ‘the kingdom of the house of David’ in ‘who builds Jerusalem’, has not fulfilled his obligation” (Babylonian Talmud ibid. 49a). “I might think a person fulfils his obligation with second tithe in Jerusalem” (Pesachim 36a). “Whoever does not mention in the Grace after Meals, in ‘for the land and for the food’, ‘a desirable land’ and ‘covenant’ and ‘Torah’ and ‘life’, has not fulfilled his obligation” (Numbers Rabbah 23). — And יצא יְדֵי קרעו: did the duty that he was obliged to rend: “Whoever said: he has fulfilled his rending (יצא ידי קירעו), since he rent for a living person” (Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3, 83c). “A relative of his died, and he thought it was his father and rent, and afterwards it was found to be his son — he has fulfilled the rending (יצא ידי קריעה)” (Nedarim 87a). — ידי חרות, ידי יין: did his duty to show himself a free man; did his duty to drink wine: “If he drank them (the four cups) undiluted, he has fulfilled. Rava said: He has fulfilled the duty of wine (ידי יין); the duty of four cups he has not fulfilled” (Pesachim 108b). — And ידי שבועה: “You are acting craftily with the oath; if so, you have not fulfilled the oath (ידי שבועה)” (Leviticus Rabbah 9). — יצא יְדֵי both of them: did the will of both of them: “Two people come before you in judgment, a Jew and an adversary and enemy — can you satisfy both of them (לצאת ידי שניהם)? Only that you exalt this one and hang that one” (Esther Rabbah, והשתיה כדת). — And יצא יָדָיו from so-and-so in this sense: “Like a king who made a feast seven days and invited all the people of the province during the seven days of the banquet; when the seven days of the banquet had passed, he said to his friend: We have already done our duty (יצאנו ידינו) by all the people of the province; you and I will make do with whatever is found, a litra of meat or of fish or of vegetables” (Numbers Rabbah 21). — *And עָלָה יְדֵי a thing, like יצא: “One who immerses vessels on Shabbat, whether unwittingly or deliberately — they have achieved immersion (עלו ידי טבילה)” (Tosefta Terumot 4:1). — *יָדוֹ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה (his hand is uppermost): he is in the right, the power and authority are his; יָדוֹ עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה (his hand is lowermost): he is not in the right, the power and the right belong to another: “Whoever has the money in his hand, his hand is uppermost” (Bava Metzia 4:2). “Whoever takes it upon himself — his hand is uppermost; if he wishes, he says to him: Give me my money, or give me that which you have defrauded me of” (ibid. 4). “Whoever has the produce in his hand, his hand is uppermost” (Shevu'ot 7:6). “One who hires craftsmen and they retracted — their hand is lowermost; if the householder retracted, his hand is lowermost; and whoever retracts, his hand is lowermost” (Bava Metzia 6:2). — And ידו לעליונה, לתחתונה: “There is none who enters with permission whose hand is uppermost (וידו לעליונה) except Reuben” (Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 5, 46d). “The hand of the documents is uppermost” (ibid. Bava Batra 9, 17a). “There is none who enters with permission whose hand is lowermost except Simeon” (ibid. Gittin 5, 46d). “The hand of the holder of the document is lowermost” (ibid. Bava Batra 9, 17a). — *מִיַּד: did such and such a thing מִיַּד, did the thing quickly, at that very moment, German sofort, French tout de suite, immédiatment, English at once, -diately: “They do not put flour into the charoset or into the mustard; and if he put it in, he should eat it at once (מיד); and Rabbi Meir forbids” (Pesachim 2:8). “A knife that was found on the fourteenth — he slaughters with it at once; on the thirteenth, he repeats the immersion etc.; if the fourteenth fell on Shabbat, he slaughters with it at once; on the fifteenth, he slaughters with it at once” (Shekalim 8:3). “A curtain that became unclean through a derivative uncleanness — they immerse it inside and bring it in at once” (ibid. 4). “Ammonites and Moabites are forbidden, and their prohibition is everlasting; but their females are permitted at once” (Yevamot 8:3). “Rabbi Judah says: They do not delay the judgment of this one, but they put him to death at once, and they write and send messengers to all the places” (Sanhedrin 11:4). “Two logs which I shall in future set apart, behold, they are terumah etc. — and he deconsecrates and drinks at once” (Tosefta Demai 8:7). “The matter is like the dye that they used to put at the side of the lintel: as soon as the sun came out and the dye entered, at once this is a fixed period” (ibid. Niddah 3:5). “If the creeping thing is in a person's hand, even if he immerses in the waters of Siloam or in the waters of Creation, he has no purification forever; if he threw it from his hand, at once he is clean” (Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 6, 33a). “At once everyone whose Passover offering was a lamb stuck it (the knife) in its fleece” (ibid.). “There is a certain man who came up from Babylon, and his name is Hillel the Babylonian etc. At once they seated him at the head and appointed him Nasi over them” (Babylonian Talmud ibid. 66a). “Solomon said twenty-four songs of praise and was not answered etc. As soon as he said: ‘O Lord God, turn not away the face of Your anointed; remember the mercies of David Your servant’, at once he was answered” (Moed Katan 9a). “They do not say: Let us wait until witnesses come; rather they permit her at once” (Ketubot 23a). “One who rents a house from a gentile or from a Cuthean affixes a mezuzah at once” (Tractate Mezuzah 2). “Like milk that was placed in a bowl etc.; as soon as one drop of its rennet goes down into it, at once it congeals and stands” (Genesis Rabbah 4). “The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him (to Titus): Wicked one, by your life, with a creature that is the least of all the creatures I have created since the six days of Creation, with it I will punish that wicked one. At once the Holy One, blessed be He, signalled to the prince of the sea, and it stood still from its raging etc.; and a gnat entered his nose” (ibid. 10). “When Moses saw this, he did not know what to do etc.; at once the divine word leapt upon Moses and instructed him what to do” (ibid. Numbers 4). “He (the Holy One, blessed be He, to Moses) said to him: Take hold of the throne of My glory and give them an answer. At once he was strengthened and gave an answer to the ministering angels” (Pesikta Rabbati 20). — כְּיַד so-and-so: according to his power and ability; כְּיַד המלך, according to the power and generosity of the king: “And King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asked, besides that which he gave her according to the bounty (כְּיַד) of King Solomon” (1 Kings 10:13). “And royal wine in abundance, according to the bounty (כְּיַד) of the king” (Esther 1:7). “And he made a release to the provinces, and gave gifts according to the bounty (כְּיַד) of the king” (ibid. 2:18). — לְיַד so-and-so: beside him, at his side: “And I will go out and stand beside (לְיַד) my father in the field where you are” (1 Samuel 19:3). “And he shall not buy vegetables of the field and sell them in the market; but he gathers and his son sells beside him (על ידו)” (Shevi'it 7:3). — And also of things that are not living creatures: “And the king stood by the side (אל יַד) of the gate, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands” (2 Samuel 18:4). “On the top of high places by the way, where the paths meet, she stands; beside (לְיַד) the gates, at the entry of the city” (Proverbs 8:2–3). “The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside (לְיַד מעגל)” (Psalms 140:6). — יש לאל יָדוֹ, see אֵל. — אין יָדַיִם לדבר: there is no substance in it: “Shall the clay say to him that fashioned it: What are you making? Or your work: He has no hands (יָדַיִם)?” (Isaiah 45:9). — He had no hands (לא היה לו יָדַיִם) to do a thing: he had no strength, no possibility: “And when the men of Ai looked behind them, they saw, and behold, the smoke of the city ascended up to heaven, and they had no power (יָדַיִם) to flee this way or that way” (Joshua 8:20). — שָׂם יָדַיִם לפלוני: gave him the strength and possibility to do a thing: “And they made way for her (Athaliah) (וישמו לה יָדַיִם), and she went by the way of the horses' entry to the king's house” (2 Kings 11:16). — And in combination with certain verbs, with differing meanings: נטה, הטה ידו על, with intent to do a deed of power and might, especially to strike him: “Stretch out your hand (יָדְךָ) with your rod over the rivers etc. And Aaron stretched out his hand (יָדוֹ) over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up” (Exodus 8:1–2). “And the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I stretch forth My hand (יָדִי) upon Egypt” (ibid. 7:5). “Therefore is the anger of the Lord kindled against His people, and He has stretched forth His hand (יָדוֹ) against them and has smitten them” (Isaiah 5:25). — יַד נטויה: ready and prepared to do a thing, to strike: “For all this His anger is not turned away, but His hand (יָדוֹ) is stretched out still” (Isaiah 5:25). — “And this is the hand (הַיָּד) that is stretched out; and who shall turn it back?” (ibid. 14:26–27), and see the entry נטה. — נָשָׂא יָדוֹ, for an oath: “And I will bring you into the land concerning which I lifted up My hand (יָדִי) to give it to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob” (Exodus 6:8). “For I lift up My hand (יָדִי) to heaven, and say: As I live forever” (Deuteronomy 32:40). And see נשא. — And נשא ידו ב so-and-so: rebelled against him: “A man of the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, has lifted up his hand (יָדוֹ) against the king, against David” (2 Samuel 20:21). — הניע יָדוֹ, with intent of mockery and contempt: “This is the joyous city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart: I am, and there is none else beside me; how is she become a desolation, a place for beasts to lie down in! Everyone that passes by her shall hiss and wag his hand (יָדוֹ)” (Zephaniah 2:15). — נֹפֵף יָדוֹ, with a plotting intent of war and destruction and the like: “This very day shall he halt at Nob; he shakes his hand (יָדוֹ) at the mount of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem” (Isaiah 10:32). — And Ben Sira said: “And even if the enemy sheds tears with his eyes, if he finds an occasion he will not be sated with blood; if evil befalls you etc., he will shake his head and wave his hand (והניף ידו)” (Ben Sira, Genizah, 12:16–18). — *נפנף בידיו, see נפנף. — *נפח בידו, as a sign of nullity, that the thing has no permanence, see נפח. — פָּרַשׂ יָדוֹ to rob a thing: “The adversary has spread out his hand (יָדוֹ) upon all her pleasant things” (Lamentations 1:10). — פרשׂ ידיו in entreaty and the like: “I have spread out My hands (יָדַי) all the day to a rebellious people, that walk in a way that is not good” (Isaiah 65:2). “I spread forth my hands (יָדַי) to You; my soul thirsts after You as a weary land” (Psalms 143:6). — And פרש בידיו, because of weeping and mourning: “Zion spreads forth her hands (בְּיָדֶיהָ); there is none to comfort her” (Lamentations 1:17). — שָׂם יָדוֹ of so-and-so on a thing: gave him dominion and power over the thing: “I have found David My servant; with My holy oil have I anointed him etc. And I will beat to pieces his adversaries before him, and smite them that hate him etc. I will set his hand (יָדוֹ) also on the sea, and his right hand on the rivers” (Psalms 89:21–26). — And שָׁת יָדוֹ על so-and-so, to compel him to one of the things: “There is no arbiter between us, that might lay his hand (יָדוֹ) upon us both” (Job 9:33). — הוֹדִיעוֹ את יָדוֹ: his power and ability: “This once will I cause them to know My hand (יָדִי) and My might” (Jeremiah 16:21). “And the hand (יַד) of the Lord shall be known toward His servants, and He will have indignation against His enemies” (Isaiah 66:14). — ארץ ממשלת יָדוֹ, over which he rules: “And all his army, and all the kingdoms of the land of his dominion (ממשת יָדוֹ), and all the peoples, fought against Jerusalem” (Jeremiah 34:1). — יָצְאָה יָדוֹ ב so-and-so: struck him, punished him and the like: “Nay, my daughters, for it grieves me much for your sakes, for the hand (יַד) of the Lord is gone forth against me” (Ruth 1:13). — And כָבְדָה יָדוֹ על so-and-so in this sense: “For there was a deadly discomfiture throughout all the city; the hand (יַד) of God was very heavy there” (1 Samuel 5:11). “And the hand (יָד) of the Lord was heavy upon the people of Ashdod, and He destroyed them and smote them with emerods” (ibid. 6). — And נחתה יָדוֹ על so-and-so: “For Your arrows are gone deep into me, and Your hand (יָדֶךָ) presses me sore” (Psalms 35:3). — הִרְפָּה יָדוֹ ממנו: ceased to punish him: “And He (God) said to the angel that destroyed the people: It is enough; now stay your hand (יָדֶךָ)” (2 Samuel 24:16). — אֶבֶן יַד: a small stone that one holds in the hand: “And if he smote him with a stone in the hand (אבן יָד), whereby a man may die, and he died, he is a murderer” (Numbers 35:17). “And they shall make fires of the weapons and burn them, both the shields and the bucklers, the bows and the arrows, and the handstaves (ובמקל יָד) and the spears” (Ezekiel 39:9). “One who slaughters with a hand sickle (במגל יד) etc., except for a harvest sickle” (Chullin 1:2). — באפס יָד: without force, suddenly: “He shall also stand up against the prince of princes; but he shall be broken without hand (באפס יָד)” (Daniel 8:25). — מָצָא חַיַּת יָדוֹ: found his livelihood: “You were wearied with the length of your way, yet you did not say: It is hopeless; you found the life (חית [Note: See the entry ד. חַיָּה, note 1.]) of your hand (יָדֵךְ [Note: So is the Masoretic reading, and most of the commentators explained ידך here in the sense of your body, yourself, and the like. But the phrase does not fit well; however, the literature has already used the expression חית ידו in the sense of his livelihood, his sustenance.]), therefore you were not faint” (Isaiah 57:10). — רְחַב יָדַיִם: wide, also of things that are not living creatures, ארץ רחבת יָדַיִם (a land wide on both hands): “Let them dwell in the land and trade therein; for, behold, the land is large enough (רחבת יָדַיִם) for them” (Genesis 34:21). “When you go, you shall come to a people secure, and the land is large (רחבת יָדַיִם), for God has given it into your hand” (Judges 18:10). “He will violently turn and toss you like a ball into a large (רחבת יָדַיִם) country; there shall you die” (Isaiah 22:18). “And they found fat pasture and good, and the land was wide (רחבת יָדַיִם) and quiet and peaceable” (1 Chronicles 4:40). “A place of broad (רחבי יָדָיִם) rivers and streams, wherein shall go no galley with oars” (Isaiah 33:21). “Yonder sea, great and wide (רחב יָדַיִם), wherein are creeping things innumerable” (Psalms 104:25). — *יָד רְחָָבָה: generous; and יָד מעוטה: stingy: “A poor man whose hand is wide (וידו רחבה) — concerning him I read: ‘Every man shall give as he is able (כמתנת ידו)’; a rich man whose hand is scanty (וידו מעוטה) — concerning him I read: ‘According to the blessing of the Lord your God which He has given you’” (Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 1, 76c). “And there was a certain man there, and he was called Abba Yudan, and he was accustomed to give to our Rabbis with a wide hand (ביד רחבה)” (Deuteronomy Rabbah 4). — °רְחַב הַיָּד: generous: “Ask of God, whose hand fills the hands of the open-handed (רחבי יד) and the short-handed (קצרי יד)” (Rabbi Samuel HaNagid 2:52). — קָפַץ את יָדוֹ from so-and-so: refrained from giving a thing to so-and-so the poor man: “You shall not harden your heart, nor shut your hand (יָדְךָ) from your needy brother” (Deuteronomy 15:7). — And the rhetorician said: “When God is angry with the community He gives wealth to the base and to the tight-fisted (ולקופצי ידים); and when He loves them He gives wealth to the generous and the good among them” (Rabbi Judah al-Harizi, Tachkemoni 44), and see the entry קפץ. — And likewise °קְבִיצַת הַיָּד, see the entry קביצה. — And likewise °יָדוֹ סגורה (his hand is closed): “And I made, for the man whose hand is closed (ידו סגורה), and with whom his generosity is stored up: Your hand is closed to every asker, a virgin whom no man has known” (Rabbi Judah al-Harizi, Tachkemoni 50). “For he is haughty of eyes, short of temper, unclean of lips, closed of hands (סגור ידים), crooked of ways” (ibid. 46). — °עַנְוַת יַד: generosity: “And this humility will not be complete until there cleaves to it humility of the hand (ענות היד), which is generosity” (Moznei Tzedek, al-Ghazali 146). — מָצָא את יָדָיו: succeeded and was able to stand and endure and do a thing: “The stout-hearted are bereft of sense, they sleep their sleep, and none of the men of might have found their hands (יְדֵיהֶם)” (Psalms 76:6). — And succeeded in understanding the thing, clarifying the thing, and the like: “Rabbi Judah son of Rabbi Simon said: How shall the expounder find his hands (ימצא … ידיו) between his numbered ones and their numbered ones? If his numbered ones, why their numbered ones?” (Numbers Rabbah 7). — °And מצא ידיו ורגליו (found his hands and feet): “How shall we find our hands and our feet (ידינו ורגלינו) in all the conditions of people with one another?” (Sefer HaChinukh, commandment 343). “And we did not find our hands and our feet in understanding it” (Pitchei Chokhmah of Ramchal 2). — גמול יָדוֹ: the recompense of his deeds: “A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth, and the recompense of a man's hands (יְדֵי) shall be rendered to him” (Proverbs 12:14). — סמך יָדוֹ, תמך בְּיָדוֹ, see סמך, תמך. — *יָדוֹ שֹׁלֶטֶת in such a place: he can touch such a place with his hand: “If one of them recognized some of his stones, he takes them and they are counted to his account. Rabbi Hoshaiah said: This says that the hand reaches (ששולטת היד) from one side” (Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 10, 12c). “My fathers stored away in a place where the hand reaches (שהיד שולטת)” (Bava Batra 11a). — *יָדָיו מונחות לו בין עיניו (his hands placed between his eyes): he does nothing with them: “They said to Rabbi Judah: If her hands were placed on her eyes all through twilight, you speak well” (Niddah 68b). — °יש יָד of so-and-so in a thing: he has a share in it: “Any merchandise in which there is the hand of an idolater in between etc.” (Rabbenu Gershom Me'or HaGolah, Bekhorot 13a). — And in the sense of °he meddles in the thing, deals with it: customary in speech. — *לאחר ידו, did a thing לאחר ידו (with the back of his hand), see אַחֵר. — *בית יד, see בַּיִת. — °So-and-so has a long hand (יָד ארוכה): he is a thief; customary in speech. — °מלאכת יד (handiwork), in medicine: an operation that the physician performs to heal a defective limb: “Healing of every wound and bruise and fresh sore by its four known operations in handiwork (במלאכת היד)” (Imrot Tehorot, חקו"ד 5:8). — °יַד אחת: they made one hand (עשו יד אחת), they agreed among themselves to be of one mind in the matter; customary in speech. — תשומת יד, see תשומת. — כתב-יד, see כתב. — And a proverb, °two hands (יָדוֹת) wash one another: “To do good to one another, like two hands washing one another; and such a love is called a good love” (Rabbi Judah of Modena, Tzemach Tzaddik 4). — b) Figuratively, any projecting thing, or one that serves for grasping, somewhat like a hand; plural יָדוֹת, יְדוֹתָיו: “Two tenons (יָדוֹת) in one board” (Exodus 26:17). “Two sockets under one board for its two tenons (יְדֹתָיו)” (ibid. 19). — And the poet said figuratively: “And the age put on garments of terror; and the knots of the בין for their song they set up, and in their heart sockets and tenons (וידות) for it; and they were unique among the people of God, and so their figures of speech were unique” (Rabbi Judah al-Harizi, Tachkemoni 18). — And יָדות of a chair: a kind of arm-rests on both sides of the chair: “The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne was round behind, and there were arms (וְיָדֹת) on either side by the place of the seat, and two lions stood beside the arms (הַיָּדוֹת)” (1 Kings 10:19). — And in a wheel, like an axle: “And the four wheels were underneath the borders, and the axletrees (וִידות [Note: See in the note to the entry גב and in the note to the entry חשוק וחשור the opinions of the commentators on each of the parts of the wheel mentioned in these verses. And the literature has already used the noun ידות in this sense.]) of the wheels were in the base etc.; and the work of the wheels was like the work of a chariot wheel: their axletrees (יְדוֹתָם), and their felloes, and their spokes, and their naves were all molten” (1 Kings 7:32–33). — And the writers used it in this sense: “And for this the wheels had hands (ידים) like the tenons (ידות) of the boards, on which the wheel turns at the time of going” (Rabbi Simeon ben Tzemach Duran, Magen Avot, the part שוסינו 3). — And the rhetorician said: “Therefore the composers of parables say: Wheels revolve upon their axletrees (ידותם), and wisdom and folly among men according to their peoples” (אסף 2, 4:9). — And the poet said: “A laden wagon sank in the mire up to the axles (ידות) of its wheels, and the wagon-owner's soul was impatient, for the disaster befell him in a place where the footsteps of man were not known” (Judah Leib Gordon, Meshalim 3:15). — And in the base (מכונה): “And on the top of the base was there a round compass half a cubit high; and on the top of the base its stays (יְדֹתֶיהָ [Note: It has not been clarified which part of the base is meant by the noun ידות.]) and its borders were of the same. And on the plates of its stays (יְדֹתֶיהָ) and on its borders he graved cherubim, lions and palm trees” (1 Kings 7:35–36). And it is common in the Talmud and Midrash in this sense, especially the handle (יד) of a vessel, the haft by which one holds it, German Griff, French manche, English handle: “King Monobaz made all the handles (ידות) of the vessels of the Day of Atonement of gold” (Yoma 3:10). “Every day its (the firepan's) handle (ידה) was short, and on this day long” (ibid. 4:4). “The handle (יד) of the axe, three fingerbreadths behind it” (Kelim 29:4). “All the handles of vessels which he inserted not in their usual manner” (Mikva'ot 10:1). “Its (the strap's) handle (ידה) was a handbreadth and its breadth a handbreadth” (Makkot 3:13). “A stick which he made into a handle (יד) for an axe” (Shabbat 48b). “He too made the stands of vessels and the rims of vessels and the handles of vessels and the handles of knives for the Day of Atonement of gold” (Yoma 36b). “All those seven years they kindled the handles of swords and the handles of spears and the handles of knives” (Leviticus Rabbah 11). — *And the יַד of a fruit: its stalk: “Whatever is a handle (יד) and not a protector becomes unclean and conveys uncleanness” (Uktzin 1:1). “The handles (ידות) of foods are like the foods” (Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 2, 14b). “They do not cover with foods etc.; Rabbi Judah says: whatever has a stalk or a handle (יד) is permitted” (Tractate Sefer Torah 3:12). — And figuratively, יַד לקרבן, יַד לשבועה, יַד לנדרים (a “handle” to a sacrifice, to an oath, to vows), and the like: not an explicit vow nor an explicit oath, but an allusion and a form of speech close to the language of a vow and an oath: “‘That I eat of yours’, ‘that I taste of yours’ — Rabbi Eleazar in the name of Rabbi Hoshaiah: they hold him to it on account of a handle (יד) to a sacrifice etc.; if he said ‘I will not eat of yours’, they hold him to it on account of a handle to an oath” (Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 1, 36d). “All handles of vows (ידות נדרים) are like vows, and all substitutes for vows are like vows. And these are handles: one who says to his fellow; and these are substitutes: קונם, קונח, קונס” (Babylonian Talmud ibid. 3a). “To make substitutes for naziriteship like naziriteship, and handles of naziriteship like naziriteship” (ibid.). “‘Behold, this is forbidden to me’ — because it is a handle to a sacrifice” (ibid. 6a). “Is there a handle for betrothal (יש יד לקידושין) [Note: And they said there: “How is this case? If you say that he said to a woman: Behold, you are betrothed to me, and said to her fellow: And you too — that is obvious, that is the betrothal itself. Rather, for example, where he said to a woman: Behold, you are betrothed to me, and said to her fellow: And you (ואת). Do we say that he said to her fellow ‘and you too’, and the betrothal takes effect on her fellow; or perhaps he said to her fellow ‘and you, look on’, and the betrothal does not take effect on her fellow?”] or not?” (ibid. b). “Is there a handle for pe'ah (יש יד לפיאה) [Note: And they said there: “How is this case? If you say that he said: This furrow shall be pe'ah, and this one too — that is proper pe'ah. Where it is a question for him is, for example, where he said ‘and this one’ and did not say ‘too’.”] or is there no handle for pe'ah etc.? Just as sacrifices have a handle, so pe'ah has a handle” (ibid.). “Is there a handle for charity (יש יד לצדקה) [Note: And they said there: “How is this case? If you say that he said: This zuz is for charity, and this one too — that is charity itself. Rather, for example, where he said ‘this one’ and did not say ‘too’.”] or is there no handle for charity?” (ibid. 7a). “Is there a handle for a privy (יש יד לבית הכסא) [Note: And they said there: “How is this case? If you say that he said: This house shall be a privy, and this one too — that too is a privy. Rather, for example, where he said ‘and this one’ and did not say ‘too’.”] or not?” (ibid.). — *ידים מוכיחות (handles that demonstrate): “Handles that do not demonstrate — are they handles?” (Kiddushin 5b, Gittin 85b, Nedarim 6b, Nazir 2b). — And they used the expression °ידים מוכיחות in the sense of clear proofs: “And there is none whose mark is more recognizable than this case, from several pretexts and clear estimations and demonstrating evidence (וידים מוכיחות), for it is revealed and known to all that this money was not repaid” (Tur Choshen Mishpat 65:21, in the name of the Rosh). “And likewise in this case there are several reasons and demonstrating evidence (וידים מוכיחות)” (ibid.). — c) a memorial monument [Note: One may conjecture that these monuments were at first perhaps more or less in the shape of a hand.], German Denkmal, French monument, English monument: “Saul came to Carmel, and behold, he is setting him up a monument (יָד)” (1 Samuel 15:12). “Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself the pillar which is in the king's dale; for he said: I have no son to keep my name in remembrance; and he called the pillar after his own name, and it is called Absalom's monument (יַד) to this day” (2 Samuel 18:18). “Even to them will I give in My house and within My walls a monument (יָד) and a name better than sons and daughters” (Isaiah 56:5). — d) place, German Ort, French place, English place: “You shall have a place (וְיָד) also outside the camp, whither you shall go forth abroad” (Deuteronomy 23:13). “As they encamp, so shall they set forward, every man in his place (יָדוֹ), by their standards” (Numbers 2:17). “And behind the doors and the doorpost have you set up your memorial etc.; you loved their bed; you saw a place (יָד [Note: So most of the commentators, in the sense of place, meaning: in every place that you saw. But some commentators explain this יד in the sense of a euphemism for the male member, like אמה in the Talmud.])” (Isaiah 57:8). “Shepherds with their flocks shall come to her; they shall pitch their tents against her round about; they shall feed every one in his place (יָדוֹ)” (Jeremiah 6:3). “And choose a place (וְיָד [Note: ראי"ס holds that the reading is corrupt, and they emend: ויד בראש דרך תשים etc.]), choose it at the head of the way to the city. Appoint a way, that the sword may come” (Ezekiel 21:24–25). — And על-יד in the sense of in the vicinity of a place: “From Ekron even to the sea, all that lay near (על-יַד) Ashdod, with their villages” (Joshua 16:46). “From the north end, beside (אל-יַד) the way of Hethlon to the entrance of Hamath, Hazar-enan at the border of Damascus, northward beside (אל-יַד) Hamath” (Ezekiel 48:1). “They have spread a net by the wayside (לְיַד מעגל); they have set snares for me” (Psalms 140:6). “On the top of high places by the way, where the paths meet, she stands; beside (לְיַד) the gates, at the entry of the city” (Proverbs 8:2–3). — יַד הנהר and the like: the bank of the river: “And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe in the river, and her maidens walked along by the river's side (על-יַד היאר)” (Exodus 2:5). “And the Canaanites dwell by the sea and along by the side (על יַד) of the Jordan” (Numbers 13:29). “By the river (על-יַד נהר) Euphrates have they stumbled and fallen” (Jeremiah 46:6). “As I was by the side (על-יַד) of the great river, which is Hiddekel” (Daniel 10:4). — e) יַד, plural יָדוֹת: a part, a share of produce and the like: “And it shall come to pass at the ingatherings that you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four parts (הַיָּדֹת) shall be your own, for seed of the field and for your food” (Genesis 47:24). “And you shall keep the watch of the house, that it be not broken down; and the two companies (הַיָּדוֹת) of you, even all that go forth on the Sabbath, shall keep the watch of the house of the Lord” (2 Kings 11:6–7). “And the rest of the people cast lots, to bring one of ten to dwell in Jerusalem the holy city, and nine parts (הַיָּדוֹת) in the other cities” (Nehemiah 11:1). — And in the Talmud and Midrash: “Rabbi Simeon says: two parts (ידות) of a loaf, of three to a kav” (Eruvin 8:2). “And he made the molten sea, ten cubits etc. If you say it was round, you find that it held one hundred and sixty parts (ידות) of purification; if you say it was square, you find that it held one hundred and twenty-two parts of purification” (Jerusalem Talmud ibid. 1, 19a). “He went round the heart of the sea etc.; it floated two parts (ידות) above” (Avot deRabbi Natan, version 2, 38). And in סהמ"א: “Reckon what you lose now against the reward that you receive against it, a thousand parts (ידות) in the World to Come” (Machzor Vitry 425). “And it became a wall for Israel on this side and on that, and the two parts (הידות) congealed” (Chizkuni, Beshallach 14:21). — So-and-so many יָדוֹת: so-and-so many times: “And Benjamin's portion was five times (יָדוֹת) as much as any of theirs” (Genesis 43:34). “And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said: We have ten parts (יָדוֹת) in the king” (2 Samuel 19:44). “And in every matter of wisdom and understanding concerning which the king inquired of them, he found them ten times (יָדוֹת) better than all the magicians and enchanters that were in all his realm” (Daniel 1:20). — And in medieval literature (בסה"מ): “It turns out that ‘the dust of Jacob’ is the little ones, who are many times (ידות) more numerous than the grown-ups; and if the grown-ups sinned, the little ones did not sin; therefore he does not desire to curse them” (Chizkuni, Balak 23:10). — *And parts of the day: “They would walk the whole day only two parts (ידות) of the day” (Tosefta Bikkurim 2:8). — And parts of the month: “And how much is the greater part of the month? Sixteen days. Rabbi Judah says: two parts (ידות) of the month; and how much are two parts of the month? Twenty days” (Eruvin 13a). — *And parts of the hour: “All the stars and constellations and the two luminaries were created at the beginning of the night of the fourth day, and none preceded the other except by two parts (ידות) of an hour” (Pirkei deRabbi Eliezer 7). “And the days of the lunar month are twenty-nine days and a half and two parts (ידות) of an hour and seventy-three portions” (ibid.). “Whoever wishes to know the place of the moon should reckon the years of the world, make them into months, and give each month twenty-nine and a half days and two parts (ידות) of an hour, which are 720 portions” (Ibn Ezra, Exodus 12:2). “You must remove nearly one of the thirteen parts (ידות) of the seventy-three portions, and seventy-two portions remain, for the day keeps growing over its fellow from the season of Tevet to the season of Tammuz” (Chizkuni, Vayishlach 32:32). — And the liturgical poet said: “To make known that they are likened only to one day of the days of the Creator of the mountains, except two parts (ידות) of an hour in measure; when the sun inclines in the west two parts of an hour, dimming the lights — so before evening comes, light will spring up for the upright” (Yotzer for the second day of Rosh Hashanah, אשר מי יעשה). — °יָדוֹת of a mile: “And each degree of them on the earth is sixty-six miles and two parts (ידות) of a mile” (Letter of Rabbi Hasdai to the Khazar). — °יד יד: part by part: “The sage shall take from each house part by part (יד יד) of flour, and knead and bake it” (Halakhot Ketzuvot of Rabbi Yehudai Gaon, Laws of Eruvin). — °And a part of the army, of the host: “But Eleazar his son, the mighty one, and with him a great and very strong band (יד) of the chosen of the ruthless, did not weep” (Josippon 65). “And Nero sent Cestius, the Roman general who was stationed in Aram, and a mighty band (ויד רמה) of the Roman army with him” (ibid.). — *ידות דרכים, see יתדות דרכים. — °יַד של נְיָר: a fixed number of sheets of paper arranged and sold together (a quire): “And he told me his name, and that he had written for me a book of twenty-three quires (ידות) of paper and called it Pela'ot HaChokhmah, and further began to write for him a long commentary on each and every word, and on one leaf of paper of that book a commentary of two quires (ידות) of paper” (Responsa of the Rashba 548). “And a book was composed against him, called Teshuvat HaMinin, containing thirty quires (ידות) of paper” (Hitabkut, Rabbi Jacob Emden). “And he wrote and composed long and broad responsa in ten quires (ידות) of paper or more” (ibid., Megillat Sefer 4). — °יַד השם: the name of one of the remedies: “And also the remedy taken (for stones of the kidneys and the bladder) in the blood of the he-goat, which is called °יד השם (the hand of God) for its exaltedness” (Canon 3:18, 2:7).
[Note: The uses of יד are so many and so varied in kind that it is difficult to fix an exact place for each of them, and some of them belong to two or three sections equally.]
