—  עיר יֹצֵאת מאה, אלף, שכך וכך אנשים יוצאים ממנה למלחמה:  נפלה לא תוסיף קום בתולת ישראל נטשה על אדמתה אין מקימה כי כה אמר אדני יי' העיר הַיֹּצֵאת אלף תשאיר מאה וְהַיֹּצֵאת מאה תשאיר עשרה לבית ישראל עמו' ה ג-ד. —  יָצָא את הדבר, עשה מה שהיה ראוי לעשות בדבר:  טוב אשר תאחז בזה וגם מזה אל תנח ידך כי ירא אלהים יֵצֵא את כלם קהל' ז יח.]
en: transitive verb, יָצָאתָ, יָצָאתִי, and likewise יָצָתִי, יְצָאֻנִי, יְצָאתֶם, וִיְצָאתֶם, יָצְאָה, יָצְאוּ, יָצָאוּ, יֹצֵא, יוֹצֵא, יוֹצָא, יֹצְאִים, יוֹצְאִים, יֹצְאוֹת, יוֹצְאוֹת, יֵצֵא, וַיֵּצֵא, יֵצְאוּ, וַיֵּצְאוּ, יֵצֵאוּ, תֵּצֵאוּ, תֵּצֶאנָה, וַתֵּצֶאןָ, וַתֵּצֶאנָה, צֵא, צֵאָה, צְאוּ, צֵאוּ, צְאֶינָה, יָצֹא, יָצֹוא, צֵאת, לָצֵאת, צֵאתִי, בְּצֵאתִי, צֵאתְךָ, בְּצֵאתְךָ, צֵאתוֹ, צֵאתֵנוּ, צֵאתְכֶם, צֵאתָם, — יָצָא from a house, from a city, from a land and the like, went from inside the house and the like to the outside, German herausgehn; French sortir; English go to out: "Behold, a people has come out [יָצָא] of Egypt" (Numbers 22:5). "And Pharaoh's army had come out [יָצָא] of Egypt" (Jeremiah 37:5). "Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you, and the people shall go out [וְיָצָא] and gather" (Exodus 16:4). "And the priest shall go out [וְיָצָא] to outside the camp" (Leviticus 14:4). "And when she has departed [וְיָצְאָה] out of his house, she may go and become another man's" (Deuteronomy 24:2). "Shall I bring your son back to the land from which you came [יָצָאתָ]?" (Genesis 24:5). "If I go out [יָצָאתִי] into the field, then behold the slain with the sword! And if I enter the city, then behold those sick with famine" (Jeremiah 14:18). "Naked I came out [יָצָתִי] of my mother's womb" (Job 1:21). "Every creeping thing upon the earth, after their families, went out [יָצְאוּ] of the ark" (Genesis 8:19). "And it came to pass, about the time of the shutting of the gate, when it was dark, that the men went out [יָצָאוּ]; I do not know where they went" (Joshua 2:5). "Remember this day, on which you came out [יְצָאתֶם] of Egypt" (Exodus 13:3). "And come out [וִיְצָאתֶם] of the vineyards" (Judges 21:21). "Why did we come out [יָצָאנוּ] of Egypt?" (Numbers 11:20). "Behold, he goes out [יֹצֵא] to the water" (Exodus 7:15). "And the watchers saw a man coming out [יוֹצֵא] of the city" (Judges 1:24). "And when I go forth [יוֹצֵא], behold, the prince of Greece comes" (Daniel 10:20). "Behold, the people that came out [הַיֹּצֵא] of Egypt" (Numbers 22:11). "This day you go out [יֹצֵאִים] in the month of Aviv" (Exodus 13:4). "The sons of Noah who went out [הַיֹּצְאִים] of the ark" (Genesis 9:18). "Of all that went out [יֹצְאֵי] of the ark" (ibid. 10). "All who went out [יֹצְאֵי] of the gate of his city" (ibid. 34:24). "And behold, Rebekah came out [יֹצֵאת], who was born to Bethuel" (ibid. 24:15). "The maiden who comes out [הַיֹּצֵאת] to draw" (ibid. 43). "And toward her afterbirth that comes out [הַיּוֹצֵת] from between her feet" (Deuteronomy 28:57). "And the daughters of the men of the city are coming out [יֹצְאֹת] to draw water" (Genesis 24:13). "Then I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, two women coming out [יוֹצְאוֹת]" (Zechariah 5:9). "At evening time, at the time when the women who draw water go out [צֵאת]" (Genesis 24:11). "And it came to pass, when the priests came out [בְּצֵאת] of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of the Lord" (1 Kings 8:10). "And it came to pass, when Moses went out [כְּצֵאת] to the tent, that all the people would rise up" (Exodus 33:8). "In the third month after the children of Israel had gone forth [לְצֵאת] out of the land of Egypt" (ibid. 19:1). "And the king of Egypt came not again any more out [לָצֵאת] of his land" (2 Kings 24:7). "But if you refuse to go out [לָצֵאת], this is the word that the Lord has shown me" (Jeremiah 38:21). "It is because of that which the Lord did for me when I came forth [בְּצֵאתִי] out of Egypt" (Exodus 13:8). "When I went out [בְּצֵאתִי] to the gate through the city" (Job 29:7). "This our bread we took hot for our provision out of our houses on the day we came forth [צֵאתֵנוּ] to go to you" (Joshua 9:12). "At the season that you came forth [צֵאתְךָ] out of Egypt" (Deuteronomy 16:6). "Blessed shall you be when you come in, and blessed shall you be when you go out [בְּצֵאתֶךָ]" (ibid. 28:6). "Because they did not meet you with bread and with water on the way, when you came forth [בְּצֵאתְכֶם] out of Egypt" (ibid. 23:5). "And when Moses came to speak with him, he would take off the veil until he came out [צֵאתוֹ]" (Exodus 34:34). "And Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed [בְּצֵאתוֹ] from Haran" (Genesis 12:4). "When he goes into the holy place before the Lord, and when he comes out [וּבְצֵאתוֹ], that he not die" (Exodus 28:35). "All the men of war died in the wilderness when they came out [בְּצֵאתָם] of Egypt" (Joshua 5:4). "On the fifteenth day of the second month after their departing [לְצֵאתָם] out of the land of Egypt" (Exodus 16:1). "Go out [צֵא] of the ark, you and your wife" (Genesis 8:16). "Arise, go out [צֵא] into the plain" (Ezekiel 3:22). "And thus said Shimei when he cursed: Get out [צֵא], get out [צֵא], you man of blood" (2 Samuel 16:7). "And he (Gaal) said to Abimelech: Increase your army and come out [וָצֵאָה]" (Judges 9:29). "Up, get out [צְאוּ] of this place" (Genesis 19:14). "Rise up, get out [צְאוּ] from among my people" (Exodus 12:31). "Go forth [צְאוּ] from Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans, with a voice of singing" (Isaiah 48:20). "Make peace with me and come out [וּצְאוּ] to me" (ibid. 36:16). "Saying to the prisoners: Go forth [צֵאוּ]; to those who are in darkness: Show yourselves" (ibid. 49:9). "O fairest among women, go your way forth [צְאִי] by the footsteps of the flock" (Song of Songs 1:8). "Go forth [צְאֶינָה] and behold, O daughters of Zion, King Solomon" (ibid. 3:11). "And all these your servants shall come down to me and bow down to me, saying: Get out, you and all the people that follow you; and after that I will go out [אֵצֵא]" (Exodus 11:8). "And I will go out [אֵצֵא] and stand beside my father in the field" (1 Samuel 19:3). "Then I arose and went forth [וָאֵצֵא] into the plain" (Ezekiel 3:23). "And I went out [וָאֵצֵאָה] by night by the gate of the valley" (Nehemiah 2:13). "You shall go out [תֵּצֵא] one way against him" (Deuteronomy 28:25). "For now you shall go forth [תֵצְאִי] out of the city" (Micah 4:10). "Let no man go out [יֵצֵא] of his place on the seventh day" (Exodus 16:29). "And it shall be that whoever goes out [יֵצֵא] of the doors of your house into the street, his blood shall be upon his head" (Joshua 2:19). "And Noah went out [וַיֵּצֵא], and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him, etc., went out of the ark" (Genesis 8:18-19). "And if a man sells his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out [תֵצֵא] as the menservants go out" (Exodus 21:7). "And Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out [וַתֵּצֵא] to meet him" (Genesis 30:16). "And Dinah the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out [וַתֵּצֵא] to see the daughters of the land" (ibid. 34:1). "Come, my beloved, let us go forth [נֵצֵא] into the field" (Song of Songs 7:12). "And none of you shall go out [תֵצְאוּ] of the door of his house until the morning" (Exodus 12:22). "For you shall not go out [תֵּצֵאוּ] in haste, nor go by flight" (Isaiah 52:12). "They shall come out [יֵצְאוּ] against you one way" (Deuteronomy 28:7). "Your destroyers and those who made you waste shall go forth [יֵצֵאוּ] from you" (Isaiah 49:17). "And they went forth [וַיֵּצְאוּ] with them from Ur of the Chaldeans, to go into the land of Canaan" (Genesis 11:31). "They have broken through and passed the gate, and have gone out [וַיֵּצְאוּ] by it" (Micah 2:13). "And they took Dinah out of Shechem's house and went out [וַיֵּצְאוּ]" (Genesis 34:26). "And you shall go out [תֵּצֶאנָה] at the breaches, every woman straight before her" (Amos 4:3). "And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took the timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out [וַתֵּצֶאןָ] after her with timbrels and with dances" (Exodus 15:20). "When David returned from slaying the Philistine, the women came out [וַתֵּצֶאנָה] of all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet Saul" (1 Samuel 18:6). — And with את after it: "They had gone out [יָצְאוּ] of the city and were not yet far off" (Genesis 44:4), like יצאו מן. — And with a suffix, יְצָאוּנִי, they went out from me: "My children have gone forth from me [יְצָאוּנִי] and they are not" (Jeremiah 10:20). — And the poet said: "And they believed in You and adorned You, for only within them did they find You, and they clung to You and did not depart from You [יְצָאוּךָ], and on the wings of song they bore You" (Rabbi Moses ibn Ezra, Supplication for עי"ת, ממרום). "The narrator said: And when I came to the inner court, and saw the Shulammite lady, and she called me to her chamber, my soul almost went out of me [יצאתני], and my thoughts were confounded by what my eyes had seen" (Rabbi Judah al-Harizi, Iggeret Leshon ha-Zahav). — יָצָא before the people, went at its head, led it into war and the like: "And our king shall judge us and go out [וְיָצָא] before us and fight our battles" (1 Samuel 8:20). — יָצָא and came in before the people, was the leader of the people: "Let the Lord etc. appoint a man over the congregation, who shall go out [יֵצֵא] before them and who shall come in before them" (Numbers 27:16-17). "As my strength was then, so is my strength now, for war, and to go out [וְלָצֵאת] and to come in" (Joshua 14:11). — יָצָא with so-and-so, kept company with him: "It is good, my daughter, that you go out [תֵצְאִי] with his maidens" (Ruth 2:24). — יָצָא from with so-and-so: "And Moses went out [וַיֵּצֵא] from Pharaoh" (Exodus 8:26). — יָצָא from the presence of so-and-so: "Jacob had scarcely gone out [יָצֹא יָצָא] from the presence of Isaac his father" (Genesis 27:30). — יָצָא from before so-and-so: "And Joseph went out [וַיֵּצֵא] from before Pharaoh" (Genesis 41:46). יָצָא after so-and-so, to search for him, to pursue him: "And there came a lion and a bear and took a lamb out of the flock, and I went out [וְיָצָאתִי] after him and smote him and delivered it out of his mouth" (1 Samuel 17:34-35). "After whom has the king of Israel come out [יָצָא]? After whom do you pursue? After a dead dog" (ibid. 24:14). — יָצָא to meet so-and-so, went to greet him: "And Moses went out [וַיֵּצֵא] to meet his father-in-law, and bowed down and kissed him" (Exodus 18:7). "And when Balak heard that Balaam had come, he went out [וַיֵּצֵא] to meet him at the city of Moab" (Numbers 22:36). "And Jephthah came to Mizpah to his house, and behold, his daughter came out [יֹצֵאת] to meet him with timbrels and with dances" (Judges 11:34). "And Jael went out [וַתֵּצֵא] to meet Sisera and said to him: Turn in, my lord" (ibid. 4:18). "And Michal the daughter of Saul came out [וַתֵּצֵא] to meet David and said: How glorious was the king of Israel today" (2 Samuel 6:20). "Therefore I came out [יָצָאתִי] to meet you, diligently to seek your face, and I have found you" (Proverbs 7:15). — And with hostile intent, went to make war with him: "And Edom came out [וַיֵּצֵא] against him (against Israel) with much people and with a strong hand" (Numbers 20:20). "And Sihon gathered all his people together and went out [וַיֵּצֵא] against Israel into the wilderness" (ibid. 21:23). "And the children of Israel came near against the children of Benjamin on the second day, and Benjamin went forth [וַיֵּצֵא] against them out of Gibeah" (Judges 20:24-25). "And Israel went out [וַיֵּצֵא] against the Philistines to battle" (1 Samuel 4:1). — יָצָא חפשי, לחפשי, see חפש. — יָצָא from the loins of so-and-so, see חלץ. — יָצָא from the bowels of so-and-so, see מעי. — And likewise יָצָא יְרֵכוֹ, see יָרֵךְ. — יָצָא in the dance, began to dance and to leap: "Again you shall adorn yourself with your timbrels and shall go forth [וְיָצָאת] in the dances of those who make merry" (Jeremiah 31:3). — And of things that are not living creatures, יָצָא the sun, it rose: "The sun had risen [יָצָא] upon the earth" (Genesis 19:23). "So let all Your enemies perish, O Lord; but let those who love Him be as the sun when it goes forth [כְּצֵאת] in its might" (Judges 5:31). "The sun shall be darkened in its going forth [בְּצֵאתוֹ], and the moon shall not cause its light to shine" (Isaiah 13:10). "From the rising of the dawn until the stars came out [צֵאת]" (Nehemiah 4:15). "And the arrow went out [וַיֵּצֵא] at his heart" (2 Kings 9:24). — יָצְאָה fire, began to burn: "For a fire has gone out [יָצְאָה] of Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon" (Numbers 21:28). — And a plant, יָצָא from the earth, a plant sprouted: "From the cedar that is in Lebanon even to the hyssop that springs out [יֹצֵא] of the wall" (1 Kings 5:13). "And there shall come forth [וְיָצָא] a shoot out of the stock of Jesse, and a twig shall grow forth out of his roots" (Isaiah 11:1). — And a river, the river יצא from such-and-such a place, its source is there: "And a river went out [יֹצֵא] of Eden to water the garden" (Genesis 2:10). "And he (Moses) smote the rock with his rod twice, and much water came forth [וַיֵּצְאוּ]" (Numbers 20:11). "And it shall come to pass on that day that living waters shall go out [יֵצְאוּ] from Jerusalem" (Zechariah 14:8). — And the river יָצָא אֶל a place, its waters flow and enter into such-and-such a place: "These waters issue forth [יוֹצְאִים] toward the eastern region" (Ezekiel 47:8). — And a spring: "And all the brooks of Judah shall flow with waters, and a fountain shall come forth [יֵצֵא] from the house of the Lord and shall water the valley of Shittim" (Joel 4:18). — And ice: "Out of whose womb came [יצא] the ice? And the hoarfrost of heaven, who has given it birth?" (Job 38:29). — And the soul, יָצְאָה נפשו, see נפש. — And the spirit, see רוח. — And the breath, see נשמה. — And the hand, יָצְאָה בו the hand of so-and-so, so-and-so brought evil upon him: "For it grieves me much for your sakes that the hand of the Lord has gone out [יָצְאָה] against me" (Ruth 1:13). — the wine יָצָא from so-and-so, so-and-so became sober, he is no longer drunk as he was before: "And it came to pass in the morning, when the wine had gone out [בְּצֵאת] of Nabal, that his wife told him these things" (1 Samuel 25:37). — And also abstract things: "For wrath has gone out [יָצָא] from before the Lord" (Numbers 17:11). "Behold, a storm of the Lord, fury, has gone forth [יָצְאָה], a whirling storm" (Jeremiah 23:19). "Lest My fury go forth [תֵּצֵא] like fire and burn so that none can quench it" (ibid. 4:4). "He shall not break his word; he shall do according to all that proceeds [הַיֹּצֵא] out of his mouth" (Numbers 30:3). "Talk no more so exceedingly proudly; let not arrogance come [יֵצֵא] out of your mouth" (1 Samuel 2:3). "Like an error which proceeds [שֶׁיֹּצְאָה] [Note: In place of שיֹצְאָה.] from before the ruler" (Ecclesiastes 10:5). "Behold, evil goes forth [יֹצֵאת] from nation to nation" (Jeremiah 25:32). "For out of Zion shall go forth [תֵּצֵא] Torah" (Isaiah 2:3). יָצָא a thing from so-and-so, so-and-so is the source, so-and-so did the thing: "She may not eat of anything that comes [יֵצֵא] of the vine" (Judges 13:14). — And abstract things: "Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said: The thing proceeds [יָצָא] from the Lord" (Genesis 24:50). "This also comes forth [יָצָאָה] from the Lord of hosts, who is wonderful in counsel" (Isaiah 28:29). "For from the prophets of Jerusalem has ungodliness gone forth [יָצָאָה] into all the land" (Jeremiah 23:15). — And in the sense of ceased, was stopped: "And from the daughter of Zion all her splendor has departed [וַיֵּצֵא]" (Lamentations 1:6). "Cast out the scoffer, and contention will go out [וְיֵצֵא], and strife and disgrace will cease" (Proverbs 22:10). יָצָא judgment, was done, was made public, the verdict was given: "Therefore the law is slacked, and justice never goes forth [יֵצֵא]; for the wicked surrounds the righteous, therefore justice goes forth [יֵצֵא] perverted" (Habakkuk 1:4). "Let my judgment come forth [יֵצֵא] from Your presence; let Your eyes behold equity" (Psalms 17:2). — יָצְאָה the year and the like, it ended, reached its end: "And the feast of ingathering at the end [בְּצֵאת] of the year" (Exodus 23:16). — the border יָצָא to such-and-such a place, turned there, ended there: "And your border shall turn about from the south of the ascent of Akrabbim and pass along to Zin etc., and it shall go forth [וְיָצָא] to Hazar-addar and pass along to Azmon" (Numbers 34:4). "And the border was drawn from the top of the mountain to the fountain of the waters of Nephtoah, and went out [וְיָצָא] to the cities of Mount Ephron" (Joshua 15:9). "And the border went out [וְיָצָא] to the side of Ekron northward" (ibid. 11). — And money on a thing, was given as the price of a thing: "And to the masons and the hewers of stone, and to buy timber and hewn stone etc., and for all that was laid out [יֵצֵא] for the house to repair it" (2 Kings 12:13). — And in Talmud and Midrash in the same senses: "With what may a woman go out and with what may she not go out? A woman may not go out with threads of wool nor with threads of linen" (Shabbat 6:1). "A man may not go out with a nailed sandal" (ibid. 2). "The woman who goes out to be executed" (Arakhin 7a). — And the infinitive *לָצֵאת [Note: And not לִיצוֹא, as is the custom of נפ"י.]: "Because they were accustomed to go out in the morning, they said to him: Moses our teacher, let us go out in the morning" (Mekhilta Beshallach 4). "And he sought to go out to a wilderness, a waste and void with nothing in it" (ibid. "At that moment the mercies of the Holy One, blessed be He, were stirred, and a heavenly voice went out and said to him, to Hadarniel: Know that from your days you are men of strife" (Pesikta Rabbati 20). And see *בת-קול. — And a woman by a bill of divorce: "Any woman who went out from him by a bill of divorce is forbidden to return to him" (Yevamot 108b). — יָצָא the time, the year, the season, it ended and was finished: "Once the Sabbath had gone out, the darkness began to grow and come" (Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 8, 12b). "If part of the first period has gone out, they complete for it part of the sixth period" (ibid. Shabbat 9, 12a). "When the first, second and third rainy seasons have gone out and no rain has fallen" (Ta'anit 19a). "And that year had not gone out, and he had not repeated it a second or third time, before that man died" (Numbers Rabbah 4). — so-and-so יָצָא his year, his week, lived the whole year, the whole week: "It happened that a certain student gave a ruling before Rabbi Eliezer his master; he said to Imma Shalom his wife: He will not live out his week; and he did not live out his week before he died" (Jerusalem Talmud Shevi'it 6, 36c). — יָצָא to freedom, יצא בן חורין, see 2. חֹר, חֵרוּת. — יצא ידי חובתו, did what he was obliged to do, see *חובה, יד. — And וְיָצָא alone without the noun יד, in this sense: "If he was reading in the Torah and the time for the reading came, if he directed his heart, he has fulfilled his obligation [יצא]" (Berakhot 2:1). "One who recites the Shema and did not make it audible to his ear has fulfilled his obligation [יצא]; Rabbi Yose says: He has not fulfilled it. If he recited it and was not exact in its letters, Rabbi Yose says: He has fulfilled it; Rabbi Judah says: He has not fulfilled it. One who recites it out of order has not fulfilled his obligation" (ibid. 2:2). "One who reads the Megillah out of order has not fulfilled his obligation; if he read it by heart, if he read it in translation in any language, he has not fulfilled it, etc.; but a foreign speaker who heard it in the Assyrian script has fulfilled it" (Megillah 2:1). "If he read it with interruptions or while dozing, he has fulfilled it; if he was writing it, expounding it or correcting it, if he directed his heart he has fulfilled it, and if not, he has not fulfilled it" (ibid. 2). "With his own offering he fulfills his obligation, and he does not fulfill it with his father's offering" (Sifra Vayikra, Chovah 4:6). "Rabbi Johanan said: The Hallel, if he heard it in the synagogue, he has fulfilled his obligation" (Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 3, 47b). "The four cups of which they spoke — one fulfills one's obligation with them whether undiluted or diluted, provided they have the taste and appearance of wine. Rabbi Jeremiah said: It is a commandment to fulfill it with red wine" (ibid.). "A child who needs his mother goes out by his mother's eruv, and one who does not need his mother does not go out by his mother's eruv" (Eruvin 82a). "Rabbi Ila'i said: I asked Rabbi Eliezer: May a person fulfill his obligation with the loaves of a thanksgiving-offering and the wafers of a nazirite?" (Pesachim 38b). "If he drank them (the four cups) undiluted, he has fulfilled his obligation; if he drank them all at once, he has fulfilled it; if he gave his children and the members of his household to drink from them, he has fulfilled it" (ibid. 108b). "The hand tefillin — he writes it on one parchment, and if he wrote it on four parchments and placed them in one compartment, he has fulfilled his obligation" (Menachot 34b). — *יָצָא from the general rule, that which was previously included among other things and afterwards was stated explicitly by itself: "This seventh day was included in the general rule; it went out from the general rule to teach about the general rule" (Mekhilta Bo, Pischa 17). "The garment too was included in all these, and why did it go out? To compare to it" (Bava Metzia 2:5). "Jericho was included, and why did it go out? Because it was as hard as all of them together" (Sifre Deuteronomy 52). "Kindling went out for a purpose: to teach about courts" (Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7, 9c). "Because pruning went out to be stringent with itself" (ibid. 10a). "Because idolatry went out to be judged by itself" (Horayot 8a). "It has gone out of the category of a living creature, and has not come into the category of a dead one" (Chullin 121b). — יָצָא such-and-such a thing, except for such-and-such a thing, German ausgenommen; French excepté; English excluded: "Abba Saul says: (one who kills unintentionally goes into exile if he was engaged in an optional matter) just as chopping wood is optional, so is everything optional; excluded is the father who strikes his son and the teacher who chastises his student (that if the son or the student died, the father and the teacher are exempt)" (Makkot 2:2). "Just as your houses are in your possession, so your territory is in your possession; excluded is the leaven of an Israelite that is in the possession of a gentile, etc.; excluded is the leaven of a gentile that is in the possession of an Israelite" (Mekhilta Bo 10). "In its mother's milk (it is forbidden); excluded is fowl, which has no mother's milk; excluded is an impure animal" (ibid. Mishpatim 20). "Just as a forest is a place that the injured party and the injurer have permission to enter, so too any place that the injured party and the injurer have permission to enter (he is liable); excluded is the courtyard of a householder, which the injured party and the injurer have no permission to enter" (Sifre Deuteronomy 182). "Just as fledglings are something of use — excluded are dead ones, which are of no use — so eggs are something of use; excluded are addled eggs, which are of no use" (ibid. 228). "Of that which you have and he does not have, you are obliged to give; excluded is gleaning, in which your hand and his hand are equal" (Jerusalem Talmud Ma'aserot 1, 48c). "Anything that is detached; excluded is one who weeds among garlic and onions" (ibid. 2, 50a). "Anything whose growth is from the ground; excluded are one who milks, one who makes cheese and one who curdles" (ibid.). "One who is not fit to return to her father's house; excluded is this one, who is fit to return to her father's house" (ibid. Terumot ש, 44d). "And you shall guard the matzot — matzah that is guarded for the sake of matzah; excluded is this one, which is not guarded for the sake of matzah" (Pesachim 38b). "You shall do no manner of servile work; excluded are the blowing of the shofar and the removing of bread from the oven, which are a skill and not work" (Rosh Hashanah 29b). "Anything that is movable and whose substance is money; excluded is land, which is not movable; excluded are slaves, who were compared to land; excluded are documents, which, although they are movable, their substance is not money; excluded is consecrated property — 'his neighbor' is written" (Bava Kamma 62b). "One that is lost from him and found with every person; excluded is this one, which is lost from him and not found with every person" (Bava Metzia 22b). "Anything whose work has not been completed with respect to challah, a laborer may eat of it; excluded are one who kneads, one who shapes and one who bakes, whose work has been completed with respect to challah, [so that] a laborer may not eat of it" (ibid. 89a). "One who lacks nothing but burial; excluded is this one, who lacks cutting off and burial" (Sanhedrin 46b). "And they shall be one flesh — those who become one flesh; excluded are domestic and wild animals, which do not become one flesh" (ibid. 58a). "One which is not offered to the Lord at all; excluded is this one, which is not offered today but is offered tomorrow" (Menachot 101a). "One whose sinew is forbidden and whose flesh is permitted; excluded is this one, whose sinew is forbidden and whose flesh is forbidden" (Chullin 101a). "Whatever are holy things of the altar, one is liable for them; excluded are the holy things of the Temple maintenance" (Keritot 2b). "There are among fetuses those that are forbidden: four months old for a small animal, eight for a large one; from that and below it is forbidden; excluded is one that has two backs and two spines" (Niddah 24a). — *כַּיּוֹצֵא [Note: See the note below.] בּוֹ, בָּהּ, בָּהֶם, a) as befits him: "My son, in humility honor yourself, and give it re[ason] as befits it" (Ben Sira, Genizah 10:28). "My son, over the dead let tears fall, be bitter and lament, a dirge according to his due; gather up his flesh and do not hide yourself at his expiring; make bitter weeping and make warm the mourning, and make his mourning as befits [כיוצא] [Note: The sense of this expression is beyond doubt, according to the context and according to the Syriac translation: היך מא דמתבעא לה, and similarly the Greek. But the reason for this expression has not been clarified, neither in its sense here nor in Talmud and Midrash. Y. Levi said that the essential intention is "what goes out to him," but this is only an explanation of the words and explains nothing. Fleischer, in the notes to Levi, says that the intention is like "with the one who goes out," and this explanation too explains nothing. And also the explanation of Z. Bacher in the explanation of the words of the early commentators, die älteste Terminol. d. jüd. Schriftausl., the entry כיוצא בו in this entry, that כיוצא בו is the companion who goes out with his companion to war, and from this branched off the concept of likeness — this too is far-fetched and does not give a natural explanation of this expression. But its use in Ben Sira is perhaps the connecting link between the use of יצא in general and its use in Talmud and Midrash in this expression, for in the sense of befitting and suitable for so-and-so, the Arabic verb חרג' خرج, which corresponds to the Hebrew verb יצא, is also used, especially in the vernacular, and they say ח'רג' خٙرج in the sense of what befits and suits so-and-so, and the expression הד'א ח'רג'כ خرﺠك, this is what is fitting and suitable for you, and חרג' אלמנשקה, fit for hanging. And from this use in the sense of befitting and fitting there branched off afterwards its use in the sense of similar.] him" (ibid. 36:16-17). — b) *similar to this, and it comes at the beginning of the statement: "And one who gathers dry wood until the second rainy season falls, etc.; similar to this [כיוצא בו], one who rents a house to his fellow 'until the rains' — until the second rainy season falls" (Shevi'it 9:6-7). "One who repays a debt in the Sabbatical year should say to him: I release it. If he said to him: Even so, he may accept it from him, as it is said: And this is the manner of the release. If they said to him: Even so, he may accept it from them" (ibid. 10:8). "In truth they said: The attendant may see where the children are reading, but he himself may not read. "One who goes from a place where they do (work on the eve of Passover) to a place where they do not, or from a place where they do not to a place where they do, they impose on him the stringencies of the place he left and the stringencies of the place he went to, and a person should not deviate, because of dissension. "It is possible for the lower one to come before the upper one has come, but it is impossible for the upper one to come before the lower one has come. "And the horns and the hooves combine to impart the impurity of foods, but not the impurity of carcasses.
