"Thus you have learned that she eats on account of her offspring, even though that offspring is disqualified, etc.; behold, her mother eats on account of the disqualified daughter. Similar to this, the daughter of a priest who does not eat on account of her offspring from an Israelite, even though that offspring, etc., behold, he is fit to be high priest, he enables his mother to eat" (the same, Terumot 6:15). "The end (of the trumpet) on which the mouth is placed at the time of blowing receives impurity by itself, and the other, wide end does not receive impurity by itself, and when joined, all of it is impure. Similar to this, the branches of the candelabrum by themselves do not receive impurity" (the same, Kelim 10:16). — כיוצא בזה, כיוצא בדבר, you say: "And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed, etc. Do Moses' hands make war or break war? Rather, to tell you: as long as Israel looked upward and subjected their hearts to their Father in heaven, they prevailed, and if not, they fell. Similar to the matter [כיוצא בדבר] you say: Make yourself a fiery serpent and set it upon a pole, and it shall come to pass that everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live. Does a serpent kill or does a serpent give life? Rather, when Israel looked upward, etc., they were healed, and if not, they wasted away" (Rosh Hashanah 3:8). "When it says: These are that Aaron and Moses, it tells that both of them are equal to each other. Similar to this [כיוצא בזה] you say: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth, etc. — it tells that both of them are equal as one. Similar to the matter you say: I am the God, the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, etc. — it tells that the three of them are equal to one another. Similar to the matter you say: Honor your father and your mother, etc. — it tells that both of them are equal to each other" (Mekhilta Bo, פתיח'). "As He has spoken — and where did He speak? And I will bring you into the land, etc. Similar to the matter you say: This is that which the Lord has spoken: a solemn rest — and where did He speak? And it shall come to pass on the sixth day, etc. Similar to the matter you say: This is that which the Lord spoke: Through those who are near to Me I will be sanctified — and where did He speak? And there I will meet with the children of Israel" (ibid. 12). "When Israel do the will of the Omnipresent, their enemies stand before them only like one horse and its rider. Similar to this you say: When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots — is it one horse and one chariot? Rather, when Israel do the will of the Omnipresent, etc." (ibid., Beshallach 2). "The limb that began the transgression — from it the punishment begins. Similar to this you say: And He blotted out every living substance, etc., both man and beast — from the one who began the transgression the punishment began" (Sifre Numbers 18). "He shall separate himself from wine and strong drink — but wine is strong drink and strong drink is wine; rather, the Torah spoke in two expressions. Similar to this you say: שחיטה is זביחה and זביחה is שחיטה" (ibid. 23). "It teaches that both of them (Miriam and Aaron) spoke against him (against Moses), but Miriam opened the matter; for Miriam was not accustomed to speak before Aaron, but only because of the need of the hour. Similar to this you say: Therefore go you and read in the scroll which you have written from the mouth of Jeremiah — and Baruch was not accustomed to speak before Jeremiah, but only because of the need of the hour" (ibid. 99). "The elders say: Our hands have not shed this blood, etc.; the priests say: Forgive Your people Israel, etc.; the holy spirit says: And the blood shall be forgiven them. Three statements side by side: what this one said, that one did not say. Similar to this you say: And she said: Discern, I pray you — Tamar said; She is more righteous than I — Judah said; And he knew her again no more — the holy spirit said. Similar to this you say: We came to the land to which you sent us — Joshua said; Let us go up at once — Caleb said; Howbeit the people are strong — the spies said" (Tosefta Sotah 9:3). "Cush the Benjamite — was his name Cush? Was not his name Saul? Rather, just as a Cushite is distinctive in his skin, so Saul was distinctive in his deeds. Similar to the matter you say: Because of the Cushite woman whom he had married — was her name Cushite? Was not her name Zipporah? Rather, just as a Cushite woman is distinctive in her skin, so Zipporah was distinctive in her deeds. Similar to the matter you say: And Ebed-melech the Cushite heard — was his name Cushite? Was not his name Zedekiah? etc." (Moed Katan 16b). "It teaches that the voice was cut off and did not go out beyond the tent. Similar to this you say: And the sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard even to the outer court" (Numbers Rabbah 14). — כיוצא בזה אתה מוצא: "Whoever made this one wise will in the end make him a fool, and whoever made this one a fool will in the end make him wise. Similar to this you find among those who give charity, etc.: whoever made this one poor will in the end make him rich, and whoever made this one rich will in the end make him poor" (Mekhilta Yitro, Amalek 2). — And at the end of the statement: "And one does not invite to the grace after meals with the divine name with fewer than ten; and for land, nine and a priest; and a person likewise [כיוצא בהן]" (Megillah 4:3). "Rabbi Johanan ben Gudgada testified concerning the deaf woman whom her father married off [שהשיאה] [Note: In the source it was printed: "השיאה".] that she goes out with a bill of divorce. They said to him: This one too is likewise" (Yevamot 14:2). "Both an ox and any animal are alike with respect to falling into a pit, keeping away from Mount Sinai, double payment, returning a lost article, unloading, muzzling, mixed species and the Sabbath; and so too wild animals and birds are likewise" (Bava Kamma 5:7). "The aprons of pitch-workers, of potters and of tree-pruners do not interpose; Rabbi Judah says: Those of fig-gatherers too are likewise" (Mikva'ot 9:7). "One is not liable for hearing the voice, for an utterance of the lips, or for the impurity of the Sanctuary and its holy things; and the prince likewise" (Horayot 2:5). "A person may not hold tefillin in his hand and a Torah scroll in his arm and pray, etc. Samuel said: A knife, coins, a bowl and a loaf — these are likewise" (Berakhot 23b). "The camel-drivers' knot and the sailors' knot, and the knots of the straps of a shoe and sandal that the leather-workers tie when making them, and likewise anything similar to this" (Rambam, Shabbat 10:1). "And at the time of writing he soaks it (the ink) in gall-nut water or the like and writes with it" (the same, Tefillin 1:4). "And truth and falsehood and everything like them" (Sefer ha-Yashar, notes to Yeshuah the Karaite 12). — And in the middle of the statement, כיוצא בו נעשה, and the like: "And the watercress that grows in rivers and the rocket of the ash heap are exempt from tithes and may be bought from anyone in the Sabbatical year, because their like is not guarded, etc. Rabbi Simeon says: All aftergrowths are permitted except the aftergrowths of cabbage, because their like is not found among the vegetables of the field" (Shevi'it 9:1). "If he found the shape of a hand or the shape of a foot, these are forbidden, because their like is worshipped" (Avodah Zarah 3:2). "He said to him: This I have not heard; something like it I have heard" (Bava Kamma 107b). "And likewise everything similar to bringing impurity" (Rambam, Tum'at Met 17:1). — יש כיוצא בו, אין כיוצא בו: "He said to him: Rabbi, I have one like you" (Mekhilta Bo, פתיח'). "Things that are like it and things that are not like it" (Sifra Vayikra, Chovah 4:8). "For the Omnipresent sent upon them a severe plague, the like of which there had not been since the day they came out of Egypt" (Sifre, Numbers 98). "Joshua said to him (to Moses): I am zealous for you; would that I were like you, and would that all Israel were like you" (ibid. 96). "Three hundred sixty-five negative commandments are in the Torah, and among all the commandments there is none like this one" (ibid. Deuteronomy 76). "A sage who died — we have none like him" (Jerusalem Talmud Horayot 3, 48b). "The Holy One, blessed be He, said to it: Solomon and a thousand like him will be annulled, but a thorn of you I will not annul from the Torah" (Exodus Rabbah 6). "There is no nation in the world like them — behold, they are asleep from the Torah and from the commandments" (ibid. Numbers 20). "Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: When Moses our teacher heard this, he said before Him: Master of the world, let Moses and a hundred like him die, and let not the fingernail of one of them be harmed" (ibid. Deuteronomy 7). "And it came to pass — it denotes trouble and joy: if trouble, there is none like it; if joy, there is none like it" (ibid., Ruth 1). — And concerning language, the language יצאה thus, thus is the way to be said, thus is the custom of the language: "If there is a sheva between them, it went forth [יצא] in this way, for the sheva is not counted with the kings" (Dikdukei ha-Te'amim, section 40). "The whole verse went forth [יצא] in this manner" (ibid.). "Know that every word in Scripture that goes out [היוצאת] in יֶנָה, as you will learn, and goes out in the plural, is always soft, like ידיו תביאינה" (ibid., section 55). — And in grammar, °פעל יוֹצֵא, whose action passes over onto another body, French transitif: "The Qal conjugation is sometimes intransitive by itself and sometimes passes over [יוצא] to another, etc., like אכל and its fellows, which are transitive verbs [פעלים יוצאים], etc.; and when you find them intransitive, even though you do not find them transitive, and you wish to build from them a transitive verb, you may do so" (Radak, Mikhlol, שדה"פ). "And the measure of צמח, which is an intransitive verb — if you need to make it transitive [יוצא], we make it" (ibid.). "And therefore all the grammarians said that אכל and בנה are single and transitive [ויוצאים] verbs, and הלך and יצא and עמד and ישב are single and intransitive" (Rabbi Abraham Balmes, Mesillat ha-Po'al). "A transitive verb [פעל יוצא] is the verb in which the action of the doer goes out to another body besides the one that receives it" (Maslul, מסל' הכנ' 1). "If the predicate is an accident from the category of change and motion, and it is an action that has another body receiving the action besides the doer, it is called a transitive verb [פועל יוצא]" (תל"ע 3:1). — And concerning the printing of books, newspapers and the like, °יָצָא לאור, was published: "This letter which is in your hands is the introduction and opening of another letter which will be published [יצא לאור] in a few days, God willing, month by month" (Ha-Me'assef, year 5544), and see אור. — And in the sense of a transitive verb, *צֵא from such-and-such a thing, subtract from it, deduct from it: "Consider: if the first festival day and the last festival day fell on the Sabbath — now take away [צא] two days from them, and there are six" (Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 76c). "And you shall keep it a feast to the Lord seven days — are they seven? Are they not eight? Rather, take away [צא] the Sabbath from them" (ibid.). — And the liturgical poet said: "Many were their journeys — they are forty-two; take away [צא] from them the number fourteen when going out of Egypt" (Rabbi Israel Najara, יסע כצאן).

— Hif'il, הוֹצִיא, הוֹצֵאתָ, הוֹצֵאת, הוֹצֵאתִי, הוֹצִיאוּ, הוֹצֵאתֶם, מוֹצִיא, מוֹצֵא, מוֹצִיאִים, הוֹצֵא, הַיְצֵא, הוֹצִיאָה, אוֹצִיא, אוֹצִיאָה, וָאוֹצִיא, וָאוֹצִא, תּוֹצִיא, וַתּוֹצֵא, הֲתֹצִיא, יוֹצִיא, וַיּוֹצֵא, תּוֹצִיא, תּוֹצֵא, וַתּוֹצֵא, נוֹצִיא, תּוֹצִיאוּ, יוֹצִיאוּ, יוֹצִאוּ, יֹצִאוּ, וַיּוֹצִיאוּ, וַיֹּצִיאוּ, וַיֹּצִאוּ, הוֹצִיאִי, הוֹצִיאוֹ, הוֹצִיאָם, הוֹצִיאַנִי, -אָנִי, הוֹצִיאָנוּ, הוֹצִיאֲךָ, הוֹצִיאָם, הוֹצֵאתַנִי, -תָנִי, הוֹצֵאתוֹ, הוֹצֵאתִיךָ, הוֹצֵאתִיהָ, הוֹצֵאתִים, הוֹצִיאֻהָ, מוֹצִיאִי, מוֹצִיאוֹ, מוֹצִיאֲךָ, מוֹצִיאָם, הוֹצִיאֵנוּ, הוֹצִיאֵהוּ, אוֹצִיאֵם, וָאוֹצִיאֵם, תּוֹצִיאֵנִי, יוֹצִיאֵנִי, וַיּוֹצִיאֵנִי, יוֹצִיאֲךָ, וַיֹּצִיאֲךָ, וַיּוֹצִיאָהּ, יוֹצִיאֵם, וַיּוֹצִיאוּהָ, וַיֹּצִיאֻהוּ, יוֹצִיאוּם, — הוֹציא so-and-so from the house and the like, caused him to go out from there: "On that very day the Lord brought [הוֹצִיא] the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt" (Exodus 12:51). "By strength of hand the Lord brought us out [הוֹצִיאָנוּ] from Egypt, from the house of bondage" (ibid. 13-14). "And he brought me forth [וְהוֹצִיאַנִי] by the way of the gate" (Ezekiel 42:15). "Lest you forget the Lord, who brought you forth [הוֹצִיאֲךָ] out of the land of Egypt" (Deuteronomy 6:12). "For with a strong hand the Lord brought you out [הוֹצִיאֲךָ] of Egypt" (Exodus 13:9). "For evil did He bring them forth [הוֹצִיאָם], to slay them in the mountains" (ibid. 32:12). "Lord, why does Your wrath burn against Your people, whom You have brought forth [הוֹצֵאתָ] out of the land of Egypt?" (ibid. 11). "Then you shall bring forth [וְהוֹצֵאתָ] that man etc. to your gates" (Deuteronomy 17:5). "And make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out [וְהוֹצֵאתַנִי] of this house" (Genesis 40:14). "Who chose Abram and brought him forth [וְהוֹצֵאתוֹ] out of Ur of the Chaldeans" (Nehemiah 9:7). "The land from which You brought us out [הוֹצֵאתָנוּ]" (Deuteronomy 9:28). "For on this very day I have brought [הוֹצֵאתִי] your hosts out of the land of Egypt" (Exodus 12:17). "Say to the children of Israel: I am the Lord, and I will bring you out [וְהוֹצֵאתִי] from under the burdens of the Egyptians" (ibid. 6:6). "I am the Lord who brought you out [הוֹצֵאתִיךָ] of Ur of the Chaldeans" (Genesis 15:7). "And I will bring them out [וְהוֹצֵאתִים] from the peoples and gather them from the countries" (Ezekiel 34:13). "And they carried him out [וְהוֹצִיאֻהוּ] and stoned him, and he died" (1 Kings 21:10). "I am the Lord your God, who brought you out [הַמּוֹצִיא] of the land of Egypt" (Leviticus 22:33). "God makes the solitary dwell in a house; He brings out [מוֹצִיא] the prisoners into prosperity" (Psalms 68:7). "And they shall bring out [מוֹצִאִים] all your wives and your children to the Chaldeans" (Jeremiah 38:23). "And they brought [וּמוֹצִיאִים] horses for Solomon out of Egypt and out of all lands" (2 Chronicles 9:28). — הַמּוֹצִיא and the one who brings in, one who goes at the head of the people to war: "When Saul was king over us, it was you who led out [הַמּוֹצִיא] and brought in Israel" (2 Samuel 5:2). "The Lord your God, who brought you forth [הַמּוֹצִיאֲךָ] out of the land of Egypt" (Deuteronomy 8:14). "And who brings me forth [וּמוֹצִיאִי] from my enemies; yes, You lift me up above those who rise up against me" (2 Samuel 22:49). "God who brought them forth [מוֹצִיאָם] out of Egypt" (Numbers 23:22). "And Ephraim shall bring out [לְהוֹצִיא] his children to the slayer" (Hosea 9:13). "The bread with which I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you forth [בְּהוֹצִיאִי] from the land of Egypt" (Exodus 16:32). "I made a covenant with your fathers on the day that I brought them forth [הוֹצִאִי] out of the land of Egypt" (Jeremiah 34:13). "What is this that you have done to us, to bring us forth [לְהוֹצִיאָנוּ] out of Egypt?" (Exodus 14:11). "As You spoke by the hand of Moses Your servant, when You brought [בְּהוֹצִיאֲךָ] our fathers out of Egypt" (1 Kings 8:53). "They forsook the covenant of the Lord, the God of their fathers, which He made with them when He brought them forth [בְּהוֹצִיאוֹ] out of the land of Egypt" (Deuteronomy 29:24). "And they committed him to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, that he should carry him [לְהוֹצִאֵהוּ] home" (Jeremiah 39:14). "And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth [כְּהוֹצִיאָם] outside" (Genesis 19:17). "It was a night of watching for the Lord, for bringing them out [לְהוֹצִיאָם] from the land of Egypt" (Exodus 12:42). "Bring forth [הוֹצִיא] the blind people that have eyes" (Isaiah 43:8). "And whatever you have in the city, bring them out [הוֹצֵא] of the place" (Genesis 19:12). "Come now therefore, and I will send you to Pharaoh, and bring forth [וְהוֹצֵא] My people, the children of Israel, out of Egypt" (Exodus 3:10). "And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Bring forth [הוֹצֵא] him who has cursed outside the camp" (Leviticus 24:13-14). "Then the men of the city said to Joash: Bring out [הוֹצֵא] your son, that he may die" (Judges 6:30). "And they spoke to the master of the house, the old man, saying: Bring forth [הוֹצֵא] the man who came into your house" (ibid. 19:22). "Turn your hand and carry me out [וְהוֹצִיאֵנִי] of the camp" (1 Kings 22:34). "Where are the men who came to you this night? Bring them out [הוֹצִיאֵם] to us" (Genesis 19:5). "And he cried: Have everyone go out [הוֹצִיאוּ] from me" (ibid. 45:1). "And Judah said: Bring her forth [הוֹצִיאוּהָ] and let her be burned" (ibid. 38:24). "Bring forth [הוֹצִיאִי] the men who have come to you" (Joshua 2:3). "Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth [אוֹצִיא] the children of Israel out of Egypt?" (Exodus 3:11). "Let me, I pray you, bring them out [אוֹצִיאָה] to you" (Genesis 19:8). "And I brought [וָאוֹצִיא] your fathers out of Egypt" (Joshua 24:6). "And I caused them to go forth [וָאוֹצִיאֵם] out of the land of Egypt" (Ezekiel 20:10). "And You brought forth [וַתֹּצֵא] Your people Israel out of the land of Egypt" (Jeremiah 32:21). "Bring me out [תּוֹצִיאֵנִי] of the net that they have hidden for me" (Psalms 31:5). "We went through fire and through water, but You brought us out [וַתּוֹצִיאֵנוּ] into abundance" (ibid. 66:12). "And He brought him forth [וַיּוֹצֵא] outside" (Genesis 15:5). "And he brought [וַיּוֹצֵא] Simeon out to them" (ibid. 43:23). "Then his servant brought her out [וַיֹּצֵא] outside" (2 Samuel 13:18). "And the man laid hold of his concubine and brought her forth [וַיֹּצֵא] to them outside" (Judges 19:25). "But the Lord has taken you and brought you forth [וַיּוֹצֵא] out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt" (Deuteronomy 4:20). "And execute judgment for me; He will bring me forth [יוֹצִיאֵנִי] to the light, and I shall behold His righteousness" (Micah 7:9). "He brought me forth [וַיּוֹצִיאֵנִי] also into a large place; He delivered me because He delighted in me" (Psalms 18:20). "And He sent an angel and brought us forth [וַיֹּצִיאֵנוּ] out of Egypt" (Numbers 20:16). "And brought you out [וַיּוֹצִיאֲךָ] with His presence, with His great power, out of Egypt" (Deuteronomy 4:37). "For you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God brought you out [וַיֹּצִיאֲךָ] from there" (ibid. 5:15). "And who may lead them out [יוֹצִיאֵם] and who may bring them in" (Numbers 27:17). "And He brought them [וַיּוֹצִאֵים] (Israel) forth with silver and gold" (Psalms 105:37). "And they brought forth [וַיּוֹצִיאוּ] him who had cursed outside the camp" (Leviticus 24:23). "And all the congregation brought him [וַיֹּצִיאוּ] outside the camp" (Numbers 15:36). "And they brought him forth [וַיֹּצִאֻהוּ] and set him outside the city" (Genesis 19:16). — Things that are not living creatures, moved the thing from inside a thing to the outside: "And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth [הוֹצִיא] bread and wine" (Genesis 14:18). "And he shall carry forth [וְהוֹצִיא] the ashes outside the camp" (Leviticus 6:4). "And You brought forth [הוֹצֵאתָ] water for them out of the rock for their thirst" (Nehemiah 9:15). "And you shall bring forth [וְהוֹצֵאתָ] to them water out of the rock" (Numbers 20:8). "And you shall bring forth [וְהוֹצֵאתָ] your stuff, as stuff for exile" (Ezekiel 12:4). "Make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it out [וְהוֹצֵאת] to me, and for yourself" (1 Kings 17:13). "I brought forth [הוֹצֵאתִי] my stuff by day, as stuff for exile, etc.; I brought it forth [הוֹצֵאתִי] in the dark, and bore it upon my shoulder" (Ezekiel 12:7). "I the Lord have drawn forth [הוֹצֵאתִי] My sword out of its sheath" (ibid. 21:10). "Do not depart from here, I pray you, until I come to you, and bring forth [וְהוֹצֵאתִי] my offering and set it before you" (Judges 6:18). "And I will bring forth [וְהֹצֵאתִי] out of his mouth that which he has swallowed" (Jeremiah 51:44). "This is the curse that goes forth over the face of the whole land etc. I will cause it to go forth [הוֹצֵאתִיהָ], says the Lord of hosts, and it shall enter" (Zechariah 5:3-4). "And they baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought forth [הוֹצִיאוּ] out of Egypt" (Exodus 12:39). "He brings forth [מוֹצֵא] the wind out of His treasuries" (Psalms 135:7). "Who brought forth [הַמּוֹצִיא] water for you out of the rock of flint" (Deuteronomy 8:15). "And they reported [מוֹצִיאִים] my words to him" (Nehemiah 6:19). "To bring out [לְהוֹצִיא] the bones out of the house" (Amos 6:10). "And when they brought out [וּבְהוֹצִיאָם] the money that was brought into the house of the Lord, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the Law of the Lord" (2 Chronicles 34:14). "Bring forth [הוֹצֵא] vestments for all the worshippers of Baal" (2 Kings 10:22). "Bring my soul out [הוֹצִיאָה] of prison" (Psalms 142:8). "Bring it out [הוֹצִיאָהּ] piece by piece; no lot has fallen upon it" (Ezekiel 24:6). — And for living creatures, beasts, birds and creeping things, הַיְצֵא in place of הוֹצֵא: "Every living thing that is with you, of all flesh, both fowl and cattle, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth, bring forth [הַיְצֵא] [Note: So the qere, and the ketiv is הוצא. Now the early authorities did not dispute much over the strangeness of this form. Ibn Janah remarked nothing about it. Radak only mentioned it and did not explain its reason. He said in the Mikhlol, שדה"פ: "And the imperative comes with the yod appearing: הַיְשר לפני דרכך, הַיְצא אתך." End quote. And in the Roots he mentioned: "And with the yod appearing, הַיְצא." End quote. And the moderns, who did seek to give a reason for this qere, found nothing acceptable. Some of them (Olsh. §256) said simply that it is not clear for what reason the Masoretes fixed this qere, and some of them, like König and others, saw in it the influence of the language of the land. But this is not a sufficient reason, and also one should not compare this form to the form הַיְשר, even though there too the ketiv is הושר, for there is a great difference between these two words. From the verb ישר the Hif'il was not common, and therefore where the Hif'il came according to the grammatical rule, הושר did not immediately give the hearer the impression that it is the Hif'il of ישר in the sense of make [Note: In the source it was printed 'עשר'.] straight; and therefore one must reckon that in speech too they perhaps said הַיְשר, and if we suspect the Masoretes of sometimes having permitted themselves a correction of the qere according to their own opinion, the correction here is truly a fitting correction, because it explains the intention, whereas the ketiv הושר obscures it. But in the verb יצא, whose Hif'il הוציא and also the imperative הוֹצֵא is so common and was used so much, and the intention of הוֹצֵא was so well known and understood by all, and in Scripture itself too the imperative הוֹצֵא occurs six times — why suddenly, one time, precisely in this place, did they say הַיְצֵא? And who said the strange הַיְצֵא instead of the simple הוֹצֵא? If this was indeed a reading transmitted from earlier, it is puzzling why they began to read thus instead of the simple and clear word הוֹצֵא; and if the Masoretes invented this qere, the matter is even more puzzling: why did they invent a strange reading in place of a correct and understandable ketiv? And it is impossible to attribute this correction to the influence of the Aramaic language, for such influence is possible and understandable only in a word that is not common in Hebrew and very common in a fixed form in Aramaic, or if the things were written at a late time, at the time of the dominance of the Aramaic language. But here, in this word, הוצא, in this place, there is neither the one nor the other. And likewise very forced is the conjecture that the qere is not היצא but יֵצא, in order to make it agree with verse 19 (REJ 1892, Janv. 138). And perforce we must assume that in the living speech too there was in use, at least at a somewhat later time, an imperative הַיְצֵא as well, instead of הוצא, and this imperative was used in a somewhat special sense, perhaps for a somewhat special matter. Now the imperative הוצא, which is the form that the grammatical rule requires, is found in Scripture in six more places, cited in the body, and from the point of view of sense and context there is no difference between them and the imperative in this place whose qere was changed — except that in all those places those brought out are persons or things that are not living creatures, and here those brought out are living creatures, cattle, fowl and creeping things. And therefore we must say that at some time the speakers of Hebrew began to say the imperative of the Hif'il of יצא with respect to living creatures not הוצֵא but הַיְצֵא, and therefore they began also to read this imperative thus within Scripture in the place where those brought out are cattle and beasts; and this qere, which was truly in use according to the custom of the spoken language at that time, the Masoretes transmitted to us, as was their custom to transmit the reading and pronunciation of their time.] with you, that they may swarm in the earth" (Genesis 8:17). — And the future: "You shall not carry forth [תוֹצִיא] any of the flesh out of the house" (Exodus 12:46). "You shall carry much seed out [תוֹצִיא] into the field" (Deuteronomy 28:38). "Can you lead forth [הֲתֹצִיא] the constellations in their season?" (Job 38:32). "And the man to whom you lend shall bring forth [יוֹצִיא] the pledge outside to you" (Deuteronomy 24:11). "And he carried out [וַיּוֹצֵא] from there all the treasures of the house of the Lord" (2 Kings 24:13). "The Lord has opened His armory and has brought forth [וַיּוֹצֵא] the weapons of His indignation" (Jeremiah 50:25). "And he brought them forth [וַיֹּצֵא] vestments" (2 Kings 10:22). "And he brought out [וַיֹּצֵא] the Asherah from the house of the Lord" (ibid. 23:6). "And He brought [וַיּוֹצִא] streams also out of the rock" (Psalms 78:16). "And he put his hand into his bosom, and when he took it out [וַיּוֹצִיאָהּ], behold, his hand was leprous, as white as snow" (Exodus 4:6). "Shall we bring you forth [נוֹצִיא] water out of this rock?" (Numbers 20:10). "And you shall bring forth [תּוֹצִיאוּ] the old because of the new" (Leviticus 26:10). "And they shall bring out [וַיּוֹצִיאוּ] the bones of the kings of Judah out of their graves" (Jeremiah 8:1). "And they brought forth [וַיֹּצִיאוּ] the pillars of the house of Baal" (2 Kings 10:26). "For by count they brought them in (the vessels and the like), and by count they took them out [יוֹצִיאוּם]" (1 Chronicles 9:28). — And made grow from the ground: "And God said: Let the earth bring forth [תּוֹצֵא] the living creature after its kind" (Genesis 1:24). "And the earth brought forth [וַתּוֹצֵא] grass, herb yielding seed after its kind" (ibid. 12). "For as the earth brings forth [תּוֹצִיא] her growth, and as the garden causes the things that are sown in it to spring forth" (Isaiah 61:11). "Who causes the grass to spring up for the cattle, and herb for the service of man, to bring forth [לְהוֹצִיא] bread out of the earth" (Psalms 104:14). — הוֹצִיא a blossom: "And behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi had budded, and put forth [וַיֹּצֵא] buds, and bloomed blossoms" (Numbers 17:23). — And fire: "You have profaned your sanctuaries, therefore I brought forth [וְאוֹצִא] a fire from the midst of you; it has devoured you" (Ezekiel 28:18). — And caused to come into being: "And if you bring forth [תּוֹצִיא] the precious out of the vile" (Jeremiah 15:19). "For the churning of milk brings forth [יוֹצִיא] butter, and the wringing of the nose brings forth [יוֹצִיא] blood; so the forcing of wrath brings forth [יוֹצִיא] strife" (Proverbs 30:33). — הוֹצִיא judgment, did justice, gave the verdict, made it public: "He shall bring forth [יוֹצִיא] judgment to the nations etc.; he shall bring forth [יוֹצִיא] judgment in truth" (Isaiah 42:1-3). — And wind, light and the like: "He makes lightnings for the rain and brings forth [וַיּוֹצֵא] the wind out of His treasuries" (Jeremiah 10:13). — And a person's spirit: "A fool utters [יוֹצִיא] all his spirit" (Proverbs 29:11), does not rule his spirit. "He uncovers deep things out of darkness and brings out [וַיֹּצֵא] to light the shadow of death" (Job 12:22). "And the thing that is hidden he brings forth [יֹצִא] to light" (ibid. 28:11). — הוֹצִיא from his heart, invented: "Shall they not teach you and tell you, and utter [יוֹצִיאוּ] words out of their heart?" (Job 8:10). — הוֹצִיא money, gave money as the price of a thing: "And they gave the money that was weighed out into the hands of those who did the work, who had the oversight of the house of the Lord, and they paid it out [וַיּוֹצִיאֻהוּ] to the carpenters and the builders who worked on the house of the Lord" (2 Kings 12:12). "And Menahem exacted [וַיֹצֵא] the money of Israel, of all the mighty men of wealth, to give to the king of Assyria, fifty shekels of silver for each man" (ibid. 15:20). — And in Talmud and Midrash, in the same senses. And הוציא a thing from the general rule, took it by itself, so that it would no longer be with the other things: "A vain oath too was included in the general rule, etc., and behold, Scripture takes it out of its general rule and is stringent with it" (Mekhilta Yitro 7). — And הוציא himself from, ceased to be together with: "This is a wicked son, who took himself out of the community; and since he took himself out of the community, you too take him out of the community: It is because of that which the Lord did for me when I came forth out of Egypt — for me and not for you; and since you took yourself out of the community, had you been there you would not have been redeemed" (Mekhilta Bo, Pischa 17). "Samuel said: A person should never take himself out of the community" (Berakhot 49b). — *הוֹצִיא his wife, gave her a bill of divorce: "One who warned his wife and she secluded herself, even if he heard it from a bird flying by, shall divorce her [יוציא] and give her the ketubbah" (Sotah 6:1). — הוֹצִיא from his fellow, claimed money from him: "He who seeks to take from his fellow — the burden of proof is upon him" (Bava Kamma 3:11). — And הוציא from so-and-so, took from him: "One who was married to two wives and sold his field, and the first wrote to the buyer: I have no claim or dispute with you — the second takes it away from the buyer" (Ketubot 10:6). — the tree הוֹצִיא its blossom and the like: "From when may one not cut down a tree in the Sabbatical year? The House of Shammai say: Any tree, from when it puts forth, etc.; olives, from when they blossom, and every other tree, from when it puts forth" (Shevi'it 4:10). — הוֹצִיא so much and so much on a thing, gave so much and so much: "A person may say to his fellow: So many laborers I spent on this field, so many dinars I spent on this dwelling; but he may not say to him: So much I spent and so much I am going to spend" (Shabbat 150b). "How much a person would want to redeem it for himself for a sela, on condition of bearing the expenses from his own house" (Ma'aser Sheni 5:4). "One who spent much on his wife's property and ate little, or a little and ate much — what he spent he spent, and what he ate he ate; if he spent and did not eat, he swears how much he spent and takes it" (Ketubot 8:5). "When a person marries off his daughter and lays out his expenses" (Genesis Rabbah 26). "There is a person who changes one gold coin and lays out from it many expenses" (ibid. Leviticus 35). — הוֹצִיא an evil name upon so-and-so: "The rapist, the seducer and one who brings out an evil name" (Sanhedrin 1:1). — And הוציא slander: "You are bringing out slander upon that righteous man" (Shabbat 96b). "So as not to bring out slander upon the early righteous ones" (Ketubot 103a). And see לעז. — *הוציא a bond of debt against so-and-so, showed that he holds a bond of debt against him and claimed his debt from him: "A creditor who produced a bond of debt and has no prosbul with it — these are not to be paid" (Ketubot 9:9). "Two who produced bonds of debt against each other, etc. — this one collects his bond of debt and that one collects his bond of debt" (ibid. 13:9). "Two who were in one city, the name of one Joseph son of Simeon and the name of the other Joseph son of Simeon, cannot produce a bond of debt against each other" (Bava Batra 10:7). "One who produces a bond of debt against his fellow: the lender says: I have not been paid anything, and the borrower says: I paid half" (Rambam, Malveh ve-Loveh 14:4). "Reuben produced a bond for a thousand gold pieces against seven men of the community" (Tur Choshen Mishpat 61:16, in the name of the Rosh). — b) הוֹצִיא so-and-so of his obligation, caused so-and-so to fulfill his obligation: "Priests, Levites and Israelites, etc., are obliged (in the grace after meals) and discharge the many of their obligation; a tumtum and an androgynos are obliged but do not discharge the many of their obligation" (Tosefta Berakhot 5:14). "Any commandments from which a person is exempt, a person discharges the many of their obligation" (Jerusalem Talmud ibid. 3, 6b). "May a resident of a town discharge a resident of a walled city of his obligation?" (ibid. Megillah 2, 73b). — And הוציא alone, without the noun יד, in this sense: "An androgynos discharges his own kind and does not discharge one not of his kind; a tumtum discharges neither his own kind nor one not of his kind; one who is half slave and half free discharges neither his own kind nor one not of his kind" (Tosefta Berakhot 5:15-16). "Why does the prayer leader go down before the ark? They said to him: In order to discharge the one who is not proficient. He said to them: Just as he discharges the one who is not proficient, so he discharges the one who is proficient" (Rosh Hashanah 34b). — c) *הוֹצִיא such-and-such a thing, caused such-and-such a thing to go out, not to be included in the matter at all: "Without blemish — to exclude one with a blemish; male — to exclude a tumtum, an androgynos and a female" (Mekhilta Bo, Pischa 4), for a tumtum, an androgynos and a female are unfit for the altar. "Which you have — to exclude one who sells the fetus of his animal to a gentile, etc.; I exclude one who sells the fetus of his animal to a gentile and I include one who buys the fetus of a gentile's animal" (ibid. 18). "His wife — to exclude a woman awaiting levirate marriage, who is not his wife; with him — to exclude a betrothed woman, who is not with him" (ibid. Mishpatim 1). "If Scripture takes her out from the hand of sale, which is severe, all the more so from the hand of boring, which is light" (ibid. 3). "Shall appear — to exclude the blind; your males — to exclude the women" (ibid. 20). "I will exclude Israel, who were not fit to ascend the mountain, and I will not exclude the elders, who were fit to ascend the mountain; I will exclude the elders, who were not seen in the speech with Moses, and I will not exclude the sons of Aaron, who were seen in the speech with Moses, etc.; or I will exclude them from the meeting and I will not exclude them from the utterances" (Sifra Vayikra, Nedavah 1:2). "I will exclude the Passover offering, which is not frequent, and I will not exclude circumcision, which is frequent — Scripture says: which ought not to be done. Or might I exclude the positive commandment concerning a menstruant? Scripture says: of all the commandments; and to include the positive commandment concerning a menstruant. Since Scripture included and excluded, in any case I exclude all the commandments that have no negative commandment and include the positive commandment concerning a menstruant, which has a negative commandment" (ibid., Chovah 4:1). "To you — to include what is planted for the public; Rabbi Judah says: To exclude what is planted for the public" (Pesachim 23a). "The homeborn — to exclude the women" (Sukkah 28a). "Of you, and not all of you — to exclude the apostate" (Chullin 5a). — *הוֹצִיא for him so much and so much from the account and the like, reduced for him, deducted for him, German abrechnen; French déduire; English to deduct: "One who deposits produce with his fellow — he deducts [יוציא] losses for him: for wheat and rice nine half-kabs per kor, etc.; Rabbi Judah says: If it was a large measure, he does not deduct losses for him, because they increase. He deducts for him a sixth for wine; Rabbi Judah says: A fifth. He deducts for him three logs of oil per hundred: a log and a half for sediment and a log and a half for absorption. If it was refined oil, he does not deduct sediment for him; if the jars were old, he does not deduct absorption for him" (Bava Metzia 3:7-8). — e) *הוֹצִיא his year and the like, lived the whole year: "And Rabbi Eliezer had a certain student who gave a halakhic ruling in his presence. Rabbi Eliezer said to Imma Shalom his wife: I wonder whether this one will live out his year; and he did not live out his year" (Eruvin 63a). — *הוֹצִיא a name, called so-and-so a name: "Rabbi Nathan said: It happened that I came to the province of Cappadocia, and there was a certain woman there who would bear male children, and they were circumcised and died. She circumcised the first and he died, etc. I said to them: Wait and leave him until the blood of the covenant comes to him, etc. And they left him and circumcised him, and the son was found to live, and they called [והציאו] his name Nathan after me" (Song of Songs Rabbah, מה יפו). — *הוֹצִיא so-and-so smooth, did not answer his question, sent him away empty, put him off: "A certain gentile asked Rabbi Joshua ben Korha: What did the Holy One, blessed be He, see to speak with Moses from within the thorn bush? He said to him: Had it been from within a carob or from within a sycamore, you would have asked me the same. But to send you away empty is impossible. Rather, why from within the thorn bush? To teach you that there is no place empty of the Divine Presence, not even a thorn bush" (Exodus Rabbah 2). "A philosopher asked Rabbi: If circumcision is so beloved, why was it not given to the first man? etc. He said to him: To send you away empty is impossible; rather, everything that He created in the six days of creation needs improvement" (Pesikta Rabbati 23). — הוֹצִיא a deed, did it, carried it out: "At the time of judgment all would deliberate over the halakha in order to bring out the judgment according to its truth, and they would see it as though a sword were placed between their thighs and Gehenna open before them, etc.; they would be afraid of how to carry out the deed so as to be saved from the judgment of Gehenna" (Numbers Rabbah 11). — °And הוציא from potential to actual, see כֹח. — f) *הוֹצִיא speech and the like, pronounced it with the organs of speech, German aussprechen; French pronocer; English -nounce: "For those who bring them out (the words of the Torah) with the mouth" (Eruvin 54a). "Rabbi Eliezer ben Jacob says: A person who is handsome and praiseworthy, and brings out an ugly word from his mouth" (Derekh Eretz Rabbah 3). — And the letters: "All the letters — when a person brings them out of his mouth, he feels them with his lips" (Otiyyot de-Rabbi Akiva, הא). — And in the science of arithmetic, °הוציא a root, extracted a root: "Let us return to extracting this root from 20,000" (Ibn Ezra, Sefer ha-Mispar, the chapter on extracting roots). And see שרש. — °הוֹצִיא a book or a newspaper to light, printed it, published it: "And now they have concluded in their counsel to publish them [להוציאם לאור] by means of printing, and to add to them what is already in their treasury and what will yet come there" (Ha-Me'assef, year 544), and see אור.

— Huf'al, הוּצָא, הוּצָאָה, מוּצֵאת, מוּצָאִים, מוּצָאוֹת. — That they brought him out: "And Judah said: Bring her forth and let her be burned. When she was brought forth [מוּצֵאת], she sent to her father-in-law, saying" (Genesis 38:24-25). "And behold, all the women who are left in the king of Judah's house shall be brought forth [מוּצָאוֹת] to the king of Babylon's princes" (Jeremiah 38:22). "Yet, behold, there shall be left in it a remnant that shall be brought forth [הַמּוּצָאִים], both sons and daughters; behold, they shall come forth to you" (Ezekiel 14:22). — And water and the like: "These waters issue forth toward the eastern region, and shall go down into the Arabah, and shall go toward the sea; into the sea shall the waters go which were made to issue forth [הַמּוּצָאִים], and the waters shall be healed" (Ezekiel 47:8). — *מוּצָא from the general rule: "An individual is excluded [מוצא] from the category of the community, and a prince is excluded from the category of the community, etc.; an anointed priest is excluded from the category of an individual, and a prince is excluded from the category of an individual" (Sifra Vayikra, Nedavah 4:5).

[Omitted from the Qal: — a city יֹצֵאת a hundred, a thousand, that so many and so many men go out from it to war: "The virgin of Israel is fallen, she shall no more rise; she is cast down upon her land, there is none to raise her up. For thus says the Lord God: The city that went forth [הַיֹּצֵאת] a thousand shall have a hundred left, and that which went forth [וְהַיֹּצֵאת] a hundred shall have ten left, to the house of Israel" (Amos 5:3-4). — יָצָא the thing, did what was proper to do in the matter: "It is good that you should take hold of this; yea, also from that do not withdraw your hand; for he who fears God shall discharge [יֵצֵא] them all" (Ecclesiastes 7:18).]

he: *, פ"י, —  עשה ביקב:  עד היקבין שיקבן מלך מלכי המלכים הקב"ה (מד"ר שה"ש, צוארך).  יקבים שיקבם המלך שלמה (פסיק' דר"כ, רני עקרה).
en: *, transitive verb, — to make in a winepress: "Up to the winepresses that the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, pressed" (Song of Songs Rabbah, צוארך). "Winepresses that King Solomon pressed" (Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, רני עקרה).

he: פ"ע, יֹקֵד, יֹקֶדֶת, עת' יֵקַד, תִּיקַד, — יָקְדָה האש, בָּערה, דָלקה, brennen; brûler; to burn: עלה עשן באפי אש יֹקֶדֶת כל היום (ישע' סה ה). ותחת כבדו יֵקַד יקד כיקוד אש (שם י יו).  כי אש קדחה באפי וַתִּיקַד עד שאול תחתית (דבר' לב כב).  — ואמר בן סירא: בעדת רשעים יוקדת אש ובגוי חנף נצתה חמה (ב"ס גני' יו ו).  — ועב' *יָקְדוּ: אמר לו הקדוש ברוך הוא למשה אתמול יקדו גדישי ואתם באים להוסיף צרה (ילקווט דבר' תתח).  — ואמר הפיטן: שקדו ויקדו גויל דת משנאי אוי איך נמשלת לפטיש תעודיך (ר"א קליר, קינ' לת"ב, ציון צפירת).  פירוש שרפה דלתותי תשקוד, את מי בדינה תפקוד, צוק אבר רותח ליקוד (אזהר' ר"א הזקן, קמ"ג 62).  טלאיך הזהרת שקליהם להקדים, ידעת העתידות ודרשת נשקדים, כבוי להמציא ללהב יוקדים, לקוחים למות לתחי נפקדים (סליח' לתענית אסתר, אתה האל).  — ופָעוּל, °יָקוּד, יְקוּדָה, כמו יֹקֵד: מצות עשה להיות אש יקודה על המזבח תמיד (רמב"ם, תמיד' ומוספ' ב א).  — ואמר המשורר: ואם קדה וקנמון וקנה עלי מחתות בבית משתה יקודים, ואם ריח לבונות ואהלים וריח אשכלות כופר חמודים (ר"מ דרעי, לקו"ק נג).

— הָפע', הוּקַד, יוּקַד, תּוּקַד, — כמו יָקַד: והאש על המזבח תּוּקַד בו לא תכבה (ויקר' ו ה).  כי אש קדחה באפי עליכם תּוּקָד כך למערבאי, למנדחאי תיקר כתיב, תוקד קרי. (ירמ' יה יד).  כי אש קדחתם באפי עד עולם תּוּקָד (שם יז ד).  — ובינ': האש  המוקד על המזבח (תנחומא צו יד).  המזבח היה מוקד באש (ילקוט דבר' תתח).
— פִע', °יִקֵּד, פ"י, — יִקֵּד את האש: תויכת בתרי שקד, רשפי לוד ליקד, רחש ישנים כערב, דם תבוסה כעורב, קץ חש וקרב (שבת פרש' החדש, קיחת עלית).
— נִתפע', *נִתּוֹקַד: קרוב למאה ושש עשרה שנה היתה האש מתוקדת בו (בהמזבח) עצו לא נשרף ונחשתו לא ניתך (מד"ר ויקר' ז).
— נִפע', °נוֹקֵד, נוֹקְדוּ, — כמו הָפעל: מיקוד מעצבי נוקדו הצלעות, ומדמי הלבבות אדמו הדמעות (מטמוני המבורג, פזמנ' לצו"ג, המגיד יו 425).
en: Intransitive verb, יֹקֵד, יֹקֶדֶת, future יֵקַד, תִּיקַד — the fire יָקְדָה, burned, blazed, German brennen, French brûler, English to burn: "These are a smoke in My nose, a fire that burns (יֹקֶדֶת) all the day" (Isaiah 65:5). "And under his glory there shall be kindled (יֵקַד) a burning like the burning of fire" (ibid. 10:16). "For a fire is kindled in My nostril, and burns (וַתִּיקַד) unto the depths of the nether-world" (Deuteronomy 32:22). — And Ben Sira said: "In the congregation of the wicked a fire burns (יוקדת), and in an impious nation wrath is kindled" (Ben Sira, Geniza 16:6). — And past *יָקְדוּ: "The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: Yesterday My stacks burned (יקדו), and you come to add trouble" (Yalkut Deuteronomy 808). — And the liturgical poet said: "My haters were diligent and burned (ויקדו) the parchment of the law; alas, how was Your testimony likened to a hammer" (Rabbi Eleazar Kallir, Kinot for Tisha b'Av, "Tziyon Tzefirat"). "Explanation of burning: my doors will be diligent; whom will You punish by its law? Pour molten lead, burning (ליקוד)" (Azharot of Rabbi Elijah the Elder, קמ"ג 62). "Your lambs You warned to bring their shekels early; You knew the future and sought the watchful; to provide extinguishing for the burning (יוקדים) flame, for those taken to death, to be remembered for revival" (Selichot for the Fast of Esther, "Atah HaEl"). — And passive participle, °יָקוּד, יְקוּדָה, like יֹקֵד: "It is a positive commandment that there be a burning (יקודה) fire on the altar continually" (Rambam, Temidin u-Musafin 2:1). — And the poet said: "And if cassia and cinnamon and calamus are burning (יקודים) upon censers in the banquet-house, and if the scent of frankincense and aloes and the scent of clusters of precious henna" (Rabbi Moses Dar'i, לקו"ק 53).

— Huf'al, הוּקַד, יוּקַד, תּוּקַד — like יָקַד: "And the fire upon the altar shall be kept burning (תּוּקַד) thereby, it shall not go out" (Leviticus 6:5). "For a fire is kindled in My nostril, which shall burn (תּוּקָד) [Note: So for the Westerners; for the Easterners תיקר is written and תוקד is read.] upon you" (Jeremiah 15:14). "For you have kindled a fire in My nostril, which shall burn (תּוּקָד) for ever" (ibid. 17:4). — And participle: "The fire that burns (המוקד) on the altar" (Tanhuma Tzav 14). "The altar was burning (מוקד) with fire" (Yalkut Deuteronomy 808).

— Pi'el, °יִקֵּד, transitive verb — יִקֵּד the fire: "Her midst was melted by fiery coals, the flames of Lod to burn (ליקד); creeping things of old as at evening, blood of trampling like a raven; the end hastened and drew near" (Sabbath of Parashat HaHodesh, "Kihat Alit").
— Nitpa'el, *נִתּוֹקַד: "For nearly one hundred and sixteen years the fire was burning (מתוקדת) on it (on the altar), yet its wood was not burned and its bronze was not melted" (Leviticus Rabbah 7).

— Nif'al, °נוֹקֵד, נוֹקְדוּ — like Huf'al: "From the burning of my griefs the ribs were set on fire (נוקדו), and from the blood of the hearts the tears grew red" (Matmonei Hamburg, hymns for צו"ג, HaMaggid 16, 425).

he: , — קל לא נמצא.

—  הִפע', הוֹקִיעַ, צווי הוֹקַע, הוֹקַעֲנוּם, וַיֹּקִיעֻם, —  הוֹקִיעוֹ, תלה אותו, צלב אותו, kruezigen; crucifier; crucifix: קח את כל ראשי העם (שחטאו בבעל פעור) וְהוֹקַע אותם ליי' נגד השמש (במד' כה ד).  ינתן לנו שבעה אנשים מבניו וְהוֹקַעֲנוּם ליי' בגבעת שאול (ש"ב כא ו).  ויתנם (דוד את ילדי רצפה) ביד הגבענים וַיֹּקִיעֻם בהר לפני יי' ויפלו שבעתים יחד (שם ט).  למלך שעשה סעודה והיה לו שני שונאים וזימן אותם וכו' הוציאם והוקיעם זה כנגד זה (פסיק' דר"כ, זכור).
—  הָפע', הוּקַע, מוּקַע, מוּקָעִים, — שהוקיעו אותו:  ויאספו את עצמות הַמּוּקָעִים (ש"ב כא יג).
en: , — The Qal is not found.

— Hif'il, הוֹקִיעַ, imperative הוֹקַע, הוֹקַעֲנוּם, וַיֹּקִיעֻם, — הוֹקִיעוֹ, hanged him, crucified him, German kruezigen, French crucifier, English crucifix: "Take all the chiefs of the people (who sinned with Baal Peor) and hang them up (וְהוֹקַע) unto the Lord before the sun" (Numbers 25:4). "Let seven men of his sons be given to us, and we will hang them up (וְהוֹקַעֲנוּם) unto the Lord in Gibeah of Saul" (2 Samuel 21:6). "And he (David) delivered them (the children of Rizpah) into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them (וַיֹּקִיעֻם) on the mountain before the Lord, and the seven fell together" (ibid. 9). "Like a king who made a feast and had two enemies, and he invited them, etc.; he brought them out and hanged them (והוקיעם) opposite each other" (Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, Zakhor).
— Huf'al, הוּקַע, מוּקַע, מוּקָעִים, — whom they hanged: "And they gathered the bones of those who were hanged (הַמּוּקָעִים)" (2 Samuel 21:13).

he: , פ"ע, עת' יֵקַע, תֵּקַע — א) יֵָקַע הדבר ממקומו, נשמט ויצא ממקומו, למשל האבר ממקום הפרק, sich verrenken; se disloquer; be dislocated: ויותר יעקב לבדו ויאבק איש עמו וכו' וירא כי לא יכל לו ויגע בכף ירכו וַתֵּקַע כף ירך יעקב בהאבקו עמו (בראש' לב כה=כו).  — ב) בהשאלה, יָקְעָה הנפש מפלוני, נטתה ממנו, התרחקה ממנו, לא רצתה בו, sich v. jem. entfremden; se détourner de qqn.  be alienated: הוסרי ירושלם פן תִּקַע נפשי ממך (ירמ' ו ח).  ויבאו אליה בני בבל למשכב דדים ויטמאו אותה בתזנותם ותטמא בם וַתֵּקַע נפשה מהם ותגל  תזנותיה ותגל את ערותה וַתֵּקַע נפשי מעליה יחזק' כג יז=יח.  — ועי' נקע.
en: , intransitive verb, future יֵקַע, תֵּקַע — a) יֵָקַע הדבר ממקומו, the thing slipped and came out of its place, for example a limb from the place of the joint, German sich verrenken, French se disloquer, English be dislocated: "And Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him, etc. And when he saw that he could not prevail against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was dislocated (וַתֵּקַע) as he wrestled with him" (Genesis 32:25-26). — b) figuratively, יָקְעָה הנפש מפלוני, the soul turned away from someone, distanced itself from him, did not want him, German sich v. jem. entfremden, French se détourner de qqn., English be alienated: "Be instructed, O Jerusalem, lest My soul be alienated (תִּקַע) from you" (Jeremiah 6:8). "And the Babylonians came to her into the bed of love, and they defiled her with their harlotry, and she was defiled with them, and her soul was alienated (וַתֵּקַע) from them; and she uncovered her harlotries and uncovered her nakedness, and My soul was alienated (וַתֵּקַע) from her" Ezekiel 23:17-18. — And see נקע.

he: פ"ע, עת' אִיקַץ, יִיקַץ, וָאִיקָץ, וַיִּיקַץ, וַיִּקַּץ, וַיִּיקֶץ, בהפס' יִקָץ, מ"ר יִקְצוּ, — יָקַץ מִשֵׁנָתוֹ, עזבתהו השֵנה, שב להיות עֵר, erwachen; se réveiller; to awake : בחלמי הנני עמד על שפת היאר והנה מן היאר עלת שבע פרות וכו' ותאכלנה הפרות הרקות והרעות וכו' ומראיהן רע כאשר בתחלה וָאִיקָץ (בראש' מא יז-כא).  וַיִּיקֶץ נח מיינו (בראש' ט כד).  וַיִּיקַץ יעקב משנתו (בראש' כח יו). וַיִּיקַץ פרעה והנה חלום (בראש' מא ז).  וַיִּיקַץ משנתו ויסע את היתד (שופט' יו יד).  וַיִּקַץ משנתו (שם כ).  וַיִּקַּץ שלמה והנה חלום (מ"א ג יא).  אולי ישן הוא וְיִקֶָץ (שם יח כז).  — ובסהמ"א: בשעה שייקץ בסוף שנתו מברך הוא על מטתו (רמב"ם תפלה ז ג).  — ובהשאל': וַיִּקַץ כישן אדני כגבור מתרונן מיין (תהל' עח סה), לאמר התעורר לעשות דבר.  הלוא פתע יקומו נשכיך וְיִקְצוּאמר ריב"ג: קד ד'כר פי כתאב חרופ אללינ פי וייקצו מזעזעיך אליא' פי וייקצו מוקפה דאלה עלי אנּ בעדהא יא' והי פא' אלפעל קאל אבו אלוליד ואליא' ענדנה ע'יר מוקפה ואלמסורת עליה לית כותיה וחטף, ע"כ, ובעבר': כבר נזכר בספר אותות הרפיון ואמר ר' יהודה בויקצו מזעזעיך היוד בויקצו מעמדה מורה שאחריה יוד והיא פא הפעל ואני אומר כי היוד אצלינו איננה מעמדת והמסֹרת עליו לית דכותיה וחטף. ורד"ק, מכלול, שדה"פ), אמר וז"ל: והיוד בו מועמדת בגעיא להורות היוד פא הפעל כמו ויצקו על העולה. ע"כ. וכעין זה כתב גם בהשרשים. והביא מנחת שי: אפשר שיהיה בלא מאריך כמו שנמצא במקצת ספרים וכו' וכן נמצא במקצת ספרים בשני יודין. מזעזעיך והיית למשסות למו (חבק' ב ז).  — ואמר הפיטן: כגבור מתרונן מיין, יקץ והריק זין (יוצ' ב פסח, אפיק רנן).  — ועי' קוץ, קיץ.
en: intransitive verb, future אִיקַץ, יִיקַץ, וָאִיקָץ, וַיִּיקַץ, וַיִּקַּץ, וַיִּיקֶץ, in pause יִקָץ, plural יִקְצוּ, — יָקַץ מִשֵׁנָתוֹ, sleep left him, he became awake again, German erwachen, French se réveiller, English to awake: "In my dream, behold, I stood upon the brink of the river. And behold, there came up out of the river seven kine etc. And the lean and ill-favoured kine did eat etc., and they were still ill-favoured as at the beginning. So I awoke (וָאִיקָץ)" (Genesis 41:17-21). "And Noah awoke (וַיִּיקֶץ) from his wine" (Genesis 9:24). "And Jacob awoke (וַיִּיקַץ) out of his sleep" (Genesis 28:16). "And Pharaoh awoke (וַיִּיקַץ), and, behold, it was a dream" (Genesis 41:7). "And he awoke (וַיִּיקַץ) out of his sleep, and plucked away the pin" (Judges 16:14). "And he awoke (וַיִּקַץ) out of his sleep" (ibid. 20). "And Solomon awoke (וַיִּקַּץ), and, behold, it was a dream" (1 Kings 3:11). "Peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked (וְיִקֶָץ)" (ibid. 18:27). — And in post-biblical literature: "When he awakes at the end of his sleep, he blesses on his bed" (Rambam, Tefillah 7:3). — And figuratively: "Then the Lord awaked (וַיִּקַץ) as one out of sleep, like a mighty man recovering from wine" (Psalms 78:65), that is, roused Himself to do something. "Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee, and awake (וְיִקְצוּ) [Note: Ibn Janah said: קד ד'כר פי כתאב חרופ אללינ פי וייקצו מזעזעיך אליא' פי וייקצו מוקפה דאלה עלי אנּ בעדהא יא' והי פא' אלפעל קאל אבו אלוליד ואליא' ענדנה ע'יר מוקפה ואלמסורת עליה לית כותיה וחטף, end of quote; and in Hebrew: "It has already been mentioned in the Book of the Weak Letters, and R. Judah said regarding ויקצו מזעזעיך that the yod in ויקצו has a meteg, indicating that after it there is a yod, which is the first radical of the verb; and I say that the yod in our view does not have a meteg, and the Masorah on it is: there is none like it, and with hataf." And Radak (Mikhlol, שדה"פ) said, in these words: "And the yod in it has a meteg with ga'ya to indicate that the yod is the first radical, like ויצקו על העולה." End of quote. And he wrote something similar also in the Shorashim. And Minhat Shai cited: "It is possible that it is without a meteg (מאריך), as is found in some books etc., and likewise it is found in some books with two yods."] that shall make thee tremble, and thou shalt be for booty unto them" (Habakkuk 2:7). — And the paytan said: "Like a mighty man recovering from wine, He awoke and emptied the weapon" (Yotzer for the second day of Passover, Afik Renen). — And see קוץ, קיץ.

he: ת"ז, סמי' יְקַר, לנק' יְקָרָה, סמי' יִקְרַת, מ"ר יְקָרִים, יְקָרוֹת  — א) אבן יְקָרָה וכדומה, שצריך לשלם בעדה מחיר רב, theuer, edel; cher, précieux; dear, precious : ותבא (מלכת שבא) ירושלמה בחיל כבד מאד גמלים נשאים בשמים וזהב רב מאד ואבן יְקָרָה מ"א י ב.  וגם אני חירם אשר נשא זהב מאופיר הביא מאפיר עצי אלמגים הרבה מאד ואבן יְקָרָה שם יא.  בעדן גן אלהים היית כל אבן יְקָרָה מסכתך אדם פטדה ויהלם יחזק' כח יג.  לא תסלה בכתם אופיר בשהם יָקָר וספיר איוב כח יו.  —  וגם שמלאכתם עולה במחיר רב: ויצו המלך ויסעו אבנים גדלות אבנים יְקָרוֹת ליסד הבית מ"א ה לא.  ומלמעלה אבנים יְקָרוֹת כמדות גזית וארז שם ז יא.  —  והון יָקָר, שמחירו רב: כל הון יָקָר נמצא נמלא בתינו שלל משלי א יג.  ובדעת חדרים ימלאו כל הון יָקָר ונעים שם כד ד.  —  ב) אדם יָקָר, טוב, יפה, נכבד, חשוב: בני ציון הַיְקָרִים המסלאים בפז איכ' ד ב.  —  ומ"ר לנק' יְקָרוֹת, יִקְרוֹתֶיךָ: בנות מלכים בִּיקְּרוֹתֶיךָכך פרשו רוב המפרשים, אך עי' בערך בִּקְרָה ובהערה שם בענין מלה זו. תהל' מה י.  —  ולנק' בסמי' *יִקְרַת: היה ירמיה הולך ובוכה וכך אמר חבל עליך יקרת המדינות פסיק' רבתי כו.  —  יְקַר רוח, שרוחו יָקָר, טוב ומשֻבח: יְקַרכתיב וקר. רוח איש תבונה משלי יז כז.  —  וכמו שֵׁם, יָקָר, דבר יָקָר: ואם תוציא יָקָר מזולל ירמ' יה יט.  —  ודבר יָקָר, גם מפשט, נחמד, חשוב, טוב מאד: יָקָר מחכמה מכבוד קהל' י א.  מה-יָּקָראמר ריב"ג: ואעלמ אנ מה יקר חסדך קמוץ אליא' ואלקאפ פאלאקרב ענדי אנ יכונ צפה וכו' אלא אנה ענד אבי זכריא פעל מאצ', ע"כ, ובעבר': ודע כי מה יקר היוד והקוף בקמץ, והוא לפי דעתי תאר, אלא שהוא אצל אבי זכריה (ר"י חיוג) פעל עבר. ורצה ריב"ג להוכיח מזה שבספרו של ר"י חיוג היה יקר פתוחה הקוף, אעפ"י שאפשר גם פעל עבר בשני קמצים. חסדך אלהים תהל' לו ח.  יָקָר בעיני יי' המותה לחסידיו שם קיו יה.  יְקָרָה היא (החכמה) מפניים משלי ג יה.  ואשת איש נפש יְקָרָה תצוד שם ו כו.  —  ובמשמ' יפה ונהדר: וירח יָקָר הלך איוב לא כו.  —  דבר לא מצוי, לא תדיר, selten; rare; scarce: ודבר יי' היה יָקָר בימים ההם אין חזון נפרץ ש"א ג א.  —  ובתו"מ, במשמ' שמחירו רב: פרה דדמיה יקרין שבת נב..  ובדמו (של החלזון) צובעין תכלת לפיכך דמיו יקרים מנח' מד..  —  ואדם יָקָר, במשמ' נכבד וחשוב: ואינו דומה המתבייש מן היקר למתבייש מן הפגום תוספתא ב"ק ט יב.  עמדו יקרים עמודו שבו יקרים שבו מגי' כג:.  נשים יקרות שבירושלם היו מתנדבות ומביאות אותן לא התנדבו נשים יקרות  משל מי וכו' משל צבור סנה' מג..  וכן הנשים היקרות לא ויתר להם בדין זה רב אלפס אלא לשגר להם סופרי הדיינין ולטעון בפניהם טוחו"מ קכד א.  —  וכנוי של כבוד לאיש ולאשה: באותה שעה בא היקר ה"ר שם טוב וכו' שו"ת תמת ישרים א.  היקרה מרת יוטא אשת מנדלין וכו' פנק' ההקדש דק"ק וירמייזא 14.  בפנינו עדים חתומי מטה באו היקרה מ' קלארה אלמנת ה"ר יוסף וארון ובנותיה וכו' והגיסים היקרים הר' שמואל לוי והר' שלמה ארזיק ונתפשרו ביניהם שו"ת פרח מטה אהרן ז.  באה היקרה דינה שמחה ובעלה וכו' והיקרה דונה שם יג.  נכנסנו לבקר את היקרה מ' ריינה שם קכא.  —  ובמשמ' חביבה ואהובה: כי עתה הנה אשתי אהובתי יקרתי עמכם ואשת נעורים היא יוסיפון, פרק ק.
en: masculine adjective, construct יְקַר, feminine יְקָרָה, construct יִקְרַת, plural יְקָרִים, יְקָרוֹת — a) A יְקָרָה stone and the like, for which one must pay a high price, German theuer, edel; French cher, précieux; English dear, precious: "And she (the queen of Sheba) came to Jerusalem with a very great retinue, camels bearing spices and very much gold and יְקָרָה (precious) stone" 1 Kings 10:2. "And also the ships of Hiram, which carried gold from Ophir, brought from Ophir a great many almug trees and יְקָרָה (precious) stone" ibid. 11. "You were in Eden, the garden of God; every יְקָרָה (precious) stone was your covering: carnelian, topaz and diamond" Ezekiel 28:13. "It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the יָקָר (precious) onyx or the sapphire" Job 28:16. — And also [stones] whose working costs a high price: "And the king commanded, and they quarried great stones, יְקָרוֹת (costly) stones, to lay the foundation of the house" 1 Kings 5:31. "And above were יְקָרוֹת (costly) stones, hewn according to measure, and cedar" ibid. 7:11. — And הון יָקָר, whose price is high: "We shall find all יָקָר (precious) wealth, we shall fill our houses with spoil" Proverbs 1:13. "And by knowledge are the chambers filled with all יָקָר (precious) and pleasant wealth" ibid. 24:4. — b) A יָקָר person, good, fine, honored, important: "The הַיְקָרִים (precious) sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold" Lamentations 4:2. — And the feminine plural יְקָרוֹת, יִקְרוֹתֶיךָ: "Kings' daughters are among your בִּיקְּרוֹתֶיךָ (honorable women)"[Note: So most of the commentators explained, but see the entry בִּקְרָה and the note there regarding this word.] Psalms 45:10. — And the feminine in the construct *יִקְרַת: "Jeremiah was walking and weeping, and thus he said: Woe to you, יקרת (most precious) of the countries" Pesikta Rabbati 26. — יְקַר רוח, whose spirit is יָקָר, good and praiseworthy: "A man of understanding is of יְקַר (cool/precious)[Note: The written text is וקר.] spirit" Proverbs 17:27. — And as a noun, יָקָר, a יָקָר thing: "And if you bring forth the יָקָר (precious) from the vile" Jeremiah 15:19. — And a יָקָר thing, also abstract, delightful, important, very good: "יָקָר (weightier) than wisdom and than honor" Ecclesiastes 10:1. "How יָּקָר[Note: Ibn Janah said: ואעלמ אנ מה יקר חסדך קמוץ אליא' ואלקאפ פאלאקרב ענדי אנ יכונ צפה וכו' אלא אנה ענד אבי זכריא פעל מאצ', end of quote; and in Hebrew: "And know that in מה יקר the yod and the qof are with qamatz, and it is in my opinion an adjective, except that according to Abu Zakariya (Rabbi Judah Hayyuj) it is a past-tense verb." And Ibn Janah wanted to prove from this that in the book of Rabbi Judah Hayyuj יקר had a patach under the qof, even though a past-tense verb is also possible with two qamatzes.] (precious) is Your lovingkindness, O God" Psalms 36:8. "יָקָר (precious) in the eyes of the Lord is the death of His pious ones" ibid. 116:15. "She (wisdom) is more יְקָרָה (precious) than rubies" Proverbs 3:15. "And a married woman hunts for a יְקָרָה (precious) life" ibid. 6:26. — And in the sense of beautiful and splendid: "Or the moon walking in יָקָר (brightness)" Job 31:26. — A thing not found, not frequent, German selten; French rare; English scarce: "And the word of the Lord was יָקָר (rare) in those days; there was no open vision" 1 Samuel 3:1. — And in the Talmud and Midrash, in the sense of: whose price is high: "A cow whose price is high" Shabbat 52a. "And with its (the chilazon's) blood they dye blue; therefore its price is high" Menachot 44a. — And a יָקָר person, in the sense of honored and important: "And one who is shamed by a יקר (respectable person) is not like one who is shamed by a blemished one" Tosefta Bava Kamma 9:12. "Stand, honored ones, stand; sit, honored ones, sit" Megillah 23b. "The יקרות (distinguished) women of Jerusalem would donate and bring them; if the distinguished women did not donate, from whose [funds] etc.? From the community's" Sanhedrin 43a. "And likewise the היקרות (distinguished) women — Rav Alfas did not waive this law for them, except to send the judges' scribes to them and to plead before them" Tur Choshen Mishpat 124:1. — And as an honorific for a man and a woman: "At that hour came the honorable Rabbi Shem Tov etc." Responsa Tummat Yesharim 1. "The honorable Mistress Yuta, wife of Mendlin etc." Pinkas of the Hekdesh of the holy community of Worms 14. "Before us, the undersigned witnesses, came the honorable Mistress Clara, widow of Rabbi Yosef Varon, and her daughters etc., and the honorable brothers-in-law Rabbi Shmuel Levi and Rabbi Shlomo Arzik, and they came to a compromise between them" Responsa Perach Matteh Aharon 7. "The honorable Dinah Simchah and her husband came etc. and the honorable Dona" ibid. 13. "We went in to visit the honorable Mistress Reina" ibid. 121. — And in the sense of dear and beloved: "For now, behold, my wife, my beloved, my dear one, is with you, and she is the wife of my youth" Yosippon, chapter 100.

he: פ"ע, עב' יָקֹשְׁתִּי, יָקְשׁוּ, יְקֹשׁוּן, — יָקֹשׁ לפלוני, שָׂם לו מוֹקֵשׁ: יָקֹשְׁתִּי לך וגם נלכדת בבל ואת לא ידעת (ירמ' נ כד).  מחטיא אדם בדבר ולמוכיח בשער יְקֹשׁוּן ויטו בתהו צדיק  (ישע' כט כא).  שמרני מיד פח יָקְשׁוּ לי (תהל' קמא ט).  — והשתמש בו הפיטן גם במשמ' נִפעל: יקשו צרי עין בבצע, ומאנו פרוסה לרעב לבצע, והאריכו וקצרו את המצע (יוצ' אחרון פסח, מה מועיל).  — וכמו פ"י, °גרם לו שיוקָש: טרדונו עונות, יקשונו זדונות, כסתנו כלימה, לכן קצרו לשונות (סמא"צ, נעי' יוה"כ, אשר לנו).  — ופָעוּל יוּקָשׁ: כי גם לא ידע האדם את עתו כדגים שנאחזים במצודה רעה וכצפרים האחזות בפח כהם יוּקָשִׁים בני האדם לעת רעה כשתפול עליהם פתאם (קהל' ט יב).  — ובמליצה, °יוֹקֵשׁ, כנוי ליצר הרע: יום יוקשי תכבוש ועצבי תחבוש, יהי לבי תמים בחקיך למען לא אבוש (רשב"ג, רשות לנשמת, אלהים אלי).  — ופָעוּל, °יָקוּשׁ, יְקוּשָׁה: אמללנו בנפש יקושה, נאנחנו מעבודה קשה (רמב"ע, מוס' יוה"כ, אמללנו).  יקוש בעניו, ולכוד בפח חבלו, וצבי עדיו, הורד ועגילו (שבת ה' אחה"פ, יקוש בעניו).  קומי יונה יקושה, עורי אבן הראשה (ספ' פזמונ', תימנ' כט).  —  ואמר המליץ: תמול שאלוני ידועי זמני למי אוי ואבוי ואל מי פצעים, עניתים לטפשים אנושים יקושים בפח איש תככים ולשוא ינעים (שלמה בונאפיד, דברי חכמ' פז).  שמע זעקת דל אסיר זקן ומחלה אשר רגלו בפח קלון יקושה (משלי ערב, דרך טובים).  — ובהשאלה, במשמ' °זמם: יקש לץ לחרף צבאות, החתומי ברית בצבא ואות (שבת זכור, אצילי).

— נִפע', נוֹקֵשׁ, נוַֹקְשָּת, נוֹקְשׁוּ, תִּוָּקֵשׁ, — שיקשו לו, שנלכד במוקש: בפעל כפיו נוֹקֵשׁ רשע (תהל' ט יז).  והיה וכו' לפח ולמוקש ליושב ירושלם וכשלו בם רבים ונפלו ונשברו וְנוֹקְשׁוּ ונלכדו (ישע' ח יד-יה).  — ובהשאלה, נוֹקַשׁ בדבר, נכשל בו: לא תחמד כסף וזהב עליהם ולקחת לך פן תִּוָּקֵשׁ בו (דבר' ז כה).  — ונוֹקַש בדבריו, נאחז בענין ע"י דבריו: בני אם ערבת לרעך תקעת לזר כפיך נוֹקַשְׁתָּ באמרי פיך נלכדת באמרי פיך עשה זאת אפוא בני והנצל כי באת בכף רעך לך התרפס ורהב רעיך (משלי ו א-ג).  — ואמר בן סירא: בבתולה אל תתבונן פן תוקש בעונשיה (ב"ס גני' ט ה).  רבים היו חבולי זהב והבוטח על פנינים כי תקלה הוא לאויל וכל פותה יוקש בו (שם לד ו-ז).  דורש תורה יפיקנה ומתלהלה יוקש בה (שם לה יה).  — ובסהמ"א: וכתוקש הנפש אל רדיפת התאות אז תגלה תפארת גדלתה (מאזני צדק אלגזלי 46).
en: Intransitive verb, past יָקֹשְׁתִּי, יָקְשׁוּ, יְקֹשׁוּן, — יָקֹשׁ for someone, to set a snare for him: "I have laid a snare for you, and you are also taken, O Babylon, and you did not know" (Jeremiah 50:24). "That make a man an offender by a word, and lay a snare for him that reproves in the gate, and turn aside the righteous with a thing of nought" (Isaiah 29:21). "Keep me from the hands of the trap which they have laid for me" (Psalms 141:9). — And the liturgical poet also used it in the sense of the Nif'al: "The stingy were ensnared by gain, and refused to break a morsel for the hungry, and lengthened and shortened the bed" (Yotzer for the last day of Passover, מה מועיל). — And as a transitive verb, °caused him to be ensnared: "Iniquities have driven us, wanton sins have ensnared us, shame has covered us, therefore tongues are cut short" (סמא"צ, Ne'ilah of Yom Kippur, אשר לנו). — And passive יוּקָשׁ: "For man also knows not his time; as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare, even so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falls suddenly upon them" (Ecclesiastes 9:12). — And in rhetoric, °יוֹקֵשׁ, an epithet for the evil inclination: "On the day You subdue my ensnarer and bind up my grief, let my heart be perfect in Your statutes, that I may not be ashamed" (Rabbi Shlomo ibn Gabirol, Reshut for Nishmat, אלהים אלי). — And passive participle, °יָקוּשׁ, יְקוּשָׁה: "We are wretched with an ensnared soul, we groan from hard labor" (Rabbi Moshe ibn Ezra, Musaf of Yom Kippur, אמללנו). "Ensnared in his affliction, and caught in the trap of his cord; and the beauty of his ornaments — brought down, with his earring" (Fifth Sabbath after Passover, יקוש בעניו). "Arise, ensnared dove; awake, chief stone" (Book of Hymns, Yemenite 29). — And the rhetorician said: "Yesterday the acquaintances of my time asked me: who has woe and who has alas, and who has wounds? I answered them: fools, men ensnared in the trap of a deceitful man, who wander about in vain" (Shlomo Bonafed, Divrei Chakhamim 87). "Hear the cry of a poor prisoner, old and sick, whose foot is ensnared in the trap of disgrace" (Mishlei Arav, Derekh Tovim). — And figuratively, in the sense of °plotted: "The scoffer plotted to revile the hosts, those sealed with the covenant with host and sign" (Shabbat Zakhor, אצילי).

— Nif'al, נוֹקֵשׁ, נוַֹקְשָּת, נוֹקְשׁוּ, תִּוָּקֵשׁ, — to have a snare set for him, to be caught in a snare: "The wicked is snared in the work of his own hands" (Psalms 9:17). "And he shall be etc. for a trap and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and many shall stumble thereon, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken" (Isaiah 8:14-15). — And figuratively, נוֹקַשׁ in a thing, to stumble in it: "You shall not covet the silver or the gold that is on them, nor take it to yourself, lest you be snared by it" (Deuteronomy 7:25). — And נוֹקַש by his words, to be caught in a matter through his words: "My son, if you have become surety for your neighbor, if you have struck your hands for a stranger, you are snared by the words of your mouth, you are caught by the words of your mouth. Do this now, my son, and deliver yourself, seeing you have come into the hand of your neighbor; go, humble yourself, and urge your neighbor" (Proverbs 6:1-3). — And Ben Sira said: "Do not gaze at a virgin, lest you be ensnared in penalties on her account" (Ben Sira, Genizah 9:5). "Many have been ruined by gold, and he who trusts in pearls; for it is a stumbling block to the fool, and every simpleton is ensnared by it" (ibid. 34:6-7). "He who seeks the Torah will obtain it, but the hypocrite will be ensnared by it" (ibid. 35:15). — And in medieval literature: "And when the soul is ensnared in the pursuit of lust, then the glory of its greatness is revealed" (Moznei Tzedek, al-Ghazali 46).

מִיִּרְאָתוֹ אתו ש"ב ג יא. מי לא יִרָאֲךָ מלך הגוים ירמ' י ז. ואתנם לו מורא וַיִּירָאֵנִי מלא' ב ה לא תִּירָאוּם כי יי' אלהיכם הוא הנלחם לכם דבר' ג כב. ויי' אתנו לא תִּירָאֻם במד' יד ט. למען יִרָאוּךָ כל הימים מ"א ח מ. גוים עריצים יִירָאוּךָ ישע' כה ג. יִירָאוּךָ עם שמש תהל' עב ה. — ובמליצה לדברים לא בע"ח: ארץ יָרְאָה ושקטה תהל' עו ט.  אל תִּירְאִי אדמה גילי ושמחי כי הגדיל יי' לעשות יוא' ב כא.

— נִפע', נוֹרָא, נוֹרָאָה, נוֹרָאוֹת, נוֹרָאֹת, תִּוָּרֵא, — שיראו ממנו, שאפשר לירא ממנו, שהכל יראים ממנו: ויאמר מה־נּוֹרָא המקום הזה בראש' כח יז. אל גדול וְנוֹרָא דבר' ז כא. נוֹרָא יי' עליהם כי רזה את כל אלהי הארץ צפנ' ב יא. כי עמך הסליחה למען תִּוָּרֵא תהל' קל ד. —  ועי' עוד ערך נוֹרָא.

— פִע', יֵרֵא, יַרְאֻנִי, מְיָרְאִים, לְיָרְאֵנִי, לְיָרְאָם, — יֵרֵא אותו, הטיל עליו אימה ופחד, in Furcht setzen; faire craindre; to put in fear: ועתה אשר באתי לדבר אל המלך אדוני את הדבר הזה כי יֵרְאֻנִי העם (שימיתו את בנה) ותאמר שפחתך אדברה נא אל המלך אולי יעשה המלך את דבר אמתו ש"ב יד יה. כי כלם מְיָרְאִים אותנו לאמר ירפו ידיהם מן המלאכה נחמ' ו ט. אגרות שלח טוביה לְיָרְאֵנִי שם יט. ויקראו בקול גדול יהודית על עם ירושלם אשר על החומה לְיָרְאָם ולבהלם למען ילכדו את העיר דהי"ב לב יח. — ובתו"מ: יעקב היה מזכיר לעשו שמו של הקב"ה ליראו ולבהלו מד"ר בראש' עה. כך הם ישראל כשהם חוטאים אין הקב"ה מעלה עליהם תדע לך שהוא כן שכן בימי הושע הכעיסו להקב"ה התחיל הקב"ה מייראן כי בני זנונים וגו' כי היא לא אשתי וגו' שם במד' ב. אין מיראין את האדם אלא בדבר שהוא יגור ממנו רש"י דבר' כח ס. כאשר אמר אדון הנביאים ע"ה על המצות המעשיות ויראת מאלקיך אני יי' שעל המצות המעשיות הוצרך ליראם מעונשי השם ר"י א"ת, רוח חן ג.  יזלזל במצוה מן המצות המיראות את האדם מלמ' התלמיד', עקב.

—  הִתפע', *הִתְיָרֵא, *נִתְיָרֵא, —  היה יָרֵא, התחיל פתאם לירא: אל תהי כאריה בביתך ומוזר ומתירא בעבודתך ב"ס גני' ד ל. וגם אם ישמע לך (השונא) ויהלך בנחת תן לבך להתירא ממנו שם יב יא. המכבה את הנר מפני שהוא מתירא מפני עכו"ם מפני לסטים מפני רוח רעה שבת ב ה. וכשהגיע (אגריפס) ללא תוכל לשים עליך איש נכרי זלגו עיניו דמעות אמרו לו אל תתירא אגריפס אחינו אתה סוט' ז ח. שכל העופות כולן נותנין את בניהם תחת רגליהם מפני שהן מתייראין מעוף אחר שהוא פורח על גביהם אבל הנשר הזה אינו מתירא אלא מאדם בלבד שלא יזרוק בו חץ מכי' יתרו, בחדש ב. שהייתי סבור שהוא יום הדין ונתייראתי ירוש' חגי' ב עז.. אם שמואל רבן של נביאים וכו' נתיירא מיום הדין אנו על אחת כמה וכמה שם. ואמר לי היה לך להתפלל בדרך ואמרתי לו מתיירא הייתי שמא יפסיקו בי עוברי דרכים ברכ' ג.. היה מתיירא מפני נכרים ומפני לסטים שם יח.. ומה במקום חיותנו אנו מתייראים במקום מיתתנו עאכ"ו שם סא:. שאלות הרבה יש לי לשאול ומתיירא אני שמא תכעוס שבת לא.. אמר (משה) לפניו רבש"ע מתיירא אני שמא ישרפוני בהבל שבפיהם שם פח:. אמר להם מפני מה אתם מכניסין ראשי בין ב' הרים גדולים בין ב' מחלוקות גדולות בין בית שמאי ובין בית הלל מתיירא אני שמא ירוצו גלגלתי יבמ' טו:. אחינו בני ישראל שמעו אחינו פלוני נשא אשה שאינה הוגנת לו מתייראים אנו שמא יתערב זרעו בזרעינו כתוב' כח:. לאדם שהיה מהלך באישון לילה ואפילה ומתיירא מן הקוצים ומן הפחתים ומן הברקנים ומחיה רעה סוט' כא.. עד שלא נתקיימה נבואתו של אוריה הייתי מתיירא שלא תתקיים נבואתו של זכריה עכשיו שנתקיימה נבואתו של אוריה בידוע שנבואתו של זכריה מתקיימת מכות כד:. היה משכים לצאת לדרך ומתיירא שמא יאבדו מנח' לו.. ויאמר שלחני כי עלה השחר אמר לו גנב אתה או קוביוסטוס אתה שמתיירא מן השחר חול' צא:. אמרה לו אעפ"י שאנשי צדוקים הן (נשותיהם) מתיראות מן הפרושים ומראות דם לחכמים נדה לג:. זה נתיירא מזה וזה נתיירא מזה מד"ר בראש' מד. והגר שפחת שרי רואה ה' מלאכים בזה אחר זה ולא נתייראה מהם שם מה. לאחד שהיה מהלך בדרך וראה כת של כלבים ונתיירא מהם וישב לו ביניהם שם פד. שני בני אדם הבטיחן הקב"ה ונתייראו הבחור שבאבות והבחור שבנביאים שם עו. אותה שעה נתברר משה על עסקיו שנתיירא אם ישאלו לו מה שמו מה יאמר להם שם שמות ג. אמר לו הקב"ה למשה לך אמור לו לאהרן אל תתירא לגדולה מזו אתה מתוקן שם במד' טו. בשעה שהיו הנביאים הולכים בשליחותו של הקב"ה רוח הקדש שהיתה שורה עליהם היתה נותנת להם אימה בעיני רואיהם שהכל מתיראים מהם שהיו דומין למלאכים שם י. אותה שעה (שראה משה את עוג) נתיירא משה אמר הקב"ה אל תתיירא שאני מפילו לפניך שם דבר' א. עד שלא חטא אדם הראשון היה שומע קול הדיבור עומד על רגליו ולא היה מתיירא כיון שחטא כששמע קול הדיבור נתיירא ונתחבא שם שה"ש, הנה מטתו. למלך שדיבר כנגד בנו ונתירא ונשמטה נפשו ממנו שם, חכו. באותה שעה נתיירא משה אמר בלבו תאמר רוח הקדש נסתלקה ממני שם, יפה את. הלך ירמיה למערת המכפלה ואמר לאבות העולם עמדו שהגיע זמן שאתם מתבקשין לפני הקדוש ברוך הוא אמרו לו למה אמר להם איני יודע מפני שהיה מתירא שלא יאמרו בימיך היתה לבנינו זאת שם איכ', פתיח'. שלחו (כל בני הגולה למרדכי ואסתר) ואמרו לא דיינו צרותיו של המן אלא שאתם מטריחין עלינו לעשות שני הימים האלה ואמר להם אם מדבר זה אתם מתייראין והרי היא כתובה בין הכרכי' שם רות, והנה בועז. אין את בתו של אברהם וכו' ואת מתיירא מן ברייה ומן אנוש שהיום הוא חי ולמחר הוא מת פסיק' רבתי לג. אתם רואים את השמים במקומם ואת הארץ במקומה ואתם מתייראים שם.

dwell in Zoar” (Genesis 19:30). “And he said, ‘She is my sister,’ for he feared to say, ‘My wife,’ lest the men of the place should kill me” (ibid. 26:7). “How were you not afraid to stretch forth your hand to destroy the Lord's anointed?” (2 Samuel 1:14). “Why then were you not afraid to speak against My servant Moses?” (Numbers 8:12). “But if you fear to go down, go down with Purah your servant” (Judges 7:10). “So the Arameans feared to help the children of Ammon any more” (2 Samuel 10:19). — And יָרֵא מעשות דבר, afraid of doing something: “And Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look upon God” (Exodus 3:7). “And Samuel feared to tell Eli the vision” (1 Samuel 3:15). “Do not fear to go down into Egypt” (Genesis 46:3). “Do not fear to serve the Chaldeans” (Jeremiah 40:9). “and they were afraid to come near him” (Exodus 34:30). — And יָרֵא מפלוני, מפני פלוני, מלפני פלוני, מדבר פלוני, to fear someone or something: “So shall the Lord your God do to all the peoples of whom
