Assemble yourselves, and let us enter into the fortified cities” (Jeremiah 8:14). — And to stay for a time: “And she shall continue in the blood of purification thirty-three days” (Leviticus 12:4). “And stay with him a few days” (Genesis 27:44). “Stay until you have weaned him etc. And the woman stayed, and nursed her son until she weaned him” (1 Samuel 1:23). “Glory in it, and stay at home; for why should you meddle with harm?” (2 Kings 14:10). “Then I came to the exiles etc., and I sat there seven days, appalled, among them” (Ezekiel 3:15). — יָשַׁב לפלוני: to wait for him: “You shall sit still for me many days; you shall not play the harlot, and you shall not be any man's” (Hosea 3:3). — יָשַׁב עם פלוני: to have dealings with him, to associate with him: “I have not sat with men of falsehood, nor will I go in with dissemblers. I hate the gathering of evildoers, and will not sit with the wicked” (Psalms 26:4–5). — יָשַׁב בסוד משחקים and the like: to be with them: “I did not sit in the assembly of those who make merry, nor rejoice” (Jeremiah 15:17). “Nor sat in the seat of the scornful” (Psalms 1:1). — b) יָשַׁב in a house, in a land: to live in it, to dwell there, German whonen; French demeurer; English to dwell, inhabit: “Abram dwelt in the land of Canaan, and Lot dwelt in the cities of the plain” (Genesis 13:12). “And he shall dwell in that city until he stands before the congregation for judgment” (Joshua 20:6). “And I will bring him (the boy, to the sanctuary), that he may appear before the LORD, and abide there forever” (1 Samuel 1:22). “And she shall put off the garment of her captivity from her, and shall remain in your house” (Deuteronomy 21:13). “Come down to me, do not tarry; and you shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you shall be near me” (Genesis 45:9–10). “And you dispossess them, and dwell in their land” (Deuteronomy 12:29). “And you dispossess them (the nations), and dwell in their cities and in their houses” (ibid. 19:1). “And you build goodly houses and dwell in them” (ibid. 8:12). “And you possess it (the land), and dwell in it” (ibid. 17:14). “The Emim dwelt there in times past” (ibid. 2:10). “Your fathers dwelt beyond the River of old” (Joshua 24:2). “And they shall build houses and inhabit them, and they shall plant vineyards and eat their fruit” (Isaiah 65:21). “And they shall dwell in their own land” (Jeremiah 23:8). “The land of Egypt, in which you dwelt” (Leviticus 18:3). “And you shall dwell in the land in safety. And the land shall yield her fruit, and you shall eat your fill, and dwell therein in safety” (ibid. 25:18–19). “For you know how we dwelt in the land of Egypt” (Deuteronomy 29:15). “And the Canaanite and the Perizzite dwelt then in the land” (Genesis 13:7). “And he dwelt in Sodom” (ibid. 14:12). “Amalek dwells in the land of the South; and the Hittite, and the Jebusite, and the Amorite dwell in the mountains; and the Canaanite dwells by the sea and along the Jordan” (Numbers 13:29). “And you shall not defile the land which you inhabit” (ibid. 35:34). “And they heard that they were their neighbors, and that they dwelt among them” (Joshua 9:16). “The house of Israel, dwelling in their own land, defiled it by their ways” (Ezekiel 36:17). “The children of Esau, who dwell in Seir” (Deuteronomy 2:4). “After Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Canaan” (Genesis 16:3). “For he feared to dwell in Zoar” (ibid. 19:30). “For He is your life and the length of your days, that you may dwell in the land which the LORD swore to your fathers” (Deuteronomy 30:20). “And Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers, that they should not dwell in Shechem” (Judges 9:41). “For your servant vowed a vow while I dwelt at Geshur in Aram” (2 Samuel 15:8). “Nor to build houses for us to dwell in; and we have neither vineyard, nor field, nor seed” (Jeremiah 35:9). “Because it (the land) did not rest on your Sabbaths, when you dwelt upon it” (Leviticus 26:35). “And so it was, at the beginning of their dwelling there, that they did not fear the LORD” (2 Kings 17:25). “All their trespasses which they committed against Me, when they dwell safely in their land” (Ezekiel 39:26). “Behold, my land is before you; dwell where it pleases you” (Genesis 20:15). “Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans; dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon” (2 Kings 25:24). “Turn again now, every one from his evil way, and from the evil of your doings, and dwell in the land that the LORD has given to you” (Jeremiah 25:5). “Build houses and dwell in them, and plant gardens and eat their fruit” (ibid. 29:5). “Let them give me a place in one of the towns in the country, that I may dwell there; for why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?” (1 Samuel 27:5). “You shall build a house, and you shall not dwell in it” (Deuteronomy 28:30). “He shall dwell with you, in your midst, in the place which he shall choose within one of your gates” (ibid. 23:17). “For a people shall dwell in Zion” (Isaiah 30:19). “They shall not build and another inhabit; they shall not plant and another eat” (ibid. 65:22). “No man shall dwell there (in Edom), nor shall any son of man sojourn in it” (Jeremiah 49:18). “And he dwelt in the land of Nod” (Genesis 4:16). “And he (Abram) came and dwelt by the terebinths of Mamre, which are in Hebron” (ibid. 13:18). “And Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites” (Numbers 21:25). “If you say: We will not dwell in this land” (Jeremiah 42:13). “And we dwelt in Egypt a long time” (Numbers 20:15). “Would that we had been content and dwelt beyond the Jordan!” (Joshua 7:7). “And you shall take our daughters to yourselves, and you shall dwell with us, and the land shall be before you” (Genesis 34:9–10). “That you may dwell in the land of Goshen” (ibid. 47:4). “They (the nations) shall not dwell in your land, lest they make you sin against Me” (Exodus 23:33). “These men are peaceable with us; therefore let them dwell in the land and trade in it” (Genesis 34:21). “And they built the cities and dwelt in them” (Judges 21:23). “And they dwelt in the cities of Hebron” (2 Samuel 2:3). “And she (the Shunammite woman) said: I dwell among my own people” (2 Kings 4:13). — יֹשֵׁב, ישׁבים: one who dwells in a land, German Einwohner; French habitant; English inhabitant; and the singular in the sense of a collective noun for the plural, יוֹשׁב הארץ, all who dwell in it: “And when the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the threshing floor of Atad, they said: This is a grievous mourning for the Egyptians” (Genesis 50:11). “And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, between me and my vineyard” (Isaiah 5:3). “Terror, and the pit, and the trap are upon you, O inhabitant of the earth” (ibid. 24:17). “And I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant” (Jeremiah 54:22). “And the men shall cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall wail” (ibid. 47:2). “The peoples have heard, they tremble; pangs have taken hold of the inhabitants of Philistia. Then the chiefs of Edom were dismayed; the mighty men of Moab, trembling takes hold of them; all the inhabitants of Canaan melted away” (Exodus 15:14–15). “The inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel” (Joshua 10:1). “And the Asherites dwelt among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, for they did not drive them out. Naphtali did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh, nor the inhabitants of Beth-anath, and he dwelt among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land; but the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and of Beth-anath became forced labor for them” (Judges 1:32–33). “All you inhabitants of the world, and you dwellers on the earth” (Isaiah 18:3). “Be still, you inhabitants of the coast, you merchants of Sidon” (ibid. 23:2). “My anger and My fury have been poured forth upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem” (Jeremiah 42:18). “Behold, I will bring evil upon this place and upon its inhabitants” (2 Kings 22:16). “It is a land that devours its inhabitants” (Numbers 13:32). “And the earth is defiled under its inhabitants” (Isaiah 24:5). “They are all of them become to Me as Sodom, and its inhabitants as Gomorrah” (Jeremiah 23:14). “And their inhabitants were of small power, they were dismayed and put to shame” (Isaiah 37:27). “Cry out and shout, O inhabitant of Zion” (ibid. 12:6). “Furnish yourself to go into exile, O daughter that dwells in Egypt” (Jeremiah 46:19). “For those nations were the inhabitants of the land from of old” (1 Samuel 27:8). — c) The land יָשְׁבָה: the land was full of inhabitants, it will not be waste and desolate: “Then shall there enter in by the gates of this city kings and princes etc.; and this city shall be inhabited forever” (Jeremiah 17:25). “And there shall be no more utter destruction, but Jerusalem shall dwell safely” (Zechariah 14:11). “When Jerusalem was inhabited and in prosperity, and her cities round about her, and the South and the Lowland were inhabited” (ibid. 7:7). “It (Babylon) shall never be inhabited, neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation” (Isaiah 13:20). “Because of the wrath of the LORD it (Babylon) shall not be inhabited, but it shall be wholly desolate” (Jeremiah 50:13). “And it shall be no more inhabited forever” (ibid. 39). “No foot of man shall pass through it, nor foot of beast shall pass through it, neither shall it be inhabited forty years” (Ezekiel 29:11). “But Judah shall be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation” (Joel 4:20). “And the king shall perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon shall not be inhabited” (Zechariah 9:5). “Dwelling in security, after the manner” (Judges 18:7). “This is the exultant city that dwelt securely” (Zephaniah 2:15). — d) A city and the like יֹשֶׁבֶת in such-and-such a place: it is situated there: “And say to Tyre, that sits [Note: So the Qere; the Ketiv is הישבתי.] at the entry of the sea, the merchant of the peoples to many isles” (Ezekiel 27:3). — And in the Talmud and Midrash, in the primary sense: “He is not required to sit and gather them one by one” (Terumot 11:6). “A man should not sit before the barber close to the time of the afternoon prayer” (Shabbat 1:2). “The first group went out and sat on the Temple Mount” (Pesachim 5:10). “If he sat in his house, he is liable; if he went off overseas, he is exempt” (Horayot 1:2). “When the Nasi enters, all the people stand, and they do not sit until he says to them: Sit etc. When a sage enters, one stands and another sits, until he has entered and sat in his place” (Tosefta Sanhedrin 7:8). “She brought out a bed for him and said to him: Sit. He said to her: I will not sit until you raise the bed” (Berakhot 8b). “Stand, precious ones, stand; sit, precious ones, sit” (Bava Batra 100b). “Like a king who bought two maidservants etc.; concerning one he decreed that she should not move from the palace, and concerning the other he decreed banishment. That maidservant sat astonished and bewildered” (Genesis Rabbah 2). — And יָשַׁב in the academy: “No academy sits unless people murmur after him and say: What did So-and-so see to sit, and what did So-and-so see not to sit?” (Sifre Deuteronomy 13). “One who comes to take upon himself (to be a ḥaver), even a Torah scholar, must take it upon himself; but a sage who sat in the academy need not take it upon himself” (Tosefta Demai 2:13). “I give thanks before You, O LORD my God, that You have set my portion among those who sit in the house of study” (Berakhot 28b). “Isaac our father was an elder and sat in the academy” (Yoma 28b). “When he (David) sat in the academy, he did not sit on cushions and pillows” (Moed Katan 16b). “Simeon my son is a sage, Gamaliel my son is Nasi, Hanina bar Hama shall sit at the head” (Ketubot 103b). “This teaches that he (Moses) sat in judgment for them (the daughters of Jethro). He said: The way of the world is that men draw water and women water the flocks, but here the women draw and the men water” (Exodus Rabbah 1). — *ישב בתענית: to fast: “When he (Adam) saw that death had been decreed because of him, he sat in fasting for one hundred and thirty years” (Eruvin 18b). — יָשַׁב בתחבולות and the like: to stay there to watch the spectacle: “Who did not sit in the תחבולות” (Avodah Zarah 18b). — And things that are not living creatures: “A jar that sits on its base in the open air” (Oholot 9:16). “Jars that sit on their bases, or lie on their sides, in the open air” (ibid. 15:3). “The thin earthenware vessels, and their bottoms and their sides, that sit without support” (Kelim 2:2). “A city that sits on the bank of a stream: if there is a margin of four before it, one measures for it from the bank of the stream” (Eruvin 61a). “The whole inhabited world sits under one star” (Pesachim 94a). “For example, an iron trivet, and the pot sits upon it” (Rabbeinu Hananel, Shabbat 37a). “For the ark had feet, because it is a way of disrespect for the ark to sit on the ground” (Ibn Ezra, Terumah 25:12). “And he arranges three (reeds) on top of each loaf, so that one loaf sits on top of those reeds” (Rashi, Exodus 25:29). — A thorn יָשַׁב לו: the thorn was stuck in his flesh: “If a thorn was stuck in its gullet, we do not fear that perhaps it pierced” (Hullin 43b). “If a thorn got stuck in him in front of an idol, he should not bend down and take it out, because he looks as if he is bowing to the idol” (Avodah Zarah 12a). “If a thorn got stuck in his belly, he should not take it out” (Niddah 13b). — And יָשַׁב in the sense of “did nothing”, and the common expression שֵׁב ואל תעשה (“sit and do not do”), in contrast to קום ועשה (“arise and do”): “Sit and do not do is different” (Berakhot 20a). “Sit and do not do is preferable” (Eruvin 100a). — And in astronomy, °יוֹשֶׁבֶׁת על הכסא, a name for one of the constellations: “The one sitting on the throne, and its stars are 13” (Ibn Ezra, Reshit Hokhmah). “Now the twelve constellations of the zodiac have already been explained, and therefore I have seen fit to explain in this place the names of the thirty-six additional figures, and I will bring out their host by number, and these are they: the one sitting on the throne, the Little Bear etc.” (Nehmad ve-Na'im 305). — And in mathematics, °עמוד יֹשֵׁב and the like: “And this is a clear thing, that the perpendicular which we drew, namely the perpendicular ט"מ, sits on the midpoint of the line א"ד, since it goes out from the line א"ד at a right angle” (Sefer ha-Tishboret of R. Abraham bar Hiyya ha-Nasi 1:33).

— Nif'al, נוֹשַׁב, נוֹשָׁבָה, נוֹשֶׁבֶת, נוֹשָׁבֶת, נוֹשְׁבוּ, נוֹשָׁבוֹת, — ארץ נוֹשָׁבָה: a land in which people have dwelt, German bewohnt; French habité; English inhabited: “And the children of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came to an inhabited land; they ate the manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan” (Exodus 16:35). “Be corrected, O Jerusalem, lest My soul be alienated from you, lest I make you a desolation, a land not inhabited” (Jeremiah 6:8). “You are Gilead to Me, the head of Lebanon; yet surely I will make you a wilderness, cities that are not inhabited [Note: So the Ketiv; the Qere is נושבו.]” (ibid. 22:6). “When I make you a desolate city, like the cities that are not inhabited” (Ezekiel 26:19). “And I will multiply men upon you, all the house of Israel, all of it; and the cities shall be inhabited, and the waste places shall be built” (ibid. 36:10). “That her land may be desolate of all that is in it, because of the violence of all those who dwell in it. And the cities that are inhabited shall be laid waste, and the land shall be a desolation” (ibid. 12:19–20). “To turn your hand against the waste places that are inhabited [Note: Against ruined cities that have been resettled.], and against the people that is gathered out of the nations” (ibid. 38:12). — And Ben Sira said: “As the judge of a people, so are his officials; and as the head of a city, so are its inhabitants. An unruly king destroys his people, but a city is inhabited through its princes” (Ben Sira, Genizah 10:2–3). — עיר נוֹשָׁבָה מימים: an ancient city: “And they shall take up a lamentation over you, and say to you: How are you destroyed, that were inhabited from days of old [Note: The vocalization of this word according to the Masorah is מִיַמִּים, as if it were the plural of ים; therefore the early and modern commentators had difficulty explaining this verse, because of the difficulty of the expression “a city inhabited from the sea”, and some of the moderns emended נשבַת מים. But perhaps one should vocalize מיָמים, the plural of יום, meaning an ancient city, inhabited from early days.], the renowned city” (Ezekiel 26:17).

— Hif'il, הוֹשִׁיב, הוֹשַׁבְתִּי, מוֹשִׁיב, מוֹשִׁיבִי, הוֹשֵׁב, אוֹשִׁיב, יוֹשֵׁב, וַיּוֹשֵׁב, וַיֹּשֶׁב, הוֹשַׁבְתִּיךָ, אוֹשִׁיבְךָ, תּוֹשִׁיבֵנִי, יוֹשִׁיבֵנִי, יוֹשִׁיבוּם, וַיֹּשִׁיבֻם, — הוֹשִׁיב את פלוני: to cause him to sit: “Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth at the head of the people; and set two men, base fellows, before him” (1 Kings 21:9–10). — הוֹשִׁיבוֹ על כסא: in particular, to give him the kingship: “As the LORD lives, who has established me and set me on the throne of David my father” (1 Kings 2:24). “And they set the king upon the throne of the kingdom” (2 Chronicles 23:20). “He does not withdraw His eyes from the righteous; but with kings upon the throne He sets them forever, and they are exalted” (Job 36:7). — הוֹשִׁיבוֹ במקום: to cause him to stay there: “God makes the solitary to dwell in a house” (Psalms 68:7). “Who makes the barren woman to dwell in her house” (ibid. 113:9). “He has made me to dwell in dark places, as those that have been long dead” (Lamentations 3:6). — And הוֹשִׁיבוֹ עם פלוני: that he be beside him, together with him: “He raises up the poor out of the dust, He lifts up the needy from the dunghill, to set them among princes” (1 Samuel 2:8). “That He may set him with princes, even with the princes of His people” (Psalms 113:8). — And Ben Sira said: “Extol her, and she will exalt you, and will seat you among nobles” (Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 7, 11b, in the name of Ben Sira). — הוֹשִׁיבוֹ במקום: to leave him there for a time: “And David came to the two hundred men who had been too faint to follow David, whom they had made to abide at the brook Besor” (1 Samuel 30:21). — הוֹשִׁיבוֹ in a tent, in a booth and the like: to cause him to dwell in it: “That I made the children of Israel dwell in booths, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt” (Leviticus 23:43). “I will yet make you dwell in tents, as in the days of the appointed feast” (Hosea 12:10). — And הוֹשִׁיבוֹ in a land: to cause him to sojourn in it, to live in it: “The land of Egypt is before you; in the best of the land make your father dwell” (Genesis 47:6). “And Joseph settled his father and his brothers, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt” (ibid. 11). “And he (the king of Assyria) carried Israel away to Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor” (2 Kings 17:6). “And he placed them (the Cutheans) in the cities of Samaria” (ibid. 24). “And the cities which Huram had given to Solomon, Solomon built them, and caused the children of Israel to dwell there” (2 Chronicles 8:2). “He turns a wilderness into a pool of water, and a dry land into watersprings. And there He makes the hungry to dwell, and they establish a city of habitation” (Psalms 107:35–36). “And I will cause you to be inhabited after your former estate” (Ezekiel 36:11). “Behold, I will gather them out of all the countries etc., and I will bring them back to this place, and I will cause them to dwell safely” (Jeremiah 32:37). “They shall come trembling as a bird out of Egypt etc., and I will make them dwell in their houses, says the LORD” (Hosea 11:11). “The nations which you have carried away and placed in the cities of Samaria” (2 Kings 17:26). “And the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, and they brought forth your fathers out of Egypt, and made them dwell in this place” (1 Samuel 12:8). — הוֹשִׁיב a land, a city: to cause there to be inhabitants in it: “And your seed shall possess the nations, and make the desolate cities to be inhabited” (Isaiah 54:3). “And I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the waste places shall be built” (Ezekiel 36:33). — And figuratively, הוֹשִׁיב אשה: to take her to himself as a wife: “And among the sons of the priests there were found some who had married foreign women” (Ezra 10:18). “In those days also I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod” (Nehemiah 13:23). “And let all those in our cities who have married foreign women come at appointed times” (Ezra 10:14). “And they finished with all the men who had married foreign women by the first day of the first month” (ibid. 17). “We have broken faith with our God, and have married foreign women of the peoples of the land” (ibid. 2). “You have broken faith, and have married foreign women, to increase the guilt of Israel” (ibid. 10). — And in the Talmud and Midrash, in the primary sense: “If one of the disciples said: I have something to argue in his favor, they bring him up and seat him among them” (Sanhedrin 5:4). “They took him (Hillel) out (from under the snow), and washed him and anointed him, and seated him opposite the fire” (Yoma 35b). “Ben Azzai said: By your name they will call you, and in your place they will seat you, and of your own they will give you” (ibid. 38a). — And הוֹשִׁיבוֹ in the academy, in the court: “I have received it from the mouth of seventy-two elders, on the day they seated R. Eleazar ben Azariah in the academy” (Zevachim 1:3). “R. Yohanan said: They seat on the Sanhedrin only men of stature and men of wisdom” (Sanhedrin 17a). “And they did him (Hezekiah) honor at his death — this teaches that they set up an academy at his grave” (Bava Kamma 16b). “He (Rabbi) said to them (to the sages of Israel): Do not eulogize me in the towns, and reconvene the academy after thirty days” (Ketubot 103a). — And הוֹשִׁיב a shopkeeper and the like: to place him in a shop to do business in it: “One may not set up a shopkeeper for half the profit” (Bava Metzia 5:4). And הוֹשִׁיב a teacher: “They ordained that teachers of children be set up in Jerusalem etc. Whoever had no father would not go up and learn. They ordained that they be set up in every district etc., and whoever's teacher grew angry with him would rebel against him and leave; until Joshua ben Gamla came and ordained that teachers of children be set up in every province and in every town” (Bava Batra 21a). — And of living creatures, הוֹשִׁיב a hen: that she sit and brood on the eggs to warm them and hatch chicks: “And a hen that ran away, one returns it to its place; and if it died, one sets another in its place” (Pesachim 4:7). “She who sets chicks said: I set them only in pairs etc.” (Tosefta Shabbat 7:17). — °And bees in a hive and the like, that they make their honey there: “And the leather with which one muzzles the animal's mouth, and the leather on which one sets the bees when one takes the honey” (Rambam, Kelim 7:2). And things that are not living creatures: to fix it there: “One may set up coops for chickens on the fourteenth” (Pesachim 4:7). “These cities are made neither small villages nor large walled towns, but medium towns; and they are set only in a place of water etc., and they are set only in a place of markets, and they are set only in a place of population” (Makkot 10a). “Large eggs that are placed on top of a hollow vessel etc.: one may not set the vessel first and afterwards arrange on it, but he should hold it in his hand and set the egg on it, and afterwards set the vessel on the coals; and likewise a pot that one sets on two jars — he may not first set them around and afterwards set the pot on them” (Rashi, Betzah 33a). “And he should slide his hands gently from under the fire-pan, and set the fire-pan on the floor” (Tosafot, Yoma 47a). “For it is customary to set beams from pillar to pillar, to build upon them the roof of the portico” (הם, Sukkah 18b).

— Pi'el, יִשֵּׁב, יִשְׁבוּ, — a) יִשֵּׁב his tent in such-and-such a place: to pitch it, fix it, establish it, German aufstellen (ein Zelt); French établir (tente); English establish tents: “Therefore, behold, I will give you to the children of the east for a possession, and they shall set their encampments in you, and make their dwellings in you” (Ezekiel 25:4). — *ישב העולם: to increase its inhabitants, to cause it to be in good order: “And are they destroyers of the world? Are they not settlers of the world?” (Sotah 22a). “David said: Master of the world, settle Your world” (Exodus Rabbah 31). “But the completely wicked, such as the heretics and the informers, are not settlers of the world” (Sefer Hanokh, Yitro 34). — °יִשֵּׁב a place: to make it inhabited and in good order: “Just as Mount Zion — the Holy One, blessed be He, will in the future restore it and resettle it [Note: So in the manuscript; in the printed editions לישובו, לישובן.], so the houses of the righteous — the Holy One, blessed be He, will in the future restore them and resettle them [Note: So in the manuscript; in the printed editions לישובו, לישובן.]” (Berakhot 58b). — *יִשֵּׁב את הארץ: to cause it to be inhabited, German bevölkern; French peupler; English to people; and in particular, to establish settlements in it, German kolonisieren; French coloniser; English -nise. — °And יִשֵּׁב a people: to place it in a place; and the poet said: “And how long will You settle in his captivity a people that counts its moments? Hear his cry and hearken” (R. Judah Halevi, Selichah, חדרי לב). — °יִשֵּׁב a house: to increase its inhabitants: “A single man and a single woman, and He pairs them together and settles a household from them” (Rashi, Sotah 2a). — And the hive, of bees: “He takes a swarm and leaves a swarm, in order to keep the hive populated” (Rambam, Mekhirah 23:13). — And the dovecote, of doves: “Because the mothers flee, it turns out that he has destroyed the whole dovecote; rather, he leaves some of them in order to keep the dovecote populated” (ibid. 11). — b) *יִשֵּׁב עצמו: to compose his mind: “R. A. bar Nagri said: And he composed himself for prayer” (Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 5, 32d). — And things that are not living creatures, יִשֵּׁב a stone and the like: to fix it well: “The builder who set the stone in place at the top of the course” (Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7, 10d). “For they made the Tabernacle and did not know how to set it up. What did they do? Each one took his work, and they came to Moses and said: Here are the boards, here are the bars etc.” (Exodus Rabbah 52). “The cloud departed, and they all prepared to journey and arranged their belongings; whoever had an animal — and if he did not have one, the cloud would take the rest” (Tanhuma Numbers 13). — And in weaving, יִשֵּׁב the threads within the fabric, that they be fixed: “One who beats (the weft) or taps on the fabric is liable, because he is as one who settles it with his hand” (Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 12, 13c). — And יִשֵּׁב between people: to arrange between them what is needed: “Jacob asked for illness. He said before Him: Master of the worlds, a man dies without illness and does not settle matters among his sons; if he is ill two or three days, he settles matters among his sons” (Genesis Rabbah 65). — °יִשֵּׁב the creases: to arrange them so that they are as they should be: “When one folds them (the garments), then one smooths out their creases” (Rashi and Rabbeinu Nissim on the Rif, Shabbat 45a). — And in abstract matters, °ישב the heart, the mind, the soul: to set them at rest, to cause them to be at ease: “For vinegar settles the soul” (Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 14, 14d). “And he spoke to the heart of the maiden etc. — words that settle the heart” (Genesis Rabbah 80). “And the matters of these four chapters etc. are fit to be presented first, for they first settle a person's mind” (Rambam, Yesodei HaTorah 4:13). “Because the soul is pained at the departure of Shabbat, one gladdens it and settles it with a pleasant fragrance” (the same, Shabbat 29:28). “One who was bitten by a scorpion or a snake may whisper over the place of the bite, even on Shabbat, in order to settle his mind and strengthen his heart” (the same, Avodat Kokhavim 11:11). — And an abstract matter: to establish, to explain: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him (to Moses): You have eased the burdens of My children; by your life, you will in the future settle and explain to My children their vows” (Leviticus Rabbah 37). “I present an introduction that is much needed to lead straight to the great and lofty subject that we are going to point out in these chapters, and to settle the mind of the pure student in it” (שעה"ש by Ibn Natif 3:3). — יִשב the words: to explain and arrange them properly: “Perhaps one of the dogs will come and attach himself to me; nevertheless it is incumbent on me to settle the matter” (Ruth Rabbah, ויהי בשכבו). “And I say, to settle it (the verse) properly according to its plain sense” (Rashi, Exodus 23:2). “That he does not settle by strict law, but makes a compromise by consent” (the same, Avot 6:6). “And the Amoraim in the Land of Israel were not quarrelsome, and were gentle with one another like oil, and settled the reasons without questions and answers” (the same, Bava Metzia 85a). “Rather, it comes to say that one can explain the baraita in another way” (Tosafot, Bava Kamma 18a). “And as for what I said to settle the Tosafot, I do not need it” (Responsa of Mahari Colon 172). “Would that you could complete your words on all the hard and strange matters that I found concerning this foundation, and settle them, for I still see no opening through which to bring them in” (Ramchal, Hoker u-Mekubbal 10). “And therefore one must know and understand that all this and the like cannot be grasped and settled properly except by the way of the LORD, which is paved — the faithful wisdom” (Avodat ha-Kodesh of R. Meir Gabbai, Sitrei Torah 19). — And יש לְיַשֵּׁב, a common expression among the commentators on the Talmud, Maharsha and the like: it is possible to explain the matter so that there is no difficulty in it. — ישב the garment: that it lie properly: “The place prepared for the neck opening, through which a person can put on the garment, and by putting his head into the opening of the garment he is able to set it on himself” (Nefutsot Yehudah 18). — °ישב עצמו: to consider in his mind what and how to do: “For this one needs great merit, to merit settling oneself one hour a day” (Maggid Sichot 64a).

— Pu'al, *יֻשּׁב, מְיֻשָּׁב, מיושב, — that one has caused to sit. a) In the primary sense, מיושב, in the sense of “in a sitting position”: “A person gives his testimony seated” (Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 7, 48d). “He (Boaz) saw a matter of modesty in her (in Ruth): (ears of grain) that were standing (she gathered) standing; (those that) had fallen (she gathered) seated” (Shabbat 113b). “He should not relieve himself standing, but seated” (Avot de-Rabbi Natan 40). “When the Holy One, blessed be He, judges Israel, He judges them standing, shortening the judgment and making compromise in judgment; but when He judges the nations of the world, He judges seated, being exacting in judgment and prolonging the judgment” (Genesis Rabbah 82). “And they fall on their faces, and he supplicates; and he lifts his head, he and they, and supplicates a little seated, as he did in the morning prayer; and he stands and says Kaddish” (Rambam, Tefillah 9:8). — b) *בית מיושב: not destroyed: “That He (the Holy One, blessed be He) showed him (Moses) the Temple settled in its tranquility” (Sifre Deuteronomy 357). — And ארץ מיושבת: “That He showed him the Land of Israel settled in its tranquility” (ibid.). “If (the city) is surrounded by a wall and is not inhabited throughout, when one comes to measure its boundary he does not measure it from the wall but from the houses” (Rashi, Eruvin 26a). — And a °מיושב person: whose condition is good, whose house was not destroyed: “And likewise Job saw himself settled, and destroyed, and settled” (Rashi, Ezekiel 14:14). — And figuratively, *אדם מיושב: deliberate, not hasty: “Like a province that rebelled against the king; the king sent a general and told him to destroy it. That general was experienced and deliberate; he said to them: Take some days for yourselves; and if not, I will do to you as I did to such-and-such a province and its fellows” (Sifre Numbers 131). “That a person should be patient in judgment, for whoever is patient in judgment is deliberate in judgment” (Avot de-Rabbi Natan 1). “Like a king who took a wife; he would say: There is none more beautiful than she, none more praiseworthy than she, none more settled than she” (Numbers Rabbah 2). — And in סהמ"א: “Despising greatness and hating dominion, settled, of good memory” (Hovot ha-Levavot, Ha-Perishut 4). “The choicest way of the commandment is to stand, because when he walks he is not so settled, and he cannot concentrate when walking as when he was standing” (Tosafot, Berakhot 13b). — And לבו מיושב: confident, not afraid: “If he was riding on the donkey: if he has someone to hold his donkey, he dismounts and prays below; and if not, he prays in his place. Rabbi says: Either way he prays in his place, for thus his heart is settled” (Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4, 8b). — And דעתו מיושבת, in this sense: “The craftsmen recite at the top of the tree etc.; and the householder, either way, goes down and prays, because his mind is not settled upon him” (Berakhot 16a). “Even if it (the serpent) eats all the delicacies of the world, its mind is not settled upon it until it eats dust” (Yoma 75a). “When a man is humble and the members of his household are humble, and he goes off overseas etc., his heart is not afraid for them, and his mind is settled in his place until the time he returns” (Avot de-Rabbi Natan 7). “When I entered the first time, my mind was not settled upon me” (Numbers Rabbah 11). “A sick man lying in bed, and his mind is settled upon him, and his tongue and his speech are correct in his mouth” (Responsa of the Geonim, Harkavy 186). “For out of my anger, and not with a settled mind, did I swear” (Rashi, Hagigah 10a). — *חלום מיושב: not frightening: “His dreams are settled for him” (Berakhot 62a). — °פרוש מיושב: fitting according to the context: “And our Rabbis expounded it in one direction in tractate Horayot, but it does not sit well with me according to the course of the passage, which the wise man concluded by saying that this too is vanity” (Rashi, Ecclesiastes 8:14). — °טעם מיושב על הלב: one that is acceptable: “There is in the Pesikta that this was Doeg, but it does not sit well with my heart” (Rashi, 2 Samuel 1:2). “Even the reasons that sit well with the heart are not important to him” (the same, Proverbs 27:7). — c) °In cantillation, נעימה מיושבת: in a medium voice: “And שופר מורם and שופר מכרבל and לשון מיושב, in which the word comes out with a settled melody, neither high nor low” (Horayat ha-Kore 87). “And if there were between the ma'arikh and the tifcha two מלכים, one on the word with the ma'arikh and one on the word with the tifcha, the melody of the ma'arikh comes out settled, without התזה” (ibid. 102). — °שופר מישב: see שופר, and see °מְיֻשָּׁב.

Nitpa'el, *נִתְיַשֵּׁב, — a) נִתְיַשֵּׁב פלוני in a place: to fix his dwelling in a place, German sich niederlassen; French s`établir; English establish o. s.: “For the deeds of the Canaanites were more corrupt than those of all the nations, and that place in which Israel settled was the most corrupt of all” (Sifra, Acharei 138). — And in the sense of “rested”: “Once they had settled, they blew the trumpets, and Judah and his banner journeyed first” (Tanhuma Numbers 13). — And the land נִתְיַשְּׁבָה: it was cultivated, and cities were built in it, and the like: “Every land that Adam decreed should be settled was settled, and every land that Adam did not decree should be settled was not settled” (Berakhot 31a). — b) *נתישב a thing: it was strengthened, it was established: “R. Berekhiah said in the name of R. A.: Although You are from eternity, Your throne was not established, and You were not known in Your world, until Your children sang a song” (Exodus Rabbah 23). “The ministering angels said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, the covenant of Abraham their father has been annulled, through whom the world is settled, and through whom they recognized You in the world” (ibid. Lamentations, Introduction). — c) Figuratively, נתישב לבו, נתישבה דעתו: he was strengthened, he rested, he was calmed from his sorrow and his agitation: “It sets him on the truth, it sets him on peace; he is settled in his heart in his study; he asks and answers” (Avot 6:6). “After his (R. A.'s) mind was settled, he said: May it be Your will that Yose's eyes return to their place; and they returned” (Hagigah 3b). “A pregnant woman who smelled consecrated meat or pork — one pokes a reed into the gravy and puts it on her mouth; if her mind is settled, good; and if not, one feeds her the gravy itself; and if her mind is settled, good; and if not, one feeds her the fat itself” (Yoma 82a). “At every time I used to say: When will I see that hour when I enter at last? And now that I have entered, my mind was immediately settled upon me” (Numbers Rabbah 14). “And they made a great feast, and he got exceedingly drunk; once his mind was settled upon him, he said to her: My daughter, see every good thing I have in the house, and take it, and go to your father's house” (ibid. Song of Songs, נגילה). “And once the letters and the couriers had gone out, his mind was settled upon him, and he said: This honor which I accorded Hezekiah, I accorded him only for the sake of his God” (ibid. Esther, והשתיה). “Even if she is blind, one desecrates Shabbat for her, for her mind will be settled by it, since she says: My companions see and do all my needs” (Ve-Hizhir, Exodus 127a). “One does not question the teacher when he enters the study hall, until his mind is settled upon him” (Rambam, Talmud Torah 4:6). “If he found his mind confused and his heart troubled, he is forbidden to pray until his mind is settled; therefore one who comes from the road and is weary or distressed is forbidden to pray until his mind is settled” (the same, Tefillah 4:15). “One does not besiege cities of idolaters less than three days before Shabbat, so that the minds of the men of war will be settled upon them and they will not be panicked and troubled on Shabbat” (the same, Shabbat 30:13). “Because his (the child's) mind is inclined after money, and his mind is not yet settled in the ways of the world” (the same, Mekhirah 29:13). — And the soul נתישבה: “How much settles the soul? Rabbi says: Like a date; R. Hanina says: Like a dried fig” (Lamentations Rabbah, כל עמה). “The rule of the matter: he should afflict his body and exert himself every day in the morning until his body begins to grow warm, and rest a little until his soul is settled, and eat” (Rambam, De'ot 4:2). “And he should wait after he comes out until his soul is settled, and his body rests, and the heat departs, and afterwards he should eat” (ibid. 17). — °The thing נִתְיַשֵּׁב: it was fixed in proper order — the sewing and the like: “For the garment is not even, and it bulges in the garment like a kind of pocket, and one must tear the garment below and crumple it before him, and the sewing settles” (Rashi, Shabbat 105b). “For as a result it (the sandal) shortens and settles to the size of his foot” (Tosafot, Yoma 78b). — And abstract matters: “For it is impossible for the love of the Creator to be settled in our heart together with the settling of the love of the world in us; and when the believer's heart is empty of the love of the world etc., the love of the Creator will be settled in his heart and fixed in his soul” (Hovot ha-Levavot, Ahavat Hashem, introduction to the gate). “That you reckon with your soul and demand of it concerning every matter that has become settled in it, of the matters of the knowledge of God and His Torah” (ibid., Heshbon ha-Nefesh 3). “And blessed is the Name, by whom actions are weighed, who brought it about that these days be set apart as days of repentance, and prepared things for us until it became settled in the heart of the people that it is a time of repentance” (Malmad ha-Talmidim, Shabbat Shuvah). “His belief will be more accepted and settled in the heart, and the belief will take hold in him with the utmost strength” (Ha-Ikkarim 1:20). “The child's wisdom is not yet fully settled, and his words are not accepted and do not sit well on the heart” (Bartenura, Avot 4:20). — And התישב בדבר: to be strengthened in it, the matter becoming clear and certain to him: “And what becomes clear to you, remember it and be settled in it; and what you are in doubt about clarifying, inquire about it from the sages of your generation” (Hovot ha-Levavot, Heshbon ha-Nefesh 3). “Submission is lowliness of the soul, its abasement, and its low esteem in its own eyes; and it is one of the qualities of the soul; and when it is settled in it, its signs will be seen on the limbs, among them the soft tongue and the low voice etc.” (ibid., Ha-Keni'ah, introduction to the gate). “Your words are good, and I am settled in this matter, especially since even these premises are necessary; surely it is impossible to deny them” (Ramchal, Hoker u-Mekubbal 10). — And the heart הִתְיַשֵּׁב: to agree, to be content: “And our Rabbis expounded it of Nadab and Abihu, but my heart is not settled to explain it so” (Rashi, Psalms 78:63). — °The thing נִתְיַשֵּׁב: it became fitting according to the context and the intent: “And Jonathan translated it as referring to their asking for a king and making Saul king, but it does not fit for me according to the language of the Hebrew” (Rashi, Hosea 10:9). “Behold, the complete counsel that will be settled for him in this — the right thought will make it understood to him” (Ralbag, Proverbs 20:18). “Tomás said: Our lord can test it: let three of the most foolish of them be called before him, and he will see their answer well settled in everything” (Shevet Yehudah 64). “And on this came two answers etc., and the second answer, which is the main one and more fitting” (Minhat Kenaot of R. Y. of Pisa 95). “Now the two verses concerning the porch, which seem to contradict each other, are reconciled” (R. Eliezer of Beaugency, Ezekiel 40:9). — d) נִתְיַשֵּׁב על דבר, בדבר: to deliberate in his heart, to take counsel: “And once the letters had gone out, he (Merodach) reconsidered in his mind and said: I did not act properly; I put the greeting of Hezekiah before that of his God” (Song of Songs Rabbah, מצאוני). “Last year the elders of our community sat and deliberated on the matter, and voted and concluded not to change those haftarot” (Ma'aseh ha-Ge'onim, Responsum of R. Meshullam 57). “A court that sees fit to decree a decree, or to institute an enactment, or to introduce a custom, must deliberate on the matter and know first whether the majority of the community can bear it” (Rambam, Mamrim 2:5). “The court must deliberate in capital cases, and wait, and not hurry” (the same, Sanhedrin 14:10). “An epileptic at the time of his seizure is disqualified (from testimony), and at the time he is well he is fit etc.; and one must deliberate much on the testimony of epileptics” (the same, Edut 9:9). “And even with movable property his (the deaf-mute's) acts are not valid until they examine him with many examinations and deliberate on the matter” (the same, Mekhirah 29:2). “And our master Moses wrote there: We have heard and received from our elders that he should not leave fewer than four hairs; and I say that one should deliberate on the matter, because it is taught in the Tosefta of Makkot: there is one who plucks two hairs and is liable on account of being a Nazirite” (Semag, §51). “And above we brought this matter from לא תחום עיניך, and one must deliberate on the matter, for it appears that there are two negative commandments here in this matter” (ibid. 165). “Every court etc. must deliberate on the matter and investigate much, and pay attention to every prohibition which it sees the generation practicing, so as not to breach it and rule leniently on it” (Sefer ha-Hinukh 495). “The wise man who deliberates in his mind and is not hasty to answer sets aside his anger” (Ha-Meiri, Proverbs 15). “And at first His will was to conduct the world by the measure of gold; afterwards He, as it were, reconsidered in His will and saw that it is good before His world that it be conducted by the measure of silver” (Kedushat Levi, Pekudei). “And he has time to deliberate and to select the choicest manners of speech, and to put away what is not pleasant and acceptable of what comes to his mind” (מא"ג, introduction to Kiryat Sefer). — °נִתְיַשְּׁבוּ זה עם זה: they came to a compromise between them, they made peace: “Two who had a quarrel with each other and afterwards made peace together — neither of them may say: You did such to me, and therefore I did such to you” (Reshit Hokhmah, Sha'ar ha-Kedushah 11).

he: —  קל לא נהוג.

—  הִפע', הוֹשִׁיט, עתי' יוֹשִׁיט, —   הוֹשִׁיט את ידו לפלוני, וכדומה, פשט ידו לעומת פלוני, ausstrecken; étendre; strech out:  כל איש ואשה אשר יבוא אל המלך אל החצר הפנימית אשר לא יקרא אחת דתו להמית לבד מאשר יוֹשִׁיט לו המלך את שרביט הזהב וחיה (אסת' ד יא).  ויהי כראות המלך את אסתר המלכה עמדת בחצר מצאה חן בעיניו וַיּוֹשֵׁט המלך לאסתר את שרביט הזהב אשר בידו ותקרב אסתר ותגע בראש השרביט (שם ה ב). —   ואמר בן סירא:  גם לאביון הושיט יד למען תשלם ברכתך (ב"ס גני' ז לב).  ראה רעך כנפשך ובכל ששנאת התבונן מקום יביט אל תושיט יד ואל תיחד עמו בטנא (שם לד יד).  וגם אם בין רבים ישבת לפני רע אל תושט יד (שם יח). —   ובתו"מ:  בהמה שמת עוברה בתוך מעיה והושיט הרועה את ידו ונגע בו (חול' ד ג).  שתי גזוזטראות זו כנגד זו ברשות הרבים המושיט והזורק מזו לזו פטור היו שתיהן בדיוטא אחת המושיט חייב והזורק פטור (שבת יא ב).  שתי עגלות זו אחר זו ברשות הרבים מושיטין הקרשים מזו לזו אבל לא זורקין (שם).  כאדם שמושיט אצבעו לתוך עינו ומחטטה (ספרי במד' פד).  לא יושיט אדם כוס יין לנזיר ואבר מן החי לבני נח שאין מאכילין את האדם דבר האסור לו (תוספתא דמאי ב כד).  כדי שתושיט ידיה ותטול העד מתחת הכר וכו' (שם נדה ג ו).  אבל אסור להושיט אצבעו בחמין (תענ' יג.).  והלא אדם מושיט אצבעו באור בעולם הזה ומיד נכוה (סנה' ק:).  הושיט ידו לקן ושחט מיעוט סימנים (חול' קמ:).  כל מה שעמלתי שבע שנים בא זה והושיטו לי בקנה אחד (מד"ר בראש' כ).  היו מכסין השלחן וכל הכלים אשר עליו בכיסוי עור תחש והיו מושיטין בדיו לישא אותו בהן (שם במד' ד).  ולמה את מושיטו בקנה (שם קהל', טוב אחרית).  לשנים שהושיטו הדסים למלך אחד הושיטה לשמו ויצאת לשם זקנו ואחד הושיטה לשם זקנו ויצאת לשמו (פסיק' דר"כ, סליחות).  לאחד שהיה מושלך לתוך המים הושיט הקברניט את החבל אמר לו תפוש את החבל הזה בידך ואל תניחו שאם תניחהו אין לך חיים (תנחומא, שלח לא).
—  הָפע', *הוּשַׁט, מוּשָׁט, מוּשֶׁטֶת, —   שהושיטו אותו, ידו מושטת:  אל תהי ידך מושטת לקחת ובעת השב קפוצה (ב"ס גני' ד לא)
en: — Qal not in use.

— Hif'il, הוֹשִׁיט, future יוֹשִׁיט, — הוֹשִׁיט את ידו לפלוני, and the like, stretched out his hand toward someone, ausstrecken; étendre; strech out: "Any man or woman who comes to the king into the inner court without being called, there is one law for him, to be put to death, except the one to whom the king holds out the golden scepter, that he may live" (Esther 4:11). "And it was, when the king saw Queen Esther standing in the court, that she found favor in his eyes, and the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand, and Esther drew near and touched the top of the scepter" (ibid. 5:2). — And Ben Sira said: "Also to the poor stretch out your hand, so that your blessing may be complete" (Ben Sira, Genizah 7:32). "Regard your neighbor as yourself, and consider all that you hate; where he looks do not stretch out a hand, and do not join with him in the basket" (ibid. 34:14). "And also if you sit among many, before a companion do not stretch out a hand" (ibid. 18). — And in Talmud and Midrash: "A beast whose fetus died within its womb, and the shepherd stretched out his hand and touched it" (Chullin 4:3). "Two balconies opposite each other in the public domain: one who hands over and one who throws from one to the other is exempt; if both were on the same story, one who hands over is liable and one who throws is exempt" (Shabbat 11:2). "Two wagons one behind the other in the public domain: they hand the boards from one to the other, but do not throw them" (ibid.). "Like a person who puts his finger into his eye and gouges it" (Sifre Numbers 84). "A person should not hand a cup of wine to a Nazirite, nor a limb from a living animal to the sons of Noah, for one does not feed a person something forbidden to him" (Tosefta Demai 2:24). "So that she can stretch out her hands and take the cloth from under the pillow etc." (ibid. Niddah 3:6). "But it is forbidden to put his finger into hot water" (Ta'anit 13a). "Does not a person put his finger into fire in this world and is immediately burned?" (Sanhedrin 100b). "He stretched his hand into the nest and slaughtered a minority of the signs" (Chullin 140b). "All that I toiled over seven years, this one came and handed it to me on one reed" (Genesis Rabbah 20). "They would cover the table and all the vessels upon it with a covering of tachash skin, and insert its poles to carry it with them" (ibid. Numbers 4). "And why do you hand it over on a reed?" (ibid. Ecclesiastes, "Better is the end"). "Like two who handed myrtles to a king: one handed it in his own name and it came out in the name of his grandfather, and one handed it in the name of his grandfather and it came out in his own name" (Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, Selichot). "Like one who was thrown into the water; the captain held out the rope and said to him: Grasp this rope in your hand and do not let it go, for if you let it go you have no life" (Tanchuma, Shelach 31).
— Huf'al, *הוּשַׁט, מוּשָׁט, מוּשֶׁטֶת, — that was held out, his hand is outstretched: "Let not your hand be stretched out to take, and closed at the time of giving back" (Ben Sira, Genizah 4:31)

he: — קל לא נהוג.

—  הִפע', הוֹשִׁיעַ, הוֹשִׁעַ, הוֹשֵׁעַ, הוֹשַׁע, הוֹשִׁיעָה, הוֹשַׁעְתִּי, הוֹשַׁעְתָּ, הוֹשַׁעְתֶּם, אוֹשִׁיעַ, אוֹשִׁיעָה, תּוֹשִׁיעַ, יוֹשִׁיעַ, יְהוֹשִׁיעַ, יוֹשַׁע, וַיּוֹשַׁע, ישַׁע, וַיּשַׁע, תּוֹשַׁע, תּוֹשִׁיעוּ, תּוֹשִׁיעוּן, יוֹשִׁיעוּ, מוֹשִׁיעַ, לְהוֹשִׁיעַ, הוֹשִׁיעוֹ, הוֹשִׁיעָם, הוֹשַׁעְתִּיךָ, הוֹשַׁעְתִּים, הוֹשַׁעְתָּנוּ, אוֹשִׁיעֵךְ, תּוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ, יוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ, יֹשִׁיעֶנּוּ, יוֹשִׁיעֲךָ, ישִׁיעֲכֶם, יוֹשִׁיעֵם, יוֹשִׁעָן, תּוֹשִׁיעֵנִי, יוֹשִׁיעוּךָ, יוֹשִׁיעֻךָ, ישַׁעֲכֶם, יוֹשִׁיעוּם, — הוֹשִׁיעַ את פלוני ולפלוני מאויביו, מצרתו, הביא לו יְשׁוּעָה: כי יי' אלהיכם ההלך עמכם להלחם לכם עם איביכם לְהוֹשִׁיעַ אתכם (דבר' כ ד).  ויקם אחרי אבימלך לְהוֹשִׁיעַ את ישראל תולע בן פואה (שופט' י א).  כי אין ליי' מעצור לְהוֹשִׁיעַ ברב או במעט (ש"א יד ו).  למה תהיה כאיש נדהם כגבור לא יוכל לְהוֹשִׁיעַ (ירמ' יד ט).  הן לא קצרה יד יי' מֵהוֹשִׁיעַ ולא כבדה אזנו משמוע (ישע' נט א).  ויאמרו אליו זקני יביש הרף לנו שבעת ימים ונשלחה מלאכים בכל גבול ישראל ואם אין מוֹשִׁיעַ אתנו ויצאנו אליך (ש"א יא ג).  חי יי' הַמּוֹשִׁיעַ את ישראל (שם יד לט).  לך והכית בפלשתים וְהוֹשַׁׁעְתָּ את קעילה (שם כג ב).  ותפל על אפיה ארצה ותשתחו ותאמר הוֹשִׁעָה המלך (ש"ב יד ד).  אנא יי' הוֹשִׁיעָה נא (תהל' קיח כה).  הוֹשִׁיעָה את עמך וברך את נחלתך (שם כח ט).  הללו ואמרו הוֹשַׁע יי' את עמך את שארית ישראל (ירמ' לא ו).  הוֹשַׁע עבדך אתה אלהי (תהל' פו ב).  במה אוֹשִׁיעַ את ישראל (שופט' ו יה).  בשלש מאות האיש המלקקים אוֹשִׁיעַ אתכם ונתתי את מדין בידך (שם ז ז).  ואת בניך אנכי אוֹשִׁיעַ (ישע' מט כה).  ואת עם עני תּוֹשִׁיעַ (ש"ב כב כח).  בצפיתנו צפינו אל גוי לא יוֹשִׁעַ (איכ' ד יז).  כי אלהים יוֹשִׁיע ציון ויבנה ערי יהודה (תהל' סט לו).  ושח עינים יוֹשִׁעַ (איוב כב כט).  ויך (שמגר) את פלשתים שש מאות איש במלמד הבקר וַיּוֹשַׁע גם הוא את ישראל (שופט' ג לא).  וַיּוֹשַׁע יי' ביום ההוא את ישראל (ש"א יד כג).  וַיּשַׁע יי' את דוד בכל אשר הלך (ש"ב ח ו).  ויכו את פלשתים וַיּוֹשַׁע יי' תשועה גדולה (דהי"א יא יד).  האתם תריבון לבעל אם אתם תּוֹשִׁיעוּן אותו (שופט' ו לא).  — ובכנ': ומלאך פניו הוֹשִׁיעָם (ישע' סג ט).  וְהוֹשִׁיעָם יי' אלהיהם ביום ההוא (זכר' ט יו).  ואת בית יהודה ארחם וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּים ביי' אלהיהם (הושע א ז).  ואם בני עמון יחזקו ממך וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּיךָ (דהי"א יט יב).  כי אתך אני לְהוֹשִׁיעֲךָ ולהצילך (ירמ' יה כ).  כי אתך  אני נאם יי' לְהוֹשִׁיעֶךָ כי אעשה כלה בכל הגוים אשר הפצותיך שם (שם ל יא).  אל יוֹשִׁעֵךְ יי' מאין אוֹשִׁיעֵךְ (מ"ב ו כז).  אם במרד ואם במעל ביי' (עשינו) אל תּוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ היום הזה (יהושע' כב כב).  אשור אל יוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ על סוס לא נרכב (הוש' יד ד).  יי' מלכנו הוא יוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ (ישע' לג כב).  ובני בליעל אמרו (על שאול) מה-יּשִׁעֵנוּ זה ויבזהו (ש"א י כז).  אהי מלכך אפוא וְיוֹשִׁיעֲךָ בכל עריך (הוש' יג י).  הנה אלהיכם נקם יבוא גמול אלהים הוא יבוא וְישַׁעֲכֶם (ישע' לה ד).  ויקם יי' מושיע לבני ישראל וַיּוֹשִׁיעֵם (שופט' ג ט).  ויבאו הרעים ויגרשום (את בנות יתרו) ויקם משה וַיּוֹשִׁעָן וישק את צאנם (שמות ב יז).  ויקם יי' שפטים וַיוֹשִׁיעוּם מיד שסיהם (שופט' ב יו).  ואיה אלהיך אשר עשית לך יקומו אם יוֹשִׁיעוּךָ בעת רעתך (ירמ' ב כח).  יעמדו נא (יועציך) וְיוֹשִׁיעֻךָ (ישע' מז יג).  ובעת רעתם יאמרו קומה וְהוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ (ירמ' ב כז).  — הוֹשִׁיעוֹ מיד פלוני ומפלוני: והיה יי' עם השפט וְהוֹשִׁיעָם מיד איביהם (שופט' ב יח).  לך בכחך זה וְהוֹשַׁעְתָּ את ישראל מכף מדין (שם ו יד).  כי הוֹשַׁעְתָּנוּ מיד מדין (שם ח כב).  ואזעק אתכם ולא הוֹשַׁעְתֶּם אותי מידם (שם יב ב).  עלה וְהוֹשִׁעֵנִי מכף מלך ארם (מ"ב יו ז).  ועתה יי' אלהינו הוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ נא מידו (שם יט יט).  יי' אלהי בך חסיתי הוֹשִׁיעֵנִי מכל רדפי והצילני (תהל' ז ב).  הוֹשִׁיעֵנִי מפי אריה (שם כב כב).  הצילני מפעלי און ומאנשי דמים הוֹשִׁיעֵנִי (שם נט ג).  וצידונים ועמלק ומעון לחצו אתכם ותצעקו אלי וָאוֹשִׁיעָה אתכם מידם (שופט' י יב).  וַיּשַׁע מחרב מפיהם ומיד חזק אביון (איוב ה יה).  אל תחרש ממנו מזעק אל יי' אלהינו וְישִׁעֵנוּ מיד פלשתים (ש"א ז ח).  וַיּוֹשִׁיעֵם מיד שונא ויגאלם מיד אויב (תהל' קו י).  — וְהוֹשִׁיעוֹ מדָּבר, ממקום, מצרה: מחמס תּשִׁעֵנִי (ש"ב כה ג).  מצרתו לא יוֹשִׁיעֶנּוּ (ישע' מו ז).  זה עני קרא ויי' שמע ומכל צרותיו הוֹשִׁיעוֹ (תהל' לד ז).  ממצוקותיהם יוֹשִׁיעֵם (שם קז יג).  וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּי אתכם מכל טמאותיכם (יחזק' לו כט).  הנני מוֹשִׁיעַ את עמי מארץ מזרח ומארץ מבוא השמש (זכר' ח ז).  —  והוֹשִׁיעוֹ ביד פלוני, שפלוני היה כמו השליח לדבר להצילו: וַיּוֹשִׁיעֵם ביד ירבעם בן יואש (מ"ב יד כז).  אם ישך מוֹשִׁיעַ בידי את ישראל (שופט' ו לו).  וידעתי כי תוֹשִׁיעַ בידי את ישראל כאשר דברת (שם לז).  — והוֹשִׁיעַ לפלוני: צעקה הנער המארשה ואין מוֹשִׁיעַ לה (דבר' כב כז).  לכו וזעקו אל האלהים אשר בחרתם בם המה יוֹשִׁיעוּ לכם בעת צרתכם (שופט' י יד).  ואתם היום מאסתם את אלהיכם אשר הוא מוֹשִׁיעַ לכם מכל רעותיכם וצרתיכם (ש"א י יט).  וזעקו אל האלהים אשר הם מקטרים להם וְהוֹשֵׁעַ לא יוֹשִׁיעוּ להם בעת רעתם (ירמ' יא יב).  ואם בני עמון יחזקו ממך והלכתי לְהוֹשִׁיעַ לך (ש"ב י יא).  עלה אלינו מהרה וְהוֹשִׁיעָה לנו ועזרנו (יהוש' י ו).  תנה עזך לעבדך וְהוֹשִׁיעָה לבן אמתך (תהל' פו יו).  ישפט עניי עם יושִׁיעַ לבני אביון (שם עב ד).  קוה ליי' וְישַׁע לך (משלי כ כב).  וַיּוֹשַׁע יי' לדויד בכל אשר הלך (דהי"א יח ו).  — והַיַּד, הַיָּמִין, הַזְּרוֹעַ: אשר מנעך יי' מבוא בדמים וְהוֹשֵׁעַ ידך לך (ש"א כה כו).  וַתּוֹשַׁע לו זרעו (ישע' נט יו).  וגם אני אודך כי תוֹשִׁיעַ לך ימינך (איוב מ יד).  על אף איבי תשלח ידך וְתוֹשִׁיעֵנִי ימינך (תהל' קלח ז).  —  והחרב: כי לא בקשתי אבטח וחרבי לא תוֹשִׁיעֵנִי (תהל' מד ז).  — והוֹשִׁיעַ את העיר וכדומה: וגנותי על העיר הזאת לְהוֹשִׁיעָהּ (ישע' לז לה).  וגברתי את בית יהודה ואת בית יוסף אוֹשִׁיעַ (זכר' י ו).  — והוֹשִׁיעַ בע"ח: וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּי לצאני ולא תהיינה עוד לבז (יחזק' לד כב).  אדם ובהמה תּוֹשִׁיעַ יי' (תהל' לו ז).  — יְהוֹשִׁיעַ: כי לא בחרב ובחנית יְהוֹשִׁיעַ יי' כי ליי' המלחמה (ש"א יז מז).  שמר פתאים יי' דלתי ולי יְהוֹשִׁיעַ (תהל' קיו ו).

— נִפע', נוֹשַׁע, נוֹשַׁעְתֶּם, נוֹשַׁעְנוּ, עת' אִוָּשֵׁעַ, אִוָּשֵׁעָה, תִּוָּשַׁע, תִּוָּשְׁעִי, יִוָּשַׁע, יִוָּשֵׁעַ, נִוָּשַׁע, נִוָּשֵׁעַ, נִוָּשֵׁעָה, תִּוָּשְׁעוּן, — שהוֹשִיעוּ אותו: אשריך ישראל מי כמוך עם נוֹשַׁע ביי' (דבר' לג כט).  ישראל נוֹשַׁע ביי' תשועת עולמים (ישע' מה יז).  הנה מלכך יבוא לך צדיק וְנוֹשָׁע הוא (זכר' ט ט).  אין המלך נוֹשָׁע ברב חיל (תהל' לג יו).  ונזכרתם לפני יי' אלהיכם וְנוֹשַׁעְתֶּם מאיביכם (במד' י ט).  עבר קציר כלה קיץ ואנחנו לא נוֹשָׁעְנוּ (ירמ' ח כ).  מהלל אקרא יי' ומאיבי אִוָּשֵׁעַ (ש"ב כב ד).  רפאני יי' וארפא הושיעני וְאִוָּשֵׁעָה (ירמ' יז יד).  סעדני וְאִוָּשֵׁעָה ואשעה בחקיך תמיד (תהל' קיט קיז).  כבסי מרעה לבך ירושלם למען תִּוָּשֵׁעִי (ירמ' ד יד).  ועת צרה היא ליעקב וממנה יִוָּשֵׁעַ (שם ל ז).  הולך תמים יִוָּשֵׁעַ ונעקש דרכים יפול באחת (משלי כח יח).  בימיו תִּוָּשַׁע יהודה וישראל ישכן לבטח (ירמ' כג ו).  בדרכיך יזכרוך הן אתה קצפת ונחטא בהם עולם וְנִוָּשֵׁעַ (ישע' סד ד).  אלהים השיבנו והאר פניך וְנִוָּשֵׁעָה (תהל' פ ד).  בשובה ונחת תִּוָּשְׁעוּן (ישע' ל יה).  פנו אלי וְהִוָּשְׁעוּ כל אפסי ארץ (שם מה כב).
en: — Qal not in use.

— Hif'il, הוֹשִׁיעַ, הוֹשִׁעַ, הוֹשֵׁעַ, הוֹשַׁע, הוֹשִׁיעָה, הוֹשַׁעְתִּי, הוֹשַׁעְתָּ, הוֹשַׁעְתֶּם, אוֹשִׁיעַ, אוֹשִׁיעָה, תּוֹשִׁיעַ, יוֹשִׁיעַ, יְהוֹשִׁיעַ, יוֹשַׁע, וַיּוֹשַׁע, ישַׁע, וַיּשַׁע, תּוֹשַׁע, תּוֹשִׁיעוּ, תּוֹשִׁיעוּן, יוֹשִׁיעוּ, מוֹשִׁיעַ, לְהוֹשִׁיעַ, הוֹשִׁיעוֹ, הוֹשִׁיעָם, הוֹשַׁעְתִּיךָ, הוֹשַׁעְתִּים, הוֹשַׁעְתָּנוּ, אוֹשִׁיעֵךְ, תּוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ, יוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ, יֹשִׁיעֶנּוּ, יוֹשִׁיעֲךָ, ישִׁיעֲכֶם, יוֹשִׁיעֵם, יוֹשִׁעָן, תּוֹשִׁיעֵנִי, יוֹשִׁיעוּךָ, יוֹשִׁיעֻךָ, ישַׁעֲכֶם, יוֹשִׁיעוּם, — הוֹשִׁיעַ someone, and to someone, from his enemies, from his distress: to bring him יְשׁוּעָה (salvation): “For the LORD your God is He that goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you” (Deuteronomy 20:4). “And after Abimelech there arose to save Israel Tola the son of Puah” (Judges 10:1). “For there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few” (1 Samuel 14:6). “Why should You be as a man astonished, as a mighty man that cannot save?” (Jeremiah 14:9). “Behold, the LORD's hand is not too short to save, nor His ear too heavy to hear” (Isaiah 59:1). “And the elders of Jabesh said to him: Give us seven days' respite, that we may send messengers throughout all the borders of Israel; and then, if there is no one to save us, we will come out to you” (1 Samuel 11:3). “As the LORD lives, who saves Israel” (ibid. 14:39). “Go and smite the Philistines, and save Keilah” (ibid. 23:2). “And she fell on her face to the ground, and prostrated herself, and said: Help, O king” (2 Samuel 14:4). “We beseech You, O LORD, save now!” (Psalms 118:25). “Save Your people, and bless Your inheritance” (ibid. 28:9). “Proclaim, praise, and say: O LORD, save Your people, the remnant of Israel” (Jeremiah 31:6). “Save Your servant, You my God” (Psalms 86:2). “With what shall I save Israel?” (Judges 6:15). “By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver Midian into your hand” (ibid. 7:7). “And I will save your children” (Isaiah 49:25). “And the afflicted people You save” (2 Samuel 22:28). “In our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save” (Lamentations 4:17). “For God will save Zion, and build the cities of Judah” (Psalms 69:36). “And the one of lowly eyes He will save” (Job 22:29). “And he (Shamgar) smote of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox-goad; and he too saved Israel” (Judges 3:31). “So the LORD saved Israel that day” (1 Samuel 14:23). “And the LORD saved David wherever he went” (2 Samuel 8:6). “And they smote the Philistines; and the LORD saved them by a great salvation” (1 Chronicles 11:14). “Will you contend for Baal? Or will you save him?” (Judges 6:31). — And with suffixes: “And the angel of His presence saved them” (Isaiah 63:9). “And the LORD their God shall save them on that day” (Zechariah 9:16). “But I will have compassion upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the LORD their God” (Hosea 1:7). “And if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will save you” (1 Chronicles 19:12). “For I am with you to save you and to deliver you” (Jeremiah 15:20). “For I am with you, says the LORD, to save you; for I will make a full end of all the nations where I have scattered you” (ibid. 30:11). “If the LORD does not save you, from where shall I save you?” (2 Kings 6:27). “If it be in rebellion, or if in treachery against the LORD (that we have done this), save us not this day” (Joshua 22:22). “Assyria shall not save us; we will not ride upon horses” (Hosea 14:4). “The LORD is our king; He will save us” (Isaiah 33:22). “But worthless men said (of Saul): How shall this man save us? And they despised him” (1 Samuel 10:27). “Where now is your king, that he may save you in all your cities?” (Hosea 13:10). “Behold, your God will come with vengeance, with the recompense of God; He will come and save you” (Isaiah 35:4). “And the LORD raised up a savior for the children of Israel, who saved them” (Judges 3:9). “And the shepherds came and drove them (Jethro's daughters) away; but Moses stood up and saved them, and watered their flock” (Exodus 2:17). “And the LORD raised up judges, who saved them out of the hand of those that plundered them” (Judges 2:16). “But where are your gods that you have made for yourself? Let them arise, if they can save you in the time of your trouble” (Jeremiah 2:28). “Let them (your counselors) now stand up and save you” (Isaiah 47:13). “But in the time of their trouble they will say: Arise, and save us” (Jeremiah 2:27). — הוֹשִׁיעוֹ from the hand of someone, and from someone: “And the LORD was with the judge, and saved them out of the hand of their enemies” (Judges 2:18). “Go in this your might, and save Israel from the hand of Midian” (ibid. 6:14). “For you have saved us from the hand of Midian” (ibid. 8:22). “And I called to you, and you did not save me out of their hand” (ibid. 12:2). “Come up and save me out of the hand of the king of Aram” (2 Kings 16:7). “And now, O LORD our God, save us, I pray, out of his hand” (ibid. 19:19). “O LORD my God, in You have I taken refuge; save me from all those who pursue me, and deliver me” (Psalms 7:2). “Save me from the lion's mouth” (ibid. 22:22). “Deliver me from the workers of iniquity, and save me from men of blood” (ibid. 59:3). “And the Sidonians, and Amalek, and Maon oppressed you; and you cried to Me, and I saved you out of their hand” (Judges 10:12). “But He saves from the sword of their mouth, and the needy from the hand of the mighty” (Job 5:15). “Do not keep silent from us, from crying to the LORD our God, that He may save us out of the hand of the Philistines” (1 Samuel 7:8). “And He saved them from the hand of the hater, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy” (Psalms 106:10). — And הוֹשִׁיעוֹ from a thing, from a place, from a distress: “You save me from violence” (2 Samuel 25:3). “He cannot save him out of his trouble” (Isaiah 46:7). “This poor man cried, and the LORD heard, and saved him out of all his troubles” (Psalms 34:7). “He saved them out of their distresses” (ibid. 107:13). “And I will save you from all your uncleannesses” (Ezekiel 36:29). “Behold, I will save My people from the land of the east and from the land of the setting sun” (Zechariah 8:7). — And הוֹשִׁיעוֹ by the hand of someone, i.e. that someone was as it were the agent to rescue him: “And He saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash” (2 Kings 14:27). “If You will save Israel by my hand” (Judges 6:36). “Then I shall know that You will save Israel by my hand, as You have spoken” (ibid. 37). — And הוֹשִׁיעַ to (ל) someone: “The betrothed girl cried out, and there was no one to save her” (Deuteronomy 22:27). “Go and cry to the gods whom you have chosen; let them save you in the time of your distress” (Judges 10:14). “But you have this day rejected your God, who saves you from all your calamities and your distresses” (1 Samuel 10:19). “And they shall go and cry to the gods to whom they offer incense, but they shall surely not save them in the time of their trouble” (Jeremiah 11:12). “And if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will come to save you” (2 Samuel 10:11). “Come up to us quickly, and save us, and help us” (Joshua 10:6). “Give Your strength to Your servant, and save the son of Your handmaid” (Psalms 86:16). “May he judge the poor of the people, save the children of the needy” (ibid. 72:4). “Hope in the LORD, and He will save you” (Proverbs 20:22). “And the LORD saved David wherever he went” (1 Chronicles 18:6). — And of the hand, the right hand, the arm: “Since the LORD has withheld you from coming into bloodguilt, and from your own hand saving you” (1 Samuel 25:26). “And His own arm brought Him salvation” (Isaiah 59:16). “Then I too will praise you, that your own right hand can save you” (Job 40:14). “You stretch forth Your hand against the wrath of my enemies, and Your right hand saves me” (Psalms 138:7). — And of the sword: “For I do not trust in my bow, and my sword shall not save me” (Psalms 44:7). — And הוֹשִׁיעַ a city and the like: “For I will defend this city, to save it” (Isaiah 37:35). “And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and the house of Joseph I will save” (Zechariah 10:6). — And הוֹשִׁיעַ animals: “And I will save My flock, and they shall no more be a prey” (Ezekiel 34:22). “Man and beast You save, O LORD” (Psalms 36:7). — יְהוֹשִׁיעַ: “For not with sword and spear does the LORD save; for the battle is the LORD's” (1 Samuel 17:47). “The LORD preserves the simple; I was brought low, and He saved me” (Psalms 116:6).

— Nif'al, נוֹשַׁע, נוֹשַׁעְתֶּם, נוֹשַׁעְנוּ, future אִוָּשֵׁעַ, אִוָּשֵׁעָה, תִּוָּשַׁע, תִּוָּשְׁעִי, יִוָּשַׁע, יִוָּשֵׁעַ, נִוָּשַׁע, נִוָּשֵׁעַ, נִוָּשֵׁעָה, תִּוָּשְׁעוּן, — that he was saved: “Happy are you, O Israel; who is like you, a people saved by the LORD” (Deuteronomy 33:29). “Israel is saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation” (Isaiah 45:17). “Behold, your king comes to you; he is righteous and saved” (Zechariah 9:9). “A king is not saved by the greatness of an army” (Psalms 33:16). “And you shall be remembered before the LORD your God, and you shall be saved from your enemies” (Numbers 10:9). “The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved” (Jeremiah 8:20). “Praised, I call upon the LORD, and from my enemies I am saved” (2 Samuel 22:4). “Heal me, O LORD, and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved” (Jeremiah 17:14). “Support me, and I shall be saved, and I will delight in Your statutes continually” (Psalms 119:117). “Wash your heart from wickedness, O Jerusalem, that you may be saved” (Jeremiah 4:14). “And it is a time of distress for Jacob, but out of it he shall be saved” (ibid. 30:7). “He who walks blamelessly shall be saved, but he who is perverse in his ways shall fall at once” (Proverbs 28:18). “In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell securely” (Jeremiah 23:6). “In Your ways they remember You; behold, You were angry and we sinned; in them we have been of old, and we shall be saved” (Isaiah 64:4). “O God, restore us, and make Your face shine, and we shall be saved” (Psalms 80:4). “In returning and rest you shall be saved” (Isaiah 30:15). “Turn to Me and be saved, all the ends of the earth” (ibid. 45:22).

he: פ"ע, יָשְׁרָה, עת' יִישַׁר, וַיִּשַׁר, תִּישַׁר — א) יָשַׁר הדבר בעיניו, היה יָשָׁר, היה רצוי לו, חשבו שהוא טוב ונכון: ויעשהו כלי אחר כאשר יָשַׁר בעיני היוצר לעשות (ירמ' יח ד).  אנכי עשיתי את הארץ וכו' ונתתיה לאשר יָשַׁר בעיני (שם כז ה).  ויאמרו כל הקהל לעשות כן כי יָשַׁר הדבר בעיני כל העם (דהי"א יג ד).  ויאמר שמשון אל אביו אותה קח לי כי היא יָשְׁרָה בעיני (שופט' יד ג).  ויצא חירם מצר לראות את הערים אשר נתן לו שלמה ולא יָשְׁרוּ בעיניו (מ"א ט יב).  לכה נא אקחך אל מקום אחר אולי יִישַׁר בעיני האלהים וקבתו לי משם (במד' כג כז).  וַיִּישַׁר הדבר בעיני אבשלם (ש"ב יז ד).  וידבר לאשה וַתִּישַׁר בעיני שמשון (שופט' יד ז).  — ויָשַׁר הדבר, היה ישר במשמ' המוסרית, במשמ' של צדק וישר: הנה עפלה לא יָשְׁרָה נפשו בו (חבק ב ד).  — ב) יָשַׁר בדרך, הלך בדרך יָשָׁר: וַיִּשַּׁרְנָהצורת עתיד לנסתרות כמו וַיֵּחַמְנָה, עי' ערך יחם, והיא הצורה הקבועה לעתיד נסתרות בערב', וכמו"כ באשורית. הפרות בדרך על דרך בית שמש במסלה אחת הלכו הלך וגעו ולא סרו ימין ושמאול (ש"א ו יב).  — *יִישַׁרבירוש' בתוך דבור ארמי: מאן דאמר חרוש בה טבאות ואנא נסיב לה מינך בתר שמיטתא יישר (כך צ"ל, וכך מוגה בפרוש הגליון בדפוס קורוטשין) (ירוש' גיט' ה מז ג). ובבבלי בתוך דבור ארמי: רבה בר מרי איקלע לבי רבא בחול חזייה דבריך לפני המזון והדר בריך לאחר המזון א"ל יישר (ברכ' מב:). ונמצא עוד בהרבה מקומות בבבלי (שבת סג:), ערוב' לד:, פסח' נג:, חול' עה:, שבוע' מ:. ובקצת מקומות ישר ביוד אחת. — והעיד ר' יוחנן על דבור זה: א"ר יוחנן בשם ר"א בנו של ר"י הגלילי אמרין לפעלא טבא יישר (פסיק' רבתי יט)., דבור של הסכמה, במשמ' כך הוא, טוב, יפה: (כשעלה רבי זירא מצא ר' בנימין בר יפת שיושב ואומר משמו של ר' יוחנן) נותנין מרדעת על גבי חמור בשבת א"ל יישר וכן תרגמה אריוך בבבל (שבת נג.).  אמר לו (רב חסדא) לא שנו אלא בלוקח מן התגר אבל בלוקח מן בעל הבית אין לו עליו אונאה א"ל רב דימי ישרוהגיה שם הב"ח יישר, כצ"ל. וכן אמר ר' אלעזר ישר (ב"מ נא.).  (ישב ר' ירמיה לפני ר' זירא ואמר) עתיד הקב"ה להוציא נחל מבית קדשי הקדשים ועליו כל מיני מגדים וכו' אמר לו ההוא סבא יישר וכן א"ר יוחנן (סנה' ק.).  אמר רב נחמן אמר שמואל לא שנו אלא ששכרו בעדים אבל שכרו שלא בעדים מתוך שיכול לומר לו לא שכרתיך מעולם יכול לומר לו שכרתיך ונתתי לך שכרך א"ל רבי יצחק יישר וכן אמר ר' יוחנן (שבוע' מה:).  רבינא ורב אחא בריה דרבא היו יושבין לפני רב אשי באת סכין לפניהם אמר לו לרב אחא בריה דרבא טול ובדוק ובדקה על הצפרן ועל שני רוחות ואמר לו יישרתרגום עברי מגוף המאמר בארמ' בחולין יז.. (הלכ' פסוק', שחיט').  — * יִישַׁר כֹּחֶךָ, דבור הכרת טובה בשביל מעשה טוב: מעשה בשנים שהיו רצין אחר הגייס נתלה אחד מהם בזית ופשחו ורדף אחר הגייס וחזרו ואמר לו חבירו יישר כחך אריה (תוספתא יבמ' יד ט).  אמר לו הקב"ה למשה (כששבר את הלוחות) יישר כחך ששברת (ב"ב יד:).  אמרו בנות יתרו למשה יישר כחך שהצלתנו מיד הרועים (מד"ר שמות א).  — ובסהמ"א: (ואם טרח שמעון בממון אחרים והרויח ובא הוא מעצמו ונתן לראובן) יישר כחו והרשות בידו (שערי צדק, תשו' הגא' ח א).  ויישר כחך שהקשית לפי סברתך (תשו' ר"ת ד).  יישר כח רבינו ומצאתי כדבריו בספר ישן (שם כז).  יישר כחו ותנוח נפשו כמה יפה כיוון (שם קא).  ויישר כח האנשים אשר בידם למחות ומוחים ביד העושים כן (שבלי הלקט, תהל' מח).  — וכמו"כ *יִישַׁר חֵילֶךָ, במשמ' זו: כמה יגיעה יגע בו בן עמרם  עד שלימד שירה ללוים ואתם אומרות שירה מאליכם יישר חילכם (מד"ר בראש' נד).

— פִע', יִשֵּׁר, יִשַּׁרְתִּי, אֲיַשֵּׁר, יְיַשֵּׁר, יְיַשֶּׁר, תְּיַשֵּׁר, יַשְּׁרוּ, יְיַשְּׁרֵם, — יִשֵּׁר הדרך, עשה שיהיה הדרך יָשָׁר, לא מעֻקל: קול קורא במדבר פנו דרך יי' יַשְּׁרוּ בערבה מסלה לאלהינו (ישע' מ ג).  אני לפניך אלך והדורים אֲיַשֵּׁרכך הקרי, הכתיב אושר. (שם מה ב).  — ובמליצה, יִשֵּׁר הדרך לפלוני, עשה שיצליח על נקלה: אנכי העירתהו בצדק וכל דרכיו אֲיַשֵּׁר הוא יבנה עירי וגלותי ישלח (ישע' מה יג).  — ובהשאלה במוסריות: וישבה לפתח ביתה וכו' לקרא לעברי דרך הַמְיַשְּׁרִים ארחותם (משלי ט יד-יה).  צדקת תמים תְּיַשֵּׁר דרכו וברשעתו יפל רשע (שם יא ה).  — יִשֵּׁר הדבר למקום פלוני, עשה שילך שמה, richten; diriger; to direct: יחזקיהו סתם את מוצא מימי גיחון העליון וַיְּיַשְּׁרֵםכך לפי הכתיב, הקרי וַיַּשְּׁרֵם בהבלעת היוד, כמו וַיַּבִּשֵׁהוּ, עי' ערך יבש. למטה מערבה לעיר דויד (דהי"ב לב ל).  —  יִשֵּׁר הפקודות וכדומה, עשה אותם בישר: כל פקודי כל יִשָּׁרְתִּי כל ארח שקר שנאתי (תהל' קיט קכח).  — ובתו"מ: זה כלב שיישר את עצמו (מד"ר שמות א).  שכל המיישר ארחותיו הוא מכבד להקב"ה (שם במד' ח).  — ואמר המליץ: לא אהבני אדם שלא היתה לו אהבתי זכה כל ימי ולא שנאני אדם שלא התפללתי בעדו שיישרהו הבורא (מבח' הפנינ' לרשב"ג 34).  — ובמשמ' העקרית: ותולה עיניו כנגדה (כנגד הירח) ומישר את רגליו ומברך (מס' סופר' כ א).

— פֻע', יֻשַּׁר, מְיֻשָּׁר, — שעשוהו ישר: וקלע כרובים ותמרות ופטרי צצים וצפה זהב מְיֻשָּׁר על המחקה (מ"א ו לה).  — ובתו"מ: אלו דברי תורה (שכתוב בהם) התעיף עיניך בו ואיננו ואפילו הכי מיושרין הן אצל רבי מאיר (מגי' יח:).  — ובסהמ"א: והנוסחא שכתב אינה משוה  עם התוספתא גם בעצמה אינה מיושרת (רמב"ם טומא' מת ח ה).  וגם תראה בגירסת ר"ח תלמיד רב האי ובגירסת רבינו ר' יצחק אלפס תלמידו כי גרסתם נכונה ומיושרת (תשו' ר"ת פט).  — °מסלה מיֻשרה, במוסריות: ועתה השבעתיך באמונת הצדק אשר היא נתיבתך הסלולה המיושרת ובתפארת האמונה אשר היא אזור חלציך (מכת' מנח' בן סרוק לחסדאי).  — ואמר המליץ: טוב ישר ממיושר ורע משניהם עקש (אסף ב נה).  — ובמשמ' העקרית: ובהתחבר אחת לסוף ישוב נגדר ובהתחבר אחת לנגדר ישוב עגול והעגול מיושר והמיושר שלם והשלם גוף (ראב"ע קהל' ז כז).  המאזנים צריך שיהיו מיושרים כל אחד לפי מה שהוא (שו"ע חו"מ רלא).

— הִפע', הִיְשִׁיר, עת' יַיְשִׁיר, יַיְשִׁירוּ, צווי הַיְשַׁר, — א) פ"ע, יַיְשִׁירוּ העינים, תבטנה ישר: עיניך לנכח יביטו ועפעפיך יַיְשִׁרוּכך הקרי, הכתיב הושר. נגדך (משלי ד כה).  — ב) הִיְשִׁיר הדרך, עשהו ישר: יי' נחני בצדקתך למען שוררי הַיְשַׁריש סוברים שזה קל, יִישְׁרוּ. לפני דרכך (תהל' ה ט).  — ובסהמ"א: עד כאן הנה היישרתיך והורתיך למה שתעיין בו (אגר' הרמב"ם, קובץ בוקסדורף 381).  שיעיין בכל המקומות שהישירוהו אל זה הטעות (רלב"ג משלי כ).  שהנביאים כולם יתכוונו להישיר כלל האנשים לעבודת השם ואהבתו (העקרים ב יד).  דע שהדרך המישירה לחקירת ידיעתו היא חקירת ההתבוננות במלאכתו ומעשה ידיו (מאזני צדק, אלגזלי 41).  שהשפע האלהי הזה הוא בא על אדם שלם בתורה ובמצותיה אשר ירצה בו ה' יתברך להנהיג ולהיישיר את העם לקיים מאמריו וצווייו (מנח' קנא' לר"י מפיסא 39).  שהטבע לא יפעל בעצמו לולי בהישרת השכל הפועל כי הוא המישיר אותו להביאו אל תכליתו לפי שהטבע אינו משכיל (דרך אמונ' לר"א ביבאגו א א).  הנני מקדים הקדמה שצריכה מאד להישיר אל הענין העצום המופלג שאנו עתידין להעיר עליו בפרקים אלו (שעה"ש לאבן לטיף ג ג).

— נִתפ', °נִתְיַשֵּׁר,  — א) נִתְיַשֵּׁר הדבר בעיניו, נהיה ישר בעיניו: והודה לו על דבר זה בשביל שנתיישר בעיניו ונהנה ממנו (ר"ח ע"ז יז.).  משה רבינו כשבא לכתוב את המצות נתיישר בעיניו לכתוב איך קבלו ישראל את התורה (סדר החכ' וקור' העתים 163).  — ב) נִתְיַשֵּׁר לדבר, פנה לעומת הדבר הזה, במשמ' העקרית או בהשאלה: כל איש אשר ימות במלחמה על ה' ועל מקדשו ועל תורתו יהיה בגורל ה' חלקו ויתיישר ללכת אל האור הגדול ולא יראה החשך המחשיך הנפשות (יוסיפון, פרק עא).  כי פרישת הרשת יהיה עקר הכונה בה ללכוד העוף ובשנית יתישר בה להאכיל העוף מזון מהמזונות  ובזה יאמר שהבא לגנוב יכוין בגניבה להמית בעליה על הכונה הראשונה ובשלישית יתישר בה לתועלת הממון וזה כלו אמר להעיר כל אלו הדברים הרעים יתישרו מאד לרציחה כאילו היתה הרציחה היא המכוונת בהם (רלב"ג משלי א).  כי לפי זה יתיישרו לשפוט בדברים לפי מה שיאות מהמסודר מהגרמים השמימיים (הוא, אסת' א).  שבחו לו (להבורא) בשירים ובזמירות ודברו בספורי כל נפלאותיו כדי שיתפרסמו לכל ויתישרו לאמונתו (הוא, דה"י טז ח).  וע"כ צריך שנבאר התכלית הזה מה הוא כדי שיתישר האדם להשיגו (העקרים ג ג).  הזקן אשר ישמעו בני אדם לקולו אשר הוא נכון לרפא נפשות השבים המתישרים הראוי עליו שלא יהיה קופץ עליהם להטריחם ולהנהיגם בדבר מיוחד כל זמן שאינו יודע מדותם (מאזני צדק, אלגזלי 88).  כשנתישרה הנפש האנושית למשוך אליה מברכותיו הושפעו עליה (אמונה רמה ד ב).  — ג) °במשמ' העקרית, נעשה ישר, ההפך מן כפוּף: אנחנו מוצאין הנרפאים מהחולי שלא יוכלו לעמוד על רגליהם מרוב חולשתם וכשישען אחד מהם על דבר נתישרה קומתו אע"פ שבלכתו חלוש יותר מחולשת גופי הזקנים (מ' אלדבי, ש"א ה).  — ד) °נעשה טוב ויפה: והנשארים (בי' הדברות) הנהגות מדיניות בהם תקון עולם וכבר נחתמו בדבור כאשר יעשה בשלמות כבר נתישר סדור העולם (אמונה רמה ג א).
en: intransitive verb, יָשְׁרָה, future יִישַׁר, וַיִּשַׁר, תִּישַׁר — a) יָשַׁר הדבר בעיניו (the thing was right in his eyes), it was right, it was pleasing to him, he thought it good and proper: "And he made it again another vessel, as it seemed right in the eyes of the potter to make it" (Jeremiah 18:4). "I have made the earth, etc., and I give it to whom it seems right in My eyes" (ibid. 27:5). "And all the assembly said that they would do so, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people" (1 Chronicles 13:4). "And Samson said to his father: Get her for me, for she pleases me well" (Judges 14:3). "And Hiram came out from Tyre to see the cities which Solomon had given him, and they did not please him" (1 Kings 9:12). "Come now, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will please God that you may curse them for me from there" (Numbers 23:27). "And the saying pleased Absalom well" (2 Samuel 17:4). "And he talked with the woman, and she pleased Samson well" (Judges 14:7). — And יָשַׁר הדבר, it was upright in the moral sense, in the sense of justice and uprightness: "Behold, his soul is puffed up, it is not upright in him" (Habakkuk 2:4). — b) יָשַׁר בדרך, to go in a straight way: "And the kine went straight [וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה; Note: a future form for the third-person feminine plural, like וַיֵּחַמְנָה, see the entry יחם; and it is the regular form of the future third-person feminine plural in Arabic, and likewise in Assyrian.] on the way, on the way to Beth-shemesh; they went along the highway, lowing as they went, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left" (1 Samuel 6:12). — *יִישַׁר [Note: In the Jerusalem Talmud, within an Aramaic statement: "מאן דאמר חרוש בה טבאות ואנא נסיב לה מינך בתר שמיטתא יישר" ("One who says: Plough it well and I will take it from you after the Sabbatical year — יישר") (so it should read, and so it is emended in the marginal commentary in the Korets edition) (Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 5, 47c). And in the Babylonian Talmud, within an Aramaic statement: "רבה בר מרי איקלע לבי רבא בחול חזייה דבריך לפני המזון והדר בריך לאחר המזון א"ל יישר" ("Rabbah bar Mari happened to come to Rava's house on a weekday; he saw that he recited a blessing before the meal and then recited a blessing after the meal; he said to him: יישר") (Berakhot 42b). And it is found further in many places in the Babylonian Talmud (Shabbat 63b), Eruvin 34b, Pesachim 53b, Hullin 75b, Shevuot 40b. And in some places ישר with one yod. — And Rabbi Yohanan testified concerning this expression: "Rabbi Yohanan said in the name of Rabbi Eleazar son of Rabbi Yose the Galilean: To a good deed one says יישר" (Pesikta Rabbati 19).], an expression of agreement, in the sense of: so it is, good, well said: "(When Rabbi Zeira went up, he found Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet sitting and saying in the name of Rabbi Yohanan:) One may put a saddle-cloth on a donkey on the Sabbath. He said to him: יישר (well said), and so Arioch explained it in Babylonia" (Shabbat 53a). "(Rav Hisda) said to him: They taught this only of one who buys from a merchant, but one who buys from a householder has no claim of overreaching against him. Rav Dimi said to him: ישר [Note: the Bach emended there יישר, and so it should read.] (well said), and so said Rabbi Eleazar: ישר" (Bava Metzia 51a). "(Rabbi Jeremiah sat before Rabbi Zeira and said:) In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will bring forth a stream from the Holy of Holies, and upon it all kinds of delicacies, etc. That old man said to him: יישר (well said), and so said Rabbi Yohanan" (Sanhedrin 100a). "Rav Nahman said in the name of Samuel: They taught this only where he hired him before witnesses, but if he hired him without witnesses, since he could say to him: I never hired you, he can say to him: I hired you and paid you your wages. Rabbi Isaac said to him: יישר (well said), and so said Rabbi Yohanan" (Shevuot 45b). "Ravina and Rav Aha son of Rava were sitting before Rav Ashi. A knife came before them. He said to Rav Aha son of Rava: Take it and examine it. He examined it on the fingernail and on two sides, and he said to him: יישר [Note: a Hebrew translation of the body of the statement in Aramaic in Hullin 17a.]" (Halakhot Pesukot, Shechitah). — * יִישַׁר כֹּחֶךָ (may your strength be firm), an expression of gratitude for a good deed: "It happened with two who were running after the troop; one of them was caught on an olive tree and tore it off and pursued the troop and returned, and his companion said to him: יישר כחך, lion!" (Tosefta Yevamot 14:9). "The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses (when he broke the tablets): יישר כחך that you broke them" (Bava Batra 14b). "Jethro's daughters said to Moses: יישר כחך that you saved us from the hand of the shepherds" (Exodus Rabbah 1). — And in medieval literature: "(And if Simeon took trouble with other people's money and made a profit, and came of his own accord and gave to Reuben) יישר כחו (well done to him), and he has the right" (Sha'arei Tzedek, Responsa of the Geonim 8, 1).
