שכבשו בשמן ישן וכו' חרובין חדשים שכבשן ביין ישן שבי' ז ז.  הכובש ג' כבשים בחבית אחת שם ט ה.  ואלו ירקות שאדם יוצא בהן ידי חובתו בפסח בחזרת וכו' ובמרור יוצאין בהן בין לחין בין יבשין אבל לא כבושין ולא שלוקין ולא מבושלין פסח' ב ו.  האשה שהיתה כובשת ירק בקדרה טהר' ב א.  זתים שכבשן בטרפיהן טהורין לפי שלא כבשן אלא למראה עוקצ' ב א.  ר' יוסי אומר כובשין בצלים של תרומה בחומץ של חולין ואין כובשין בצלים של תרומה בחומץ של תרומה תוספתא תרומ' ט ג.  הכובש עד שיכבוש כל צרכו השולק עד שישלוק כל צרכו ירוש' מעשר' ד נא..  זית כבוש אומר עליו בורא פרי העץ שם ברכ' ו י..  אתרוג תפוח סרוח כבוש שלוק וכו' ומנומר פסול סוכ' לו..  — *כָּבַשׁ דרך, התקין דרך שיהיה נוח לעבור בו, שוה פניו, עשה אותו קשה, רצף באבנים וכדומה: פעם אחת הייתי מהלך בדרך והיתה דרך עוברת בשדה והייתי מהלך בה אמרה לי תינוקת אחת רבי לא שדה היא זו אמרתי לה לא דרך כבושה היא אמרה לי ליסטים כמוך כבשוה ערוב' נג:.  — *כָּבַשׁ גדר וכדומה, מלא אותו בעפרכך בערבית בענין בור וכדומה. וכדומה בין האבנים שלא יוכלו מים לעבר דרך בו: מעשה במערה שהיתה בגינתו של מוסק אחד ברמוןכך לפי כ"י ארפ' וכך גרס' ר"ש מקוא' ח א. שהיו כהנים כובשיםופרש ר"ש שם: כדי שיהו (המים) נקווים למקום אחד. את הגדר ויורדין וטובלין בתוכה תוספתא מקוא' ו ב.

— נִפע', נִכְבַּשׁ, נִכְבְּשָׁה, נִכְבָּשֹוֹת, *לִכָּבֵשׁ, ליכבש, — א) נִכְבְּשָׁה הארץ, שכָּבַשׁ אותה אדם, ונִכְבְּשָׁה לפני פלוני, שפלוני היה השליט עליה: ועבר לכם כל חלוץ את הירדן לפני יי' עד הורישו את איביו מפניו וְנִכְבְּשָׁה הארץ לפני יי' במד' לב כא-כב.  ויקהלו כל עדת בני ישראל שלה וישכינו שם את אהל מועד והארץ נִכְבְּשָׁה לפניהם יהוש' יח א.  — ובתו"מ: ומפני מה לא קדשוה (את הבָּצָע העליונה) מפני שתורפה של ירושלם משם ונוחה ליכבש משם תוספתא סנה' ג ד.  א"ר יהושע השבת כולה קדש וכל מה שנכבש בשבת יהיה קדש ליי' מד"ר במד' יד.  כיון שנכבשה ירושלם היו כל גדולי המלכות נוטלים את הנשים הנאות שבירושלם ומושיבים אותן עמהם בקרון פסיק' רבתי לא.  —  ונִכְבְּשָׁה האשה, נאנסה: והנה אנחנו כבשים את בנינו ואת בנתינו לעבדים ויש מבנתינו נִכְבָּשׁוֹת ואין לאל ידנו נחמ' ה ה.  — ובמשמ' יותר קלה, °נכנעה: לפי שנקבותיהם (של שאר בע"ח) אינן מתחברות לזכרים ולא נכבשות ונשמעות אליהם אלא לענין המשגל בלבד להיותן נפרדות מהזכרים ודבר אין להן עמהם אמנם נקבת האדם הוצרכה להיות לו עזר בעשיית צרכיו ובתקון מזונותיו ועניני ביתו ולכן היה ראוי שתהיה נכבשת ונשמעת אליו בכל אשר יצוה עליה ר"י אברבנאל, בראש' ב כא.  *ונכבש לו בדברים, בדעות, נכנע לפניו, קבל דעתו: שני חברים שהיו עסוקין בדבר הלכה ונכבשין זה לזה בהלכה מד"ר שה"ש, ברח דודי.  — *נִכְבַּשׁ על אשה, עם אשה, שכב אותה: בת כהן לישראל וילדה הימנו בן והלך הבן ונכבש על השפחה וילדה הימנו בן יבמ' ז ה.  הלך הבן ונכבש עם השפחה ספרא, אמור ו.  — *נִכְבַּשׁ על דבר, נדבק בו: מה הרים הללו נכבשים לתהום שלא יעלה ויציף את העולם כך הם הצדיקים נכבשים על הפורענות שלא יצאו וישרפו את העולם מד"ר בראש' לג.  — ב) *נכבש הפרי בחמץ וכדומה: חגבים טמאים שנכבשו עם חגבים טהורים תרומ' י ט.  כל הנכבשין זה עם זה מותרין אלא עם החסית שם י.  הלוף והחרדל והתורמוסין ושאר כל הנכבשין בין שימתיקו ובין עד שלא ימתיקו ניקחין בכסף מעשר תוספתא מע"ש א יג.  — ג) °נִכְבַּשׁ העפר וכדומה, נדחק ונלחץ בכח שיהיה דבוק יחד: וזורקים העפר באמצע להגביה התל ועשוי מדרגות מדרגות וכו' כדי שיעמוד העפר ולאחר שנכבש יפה נוטלים המלבנים מעמידי המדרגה רש"י יחזק' לח כ.

— פִע', כִּבֵּשׁ, *מְכַבֵּשׁ, — א) כִּבֵּשׁ גוי וכדומה, הכניעו בכח מלחמה: גם אתם (את כלי הכסף והזהב) הקדיש המלך דוד ליי' עם הכסף והזהב אשר הקדיש מכל הגוים אשר כִּבֵּשׁ ש"ב ח יא.  — ובתו"מ, כִּבֵּשׁ ארץ: הא למדנו שז' שנה היו מכבשין סעו"ר יא.  הוא (דוד) לא עשה כן אלא חזר וכיבש ארם נהרים וארם צובה ואת היבוסי שהיה סמוך לירושלם לא הוריש אמר לו הקב"ה סמוך לפלטירין שלך לא הורשת היאך אתה חוזר ומכבש ארם נהרים וארם צובה ספרי דבר' נא.  וכי כמה ארצות כיבש יהושע שם שנג.  וכי תעלה על דעתך שישראל מכבשין את הארץ לפני המקום תוספתא ע"ז ב ה.  לא נתחייבו ישראל בנטע רבעי אלא לאחר י"ד שנה ז' שכיבשו וז' שחילקו ירוש' פאה ז כ ג.  שבעה עשר יובלות מנו ישראל משנכנסו לארץ ועד שיצאו וכו' מהם שבע (שנים) שכיבשו ושבע שחילקו ערכ' יב:.  שכן מצינו שלא כיבשו יריחו אלא בשבת קונדר' ר' שמעון הדרשן, משקין ב, גני'.  שידע הקב"ה כי אמת דבר (משה) וכי אם הוא משמיד את העם במדבר ואינו מכבש לפניהן את ארץ כנען האומות אומרין עליו כי קצרה ידו ר"נ גאון, ברכ' לב..  — וכִבֵּשׁ עמים, מלכים, וכדומה: וכי מה עמים כיבש יהושע והלא לא כיבש אלא ל"א מלכים מלמד שכיבש  מלכים ושלטונים שהיו מסוף העולם ועד סופו ספרי דבר' שנג.  — כִּבֵּשׁ את פלוני, הכניעו: אין לי אלא בנכרי שלא כיבשתו ואין שרוי עמך בחצר נכרי שכיבשתו ושרוי עמך בחצר מניין פסח' ח:.  — וכִבֵּשׁ אשה, כמו כָּבַשׁ: איש דרכו לכבש ואין אשה דרכה לכבש יבמ' סה:.  — ב) *לחץ ודחק, כִּבֵּשׁ אפר וכדומה, לחצו ודחקו: ואין גורפין תנור וכירים אבל מכבשין ביצ' ד ה.  — וכִבֵּשׁ דבר, הסתיר: בשעה שתלמידיך קטנים תהי מכבש לפניהם דברי תורה הגדילו ונעשו ת"ח תהי מגלה להם סתרי תורה מד"ר שה"ש, כי טובים. — *כִּבֵּשׁ המעין, כלאהו, עצרהו: וכיבש הקב"ה מעיינו והוליד לחמש מאות שנה מד"ר בראש' כו. — *כִּבֵּשׁ את עינו מפלוני, סגר אותה, לא הביט אליו: בשעה שבקש הקב"ה להחריב את ביהמ"ק אמר כל זמן שאני בתוכו אין אומות העולם נוגעין בו אלא אכבש את עיני ממנו ואשבע שלא אזקק לו עד עת קץ ויבאו האויבים ויחריבו אותו מד"ר איכ', פתיח'.  — ג) *כִּבֵּשׁ זתים וכדומה: מי שכיבש זיתיו בטומאה ומבקש לתורמן בטהרה תוספתא תרומ' ג יח.  — ד) *כִּבֵּשׁ ריחים, עשה אותם ראויים למלאכה, נקר אותם: מעמידין תנור וכיריים וריחים במועד ר' יהודה אומר אין מכבשיןואמרו בגמ' (שם דף י.): מאי מכבשין רב יהודה אמר מנקר ריחיא רב יחיאל אמר בת עינא. ולא נתברר מקור שמוש זה. את הריחים בתחלה מו"ק א ט.

— הִפע', הִכְבִּישׁ, וַיַּכְבִּישׁוּם, —  כמו קל כָּבַשׁ: וישבו את העבדים ואת השפחות אשר שלחו חפשים ויכבישוםכך הכתיב, והקרי וַיִּכְבְּשׁוּם, ובקצת ספרים גם הכתיב ויכבשום, חסר. לעבדים ולשפחות ירמ' לד יא.

— פֻע', *כֻּבַּשׁ, מְכֻבַּשׁ, מכובש, שכבּשוהו: וכי תעלה על דעתך שישראל מכבשין את הארץ לפני המקום אלא כל זמן שהן עליה כאילו היא מכובשת הא אינן עליה כאילו אינה מכובשת תוספתא ע"ז ד ה.  — מְכֻבָּשׁ באבנים טובות, שאבנים טובות קבועות בו, inkrustirt; incrusté: כיצד עשה שלמה המלך הכסא בחכמתו שנתן לו הקב"ה והוא מכובש באבנים טובות ומרגליות דמות כסא שלמה, ביה"מ יליניק, חדר ב.

— נִתפ', *נִתְכַּבֵּשׁ, — כמו נִכְבַּשׁ, נתכבשה הארץ: אתמול אני הוא שטיהרתי ועכשיו אני אומר שמא נתכבשה (אשקלון) מדבר תורה והיאך אני פוטרה (מן המעשרות) מדבר תורה ירוש' שבי' ו לו ג, שם יבמ' ז ח..  שהיה ליל של פסח והיו מתייראים לומר עכשיו ירושלם מתכבשה בידו כיון שהשכימו בבקר לעמוד ולקרות ק"ש ולהתפלל מצאו אויביהם פגרים מתים מד"ר שמות יח.  כל בירה ובירה שהיתה בירושלם לא היתה ראויה להתכבש פחות מארבעים יום שם איכ', הרס בעברתו.  שכל זמן שהנרות דולקות האומות מתכבשות מד"ר תדשא ב, אפשטין.
en: [Note: In Aramaic and Syriac כֱּבַשׁ. In Arabic kabasa كَبَس, in all the senses found in Hebrew.], transitive verb, כָּבְשׁוּ, יִכְבּוֹשׁ, תִּכְבְּשֹוּ, כֹּבְשִׁים, לִכְבּשׁ, לִכְבּוֹשׁ, כִּבְשֻׁהָ, יִכְבְּשׁוּם, — a) כָּבַשׁ someone or something, he pressed and forced until he subdued him and took him by force; כָּבַשׁ the land, he took it under his lordship and ruled over it, German unterwerfen, French assujettir, English subdue: "And God said unto them (to Adam and Eve): Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it (וְכִבְשֻׁהָ); and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that creepeth upon the earth" (Genesis 1:28). And in the Talmud and Midrash, in particular, to take a land in war: "A city that was conquered by a siege, and a ship that was lost at sea, and one who goes out to be executed" (Gittin 3:4). "When Moses conquered the land of two nations, Sihon and Og, and gave it to the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half tribe of Manasseh, they said to him: It seems that the decree was decreed only conditionally" (Mekhilta, Beshalach, Amalek 2). "He (Moses) said to them (to Israel): Every place that you conquer, except for these places, is yours etc. Once you have conquered the Land of Israel, you will be permitted to conquer outside the Land" (Sifre Deuteronomy 51). "Why did David conquer Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, while the commandments are not in force there?" (ibid.). "'Ye shall henceforth return no more that way' — to settle you may not return, (but) you may return for trade and for commerce and to conquer the land" (Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10, 29d). "Many cities were conquered by those who came up from Egypt and were not conquered by those who came up from Babylon" (Chullin 7a). "Rabbi Joshua said: Since we are conquering it (Jericho) first, let us consecrate all its spoil to the Most High" (Numbers Rabbah 14). "Were Heshbon full of gnats, no creature could conquer it etc. Israel were toiling at it to conquer each and every city" (ibid. 19). "He (Nebuchadnezzar) called Nebuzaradan and raised him to be head over all the armies, and said to him: Go, conquer Jerusalem" (Pesikta Rabbati 26). "That you should not praise yourselves and say: You conquered it (Jerusalem) — a conquered city you conquered, a slain people you slew" (ibid.). — And כבש someone as a slave, he made him a slave against his will: "And all the princes and all the people hearkened, that had entered into the covenant to let every one his man-servant, and every one his maid-servant, go free, and not to make bondmen of them any more; they hearkened, and let them go; but afterwards they turned, and caused the servants and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return, and brought them into subjection (וַיִּכְבְּשׁוּם) [Note: So the qere; the ketiv is ויכבישום, see Hif'il.] for servants and for handmaids etc. And ye had done that which is right in My eyes, in proclaiming liberty every man to his neighbour etc. but ye turned and profaned My name, and caused every man his servant, and every man his handmaid, whom ye had let go free at their pleasure, to return; and ye brought them into subjection (וַתִּכְבְּשׁוּ), to be unto you for servants and for handmaids" (Jeremiah 34:10-16). "and, lo, we bring into bondage (כֹבְשִׁים) our sons and our daughters to be servants" (Nehemiah 5:5). "And now ye purpose to keep under (לִכְבּשׁ) the children of Judah and Jerusalem for bondmen and bondwomen unto you" (2 Chronicles 28:10). — *And to conquer a people in war: "Come and subdue the Jews who have rebelled against you" (Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 5, 55b). "That they should be despised and lowly, down below, and should not raise their head in Israel, but should be subdued under their hand" (Rambam, Laws of Kings 6:1). — *And כָּבַשׁ לפני someone, he humbled him before him: "A person who raises two starlings in his house, one large and one small; he subdued the large one before the small one" (Lamentations Rabbah, "Remember, O Lord"). — כָּבַשׁ אִשָּׁה, he took her by force and raped her: "Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman was fallen upon the couch whereon Esther was. Then the king said: Will he even force (לִכְבּוֹשׁ) the queen before me in the house?" (Esther 7:8). — And in the Talmud and Midrash: "And she was crying out: My lord the king, behold, he is forcing me before you" (Esther Rabbah, "And the king arose"). — And the male and the female כָּבְשׁוּ each other, acted with exertion of strength: "Judah and Tamar both pressed each other at the time that he lay with her" (Arukh, entry כבש). — *כָּבַשׁ his inclination, he prevailed over it, subdued it: "Who is mighty? He who subdues his inclination" (Avot 4:1). "Abraham said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that at the time You told me to offer up Isaac my son, I had what to answer and say before You: Yesterday You told me 'for in Isaac shall seed be called to thee,' and now You say 'and offer him there for a burnt-offering.' Heaven forbid, I did not do so, but I subdued my inclination and did Your will" (Jerusalem Talmud Ta'anit 2, 65d). "That I had what to answer You, and I subdued my inclination and did not answer You" (Leviticus Rabbah 29). "That he sees his field ownerless and his trees ownerless and the fences broken through, and sees his fruits being eaten, and he subdues his inclination and does not speak" (Tanchuma Leviticus 1). — °שֵׂכֶל כֹּבֵשׁ, (an intellect) that has the power to subdue the inclination and the like: "The way of life You made known to me, and graced me with a subduing intellect; You warned me of the day of reckoning, when You visit the moist and the dry" (Rabbi Judah ha-Levi, "Atah Konanta"). — *כָּבַשׁ his anger and the like: "May it be the will before Me that My mercy subdue My anger, and My mercy prevail over My attributes, and I deal with My children with the attribute of mercy" (Berakhot 7a). "This is the might of His might (of the Holy One, blessed be He), that He subdues His anger [Note: So in manuscript (Dikdukei Soferim); in the printed editions יצרו (His inclination).], that He grants long-suffering to the wicked" (Yoma 69b). "Flesh and blood — wrath subdues him, but the Holy One, blessed be He, subdues wrath" (Genesis Rabbah 49). "Flesh and blood — jealousy subdues him, but the Holy One, blessed be He, subdues jealousy" (ibid.). "Charity subdues calamity, that it not come to the world" (ibid., Leviticus Rabbah 27). — b) In the principal sense of pressing and squeezing: "A householders' press may be loosened but not pressed down; and that of the launderers, one may not touch it" (Shabbat 20:5). "Such as boards with which they press the garments" (Rabbenu Hananel, ibid. 123a). — *כָּבַשׁ על someone, he weighed upon him, pressed him hard: "A murderer who struck his fellow with a stone or with iron, or held him down (כבש עליו) in the water or in the fire, and he could not get up from there, and he died" (Sanhedrin 9:1). "No vessels may be dragged, except for a wagon, because it presses (the earth) down" (Beitzah 2:10). "If he tied the ship with something that can hold it, pressed down the stone on the cloak" (Oholot 8:5). "Like a bird that is held in the hand of a man, that if he presses his hand a little he strangles it" (Mekhilta, Beshalach 2:6). "It once happened that the Boethusians pressed great stones down upon it (upon the willow) on the eve of the Sabbath" (Tosefta Sukkah 3:1). "One who says to his fellow, 'Press your hand on me in the mikveh' — this is disgraceful. Rabbi Judah says: 'Press your hand on him until his soul departs'" (ibid., Mikva'ot 5:14). "Like flesh and blood who has bags of olives: he pressed the beam on them one upon the other, and the oil runs down from above and the oil runs down from below; so the mountain on this side and the mountain on that side press upon the springs" (Exodus Rabbah 15). "These mountains press down upon the deep, so that it not flood the world" (ibid., Leviticus Rabbah 27). — *כָּבַשׁ his weight (כֹּבְדוֹ), he pressed and bore down: "This says that a person (laying hands on the sacrifice) must press his weight" (Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 2, 77d). — *כָּבַשׁ a thing, he held back the thing, withheld, concealed: "One who suppresses his prophecy, and one who disregards the words of a prophet" (Sanhedrin 11:5). "One who suppresses his prophecy: Jonah son of Amittai (who did not want to prophesy)" (Tosefta ibid. 14:15). "When the disciples are young, hold back from them words of Torah; when they have grown up and become like he-goats, reveal to them the secrets of Torah" (Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2, 41d). "They compel the lender to produce the document and judge for him according to it etc. and they do not withhold from him his testimony and his proofs" (HaTerumah 28:6). "And further they included in this warning not to withhold testimony, so that his fellow not lose his money" (Sefer ha-Chinukh, commandment 251). — *כָּבַשׁ someone's wages, he held them back, delayed them: "One who withholds the wages of a hired worker transgresses five negative commandments" (Tosefta Bava Metzia 10:3). "Whoever withholds the wages of a hired worker, it is as though he takes his life from him" (Gemara ibid. 112a). — *כָּבַשׁ the deposit and the like: "You entrust your soul into My hand etc. and I do not withhold your deposit, but return it to you every morning" (Pesikta Rabbati 31). — *כָּבַשׁ him, he detained him: "Like a king for whom a festival arrived; his tenants came etc. the matron was hinting to them: While he is dealing with you, ask your needs from his hand. Since they did not understand, the matron detained them one more day so that they would ask their needs from the king" (Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, "On the eighth day"). "Those (of the king's children) who were married in a distant place would come to him, and when they sought to go, he would detain them one more day with him" (ibid.). — *כָּבַשׁ someone, he confined him: "The man confines his wife, that she not go out to the market, for every woman who goes out to the market will in the end stumble" (Genesis Rabbah 8). — *כָּבַשׁ his face [Note: In Arabic kabasa his head and the like: he put it in and hid it in his garment.], he hid it, out of shame and the like: "When the prophet would come to reprove him, he (Ahaz) would flee to a place of uncleanness and bury his face in the place of uncleanness, saying that the Shekhinah does not rest in a place of uncleanness" (Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10, 27d). "Like a king who came to his children from time to time; each one said: With me he will stay. The youngest of them all said: Is it possible that my father would leave my older brothers and stay with me? He went and stood with his face downcast and his soul sorrowful. His father saw him standing with his face downcast and his soul sorrowful over it. He said: Have you seen my youngest son, who stands with his face downcast and his soul sorrowful? Now, the food and drink shall be from you, and my lodging with him" (Sifre Deuteronomy 352). "Simeon ben Shetach said to him: King Yannai, stand on your feet and let them testify against you etc. He (Simeon) turned to his right — they (the judges) buried their faces in the ground; he turned to his left, and they buried their faces in the ground. Simeon ben Shetach said to them: You are masters of thoughts etc." (Sanhedrin 19b). "When you bring guests into your house, do not show them your face cast down to the ground, for whoever shows his face cast down to the ground, even if he gave all the gifts in the world, it is accounted to him as though he gave nothing" (Bartenura on Avot 1:15). — כבש stones and the like, he pressed and pushed them into a tight place, and in poetic language, ate much: "The Lord of hosts will defend them; and they shall devour, and shall subdue (וכבשו) [Note: The phrase is forced, and the ancients already struggled with the explanation of the words. Ibn Janah explained: they will subdue the enemy with sling-stones. And Radak: they will subdue the men of the sling-stones. And the other commentators explained in a similar way. But apart from the fact that this does not fit the phrasing "וכבשו sling-stones," it is difficult why this saying entered between the two verbs "devour" and "drink." Therefore the moderns decided that the text is corrupt, and emended it with various emendations. But according to the transmitted (Masoretic) reading, we must say that they used to say כבש sling-stones of one who ate much.] the sling-stones; and they shall drink, and make a noise as through wine" (Zechariah 9:15). — *כָּבַשׁ standing grain, he bent it to one side: "One who bends standing grain toward the fire, and one who breaches a fence before an animal, is not liable to pay according to the law" (Jerusalem Talmud Bava Kamma 6, 5b). "Any (tree) that the yoke (of the plowing ox) bends (is not called a tree in commercial transactions)" (Bava Batra 70a). "And if it is the other trees that he reserved, he reserved among them only any that the yoke does not bend; and any that the yoke bends belongs to the buyer and is counted as part of the field" (Rambam, Laws of Sale 24:14). "And if there is nothing in it (in the field he sold, apart from the trees) but other trees, he reserved them (for the seller) — and not all of them, but those that are thick and the yoke does not bend them; but the thin ones that the yoke bends, he sold nothing of them" (Tur and Shulchan Arukh, Choshen Mishpat, Laws of Sale 216:4). — °כָּבַשׁ the fire, he reduced it: "That the idolater lit and the idolater baked, and a Jew came and stirred (the fire) a little or banked it down — since he took part in the work of the bread, it is permitted" (Rambam, Forbidden Foods 17:13). — And figuratively, כָּבַשׁ someone's iniquities, he pressed and squeezed them together and hid them so that they would not be seen: "He will again have compassion upon us; He will subdue (יִכְבּוֹשׁ) [Note: In some books יכבשׁ, defective spelling.] our iniquities; and Thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea" (Micah 7:19). — And the liturgical poet said: "Pure of eyes, who dwells in heaven, who is a God like You, who subdues iniquities, who puts on righteousness, who is a God like You" (Morning service of Yom Kippur, "Adir ve-Na'or"). "Good and doing good to the creatures, who knows all hidden things, who subdues iniquities, who puts on righteousness" (ibid., "Rachum ve-Chanun"). — *כָּבַשׁ על a sin, he restrained himself, forgave and pardoned: "The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Over everything I restrain Myself, but over lewdness I am angry" (Numbers Rabbah 9). — c) *כָּבַשׁ fruits in vinegar or in oil and the like, he put them into the vinegar and left them there for some time, so that they would keep (pickled them): "Unconsecrated olives that he pickled with olives of terumah etc. an unclean fish that he pickled with a clean fish" (Terumot 10:7-8). "One who pickles, one who stews, one who salts" (Ma'asrot 4:1). "New roses that he pickled in old oil etc. new carobs that he pickled in old wine" (Shevi'it 7:7). "One who pickles three pickles in one barrel" (ibid. 9:5). "And these are the vegetables with which a person fulfills his obligation on Passover: with lettuce etc. And with bitter herbs one fulfills the obligation whether moist or dry, but not pickled, nor stewed, nor cooked" (Pesachim 2:6). "A woman who was pickling vegetables in a pot" (Tohorot 2:1). "Olives that he pickled with their leaves are clean, for he pickled them only for appearance" (Uktzin 2:1). "Rabbi Yose says: One may pickle onions of terumah in vinegar of unconsecrated produce, but one may not pickle onions of terumah in vinegar of terumah" (Tosefta Terumot 9:3). "One who pickles — until he has pickled as much as needed; one who stews — until he has stewed as much as needed" (Jerusalem Talmud Ma'asrot 4, 51a). "Over a pickled olive one says 'who creates the fruit of the tree'" (ibid., Berakhot 6, 10a). "An etrog that is withered, rotten, pickled, stewed etc. or spotted is unfit" (Sukkah 36a). — *כָּבַשׁ a road, he made a road convenient to pass through, levelled its surface, made it hard, paved it with stones and the like: "Once I was walking on the road, and there was a path passing through a field, and I was walking on it. A little girl said to me: Rabbi, is this not a field? I said to her: Is it not a trodden (כבושה) path? She said to me: Robbers like you have trodden it" (Eruvin 53b). — *כָּבַשׁ a wall and the like, he filled it with earth [Note: So in Arabic, regarding a pit and the like.] and the like between the stones, so that water could not pass through it: "It once happened with a cave that was in the garden of an olive-harvester in Rimmon [Note: So according to the Erfurt manuscript, and so is the reading of Rabbi Samson (of Sens) on Mikva'ot 8:1.] that the priests would seal up (כובשים) [Note: And Rabbi Samson explained there: so that (the water) would collect in one place.] the wall and go down and immerse in it" (Tosefta Mikva'ot 6:2).

— Nif'al, נִכְבַּשׁ, נִכְבְּשָׁה, נִכְבָּשֹוֹת, *לִכָּבֵשׁ, ליכבש, — a) נִכְבְּשָׁה the land, that a person conquered it; and נִכְבְּשָׁה before someone, that he was the ruler over it: "and every armed man of you will pass over the Jordan before the Lord, until He hath driven out His enemies from before Him, and the land be subdued (וְנִכְבְּשָׁה) before the Lord" (Numbers 32:21-22). "And the whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled themselves together at Shiloh, and set up the tent of meeting there; and the land was subdued (נִכְבְּשָׁה) before them" (Joshua 18:1). — And in the Talmud and Midrash: "And why did they not sanctify it (the upper marsh)? Because the weak point of Jerusalem is from there and it is easy to be conquered from there" (Tosefta Sanhedrin 3:4). "Rabbi Joshua said: The Sabbath is entirely holy, and all that is conquered on the Sabbath shall be holy to the Lord" (Numbers Rabbah 14). "Once Jerusalem was conquered, all the great men of the kingdom would take the beautiful women of Jerusalem and seat them with them in the carriage" (Pesikta Rabbati 31). — And נִכְבְּשָׁה the woman, she was raped: "and, lo, we bring into bondage our sons and our daughters to be servants, and some of our daughters are brought into bondage (נִכְבָּשׁוֹת) already; neither is it in our power to help it" (Nehemiah 5:5). — And in a lighter sense, °she submitted: "For their females (of the other animals) do not join the males, and do not submit (נכבשות) and obey them except for the matter of copulation alone, since they are separate from the males and have nothing to do with them; but the female of man had to be a help to him in doing his needs and in preparing his food and the affairs of his house, and therefore it was fitting that she submit and obey him in all that he commands her" (Abarbanel on Genesis 2:21). *And נכבש to him in words, in opinions, he yielded before him, accepted his opinion: "Two companions who were engaged in a matter of halakhah and yield to each other in the halakhah" (Song of Songs Rabbah, "Make haste, my beloved"). — *נִכְבַּשׁ על a woman, with a woman, he lay with her: "The daughter of a priest (married) to an Israelite, and she bore him a son, and the son went and had relations with the maidservant, and she bore him a son" (Yevamot 7:5). "The son went and had relations with the maidservant" (Sifra, Emor 6). — *נִכְבַּשׁ על a thing, he clung to it: "Just as these mountains are pressed upon the deep, so that it not rise up and flood the world, so are the righteous pressed upon the calamity, so that they not go forth and burn the world" (Genesis Rabbah 33). — b) *the fruit נכבש (was pickled) in vinegar and the like: "Unclean locusts that were pickled with clean locusts" (Terumot 10:9). "All things pickled with one another are permitted, except with asafoetida" (ibid. 10). "Arum, and mustard, and lupines, and all other things that are pickled, whether they become sweet or before they become sweet, may be bought with second-tithe money" (Tosefta Ma'aser Sheni 1:13). — c) °נִכְבַּשׁ the earth and the like, it was pushed and pressed with force so that it is stuck together: "And they throw the earth in the middle to raise the mound, and it is made in steps upon steps etc. so that the earth stands, and after it has been well pressed they remove the bricks that hold up the step" (Rashi on Ezekiel 38:20).

— Pi'el, כִּבֵּשׁ, *מְכַבֵּשׁ, — a) כִּבֵּשׁ a nation and the like, he subdued it by force of war: "These also (the vessels of silver and gold) did King David dedicate unto the Lord, with the silver and gold that he dedicated of all the nations which he subdued (כִּבֵּשׁ)" (2 Samuel 8:11). — And in the Talmud and Midrash, כִּבֵּשׁ a land: "Thus we have learned that for seven years they were conquering" (Seder Olam Rabbah 11). "He (David) did not do so, but went on to conquer Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and the Jebusite who was near Jerusalem he did not drive out. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: Near your palace you did not drive out; how are you going on to conquer Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah?" (Sifre Deuteronomy 51). "And how many lands did Joshua conquer?" (ibid. 353). "And would it enter your mind that Israel conquers the land before the Omnipresent?" (Tosefta Avodah Zarah 2:5). "Israel became obligated in fourth-year planting only after fourteen years: seven that they conquered and seven that they divided" (Jerusalem Talmud Peah 7, 20c). "Seventeen jubilees Israel counted from when they entered the Land until they went out etc. of them seven (years) that they conquered and seven that they divided" (Arakhin 12b). "For so we have found that they conquered Jericho only on the Sabbath" (Kuntres of Rabbi Shimon ha-Darshan, Mashkin 2, Genizah). "For the Holy One, blessed be He, knew that (Moses) spoke the truth, and that if He destroys the people in the wilderness and does not conquer before them the land of Canaan, the nations would say of Him that His hand is short" (Rabbenu Nissim Gaon, Berakhot 32a). — And כִבֵּשׁ peoples, kings and the like: "And what peoples did Joshua conquer? Did he not conquer only thirty-one kings? This teaches that he conquered kings and rulers who were from one end of the world to the other" (Sifre Deuteronomy 353). — כִּבֵּשׁ someone, he subdued him: "I have only a gentile whom you have not subdued and who does not dwell with you in the courtyard; a gentile whom you have subdued and who dwells with you in the courtyard, from where?" (Pesachim 8b). — And כִבֵּשׁ a woman, like כָּבַשׁ: "It is a man's way to subdue, and it is not a woman's way to subdue" (Yevamot 65b). — b) *to press and squeeze, כִּבֵּשׁ ashes and the like, he pressed and squeezed them: "And one may not sweep out an oven or a stove, but one may press down (the ashes)" (Beitzah 4:5). — And כִבֵּשׁ a matter, he hid it: "When your disciples are young, hold back from them words of Torah; when they have grown up and become Torah scholars, reveal to them the secrets of Torah" (Song of Songs Rabbah, "For better"). — *כִּבֵּשׁ the spring, he shut it up, held it back: "And the Holy One, blessed be He, held back his spring, and he begot at five hundred years" (Genesis Rabbah 26). — *כִּבֵּשׁ his eye from someone, he closed it, did not look at him: "When the Holy One, blessed be He, sought to destroy the Temple, He said: As long as I am within it, the nations of the world do not touch it; rather I will close My eyes from it and swear that I will not attend to it until the time of the end; and the enemies will come and destroy it" (Lamentations Rabbah, Petichta). — c) *כִּבֵּשׁ olives and the like: "One who pickled his olives in uncleanness and wishes to set aside their terumah in cleanness" (Tosefta Terumot 3:18). — d) *כִּבֵּשׁ millstones, he made them fit for work, dressed (pecked) them: "One may set up an oven, a stove and millstones during the intermediate days of the festival. Rabbi Judah says: One may not dress (מכבשין) [Note: And they said in the Gemara (ibid. folio 10a): "What is מכבשין? Rav Judah said: pecking the millstone; Rav Yechiel said: (making) the eye (of the millstone)." And the origin of this usage has not been clarified.] the millstones for the first time" (Mo'ed Katan 1:9).

— Hif'il, הִכְבִּישׁ, וַיַּכְבִּישׁוּם, — like Qal כָּבַשׁ: "but they turned, and caused the servants and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return, and brought them into subjection (ויכבישום) [Note: So the ketiv; the qere is וַיִּכְבְּשׁוּם, and in some books the ketiv too is ויכבשום, defective spelling.] for servants and for handmaids" (Jeremiah 34:11).

— Pu'al, *כֻּבַּשׁ, מְכֻבַּשׁ, מכובש, that has been conquered: "And would it enter your mind that Israel conquers the land before the Omnipresent? Rather, all the time that they are on it, it is as though it is conquered; when they are not on it, it is as though it is not conquered" (Tosefta Avodah Zarah 4:5). — מְכֻבָּשׁ with precious stones, that has precious stones set in it, German inkrustirt, French incrusté: "How did King Solomon make the throne with his wisdom that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave him? And it was inlaid with precious stones and pearls" (Demut Kisse Shlomo, Beit ha-Midrash [Jellinek], Room 2).

— Nitpa'el, *נִתְכַּבֵּשׁ, — like נִכְבַּשׁ, the land נתכבשה (was conquered): "Yesterday I was the one who declared it clean, and now I say: perhaps it (Ashkelon) was conquered by Torah law; and how can I exempt it (from tithes) by Torah law?" (Jerusalem Talmud Shevi'it 6, 36c; ibid. Yevamot 7, 8a). "For it was the night of Passover, and they were afraid, saying: Now Jerusalem is being conquered by his hand. When they rose early in the morning to stand and recite the Shema and to pray, they found their enemies dead corpses" (Exodus Rabbah 18). "Every single fortress that was in Jerusalem could not be conquered in less than forty days" (ibid., Lamentations Rabbah, "He hath thrown down in His wrath"). "For as long as the lamps are burning, the nations are subdued" (Midrash Tadshe 2, Epstein).

he: בערב' חַ'בַא حٓبآ., פ"ע, יִכְבֶּה, תִּכְבֶּה, *כָּבְתָה, וגם *כָּבַתכמו עָשַׂת במקרא., — כָּבְתָה האֵשׁ, חדלה פתאם מלבער, erlöschen; S'éteindre; be extinguished : והאש על המזבח תוקד בו לא תִכְבֶּה ובער עליה הכהן עצים בבקר בבקר וכו' אש תמיד תוקד על המזבח לא תִכְבֶּה (ויקר' ו ה-ו).  ונר אלהים טרם יִכְבֶּה ושמואל שכב בהיכל יי' (ש"א ג ג).  ונהפכו נחליה לזפת ועפרה לגפרית והיתה ארצה לזפת בערה לילה ויומם לא תִכְבֶּה לעולם יעלה עשנה (ישע' לד ט-י).   כי תולעתם (של הפגרים) לא תמות ואשם (שהפגרים נשרפים בה) לא תִכְבֶּה  (שם סו כד).  והצתי אש בשעריה ואכלה ארמנות ירושלם ולא תִכְבֶּה (ירמ' יז כז).  הנני מצית בך אש ואכלה בך כל עץ לח וכל עץ יבש לא תִכְבֶּה להבת שלהבת (יחזק' כא ג).  באפס עצים תִּכְבֶּה אש (משלי כו כ).  לא יִכְבֶּה בלילה נרה (שם לא יח).  — ובתו"מ: אינו רוצה שיבערו (הגחלים) ואינו רוצה שיכבו (ירוש' שבת ב ה.).  ספר שאחז בו האור מצד אחד נותן מים מצד השני ואם כבה כבה (שם יו יה ד).  אחז בה (בהטלית) האור משני צדדין נוטלה ומתעטף בה ואם כבתה כבתה (שם).  כל ימים שהיה שמעון הצדיק קיים היה נר מערבי דולק משמת שמעון הצדיק פעמים כבה פעמים דלק (שם יומ' ו מג ג).  ארבעים שנה עד שלא נחרב ביהמ"ק היה נר מעריב כבה ולשון של זהורית מאדים (שם).  כבתה (הפתילה) זקוק לה ומותר להשתמש לאורה (שבת כא.).  מוטב תכבה נר של בשר ודם מפני נרו של הקב"ה (שם ל:).  נר הדולק בשבת כבתה מותר לטלטלה וכו' מסתפק מן הנר הכבה ומן השמן המטפטף (שם מד.).  אדם יושב ומצפה אימתי תכבה נרו (שם מו:).  המעצמו (את עיני המת) עם יציאת הנפש הרי זה שופך דמים משל לנר שכבה והולכת אדם מניח אצבעו עליה מיד כבתה (שם קגא:).  הלכה אותה אשה לביתה שהיה ליל שבת ומצאה הנר שלה שכבה אמר לה בעלה היכן היית עד עכשיו (מד"ר דבר' ה).  — ועבר *כָּבַת: בר סירא אמר היתה לפניו גחלת ונפנה בה וביערה רקק בה וכבת (מד"ר ויקר' לג).  עששית אעפ"י שלא כבת מברכין עליה (ירוש' ברכ' ח יב:).  קטורת שכבת חוממה אפילו בקרטין וכו' פתילה שכבת צריכה דישון (שם יומ' ב לט ד).  — וגם בפָעוּל °כָּבוּי, כמו בפועל: כשהיה נר דולק ונר כבוי ונתכוין להדליק זה תְּחִלָה (רש"י כרית' כ.).  ומבעיר התחתונות שהיו כבויות מחמת המשא שהיה עליהן (שם).  דהיאך יקח הבשר מעל הגחלים אולי הגחלים אינן כבויין (מרדכי שבת רנא).  — ובהשאלה לענין החרון, הכעס, וכדומה: ונצתה חמתי במקום הזה ולא תִכְבֶּה (מ"ב כב יז).  הנה אפי וחמתי נתכת אל המקום הזה וכו' ובערה ולא תִכְבֶּה (ירמ' ז כ).  — והחיים, פסקו: ישכבו (אנשי החיל שנפלו במלחמה) בל יקומו דעכו כפשתה כָבוּ (ישע' מג יז).  — ו°אֵשׁ התאוות: נמסו התאוות מלבותם ונעקר מהם הכוסף לתענוגים וכו' וכבתה אש היצר מלבותם (חו"ה, אהב' יי' ז).

— פִע', כִּבָּה, פ"י, כִּבּוּ, תְּכַבֶּה, תְּכַבֶּנָּה, מְכַבֶּה, יְכַבּוּ, וַיְכַבּוּ, כַּבּוֹת, כַּבּוּתְךָ, — כִּבָּה את האש, עשה שתִכְבֶּה, auslöschen;  éteindre;  extinguish : ובערו שניהם יחדו ואין מְכַבֶּה (ישע' א לא).  פן יצלח כאש בית יוסף ואכלה ואין מְכַבֶּה לבית אל (עמו' ה ו).  קנה רצוץ לא ישבור ופשתה כהה לא יְכַבֶּנָּה (ישע' מב ג).  גם סגרו דלתות האולם וַיְכַבּוּ את הנרות וקטרת  לא הקטירו (דהי"ב כט ז).  — ואמר בן סירא: אש לוהטת יכבו מים כן צדקה תכפר חטאת (ב"ס גני' ג ל).  — ובתו"מ: המכבה את הנר מפני שהוא מתירא מפני עכו"ם מפני לסטים (שבת ב ה).  הבונה והסותר המכבה והמבעיר (שם ז ב).  נכרי שבא לכבות אין אומרים לו כבה ואל תכבה מפני שאין שביתתו עליהן אבל קטן שבא לכבות אין שומעין לו (שם טז ו).  ולא כבו הגשמים אש של עצי המערכת (אבות ה ה).  כהן שבא לעשות חשבון עם ישראל והדליק על גביו שמן שריפה ועמד והלך לו אעפ"י כן אין מחייבין אותו לכבותו עד שיכבה מאיליו (ירוש' תרומ' יא מח:).  הבעיר וכיבה בנפיחה אחת (שם שבת ב ה.). החותה גחלים מתחת הקדירה בשבת וכו' חייב שתים אחת שכיבה את העליונות ואחת שהבעיר את התחתונות (שם).  מעשה שנפלה דליקה בחצר יוסי בן סימאי בשיחין וירדו בני קצרה של ציפורין לכבותו ולא הניח להן לכבות אמר להן הניחו לגבאי שיגבה את חובו מיד קשר עליו הענן וירדו גשמים וכיבוהו (שם נדר' ד לח ד).  עששית שהיתה דולקת והולכת כל היום כולו למ"ש מכבה ומדליקה (שבת כג.).  ברזל קשה אור מפעפעו אור קשה מים מכבין אותו (ב"ב י.).  אמר (המלך)  כבו הפנסין והנרות כדי שאדבר עם אוהבי בצינעה (מד"ר קהל', ידעתי כי).  — ובענין ברזל מלֻבּן באש: שכן לוטשי הברזל עושים מחמים את הברזל עד שיעשה גחלת ומכבין אותו במים כדי לחסמו (רמב"ם שבת יב ב).  — ובהשאלה, גם בענין חֹם הגוף של החולה וכדומה: (האש) של חנניה מישאל ועזריה אש של הדיוט והכל יכולים לכבותה וזו של חולה של שמים היא ומי יוכל לכבותה (נדר' מא.).  — ו*כִבַּתכמו עשׂת וכדומה., בענין אש הגיהנם: אמרו רבותינו אשתו של קרח כשירדה לגיהנם כיבת אותה (מד"ר במד' יח).  — ובמליצה, כִּבָּה גחלתו של פלוני, לא השאיר לו שום יורש: והנה קמה כל המשפחה על שפחתך ויאמרו תני את מכה אחיו ונמתהו בנפש אחיו אשר הרג ונשמידה גם את היורש וְכִבּוּ את גחלתי אשר נשארה לבלתי שום לאישי שם ושארית על פני האדמה (ש"ב יד ז).  — כִּבָּה את נר העם, במליצה להמלך: אז (כשנצל דוד מן הסכנה) נשבעו אנשי דוד לו לאמר לא תצא עוד אתנו למלחמה ולא תְכַבֶּה את נר ישראל (ש"ב כא יז).  — ואש הכעס וכדומה: פן תצא כאש חמתי ובערה ואין מְכַבֶּה מפני רע מעלליכם (ירמ' ד ד).  — ואש האהבה: מים רבים לא יוכלו לְכַבּוֹת את האהבה ונהרות לא ישטפוה (שה"ש ח ז).  — והשתמשו המליצים והמשוררים בפעל זה הרבה בהשאלה מליצית, ואמרו בעתיד מקֻצר °יְכַבּ במקום יְכַבֶּה, ובצווי °כַּב: כבה חמת הכוס במי שלג משקה כמו חכם יכב קצף, וראה עלי פנים בעת הורק בו משפת בקבוק כמו קצף (רמב"ע, תרשיש ב).  מי זה אשר יליץ בעד נפשי יכב מחר יקוד אשך ולפידך (עמנ', מחב' יט).  ואור אשי במי ישעך כַּב ושא פני וגל עיני בתורתך (מנח' מלונזנו, שתי הידות, פזמ', אודך אורי).  — ובא גם במשמ' פ"ע, בענין כליון האֻמה: וכסיתי בְכַבּוֹתְךָקצת החדשים מנקדים בִכְבּוֹתְךָ, בקל. שמים והקדרתי את ככביהם (יחזק' לב ז).

— נִפע', °נִכְבָּה, °נִכְבֵּת, נכבית, לְהִכָּבוֹת, לִכָּבוֹת, ליכבוֹת,  — כמו כָּבָה בקל: הגחלת של עץ אם תסיר אדמומיתה נכבת כבר (ר"ח שבת מב.).  שהאש אינה נכבית בעבור שמדליקין ממנה דבר (תקון מדות הנפ' מה).  משיתחילו הפחמין (שצולים עליהם בשר) ליכבות תחתיו מפני שמנו (רגמ"ה חול' קיב.).  האור העליון הפשוט שאין בו הרכבה ואינו  נכבה כהכבות שאר האור הנמצא אצלינו שהוא נכבה מפני הרכבתו (פי' משלי לזרח' הלוי ה).  שבשביל שנכבו (הלפידים) פעם אחת הם נוחין לידלק בפעם אחרת (הלבוש, או"ח שכב ב).  — ואמר המשורר: אך רגע אכאב ביקוד כי יכאָבו, איך נרם ומוקדם גם רגע יִכָבוּכך הנקוד, וכך לפי החרוז. (אד"ם שש"ק, המבכה).  — ובענין °סיד החי כשנותנים אותו במים: שני מימי זרניך שרופים וקלפת רמון ואלום תימני ועפצים וסיד בלתי נכבה מכל אחד שנים עשר זוזים (קאנון ג יו ב ו).

— פֻע', °כֻּבָּה, מְכֻבָּה, — כמו נִכְבָּה: זריקת המים הנעשית ע"י קנה מים היורה כחץ והיא פתאומית ויכובה בנקל יותר במעט מים מאשר יוצק עליו מים רבים ובנחת (מעשה טוביה, יסודי עולם א ב).  מדוע פתילת הנר המכובה פתאם בקושי תאחז האור (שם ג).  — ואמר המשורר: אך סורו כלכם וכבר אש הוּצתה, הן אש לבן היא איננה מכאבת, הלא גם תוכו קדחת הלהבת, ועדי כי שׂרף גם לא כֻבָּתָהכך הנקוד, וכך לפי החרוז. (אדם, שש"ק, מיכל דמעה).

— הִתפ', °הִתְכַּבָּה, — כמו כָּבָה בקל: שהיה מיצר שהנר היה הולך להתכבות וכו' (ר"א אזקרי, חרדים ח).  מדוע תתכבה הלהב מרוח גדול פתאום וכו' ואיך יתכבה אש לעת שזורקים בו סמרטוטים או זבל או בגדי פשתן לחים וכיוצא בהם (מעשה טוביה, יסודי עולם א ב).  ובשביל זה יתמה הרואה איך האש דולק במים ואינו מתכבה (שם).  כמו שיתכבה הנר בסבת נפיחה חזקה עשויה במפוח (שם, ארץ החדשה ב א).
en: In Arabic חַ'בַא حٓبآ., intransitive verb, יִכְבֶּה, תִּכְבֶּה, *כָּבְתָה, and also *כָּבַת [Note: like עָשַׂת in the Bible.], — כָּבְתָה האֵשׁ, it suddenly ceased burning, German erlöschen; French S'éteindre; English be extinguished: "And the fire upon the altar shall be kept burning thereby, it shall not go out, and the priest shall burn wood on it every morning etc. A perpetual fire shall be kept burning upon the altar; it shall not go out" (Leviticus 6:5-6). "And the lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD" (1 Samuel 3:3). "And its streams shall be turned into pitch, and its dust into brimstone, and its land shall become burning pitch; it shall not be quenched night nor day, its smoke shall go up forever" (Isaiah 34:9-10). "For their worm (of the corpses) shall not die, and their fire (in which the corpses are burned) shall not be quenched" (ibid. 66:24). "Then I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem, and it shall not be quenched" (Jeremiah 17:27). "Behold, I will kindle a fire in you, and it shall devour every green tree in you and every dry tree; the flaming flame shall not be quenched" (Ezekiel 21:3). "Where there is no wood, the fire goes out" (Proverbs 26:20). "Her lamp does not go out by night" (ibid. 31:18). — And in the Talmud and Midrash: "He does not want them (the coals) to burn and he does not want them to go out" (Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2, 5a). "A book that caught fire on one side: one puts water on the other side, and if it goes out, it goes out" (ibid. יו יה ד). "If it (the tallit) caught fire on both sides, he takes it and wraps himself in it, and if it goes out, it goes out" (ibid.). "All the days that Simeon the Righteous was alive, the western lamp was burning; once Simeon the Righteous died, sometimes it went out, sometimes it burned" (ibid. Yoma 6, 43c). "Forty years before the Temple was destroyed, the western lamp would go out, and the strip of crimson wool would turn red" (ibid.). "If it (the wick) went out, he must attend to it, and it is permitted to make use of its light" (Shabbat 21a). "Better that the lamp of flesh and blood be extinguished before the lamp of the Holy One, blessed be He" (ibid. 30b). "A lamp burning on the Sabbath that went out may be moved etc. He may draw from the lamp that is going out and from the oil that drips" (ibid. 44a). "A man sits and waits for when his lamp will go out" (ibid. 46b). "He who closes them (the eyes of the dead) as the soul departs is a shedder of blood; it is like a lamp that is going out: if a man puts his finger on it, it goes out at once" (ibid. קגא:). "That woman went home, for it was Friday night, and found that her lamp had gone out; her husband said to her: Where have you been until now?" (Deuteronomy Rabbah 5). — And the past *כָּבַת: "Ben Sira said: There was a coal before him; he turned to it and kindled it, he spat on it and it went out" (Leviticus Rabbah 33). "Over a glass lamp, even though it has not gone out, one says the blessing" (Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 8, 12b). "Incense that went out, its heat, even in small grains etc. A wick that went out requires clearing away" (ibid. Yoma 2, 39d). — And also in the passive participle °כָּבוּי, as with the verb: "When there was a burning lamp and an extinguished lamp and he intended to light this one first" (Rashi Keritot 20a). "And he kindles the lower ones which had gone out because of the load that was on them" (ibid.). "For how could he take the meat off the coals, perhaps the coals are not extinguished" (Mordekhai Shabbat 251). — And figuratively, of wrath, anger and the like: "And My wrath shall be kindled against this place, and it shall not be quenched" (2 Kings 22:17). "Behold, My anger and My wrath shall be poured out upon this place etc. and it shall burn and shall not be quenched" (Jeremiah 7:20). — And of life, ceased: "They shall lie down (the soldiers who fell in battle), they shall not rise; they are extinguished, quenched like a wick" (Isaiah 43:17). — And of °the fire of the desires: "The desires melted from their hearts, and the longing for pleasures was uprooted from them etc. and the fire of the evil inclination was extinguished from their hearts" (Chovot HaLevavot, Love of God 7).

— Pi'el, כִּבָּה, transitive verb, כִּבּוּ, תְּכַבֶּה, תְּכַבֶּנָּה, מְכַבֶּה, יְכַבּוּ, וַיְכַבּוּ, כַּבּוֹת, כַּבּוּתְךָ, — כִּבָּה את האש, he made it go out, German auslöschen; French éteindre; English extinguish: "And both shall burn together, and none shall quench them" (Isaiah 1:31). "Lest He break out like fire in the house of Joseph, and it devour, and there be none to quench it for Bethel" (Amos 5:6). "A bruised reed He shall not break, and a dimly burning wick He shall not quench" (Isaiah 42:3). "They also shut the doors of the porch and put out the lamps, and did not burn incense" (2 Chronicles 29:7). — And Ben Sira said: "Water quenches a blazing fire, so charity atones for sin" (Ben Sira, Genizah 3:30). — And in the Talmud and Midrash: "He who extinguishes the lamp because he is afraid of idolaters, of robbers" (Shabbat 2:5). "Building and demolishing, extinguishing and kindling" (ibid. 7:2). "A gentile who comes to extinguish: one does not say to him 'Extinguish' or 'Do not extinguish', since his resting is not their obligation; but a minor who comes to extinguish, one does not listen to him" (ibid. 16:6). "And the rain did not extinguish the fire of the wood of the altar pile" (Avot 5:5). "A priest who came to make an account with an Israelite and lit burning-oil over him, and got up and went away: even so they do not obligate him to extinguish it, until it goes out by itself" (Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 11, 48b). "If he kindled and extinguished with a single blow" (ibid. Shabbat 2, 5a). "One who rakes coals from under the pot on the Sabbath etc. is liable for two: one for extinguishing the upper ones and one for kindling the lower ones" (ibid.). "It happened that a fire broke out in the courtyard of Yose ben Simai in Shikhin, and the men of the garrison of Sepphoris came down to put it out, and he did not let them put it out; he said to them: Let the collector collect his debt. At once a cloud gathered over it and rain came down and put it out" (ibid. Nedarim 4, 38d). "A glass lamp that was burning on all day long: at the conclusion of the Sabbath he extinguishes it and lights it" (Shabbat 23a). "Iron is hard, fire melts it; fire is hard, water extinguishes it" (Bava Batra 10a). "He (the king) said: Put out the lanterns and the lamps so that I may speak with my friend in privacy" (Ecclesiastes Rabbah, "ידעתי כי"). — And of iron made white-hot in the fire: "For the iron-polishers heat the iron until it becomes a coal, and quench it in water to harden it" (Rambam, Shabbat 12:2). — And figuratively, also of the heat of a sick person's body and the like: "(The fire) of Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah was a fire of an ordinary person, and anyone can extinguish it; but this one of a sick person is of Heaven, and who can extinguish it?" (Nedarim 41a). — And *כִבַּת [Note: like עשׂת and the like.], of the fire of Gehinnom: "Our Rabbis said: The wife of Korah, when she went down to Gehinnom, extinguished it" (Numbers Rabbah 18). — And in poetic speech, כִּבָּה גחלתו של פלוני, he left him no heir at all: "And behold, the whole family has risen against your maidservant, and they say: Give up him who struck his brother, that we may put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed, and we will destroy the heir also; and they would quench my coal which is left, so as to leave my husband neither name nor remnant upon the face of the earth" (2 Samuel 14:7). — כִּבָּה את נר העם, in poetic speech for the king: "Then (when David was saved from the danger) David's men swore to him, saying: You shall go out no more with us to battle, that you not quench the lamp of Israel" (2 Samuel 21:17). — And the fire of anger and the like: "Lest My wrath go forth like fire and burn, and none can quench it, because of the evil of your doings" (Jeremiah 4:4). — And the fire of love: "Many waters cannot quench love, nor can rivers drown it" (Song of Songs 8:7). — And the writers of florid prose and the poets used this verb much in poetic figurative use, and said in the shortened future °יְכַבּ instead of יְכַבֶּה, and in the imperative °כַּב: "Quench the heat of the cup with snow-water, a drink as a wise man quenches anger, and see on it a face when it is poured from the lip of the bottle, like foam" (Moses ibn Ezra, Tarshish 2). "Who is it that will intercede for my soul, will quench tomorrow the blaze of Your fire and Your torch" (Immanuel, Machberot 19). "And quench the light of my fire with the waters of Your salvation, and show me favor and open my eyes in Your Torah" (Menachem Lonzano, Shtei HaYadot, Pizmonim, "אודך אורי"). — And it also occurs in the sense of an intransitive verb, of the extinction of the nation: "And when I extinguish you (בְכַבּוֹתְךָ) [Note: some of the modern scholars vocalize בִכְבּוֹתְךָ, in Qal.] I will cover the heavens and darken their stars" (Ezekiel 32:7).

— Nif'al, °נִכְבָּה, °נִכְבֵּת, נכבית, לְהִכָּבוֹת, לִכָּבוֹת, ליכבוֹת, — like כָּבָה in Qal: "The coal of wood, if you remove its redness, is already extinguished" (Rabbenu Chananel, Shabbat 42a). "For the fire is not extinguished because something is lit from it" (Tikkun Middot HaNefesh 45). "Once the charcoals (on which meat is roasted) begin to go out under it because of its fat" (Rabbenu Gershom Me'or HaGolah, Chullin 112a). "The supernal simple light, in which there is no compounding, and which is not extinguished as the rest of the light found among us is extinguished, which is extinguished because of its compounding" (Commentary on Proverbs by Zerachiah HaLevi 5). "For because they (the torches) were extinguished once, they catch fire easily another time" (the Levush, Orach Chayim 322:2). — And the poet said: "Only for a moment shall I ache in the blaze when they ache, how their lamp and their burning, too, in a moment shall be extinguished (יִכָבוּ) [Note: so vocalized, and so according to the rhyme.]" (Adam HaKohen, Shirei Sefat Kodesh, "המבכה"). — And of °quicklime when it is put in water: "Two kinds of burnt arsenic, and pomegranate peel, and Yemenite alum, and gallnuts, and unslaked lime, of each one twelve zuz" (Canon ג יו ב ו).

— Pu'al, °כֻּבָּה, מְכֻבָּה, — like נִכְבָּה: "The jet of water made by a water pipe that shoots like an arrow and is sudden, and it is extinguished more easily with a little water than when much water is poured on it slowly" (Ma'aseh Tuviyyah, Yesodei Olam 1:2). "Why does the wick of a lamp that was suddenly extinguished catch the fire with difficulty?" (ibid. 3). — And the poet said: "But turn aside, all of you, for already a fire has been kindled; behold, it is the fire of her heart, it does not cause pain, does not the flame burn within it too, and until it burned it was not extinguished (כֻבָּתָה) [Note: so vocalized, and so according to the rhyme.]" (Adam, Shirei Sefat Kodesh, "מיכל דמעה").

— Hitpa'el, °הִתְכַּבָּה, — like כָּבָה in Qal: "For he was distressed that the lamp was about to go out etc." (R. Eleazar Azikri, Charedim 8). "Why is the flame extinguished suddenly by a great wind etc. and how is fire extinguished when rags or dung or wet linen garments and the like are thrown on it" (Ma'aseh Tuviyyah, Yesodei Olam 1:2). "And because of this the observer will wonder how the fire burns in water and is not extinguished" (ibid.). "Just as the lamp is extinguished because of a strong blast made with a bellows" (ibid., Eretz HaChadashah 2:1).

en: Masculine adjective, feminine כְּבֻדָּה, כבוּדה — of honour, of splendour, German prächtig, French magnifique, English magnificent: “And you sat upon a stately bed [note: so, with the ד with dagesh, in all the books, manuscripts and printings, except two manuscripts and three printed books (תנ"ך גזנ', new edition).], and a table prepared before it” (Ezekiel 23:41). — And as a noun: “All glorious is the king's daughter within; her clothing is of settings of gold” (Psalms 45:14).

נְשִׂיא כָבוֹד, שַׁעַר כָּבוֹד, עי' משפט, נשיא, שער.  — ומליצה, שָׁכַן כָּבוֹד, עי' שׁכן.  גאוה. — גאון. —  גדולה. —  הוד. —  הדר. —  °חשׁוב. —  *חשׁיבות. —  *סִלְסוּל. —  שׂררה וכו' ועי' עוד בערך גַּאֲוָה. —  וההפך: קלון, חרפה, וכו'.
en: כָּבֹד, masculine noun, construct כְּבוֹד, כְּבֹד, כְּבוֹדִי, כְּבֹדִי, כְּבוֶֹדָך, כְּבֹדֶךָ, כְּבוֹדֵךְ, כְּבוֹדוֹ, כְּבוֹדָהּ, כְּבוֹדְכֶם, כְּבוֹדָם, — a) importance of distinction that a person or thing has in the eyes of people because of good qualities or great deeds or exalted talent and the like, German Ehre; French honneur; English honour: "And you shall tell my father of all my honor in Egypt (that he is ruler over all Egypt), and of all that you have seen" Genesis 45:13. "The glory has departed from Israel, because the ark of God has been taken" 1 Samuel 4:21. "And I have also given you what you have not asked, both riches and honor, so that there shall not be any among the kings like you" 1 Kings 3:13. "The wise shall inherit honor, but shame exalts fools" Proverbs 3:35. "As snow in summer and as rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool" ibid. 26:1. "Length of days is in her (wisdom's) right hand; in her left hand riches and honor" ibid. 3:16. "He who pursues righteousness and mercy finds life, righteousness and honor" ibid. 21:21. "For You have made him (man) a little lower than God, and have crowned him with glory and majesty" Psalms 8:6. "The glory of this latter house shall be greater than that of the former" Haggai 2:9. "He has stripped me of my glory and taken the crown from my head" Job 19:9. "A son honors his father, and a servant his master; if then I am a father, where is My honor? And if I am a master, where is My fear?" Malachi 1:6. "And the nations shall see your righteousness, and all kings your glory, and you shall be called by a new name" Isaiah 62:2. "The more they increased, the more they sinned against Me; I will change their glory into shame" Hosea 4:7. "And they consecrated themselves to shame, and became abominations like the thing they loved. As for Ephraim, their glory shall fly away like a bird" ibid. 9:10=11. "And what will you do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which shall come from afar? To whom will you flee for help? And where will you leave your glory?" Isaiah 10:3. "Come down from your glory and sit in thirst, O inhabitant, daughter of Dibon" Jeremiah 48:18. "You are filled with shame instead of glory; drink you also, and be uncovered" Habakkuk 2:16. "Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of Your name, and deliver us and forgive our sins for Your name's sake" Psalms 79:9. — עשה or נתן כָּבוֹד to someone, to do deeds that will be an honor to someone, as a sign that one honors him, because one honors him: "And Joshua said to Achan, My son, give, I pray you, glory to the LORD God of Israel, and make confession to Him" Joshua 7:19. "And they (the diviners) said, If (you) send away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it empty, but you shall surely return to Him a guilt offering, etc., and you shall give glory to the God of Israel; perhaps He will lighten His hand from upon you" 1 Samuel 6:3-5. "Let them give glory to the LORD, and declare His praise in the islands" Isaiah 42:12. "Give glory to the LORD your God before He causes darkness, and before your feet stumble upon the dark mountains" Jeremiah 13:16. "If you will not hear, and if you will not lay it to heart, to give glory to My name, says the LORD of hosts, then I will send the curse upon you" Malachi 2:2. "Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength" Psalms 96:8. "And they buried him in the ascent of the tombs of the sons of David, and they did him honor at his death" 2 Chronicles 32:33. — כִּסֵּא כָּבוֹד: "He raises up the poor from the dust, He lifts up the needy from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory" 1 Samuel 2:8. And see כסא. — b) beauty and splendor, German Pracht; French splendeur; English splendour: "And you shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother, for glory and for beauty" Exodus 28:2. "And He shall consume the glory of his forest and of his fruitful field, both soul and body" Isaiah 10:18. "The glory of Lebanon shall come to you, the cypress, the plane tree and the box tree together, to beautify the place of My sanctuary" ibid. 60:13. — And splendor of greatness and majesty, especially of God, German Herrlickeit; French majesté; English majesty, and a term for the cloud with fire blazing within it, of the revelation of the Divinity: "And they looked toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud" Exodus 16:10. "And the glory of the LORD abode upon Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it, etc. And the appearance of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain in the eyes of the children of Israel" ibid. 24:16-17. "And it came to pass, when the priests came out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of the LORD, so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD. Then Solomon said, The LORD has said that He would dwell in thick darkness" 1 Kings 8:10-12. "So I arose and went out into the plain, and behold, the glory of the LORD stood there, like the glory which I saw by the river Chebar" Ezekiel 3:23. — And the greatness of God's works: "The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament shows His handiwork" Psalms 19:2. "Declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among all the peoples" ibid. 96:3. — אֵל הַכָּבוֹד: "The voice of the LORD is upon the waters; the God of glory thunders" ibid. 29:3. — מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד: "Lift up your heads, O gates, and be lifted up, you everlasting doors, that the King of glory may come in. Who is this King of glory? The LORD strong and mighty" ibid. 24:7=8. — And splendor of kingship and the like: "And the fortress shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Aram; they shall be as the glory of the children of Israel" Isaiah 17:3. "When he showed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the honor of his excellent majesty" Esther 1:4. "And Haman told them of the glory of his riches and the multitude of his children" ibid. 5:11. "It (the parched land) shall blossom abundantly, etc.; the glory of Lebanon shall be given to it, the majesty of Carmel" Isaiah 38:2. — c) wealth, possessions, splendid vessels, German Reichtum; French richesse; English riches: "And he (Jacob) heard the words of Laban's sons, saying, Jacob has taken all that was our father's, and from what was our father's he has made all this wealth" Genesis 31:1. "And they shall hang upon him (upon the peg in the wall) all the glory of his father's house, the offspring and the issue, all the small vessels" Isaiah 22:24. "Behold, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the wealth of the nations like a flowing stream" ibid. 66:12. "Take the spoil of silver, take the spoil of gold, for there is no end to the store, wealth of all precious vessels" Nahum 2:10. "You shall eat the riches of the nations, and in their wealth you shall boast yourselves" Isaiah 61:7. — d) the essence of a person's being, his soul, his body [Note: The scholars have already remarked on the similarity between this use of the word כבוד in Hebrew and the use of the Arabic word עִרצ' عِرض, whose root meaning is breadth, and which is used also in the sense of wealth and household goods, and also in the sense of honor, and also in the sense of the essence of a person's being, his nature, his soul, his body. And al-Jawhari says in the Sihah: ואלערצ' איצ'א אלג'שד וכו' ואלערצ' איצ'א אלנפש יקאל אכרמת ענה ערצ'י אי צנת ענה נפשי ופלאנ נקי אלערצ' אי ברי מנ אנ ישתמ ויעאב וקיל ערצ' אלרג'ל חשׂבה, end of quotation, — and in Hebrew: "And al-'ird is likewise the body, etc., and al-'ird is likewise the soul; they say אכרמת ענה ערצ'י, that is, I kept my soul far from him; and פלאנ נקי אלערצ', that is, pure of disgrace and reproach; and some say ערצ' אלרג'ל is a man's good qualities." — And in the Lisan al-'Arab: וערצ' אלרג'ל חשׂכה וקיל נפשה וקיל ח'ליקתה אלמחמודה וקיל מא ימדח בה ויד'מ וכו' וקאל אלערצ' נפש אלרג'ל וקאל פי קולה יג'רי מנ אעראצ'המ מת'ל ריח אלמשׂב אי מנ אנפשהמ ואבדאנהמ וכו' וערצ' אלרג'ל חשבה ויקאל פלאנ כרימ אלערצ' אי כרים אלחשב, end of quotation, — and in Hebrew: "ערצ' אלרג'ל is a man's good qualities and his honor, and some say his soul, and some say his praiseworthy nature, and some say that for which he is praised and blamed; and (Ibn Qutaybah) said: al-'ird is a person's soul; and he said that in the saying וג'רי מנ אעראצ'המ מת'ל ריח אלמשב (there wafts from their a'rad as it were the scent of musk) the intention of the noun אעראצ'הם is their souls and their bodies, etc.; and ערצ' אלרג'ל is a man's praiseworthy nature, and they say פלאנ כרימ אלערצ' (so-and-so is exalted of 'ird), that is, exalted of nature and of praiseworthy qualities."], German Seele, Körper; French äme, corps; English soul, corps: "O my soul, do not come into their council; unto their assembly, my glory, be not united" Genesis 49:6. "Therefore my heart is glad and my glory rejoices; my flesh also shall dwell in safety" Psalms 16:9. "My heart is steadfast, O God; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory" ibid. 108:2. "Let the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it, and tread my life down to the earth, and my glory [Note: Dunash already objected against Rav Saadia Gaon, who explained this כבוד too in the sense of soul, whereas its meaning is in the sense of body, and these are his words: "And (Rav Saadia Gaon) said in explaining וכבודי לעפר ישכן סלה that the glory of the body is the soul, and this is a great error, because the soul is the pearl which the eye does not behold and which is not buried in the dust, etc.; וכבודי לעפר ישכן is said of the body and not said of the soul. Beware, my son, and search out and weigh every word in the balance" (Responsa of Dunash against Rav Saadia Gaon, §41). And likewise R. Judah ibn Bal'am, as Ibn Ezra cited in his name, and these are his words: "R. Judah ibn Bal'am arose and mocked him (R. Moses ha-Kohen, who explained it as Rav Saadia Gaon did, as the soul), for how can the כבוד be the soul when it is written וכבודי לעפר ישכן סלה, and the soul does not dwell in the dust" (Safah Yeterah, §38). And although Ibn Ezra testified there that both R. Adonim and Ibn Bal'am retracted and conceded that the כבוד is the soul, and although R. Jonah ibn Janah too explained כבוד here in the sense of soul, nevertheless the opinion of R. Adonim ben Labrat and Ibn Bal'am is more correct, that here the intention is the body, and the Arabic language supports them, for כבוד is a term both for the soul and for the body.] lay in the dust" ibid. 6:7. — And in Ben Sira and in Talmudic and Midrashic literature, in the principal sense: "Do not glorify yourself in your father's dishonor, for it is no honor to you; a man's honor is his father's honor, and he who dishonors his mother multiplies sin. My son, hold fast to your father's honor, and do not grieve him all the days of his life" Ben Sira (Genizah) 3:10-12. "When Rabbi Akiva died, the honor of the Torah ceased" Sotah 9:15. "Rabbi Eleazar ben Shammua says: Let the honor of your disciple be as dear to you as your own, and the honor of your fellow as the fear of your teacher" Avot 4:12. "The Holy One, blessed be He, has regard for the dignity of His creatures" Mekhilta Mishpatim, Nezikin 12. "You have destroyed yourself and you have destroyed your honor" Sifre Numbers 131. "Great is human dignity, for it overrides a commandment" Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 7, 56a. "They cleared a courtyard because of the impurity and prepared a seat for Jehoshaphat king of Judah; they said: Let this one, who ran after honor, come after that one, who fled from honor" ibid. Sotah 9, 24c. "Everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created, He created only for His glory" Yoma 38a. "Your fathers sought to increase their own honor and wished to diminish the honor of the Omnipresent" ibid. "It is revealed and known before You that I did it not for my honor nor for the honor of my father's house, but for Your honor I did it, so that disputes should not multiply in Israel" Megillah 3a. "It once happened that the sons of Rabbi Akiva died; all Israel came in and eulogized them with a great lament. At the time of their departure Rabbi Akiva stood on a large bench and said: Our brothers, the house of Israel, hear: even had his two sons been bridegrooms, he is comforted on account of the honor that you have done" Moed Katan 21b. "Leave the honor of your mother and do the honor of your father, for you and your mother are both obligated in the honor of your father" Kiddushin 30a. "When the Holy One, blessed be He, said 'I am' and 'You shall have no', the nations of the world said: He seeks His own honor" ibid. "A teacher who has waived his honor, his honor is waived; a prince who has waived his honor, his honor is not waived" ibid. 32b. "How long will you leave aside the honor of the Omnipresent and occupy yourselves with the honor of people?" ibid. "Whoever has no regard for the honor of his Maker, it would have been fitting for him not to have come into the world" ibid. 40a. "That a person should not say, I will read so that they will call me a sage, etc., but learn out of love, and honor will come in the end" Nedarim 62a. "A person should always be careful about the honor of his wife, for blessing is found in a man's house only on account of his wife" Bava Metzia 59a. "Whoever increases the honor of Heaven and diminishes his own honor, the honor of Heaven is increased and his own honor is increased" Numbers Rabbah 4. "The Holy One, blessed be He, said: You stood up from your throne and took three steps in My honor; by your life, I will raise up from you three kings" ibid. Song of Songs, מצאוני. "For I was afraid of you, lest I give your honor to flesh and blood, and I did not wish to bow down to anyone but You" ibid. Esther, ותאמר אסתר. "Joseph gave his life for the honor of his mother, and Esau sought to kill his mother" Pesikta Rabbati 12. — *מפני כבוד a thing, in order to do it honor, so as not to profane its honor: "Between sections one greets (a distinguished person) out of respect and returns a greeting" Berakhot 2:1. "One may not kindle (on the Sabbath) with tar, out of respect for the Sabbath" Shabbat 2:2. "That you said it only out of respect for me — this is my honor" Tosefta Nedarim 4:8. "Out of respect for the Sabbath they permitted it" Jerusalem Talmud Demai 4, 23d. "Among all partners, each can prevent the other in the courtyard, except for laundering, out of respect for the daughters of Israel" ibid. Nedarim 5, 39a. "If there were two corresponding roads, one far and clean and one near and unclean, etc., he goes by the near one out of respect for the public" ibid. Nazir 7, 56a. "For one does not roll up a Torah scroll in public, out of respect for the congregation" Yoma 70a. — *נהג בפלוני כָּבוֹד: "He who learns from his fellow, etc., even a single letter, must treat him with honor" Avot 6:3. "Behold, I make known to you the endearment of My children, so that you treat them with honor" Mekhilta Beshallah 2, Petihta. "Rebuke Ishmael my son, who does not treat me with honor, etc. They (the sages) said: Is it possible (that) Rabbi Ishmael does not treat his parents with honor?" Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1, 15c. "At first, before they (the Egyptians) had seen the honor of Israel, they did not treat them with honor, but in the end, when they saw their honor, they treated them with honor" Sotah 13a. "Rabbi Akiva had twelve thousand pairs of disciples, from Gabbath to Antipatris, and all of them died in one period because they did not treat one another with honor" Yevamot 62b. — *חָלַק כָּבוֹד to someone: "Jericho too could have produced a whole column, but in order to pay honor to Jerusalem it produced half a column" Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 4, 30c. "Wherever there is a desecration of the Name, one does not pay honor to a teacher" Berakhot 19b. "'And He called to Moses,' while all Israel were standing — Scripture comes only to pay honor to Moses" Yoma 4b. "And if I see them paying honor to one another, I know that they are worthy people" Genesis Rabbah 48. "The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: You paid honor one to the other, and I pay you honor, that you shall offer on My Sabbath day" ibid. Numbers 14. "They paid honor to Rabbi Judah because he was a native of the town, and not because he was greater than they in Torah" ibid. Song of Songs, סמכוני. — And a figure of speech, *כְּבוֹדוֹ במקומו, that it was not diminished, it remained as it was before: "Your fathers sought to increase their own honor and wished to diminish the honor of the Omnipresent; now the honor of the Omnipresent is in its place, and He diminished their honor" Yoma 38a. "Whoever diminishes the honor of Heaven and increases his own honor, the honor of Heaven is in its place and his own honor is diminished" Numbers Rabbah 4. — And especially as a kind of apology and asking of pardon when one says something somewhat to a person's discredit: "Rabbi Judah: The father of this one despised Torah scholars, and he too despises Torah scholars. Rabbi Yose said to him: Let the honor of the elder remain in its place; rather, from the day the Temple was destroyed the priests have conducted themselves with self-esteem, in that they do not entrust pure things to everyone" Bekhorot 30b. "With his honor remaining in its place, he did not understand the intention of the sage Ralbag" R. Isaac Abravanel, Shamayim Hadashim 3. — And proverbs: "For a man's honor is his garment" Aggadat Bereshit 63. "Whoever runs after honor, honor flees from him [Note: A saying common in the mouth of the people, based on the saying in Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 9, 24c: "Let this one, who ran after honor, come after that one, who fled from honor," cited above.]". "A man's honor and his disgrace are only in the man he sits with" Mivhar ha-Peninim, Gate of Sitting in Company. "Where there is no honor there is no disgrace" R. Simeon ben Tzemah Duran, Tiferet Yisrael. "Lowliness and noble lineage are two twins, and humility and honor are two pleasant brothers" R. Menahem Meiri, Meshiv Nefesh, in the name of the Arab sages. — And in the sense of greatness, splendor and majesty: "Moses stood by the sea; Moses told it in the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, to split, and it did not accept it; he showed it the staff, and it did not accept it, until the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself over it in His glory; and as soon as the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself in His glory and His might, the sea began to flee" Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 5, 55a. — And a figure of speech, בעצמו ובכבודו: "The Holy One, blessed be He, said: They associated themselves with Me; I too will associate Myself with them, to count them Myself in My own person and My glory" Numbers Rabbah 4. — *בכבודכם, yourselves: "When my end arrives and the Omnipresent decrees my death, you shall fulfill my testament, as our Rabbis of blessed memory warned that it is a commandment to fulfill the words of the dead, and you shall see for yourselves whether everything is found at the time of my death" Responsa of the Geonim, Harkavy 370. — *כְּבוֹד so-and-so, an expression of courtesy when a person mentions the name of someone great and dear to him: "The distinguished, precious, learned and understanding disciple, crown of the disciples, glory of the sages, the honored sage R. Samuel son of the sage Rabbi Judah ibn Tibbon" Letter of Rambam to R. Samuel ibn Tibbon. "The precious, honored sage, the honored Rabbi Meir" ibid. "I have already informed the glory of the honor of the greatness of the holiness of our master and teacher Pinhas" the same, to R. Pinhas בר"ש. "Master and Rabbi Jonathan ha-Kohen, treasure of the priests, son of the honored, great and holy master and Rabbi David, of blessed memory" the same, to R. Jonathan ha-Kohen. "And the honored son knows, as God, blessed be He, lives, etc., and what I desire of the honored, beloved son (that is, of you) is that you do not answer this man, your adversary, etc., and the honored son knows that these greatnesses and dominions, etc." the same, to Joseph Aknin. "Jonathan ha-Kohen, treasure of the sages, son of the honored, our lord, our holy one, our teacher and our master David, of blessed and saintly memory" the same, Pe'er ha-Dor, responsum 41. "The precious young man, son of the honored greatness of the holiness of our master and teacher Zechariah the elder" ibid. 154. "A ruling came from the honored greatness of the holiness of the glory of our lord, our master Moses the judge" Samuel ha-Levi, responsum on Rambam's ruling. "Saadia son of R. Maimon son of R. Moses son of R. Maimon, son of the honored sage, the judge Rabbi Moses son of R. Maimon, may his memory be for the life of the world to come" R. Saadia ibn Danan, in Responsa Pe'er ha-Dor 225. "A courtyard in which the honored R. Jacob di Viana lived, and which belonged to the honored Rabbi Moses the physician Vidal, the maternal grandfather of the honored Rabbi Joseph mentioned above" Responsa of Ralbah 25. "And my heart has not let me get my breath back, to find a soft answer arranged for my honored lord, for there is no word on my tongue" Iggeret Dofi ha-Zeman, to ר"י עובדיה. "And the incident that happened was thus: my honored lord father of blessed memory bought houses, etc." Responsa Maharshakh 2:81. — °כבוד חכמתו: "And behold, I open wide my mouth, waiting as for the latter rain for his clear answers and his pure sayings on all that I asked of his honored wisdom in my earlier letters" Letter of R. Samuel ibn Tibbon to Rambam. — And with suffixes °כבודך, כבודכם, כבודו, כבודם: "And I entreat your honor to explain to me the places where I shall use my qualities in a praiseworthy and in a blameworthy way" Hovot ha-Levavot, Avodat ha-Elohim 10. "The writer informs his honor that his precious letter has reached the hand of his servant" Letter of R. Samuel ibn Tibbon to Rambam. "And I am afraid of adding to my questions lest I greatly trouble his honor, etc., for I know that it will be good in the eyes of his honor to remove wrong from our tents" ibid. "It is known before your honor that no dispute has arisen from this, and the experts who are here in the permitted and forbidden, and all the sages here, incline to forbid" Minhat Kenaot by Abba Mari 5. "And now I will tell before your honors the things that I know" ibid. 12. "And furthermore, your honor knows that the hire of vessels and animals is subject to the law of overreaching" Responsa of the Rosh 13:20. "And I say that all that your honor objected here, you objected well, and your opinion agreed with the opinion of the early authorities" Responsa of R. Nissim Gerondi 8. "Your honor wrote, holding to what you wrote at first, that the levir has no produce at all" Responsa of Rivash 387. "And it came to pass today that God, blessed be He, brought this bearer before me, and I decided to clear myself of other affairs in order to reply to your honor; but first let me set before your honor what people who were there told me about the matter of that customs duty" Responsa of Maharik 195. "And therefore I decided to write to your honors what seems right in my humble opinion, because of the great urging with which they urged me to express an opinion" ibid. 181. "I, the poorest in my thousand, etc., inform your exalted honors that it was told to me and I heard of the matter that occurred" Tashbetz 3:286. "And as your honor wrote in one responsum" Responsa Besamim Rosh 56. "And the stars of the heavens, their constellations in this generation, who has counted, except one from the city, etc., and a second to him from the land of Egypt, etc., and your honor the third; your wisdom is wonderful in my eyes" introduction to Elim, by Joseph Delmedigo. "And also those appointed officials retracted and wish to hold you back, and your honor claims that the officials have already waived their claim on you" Responsa Binyamin Ze'ev 225. "I examined and investigated the writing that your honor brought in his hand from the city of Florence, may God protect it, amen" Responsa Mayim Rabbim, Yoreh De'ah 18. "And perhaps you will want some further thing of me; I beseech your honors to come to my house of study today" Responsa Tummat Yesharim 33. "I asked of his honor several times to hand it over to me to print it" Manasseh ben Israel, at the beginning of the book Elim. "In reply to their honors' letter of the 13th of this month" Letters of יל"ג 1:69. "If their honors consent to this, let them inform me approximately how much they can pay for each and every sheet" ibid. — And likewise in Hebrew speech in the Land of Israel, כבודו שֹׁמע, כבודו ראה and the like. — °חוץ מכבודך, a kind of asking of pardon when a person finds fault with the words of one greater than he and the like: "And saving your honor, your intention is not good" Responsa of R. Nissim Gerondi 5. "Saving your honor, all those fine distinctions are needless" Responsa of Rivash 24. "And in any case, either way, it appears that even if he is a sage, saving his honor, he did not act as a sage" ibid. 216. "And saving the honor of his wisdom, it does not appear at all that Israel were in doubt about the existence of God" Minhat Kenaot, by ר"י מפיסא, 16. "And saving his honor, it is impossible to say so" Responsa of Maharik 72. "And saving their honor (of the sages of the Talmud), their saying in this is not true" R. Isaac Abravanel, 1 Kings 19. "And the commentators have already thought that of these two divisions, etc., and saving their honor, it is not so" the same, Nahalat Avot 4. "And the Rabbi (Rambam) sensed that this is not among their purposes, and saving his honor, the matter is not so" the same, Shamayim Hadashim 4:6. — And חוץ לכבודו: "And how much (Rambam) sank his intellect in the Greek mire, saving his honor, of blessed memory" R. Jacob Emden, Migdal Oz 108a. — And במחילה מכבודו: "With pardon of your honor, the merchant, you have of heaviness a portion fit to make heavy the hearts of men" She'erit ha-Nahalah 22. "And as for what my father-in-law the Rabbi, may God preserve him, wrote, that it is forbidden to drink it, etc. — with pardon of his honor, it is not something intoxicating" Halakhot Ketanot by R. Jacob Hagiz, Orah Hayyim 9. "And they did not write to us what occurred to their minds in this matter, and all this is, with pardon of their honor, because they did not set their hearts to search out and seek where the cause of the making of the songs comes from" introduction to Ruah Hadashah. "For I have seen that the great commentator Rashi of blessed memory, with pardon of his honor, also fell into this pitfall of his grandson the Rashbam regarding the time of the months of the Kallah" שי"ר, Toledot ר"ח. — °בְּכָבוֹד, בכבוד אדוני, an expression of courtesy when one invites a person to something, or when he asks for something and one answers him so, in the sense of willingly and with feelings of respect. — e) in the astronomy of the ancients, °a description of the stars according to their size and their light: "Every star whose light is great they call of the first magnitude, and what is less than it, of the second magnitude" Ibn Ezra, Reshit Hokhmah, Paris manuscript. "And they place only the stars that are of the first magnitude or of the second magnitude; and the meaning of first and second magnitude is that King Ptolemy divided all the fixed stars into six parts according to the size of their bodies, and the largest are fifteen whose value is equal, and they are of the first magnitude; and others whose value is equal are of the second magnitude, and after them of the fourth magnitude, and after them of the fifth magnitude, and after them of the sixth magnitude" the same, Kelei ha-Nehoshet 1. "There arose a great sage who translated an honored book on the constellations, etc., and the measure of the upper stars that are in the sphere of the zodiac, and he divided them into six degrees, and the first degree he calls the first magnitude" the same, preface to the translation of the book אלמתני.
