he: עי' הערה לקמן., — קל לא נמצא.

— הִפע' מקור, הָכִיל, לְהָכִיל, — הֵכִילָה החרב וכדומה, הבריקה ונוצצה והאצילה מעצמה כעין ניצוצי ברק מתחלפים ומשתנים, flimmern; scintiller; to glitter sparkle: ואתה בן אדם הנבא ואמרת כה אמר אדני יי' אל בני עמון ואל חרפתם ואמרת חרב חרב פתוחה לטבח מרוטה לְהָכִילהתרגומ' הקדמונ' ראו במלה זו פע' מענין כליון, וכעין זה פרש גם ריב"ג, אמר (שם, בהמשתלחק) וז"ל: ומנ הד'א אלאצל והד'א אלמעני להכיל למען ברק, ע"כ, ובעבר': ומזה השרש (שרש מיוחד כיל שממנו אכלך בדרך) וזו המשמע' (של כליון והשמדה) להכיל למען ברק. וכן בהשרשים. אבל רד"ק פרש מן א. כול: פרוש החרב הוחדה להחזיק ולסבול ההרג ולמען הרבות ברקה להפחיד העמים. ע"כ. והביא שם בשם אביו שפרש להכיל כמו להאכיל. אך כל זה אינו מניח הדעת בפרוש הכתוב. ומהחדשים, קצתם מקימים הנוסחה המסורה ומתקשים בפרוש הכתוב ופרשוה בדרכים זרים, וקצתם פסלו את הנוסחה, אעפ"י שאין ספק בדבר כי כבר לפני המתרגמים הקדמונ' היתה הנוסחה כמו שהיא בידינו. Kornil הגיה להחל במקום להכיל, אבל בהגהה זו לא נרפא הכתוב, כי אין שום טעם במליצה שהחרב מרוטה להתחיל למען ברק, ובודאי שמבחינת סגנון המליצה בלבדו יותר מוטעמת היא הגהת קצת החדשים שפשוט מחקו את המלה להכיל וגֹרסים מרוטה למען ברק, כמו בפסוק יה: למען טבח טבח הוחדה למען היה לה ברק מרטה. אבל, נתוּח בסכין חריפה כזה הוא דרך קל מאד בפרוש ספר עתיק ואין צרך בחכמה יתרה לדרך כזה, ואולם כאן בהכתוב אי אפשר לקבל הגהה זו כי אין להבין מאין באה המלה להכיל תחת ידי הסופרים המעתיקים, הואיל ובכל הפסוקים לפניה ולאחריה אין מלה קצת דומה לה שנוכל לאמר כי נסרכה משם להנה. ובהיות שאין שום יסוד שירשה לנו למחוק המלה, ולא מצאו החכמים הגהה בצורת המלה שתרפא את המליצה רפואה שלמה, אנו חיבים להניח את המלה להכיל כצורתה בנוסחה המסורה, ועל פי פסוק יה שהובא קודם שנתן שם הסבה למריטת החרב למען היות לה ברק אי אפשר לפרש את המלה הכיל כאן אלא כמו"כ במשמ' מבריק ונוצץ, והמליצה להכיל למען ברק אינה אלא כפל הענין במלים שונות הרגילה במליצת המקרא. ומי שיקשה לו לקבל כפילת מלים אלה ללא צרך במקום הזה יוכל להניח כי העקר הוא המלה להכיל במשמ' להבריק ולנוצץ ונוספו המלים למען ברק על הגליון לפרוש, ונכנסו אח"כ בתוך גוף הכתוב, כמו שכבר העירו המפרשים על מציאות הוספות לפרוש במקומות אחרים במקרא. ואם אין ראיה מפורשת לפרוש מלת הכיל במשמ' להבריק ולנוצץ, סמך לו יש בלשון הערבית. כי הנה גם עצם השרש כיל בערב' שהוא כול העברי ומשמש בעקרו באותה המשמ' כמו בעבר' בענין מדידה, שחשד פרנק' שבמשמ' זו אינו ערבי, עי' הערה לא. כול, הוא משמש עוד בקצת משמ' אחרות, כמו בענין הצֹר שהקישו עליו ואינו נותן ניצוצות, וכמו"כ להפך במשמ' גצים הנפרשים מן הצֹר כשמקישים עליו, ואין שום יחס בין משמ' זו ובין משמ' העקרית של השרש כיל בענין מדידה. ועל כרחנו אנו צריכים לאמר כי היו שם בלשון שני שרשים של כול או של כיל או אחד כול ואחד כיל, שהאחד מהם שמש במשמ' מדידה והשני באיזו משמ' אחרת שממנה נסתעפה המשמ' בדבר הצור והגצים שיוצאים ממנו כשמקישים עליו בברזל, ואפשר שזו היא המשמ' שממנה נסתעפה משמ' הברקה להמלה הכיל. ויש עוד בערב' צרוף אחר לוח لوح וגם הוא משמש בשתי משמעות, האחת כמו לוח בעבר', בענין לוּח של עץ וכדומה, והשנית במשמ' רחוקה מאד מזו, והיא: הבריק ונוצץ. אמר אלג'והרי בהצחאח: לאח אלשׁי ילוח לוחא אי למח וכו' ולאח אלברק ואלאח אד'א אומצ' ולאח אלנג'מ ואלאח אד'א בדא קאל אבנ אלשכית לאח שהיל אד'א בדא ואלאח אד'א תלאלא וכו' ואלאח בשיפה למע בה, ע"כ ובעבר': לאח הדבר ר"ל נוצץ וכו' ולאח הברק וגם אלאח כשהתחיל לנצנץ, ולאח הכוכב ואלאח כשהתחיל להאיר, אמר אבן אלשכית לאח הכוכב שהיל כשהתחיל מאיר ואלאח כשהוא מבריק ונוצץ וכו' ואלאח בחרבו הבריק בה. וכמו"כ בלשאן אלערב: אלאח באלשיפ ולוח למע בה וחרכה ולאח אלנג'מ בדא ואלאח אצ'א ובדא ותלאלא ותשע צ'וה, ע"כ, ובעבר': אלאח בהסיף הבריק בו והניפו ולאח הכוכב יצא והתחיל להאיר ואלאח האיר ונצנץ ופשט קרני נגהו. והביא בית של אלמתלמש שאמר: וקד אלאח שהיל בעד מא הג'עוא כאנה צ'רמ באלכפ מקבוש, ע"כ, ובעבר': וכבר האיר ונצנץ הכוכב שהיל אחרי אשר נמו שנתם כאלו היה לפיד בכף היד דולק. מכל זה אנו רואים כי הצרוף לוח, בקל לאח ובהפע' אלאח, משמש במשמ' הבריק ונצנץ, להברק ולהכוכבים, וגם לברק החרב כשמניפים אותה באור השמש. והנה הצרוף לוח איננו ממש צרוף כול, כי במקום הכף שמלה העברית יש בהמלה הערב' ח, אבל בקצת מקרים נהוג בין שתי לשונות הללו חלוף בין כ— ח' ובמקום כ בעברית תבוא בערב' לפעמים ח' خ, כמו במקום כבה — ח'בא خبا, כנע — ח'נע خنع, רך— רח'י رخى, ובהיות שהצרוף לוח משמש בערב' בשתי משמ', לוח של עץ וברק ונצנוץ, שהן רחוקות מאד זו מזו, יש לחשב כי היו כאן בתחלה שני שרשים מתחלפים זה מזה באות אחת, והצרוף לוח המשמש עתה בערב' במשמ' של ברק היה קודם לוח' لوخ שהוא בעבר' לוכ, שהוא כול. וכבר העירו חל"ע על מנהג זה בתוך הלשון הערב' בעצמה שצרוף מהצרופים שלה נתחלף בזמן מן הזמנים באות אחת שלו לאות אחרת דומה לה. כך R. Ruzhcka בעתון OLZ, 16 252, בדבר הסתעפות ע'פר מן עפר. עכ"פ, אפילו אם לא נאמר כי הכיל הוא הוא לאח שבערב', אנו רואים כי יש בלשון הזו פעל קצת דומה להכיל שמשמ' היא נצנץ. למען ברק (יחזק' כא לג).
en: [Note: See the note below.], — Qal not found.

— Hif'il infinitive, הָכִיל, לְהָכִיל, — הֵכִילָה the sword and the like, flashed and sparkled and gave off from itself something like alternating and changing sparks of lightning, German flimmern, French scintiller, English to glitter sparkle: "And thou, son of man, prophesy and say, Thus saith the Lord GOD concerning the Ammonites, and concerning their reproach; even say thou, The sword, the sword is drawn: for the slaughter it is furbished, to flash (לְהָכִיל) [Note: The ancient translations saw in this word a verb in the sense of destruction (כליון), and Rabbi Jonah ibn Janah also explained it in a similar way; he said (ibid., in al-Mustalhaq), in these words: ומנ הד'א אלאצל והד'א אלמעני להכיל למען ברק, end quote, and in Hebrew: "And from this root (a separate root כיל, from which אכלך בדרך) and this meaning (of destruction and annihilation) is להכיל למען ברק." And likewise in the Book of Roots. But Radak explained it from כול I: "The meaning: the sword was sharpened to hold and endure the killing, and in order to increase its flash, to frighten the nations." End quote. And he brought there in the name of his father that he explained להכיל as like להאכיל. But none of this satisfies the mind as an interpretation of the verse. And of the moderns, some uphold the traditional reading and struggle with the interpretation of the verse and have explained it in strange ways, and some have rejected the reading, even though there is no doubt that the reading was already as we have it before the ancient translators. Kornil emended להחל instead of להכיל, but by this emendation the verse is not healed, for there is no sense at all in the expression that the sword is furbished to begin for the sake of flashing; and certainly from the standpoint of the style of the expression alone, the emendation of some of the moderns, who simply deleted the word להכיל and read מרוטה למען ברק, as in verse 15: "It is sharpened to make a sore slaughter; it is furbished that it may glitter (למען היה לה ברק מרטה)", is more sensible. But surgery with such a sharp knife is a very easy way of interpreting an ancient book, and no special wisdom is needed for such a way; and here in this verse it is impossible to accept this emendation, for one cannot understand where the word להכיל came from into the hands of the copying scribes, since in all the verses before it and after it there is no word even somewhat resembling it of which we could say that it was dragged from there to here. And since there is no basis at all that would permit us to delete the word, and the scholars have not found an emendation of the form of the word that would heal the expression completely, we are obliged to leave the word להכיל in its form in the traditional reading; and according to verse 15 quoted above, which gives there the reason for the furbishing of the sword, "that it may glitter", it is impossible to interpret the word הכיל here except likewise in the sense of flashing and sparkling, and the expression להכיל למען ברק is nothing but the doubling of the idea in different words that is usual in biblical rhetoric. And whoever finds it hard to accept the doubling of these words needlessly in this place may suppose that the essential word is להכיל in the sense of to flash and to sparkle, and the words למען ברק were added in the margin as an explanation and afterwards entered into the body of the text, as the commentators have already remarked on the presence of explanatory additions in other places in the Bible. And if there is no explicit proof for interpreting the word הכיל in the sense of flashing and sparkling, there is support for it in the Arabic language. For behold, even the root כיל itself in Arabic, which is the Hebrew כול and is used originally in the same sense as in Hebrew, concerning measuring — about which פרנק' suspected that in this sense it is not Arabic, see the note to כול I — is also used in some other senses, as of a flint that was struck and gives no sparks, and likewise, conversely, in the sense of sparks scattered from the flint when it is struck; and there is no relation at all between this sense and the principal sense of the root כיל concerning measuring. And perforce we must say that there were in the language there two roots כול, or two כיל, or one כול and one כיל, one of which served in the sense of measuring and the other in some other sense, from which branched off the sense concerning the flint and the sparks that come out of it when it is struck with iron; and it is possible that this is the sense from which the sense of flashing branched off for the word הכיל. And there is in Arabic yet another combination, לוח لوح, and it too is used in two senses: one like לוח in Hebrew, concerning a board (לוּח) of wood and the like, and the other in a sense very remote from this, namely: flashed and sparkled. Al-Jawhari said in al-Sihah: לאח אלשׁי ילוח לוחא אי למח וכו' ולאח אלברק ואלאח אד'א אומצ' ולאח אלנג'מ ואלאח אד'א בדא קאל אבנ אלשכית לאח שהיל אד'א בדא ואלאח אד'א תלאלא וכו' ואלאח בשיפה למע בה, end quote, and in Hebrew: "לאח the thing, that is, sparkled etc.; and לאח the lightning, and also אלאח, when it began to flicker; and לאח the star, and אלאח, when it began to shine; Ibn al-Sikkit said: לאח the star Suhayl, when it began to shine, and אלאח when it flashes and sparkles etc.; and אלאח with his sword, he flashed with it." And likewise in Lisan al-Arab: אלאח באלשיפ ולוח למע בה וחרכה ולאח אלנג'מ בדא ואלאח אצ'א ובדא ותלאלא ותשע צ'וה, end quote, and in Hebrew: "אלאח with the sword: flashed with it and brandished it; and לאח the star: came out and began to shine; and אלאח: shone and sparkled and spread out the rays of its brightness." And he cited a verse of al-Mutalammis, who said: וקד אלאח שהיל בעד מא הג'עוא כאנה צ'רמ באלכפ מקבוש, end quote, and in Hebrew: "And already the star Suhayl shone and sparkled after they had slumbered their sleep, as if it were a torch burning in the palm of the hand." From all this we see that the combination לוח, in Qal לאח and in Hif'il אלאח, is used in the sense of flashed and sparkled, for lightning and for the stars, and also for the flash of a sword when it is brandished in the light of the sun. Now the combination לוח is not exactly the combination כול, for in place of the kaf of the Hebrew word there is ח in the Arabic word; but in some cases an interchange between כ and ח' is customary between these two languages, and in place of a Hebrew כ there sometimes comes in Arabic ח' خ, as in place of כבה — ח'בא خبا, כנע — ח'נע خنع, רך — רח'י رخى; and since the combination לוח is used in Arabic in two senses, a board of wood and flashing and sparkling, which are very remote from each other, one must think that there were here at first two roots differing from each other in one letter, and the combination לוח that is now used in Arabic in the sense of flashing was previously לוח' لوخ, which in Hebrew is לוכ, which is כול. And חל"ע have already remarked on this phenomenon within the Arabic language itself, that one of its combinations was changed at some period in one of its letters into another letter similar to it. So R. Ruzhcka in the journal OLZ, 16 252, concerning the derivation of ע'פר from עפר. In any case, even if we do not say that הכיל is the very same as the Arabic לאח, we see that there is in this language a verb somewhat similar to הכיל whose meaning is: sparkled.] because of the flashing" (Ezekiel 21:33).

he: בארמ' וערב', עי' הערה להשרש., פ"י, עב' כָּל, כַּלְתִּי, כַּלְתָּ, צווי כּוּל, — כָּל העפר וכדומה, מדד אותו messen; mesurer; to measure: מי מדד בשעלו מים ושמים בזרת תכן וְכָל בשלש עפר הארץ ושקל בפלס הרים וגבעות במאזנים (ישע' מ יב).  — ואמר הפיטן: כָּל להשקות נשי מתחתיות מים, כשָׁר בבעלי זרוע כי יחמסו מים (ר"א קליר, גשם, אקשטה).  ומדדת ושקלת וְכַלְתָּ ואמדת וצברת (פר' שקל', אז ראית).  — ואמר המשורר: ומי מי ים בכף מדד וְכָל בחמת (רמב"ע, דיואן קכד, כ"י בודליאנה).

— הפע', הֵכִיל, הָכִיל, יָכִיל, יָכִלוּ, יְכִילֶנוּ, — א) הֵכִיל בו כך וכך, יש בו מקום כדי כך וכך, שאפשר להכניס בו כך וכך, fassen; contenir; contain: ויעש את הים מוצק עשר באמה משפתו עד שפתו עגל סביב וכו' אלפים בת יָכִיל (מ"א ז כג-כו).  ויעש עשרה כירות נחשת ארבעים בת יָכִיל הכיור האחד (שם לח).  ביום ההוא קדש המלך את תוך החצר אשר לפני בית יי' כי עשה שם את העלה ואת המנחה ואת חלבי השלמים כי מזבח הנחשת אשר לפני יי' קטן מֵהָכִיל את העלה ואת המנחה ואת חלבי השלמים (שם ח סד).  כוס אחותך תשתי העמקה והרחבה תהיה לצחק וללעג מרבה לְהָכִיל (יחזק' כג לב), ר"ל שתכיל הרבה.  — ומצוי בספרות במשמ' זו: חמש כדות גדולות שאין מכילה הקופה יותר מכדה אחת (ר"ח, שבת קכז.).  וכמה מכילה מדה זו כמו ארבעים ושלש ביצים בינוניות (רמב"ם, ביכור' ו).  — והלֵב וכדומה: לא גילה לי אדם מעולם סוד שהפקדתיו והאשמתיו אבל האשמתי את לבי מפני שהיה צר יותר להכילו בעת שהפקדתיו בלבו (מבח' הפנינ', שער הסוד).  — ובדברים מפשטים: כי כל אשר אין לו חקר לא יכילהו מקום וכו' ולא יתכן להכיל נקצב ללא נקצב ואיך יכילך מקום ואתה יצרתו וכו' כי כל נמצא זולתך מקום יכילהו וזמן יתארהו (ר' בחיי, בקשה, יי' שפתי).  הצורה היותר מכילה שבצורות היא הכדורית (ר"א ברר"ח הנשיא, אשפירא א).  — ב) הֵכִיל הכלי את המים וכדומה, החזיק אותם שלא יצאו ממנו, halten; retenir; to hold: לחצב להם בארת בארת נשברים אשר לא יָכִלוּ המים (ירמ' ב יג). ג) בהשאלה, הֵכִיל דברי פלוני, יכול לשאתם ולסבלם, aushalten; supporter; sustain: וישלח אמציה כהן בית אל אל ירבעם מלך ישראל לאמר קשר עליך עמוס בקרב בית ישראל לא תוכל הארץ לְהָכִיל את כל דבריו (עמו' ז י).  — והכעס וכדומה: ואת חמת יי' מלאתי נלאיתי הָכִיל שפך על עולל בחוץ ועל סוד בחורים יחדו (ירמ' ו יא).  מקצפו תרעש הארץ ולא יָכִלוּ גוים זעמו  (שם י י).  — ואת המעשים הגדולים: כי גדול יום יי' ונורא מאד ומי יְכִילֶנּוּ (יוא' ב יא).  — ובסהמ"א: כי תשנא (האשה) את שונאיה שמאסוה ולא יכילוה (ראב"ע משלי ל כב).
en: [Note: In Aramaic and Arabic; see the note to the root.], transitive verb, past כָּל, כַּלְתִּי, כַּלְתָּ, imperative כּוּל, — כָּל the dust and the like, to measure it, German messen, French mesurer, English to measure: "Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span, and comprehended (וְכָל) the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales and the hills in a balance?" (Isaiah 40:12). — And the liturgical poet said: "He measured (כָּל) to give drink to the women of the waters below, as he contended with the men of the arm who robbed the waters" (Rabbi Eleazar Kalir, Geshem, אקשטה). "And you measured and weighed and meted out (וְכַלְתָּ) and estimated and heaped up" (Parashat Shekalim, אז ראית). — And the poet said: "And who measured the waters of the sea in the hollow of the hand and meted out (וְכָל) with a span" (Rabbi Moses ibn Ezra, Diwan 124, Bodleian manuscript).

— Hif'il, הֵכִיל, הָכִיל, יָכִיל, יָכִלוּ, יְכִילֶנוּ, — a) הֵכִיל בו so and so much, it has room for so and so much, so that so and so much can be put into it, German fassen, French contenir, English contain: "And he made the molten sea of ten cubits from brim to brim, round in compass etc.; it held (יָכִיל) two thousand baths" (1 Kings 7:23-26). "And he made ten lavers of brass; one laver contained (יָכִיל) forty baths" (ibid. 38). "The same day did the king hallow the middle of the court that was before the house of the LORD; for there he offered the burnt-offering, and the meal-offering, and the fat of the peace-offerings, because the brazen altar that was before the LORD was too little to receive (מֵהָכִיל) the burnt-offering, and the meal-offering, and the fat of the peace-offerings" (ibid. 8:64). "You shall drink of your sister's cup, which is deep and large; it shall be for a laughing-stock and a derision, it contains much (מרבה לְהָכִיל)" (Ezekiel 23:32), that is, that it will hold much. — And it is common in the literature in this sense: "Five large jars, for the basket does not hold (מכילה) more than one jar" (Rabbenu Hananel, Shabbat 127a). "And how much does this measure hold (מכילה)? About forty-three medium eggs" (Rambam, Bikkurim 6). — And the heart and the like: "No person ever revealed to me a secret that I entrusted it and blamed him, but I blamed my own heart, because it was too narrow to contain it (להכילו) when I entrusted it to his heart" (Mivchar ha-Peninim, Gate of the Secret). — And of abstract things: "For whatever has no limit, no place can contain it (יכילהו) etc., and it is not possible for the bounded to contain (להכיל) the boundless; and how can a place contain You (יכילך), when You formed it etc.; for every existing thing besides You, a place contains it (יכילהו) and time describes it" (Rabbi Bahya, Bakkashah, יי' שפתי). "The most capacious (היותר מכילה) of the shapes is the spherical" (Rabbi Abraham bar Hiyya ha-Nasi, אשפירא 1). — b) הֵכִיל the vessel the water and the like, to hold it so that it does not come out of it, German halten, French retenir, English to hold: "To hew them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold (יָכִלוּ) no water" (Jeremiah 2:13). c) Figuratively, הֵכִיל the words of so-and-so, to be able to bear and endure them, German aushalten, French supporter, English sustain: "Then Amaziah the priest of Beth-el sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying: Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel; the land is not able to bear (לְהָכִיל) all his words" (Amos 7:10). — And anger and the like: "Therefore I am full of the fury of the LORD, I am weary with holding it in (הָכִיל); pour it out upon the babes in the street, and upon the assembly of young men together" (Jeremiah 6:11). "At His wrath the earth trembles, and the nations are not able to abide (יָכִלוּ) His indignation" (ibid. 10:10). — And great deeds: "For the day of the LORD is great and very terrible, and who can abide it (יְכִילֶנּוּ)?" (Joel 2:11). — And in medieval literature: "For she (the woman) hates her enemies who despised her and would not bear her (יכילוה)" (Ibn Ezra, Proverbs 30:22).

he: עי' הערה להשרש., פ"י, עתי' בכנ' יְכוּנֶנּוּ, עב' כָּןר"י חיוג., כַּנְתִּי, עתי' אָכוּן, — כָּן את הדבר, עשהו ותקן אותו שיהיה טוב וחזק ומתֻקן, herstellen; former; to form: הלא בבטן עשני עשהו וַיְכוּנֶנּוּ ברחם אחד איוב לא יה.

— נִפע', נָכוֹן, נְכוֹן, נָכוֹנָה, נָכוֹנוּ, נְכוֹנִים, נְכֹנִים, הִכּוֹן, תִּכּוֹן, יִכּוֹן, יִכּוֹנוּ, — א) נָכוֹן הדבר, הָחלט ואין בו יותר פקפוק, ; beschlossen; décidé; resolved: ועל השנות החלום אל פרעה פעמים כי נָכוֹן הדבר מעם האלהים וממהר האלהים לעשתו בראש' מא לב.  — ומה שאין ספק בו: ונדעה נרדפה לדעת את יי' כשחר נָכוֹן מצאו הוש' ו ג.  — ובמשמ' עשו לו או עשה לעצמו כל מה שנצרך למה שהוא נועד לו, sich vorbereiten vorber. s.; se préparer, être-ré; prepare o. s.: והיה נָכוֹן לבקר ועלית בבקר אל הר סיני שמות לד ב.  והיו נְכֹנִים ליום השלישי כי ביום השלשי ירד יי' לעיני כל העם על הר סיני שם יט יא.  היו נְכֹנִים לשלשת ימים אל תגשו אל אשה שם יה.  ויצו אתם לאמר ראו אתם ארבים לעיר מאחרי העיר וכו' והייתם כלכם נְכֹנִים ואני וכל העם אשר אתי נקרב אל העיר יהוש' ח ד-ה.  עקב כי זאת אעשה לך הִכּוֹן לקראת אלהיך ישראל עמו' ד יב.  הִכֹּן והכן לך אתה וכל קהליך הנקהלים עליך והיית להם למשמר יחזק' לח ז.  ושלחו מנות לאין נָכוֹן לו נחמ' ח י.  ידע  כי נָכוֹן בידו יום חשך איוב יה כג.  יהי רעב אנו ואיד נָכוֹן לסלעו שם יח יב.  — ובמשמ' הגיע לשלמותו, לצורתו הנאותה: ותרבי ותגדלי ותבאי בעדי עדיים שדים נָכֹנוּ ושערך צמח יחזק' טז ז.  — ובמשמ' נועד לדבר: כי אני לצלע נָכוֹן ומכאובי נגדי תמיד תהל' לח יח.  לפיד בוז לעשתות שאנן נָכוֹן למועדי רגל איוב יב ה.  — ב) נָכוֹן על דבר, נוסד, נשען ומתחזק עליו, aufgestelt; établi; established: הניחה אותי והימשני את העמדים אשר הבית נָכוֹן עליהם שופט' יו כו.  וילפת שמשון את שני עמודי התוך אשר הבית נָכוֹן עליהם ויסמך עליהם שם כט.  והיה באחרית הימים נָכוֹן יהיה הר בית יי' בראש ההרים ישע' ב ב.  — ובמשמ' היה חזק וקים, שאינו מט, כסא מלכות וכדומה, -fest s. ; étre firm; be: ונאמן ביתך וממלכתך עד עולם לפניך כסאך יהיה נָכוֹן עד עולם ש"ב ז יו.  ובית עבדך דוד יהיה נָכוֹן לפניך שם כו.  והמלך שלמה ברוך וכסא דוד יהיה נָכוֹן לפני יי' עד עולם מ"א ב מה.  תועבת מלכים עשות רשע כי בצדקה יִכּוֹן כסא משלי יו יב.  הגו רשע לפני מלך וְיִכּוֹן בצדק כסאו שם כה ה.  —  והמלכות וכדומה: כי כל הימים אשר בן ישי חי על האדמה לא תִכּוֹן אתה ומלכותך ש"א כ לא.  ושלמה ישב על כסא דוד אביו וַתִּכֹּן מלכתו מאד מ"א ב יב. — ותֵבֵל וכדומה: יי' מלך גאות לבש לבש יי' עז התאזר אף תִּכֹּון תבל בל תמוט תהל' צג א.  — ונָכוֹן היום, התחזק, כבר אור היום בשלמותו: וארח צדיקים כאור נגה הולך ואור עד נְכוֹן היום משלי ד יח.  — ובמשמ' התמיד והתקים זמן רב: והיו בניו כקדם ועדתו לפני תִּכּוֹן ירמ' ל כ. זרעו לעולם יהיה וכסאו כשמש נגדי כירח יִכּוֹן עולם ועד בשחק נאמן תהל' פט לז-לח.  נָכוֹן כסאך מאז מעולם אתה שם צג ג.  דבר שקרים לא יִכּוֹן לנגד עיני שם קא ז.  בני עבדיך ישכונו וזרעם לפניך יִכּוֹן שם קב כט.  איש לשון בל יִכּוֹן בארץ שם קמ יב.  לא יִכּוֹן אדם ברשע ושרש צדיקים בל ימוט משלי יב ג.  שפת אמת תִּכּוֹן לעד שם יט.  מלך שופט באמת דלים כסאו לעד יִכּוֹן שם כט יד.  מדוע רשעים יחיו עתקו גם גברו חיל זרעם נָכוֹן לפניהם עמם וצאצאיהם לעיניהם איוב כא ז-ח.  — ובהשאלה, דבר נָכוֹן, שנתברר כי כן הוא, כי הוא אמת, richtig; constaté; verified:  ודרשת וחקרת ושאלת היטב והנה אמת נָכוֹן הדבר נעשתה התועבה הזאת בקרבך דבר' יג יה.  — אֶל נָכוֹן, תה"פ, בודאוּת, gewiss, sicher; surement; certainly: וראו ודעו  מכל המחבאים אשר יתחבא שם ושבתם אלי אֶל נָכוֹן והלכתי אתכם ש"א כג כג.  וישלח דוד מרגלים וידע כי בא שאול אֶל נָכוֹן שם כו ד.  — נָכוֹן לעשות, נאה ויאות: ויקרא פרעה אל משה ולאהרן ויאמר לכו זבחו לאלהיכם בארץ ויאמר משה לא נָכוֹן לעשות כן כי תועבת מצרים נזבח ליי' אלהינו שמות ח כא-כב.  — נְכוֹנָה, כמו שֵׁם, במשמ' דבר נכון, נאות, כמו שראוי: כי לא דברתם אלי נְכוֹנָה כעבדי כאיוב איוב מב ז.  כי אין בפיהו נְכוֹנָה תהל' ה י.  — לבו נָכוֹן עם פלוני, נאמן לו: ויפתוהו בפיהם ובלשונם יכזבו לו ולבם לא נָכוֹן עמו ולא נאמנו בבריתו תהל' עח לו-לז.  — ויָדוֹ, נכונה ידו עם פלוני, עוזר לו ומסַיֵּע אותו: מצאתי דוד עבדי בשמן קדשי משחתיו אשר ידי תִּכּוֹן עמו אף זרועי תאמצנו לא ישיא אויב בו ובן עולה לא יעננו תהל' פט כא-כג.  — לֵב נָכוֹן, רוח נָכוֹן, שוקט, בטוח: נָכוֹן לבי אלהים נָכוֹן לבי אשירה ואזמרה תהל' נז ח.  משמועה רעה לא יירא נָכוֹן לבו בטח ביי' שם קיב ז. לב טהור ברא לי אלהים ורוח נָכוֹן חדש בקרבי שם נא יב.  —  ג) נָכוֹן הדבר, נערך ונסתדר בסדר נאה, ausegrichtet, geordnet; שאם הוזקקנו לעונתו של שטר ונמצאת עונתו מכוונת בשבת או בעשרה בתשרי ששטר מאוחר הוא וכשר ב"ב קעא..  — וכמו תה"פ במשמ' זו גם לנק': וגוש של זתים שנפל לתנור והוסק כביצה מכוון טהור יותר מכביצה טמא כלים ג ב.   טמא מת שסחט זתים וענבים כביצה מכוון טהור שם ג.  — ב) מכֻון כנגד דבר, עמד למולו: קורות הבית והעליה שאין עליהן מעזיבה והן מכוונות (עליונות נגד תחתונות) טומאה תחת אחת מהן תחתיה טמא אהל' יב ה.  בסילקי ששני פתחיה מכוונין זה כנגד זה תוספתא טהר' ז יג.  נטע שלש כנגד שלש ואחת מכוונת כנגד האמצעי ירוש' כלא' ד כט ג.  בית קדשי הקדשים שלמטן מכוון כנגד בית קדשי הקדשים שלמעלן שם ברכ' ד ח ג.  — ושעומד בשורה ישרה: כורת מכוון ונוף אין מכוון הרי זה כרם נוף מכוון וכורת אין מכוון הרי זה אינו כרם כיצד ידוע אם מכוון אם לאו מותח החוט על גבי גפנים אם היו כולן נוגעות כאחת ה"ז כרם אחת נכנסת ואחת יוצאה אינו כרם הבאי לפי עניות דעתן רמב"ם, ת"ת א יג.  — °דברים מכֻונים, כמו שצריך להיות, בדעת: ומצאנוהו חולה מוטל במטה ודעתו מיושבת עליו ולשונו ודיבורו מכוונים בפיו יודע לאמר ולשמוע לשאל ולהשיב תשו' הגא', הרכבי שע. (אשת פוטיפרע ויוסף) לדבר עבירה נתכוונו סוט' לו:.  א"ר לוי שטן ופנינה לשם שמים נתכוונו ב"ב טז..  כולם (כל אנשי דור הפלגה) לשם עכו"ם נתכוונו סנה' קט..  נתכוונו למזוג בחמין ומזגו לו בצונן ערכ' טז:.  ותגנוב  רחל את התרפים אשר לאביה והיא לא נתכוונה אלא לשם שמים מד"ר בראש' עד.  שבטו של זבולן וכו' בין מתכוונין בין שאינן מתכוונין  הם יוצאים (למלחמה) ומנצחים שם ויקר' כה.  אמר דוד לפני הקב"ה רבון העולם כלום נתכוון אבא ישי להעמידני והלא לא נתכוון אלא להנאתו שם יד.  שמה שאמר (ראובן לאחיו) לא נכנו נפש ומה שאמר להם השליכו אותו (אל הבור) לא נתכוון אלא להצילו שם במד' יג.  שלא דברה (מרים) כי אם באחיה חביבה שלא בפניו ולא נתכוונה אלא להחזירו לאשתו תנחומא מצורע ו.  — ומצוי בסהמ"א.  — לבו מִתְכַּוֵּן: אמרו לו תלמידיו (לר"ח בן דוסא שהכישו חברבר ולא הפסיק תפלתו) רבי לא הרגשת אמר להן יבא עלי ממה שהיה לבי מתכוין בתפילה אם הרגשתי ירוש' ברכ' ה ט..  — במִתְכַּוֵּן, כמו בכַוָּנָה, בלא מִתְכַּוֵּן, בלא כונה: וחומר שאר מצות משבת שבשאר מצות שגג בלא מתכוין חייב מה שאין כן בשבת שבת עב:.  אכלן דמאי יצא אכלן בלא מתכוין יצא פסח' קיד:.  כגון שנתכוון לחתוך שום דבר אחר ושחט העור בלא מתכוון רגמ"ה בכור' י:.  — נִתְכַּוֵּן, במשמ' עשה דבר בכונה לשם הדבר ההוא: היה צריך לכתוב את יהודה ונתכוין וכתב את השם מס' ספר תורה, ירוש' ה ד.  — ג) °יִתְכַּוְנוּ הדברים, יהיו נאותים, תהיה להם כונה: וכאי צד יתכוונו הדברים כך פרשה אדוננו מאיר עינינו רב יהודה גאון וכו' תשו' הגא', הרכבי שפא.  — °נִתְכַּוְנוּ דברי העדים, שהיו דברי en: [Note: See the note to the root.], transitive verb, future with suffixes יְכוּנֶנּוּ, past כָּן [Note: R. Judah Hayyuj.], כַּנְתִּי, future אָכוּן, — כָּן את הדבר, made the thing and set it right so that it would be good and strong and in order, German herstellen, French former, English to form: "Did not He who made me in the womb make him? And did not One fashion us (וַיְכוּנֶנּוּ) in the womb?" (Job 31:15).

— Nif'al, נָכוֹן, נְכוֹן, נָכוֹנָה, נָכוֹנוּ, נְכוֹנִים, נְכֹנִים, הִכּוֹן, תִּכּוֹן, יִכּוֹן, יִכּוֹנוּ, — a) נָכוֹן הדבר, was decided and there is no further doubt about it, German beschlossen, French décidé, English resolved: "And for that the dream was doubled to Pharaoh twice, it is because the thing is established (נָכוֹן) by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass" (Genesis 41:32). — And of that about which there is no doubt: "And let us know, let us eagerly strive to know the Lord; His going forth is sure (נָכוֹן) as the morning" (Hosea 6:3). — And in the sense of: they did for him, or he did for himself, all that was needed for that for which he was destined, German sich vorbereiten vorber. s., French se préparer, être-ré, English prepare o. s.: "And be ready (נָכוֹן) by the morning, and come up in the morning to Mount Sinai" (Exodus 34:2). "And be ready (נְכֹנִים) for the third day, for on the third day the Lord will come down in the sight of all the people upon Mount Sinai" (ibid. 19:11). "Be ready (נְכֹנִים) for the third day; do not come near a woman" (ibid. 15). "And he commanded them, saying, Behold, you shall lie in ambush against the city, behind the city, etc., and be all of you ready (נְכֹנִים); and I and all the people that are with me will approach the city" (Joshua 8:4-5). "Because I will do this to you, prepare (הִכּוֹן) to meet your God, O Israel" (Amos 4:12). "Be prepared (הִכֹּן), and prepare for yourself, you and all your company that are assembled to you, and be a guard to them" (Ezekiel 38:7). "And send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared (נָכוֹן)" (Nehemiah 8:10). "He knows that the day of darkness is ready (נָכוֹן) at his hand" (Job 15:23). "His strength shall be hunger-bitten, and calamity shall be ready (נָכוֹן) for his stumbling" (ibid. 18:12). — And in the sense of reached its perfection, its fitting form: "And you increased and grew up, and you came to excellent beauty; your breasts were fashioned (נָכֹנוּ), and your hair was grown" (Ezekiel 16:7). — And in the sense of destined for something: "For I am ready (נָכוֹן) to halt, and my pain is continually before me" (Psalms 38:18). "A contemptible brand in the thought of him who is at ease, ready (נָכוֹן) for them whose foot slips" (Job 12:5). — b) נָכוֹן על דבר, founded on it, leaning on it and supported by it, German aufgestelt, French établi, English established: "Let me feel the pillars upon which the house rests (נָכוֹן)" (Judges 16:26). "And Samson took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house rested (נָכוֹן), and leaned upon them" (ibid. 29). "And it shall come to pass in the end of days that the mountain of the Lord's house shall be established (נָכוֹן) at the top of the mountains" (Isaiah 2:2). — And in the sense of being strong and enduring, not tottering, of a royal throne and the like, German -fest s., French étre firm, English be: "And your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before you; your throne shall be established (נָכוֹן) forever" (2 Samuel 7:16). "And the house of your servant David shall be established (נָכוֹן) before you" (ibid. 26). "But King Solomon shall be blessed, and the throne of David shall be established (נָכוֹן) before the Lord forever" (1 Kings 2:45). "It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness, for the throne is established (יִכּוֹן) by righteousness" (Proverbs 16:12). "Take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established (וְיִכּוֹן) in righteousness" (ibid. 25:5). — And the kingdom and the like: "For as long as the son of Jesse lives upon the earth, you shall not be established (תִכּוֹן), nor your kingdom" (1 Samuel 20:31). "And Solomon sat upon the throne of David his father, and his kingdom was established (וַתִּכֹּן) greatly" (1 Kings 2:12). — And the world and the like: "The Lord reigns; He is clothed in majesty; the Lord is clothed, He has girded Himself with strength; indeed, the world is established (תִּכֹּון), it cannot be moved" (Psalms 93:1). — And נָכוֹן היום, grew strong, the daylight already in its fullness: "But the path of the righteous is as the light of dawn, that shines more and more unto the full day (נְכוֹן היום)" (Proverbs 4:18). — And in the sense of continued and endured a long time: "Their children also shall be as of old, and their congregation shall be established (תִּכּוֹן) before Me" (Jeremiah 30:20). "His seed shall endure forever, and his throne as the sun before Me; it shall be established (יִכּוֹן) forever as the moon, and as the faithful witness in the sky" (Psalms 89:37-38). "Your throne is established (נָכוֹן) of old; You are from everlasting" (ibid. 93:3). "He who speaks falsehood shall not be established (יִכּוֹן) before My eyes" (ibid. 101:7). "The children of Your servants shall dwell securely, and their seed shall be established (יִכּוֹן) before You" (ibid. 102:29). "A slanderer shall not be established (יִכּוֹן) in the earth" (ibid. 140:12). "A man shall not be established (יִכּוֹן) by wickedness, but the root of the righteous shall never be moved" (Proverbs 12:3). "The lip of truth shall be established (תִּכּוֹן) forever" (ibid. 19). "The king who faithfully judges the poor, his throne shall be established (יִכּוֹן) forever" (ibid. 29:14). "Why do the wicked live, become old, yes, grow mighty in power? Their seed is established (נָכוֹן) in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes" (Job 21:7-8). — And figuratively, דבר נָכוֹן, a thing that has been verified to be so, that it is true, German richtig, French constaté, English verified: "Then you shall inquire, and make search, and ask diligently; and behold, if it be truth, and the thing certain (נָכוֹן), that such an abomination has been done in your midst" (Deuteronomy 13:15). — אֶל נָכוֹן, adverb, with certainty, German gewiss, sicher, French surement, English certainly: "See therefore, and take knowledge of all the lurking places where he hides himself, and come back to me with certainty (אֶל נָכוֹן), and I will go with you" (1 Samuel 23:23). "And David sent out spies, and knew that Saul had come for certain (אֶל נָכוֹן)" (ibid. 26:4). — נָכוֹן לעשות, fitting and proper: "And Pharaoh called for Moses and for Aaron, and said, Go, sacrifice to your God in the land. And Moses said, It is not right (נָכוֹן) to do so, for we shall sacrifice the abomination of Egypt to the Lord our God" (Exodus 8:21-22). — נְכוֹנָה, like a noun, in the sense of a right, fitting thing, as is proper: "For you have not spoken of Me what is right (נְכוֹנָה), as My servant Job has" (Job 42:7). "For there is nothing right (נְכוֹנָה) in his mouth" (Psalms 5:10). — לבו נָכוֹן עם פלוני, faithful to him: "But they beguiled Him with their mouth, and lied to Him with their tongue; for their heart was not steadfast (נָכוֹן) with Him, neither were they faithful in His covenant" (Psalms 78:36-37). — And his hand, נכונה ידו עם פלוני, helps him and assists him: "I have found David My servant; with My holy oil have I anointed him; with whom My hand shall be established (תִּכּוֹן), My arm also shall strengthen him. The enemy shall not exact from him, nor the son of wickedness afflict him" (Psalms 89:21-23). — לֵב נָכוֹן, רוח נָכוֹן, calm, secure: "My heart is steadfast (נָכוֹן), O God, my heart is steadfast (נָכוֹן); I will sing and make melody" (Psalms 57:8). "He shall not be afraid of evil tidings; his heart is steadfast (נָכוֹן), trusting in the Lord" (ibid. 112:7). "Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast (נָכוֹן) spirit within me" (ibid. 51:12). — c) נָכוֹן הדבר, was arranged and ordered in a fitting order, German ausegrichtet, geordnet, French arrangé, English -ged: "So all the work of Solomon was prepared (וַתִּכֹּן) unto the day" (2 Chronicles 8:16). "So the service of the house of the Lord was set in order (וַתִּכּוֹן)" (ibid. 29:35). "So the service was prepared (וַתִּכּוֹן), and the priests stood in their place, and the Levites by their courses, according to the king's commandment" (ibid. 35:10). "So all the service of the Lord was prepared (וַתִּכּוֹן) the same day, to keep the passover" (ibid. 16). — And a person's way, was fitting, according to the will: "Oh that my ways were directed (יִכֹּנוּ) to observe Your statutes!" (Psalms 119:5). "Make level the path of your feet, and let all your ways be established (יִכֹּנוּ)" (Proverbs 4:26). — And in the sense of °possible and proper: "And it is not proper (יכון) to compare that which can be investigated with that which cannot be investigated" (Bakkashah of R. Bachya, Adonai Sefatai). "Then the movement will decide its matter, and it can be (ויכון) that from this he is one who desires and his soul is not lazy, 'and the soul of the diligent shall be made fat'" (Ibn Janah, Book of Roots, חרץ). — And the use is common in writing and in speech, זה נכון, in the sense of: this is what best agrees with the nature of the thing, true, correct: "And the wonder is that they said מתיהדים, and behold, יהודה has turned into a verb; and what is correct (והנכון) in my eyes is that its meaning is that they traced their lineage to Judah" (Ibn Ezra, Tzachot, Sha'ar HaShemot). "תורק: some say it is the name of a place, and what is correct (והנכון) is that it is oil, like oil that is poured out, whose scent spreads" (he, Song of Songs 1:3). "And the matter is that everything will be forgotten in the days to come as in the time that has passed; and it is more correct (נכון) for its meaning to be like הן הוא" (Ecclesiastes 2:16). "And it may be that the dagesh in these is for the beauty of the reading and not for the missing nun, and that is correct (הנכון)" (Radak, Mikhlol, שדה"פ 5). "And we have already written that their root is יבש, and the tzere under the added letters points to them, and that is correct (הנכון)" (ibid. 101b). — And words on the lips, ordered and fluent: "Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise, and apply your heart to my knowledge. For it is a pleasant thing if you keep them within you, if they be established (יִכֹּנוּ) together upon your lips" (Proverbs 22:17-18). — And thoughts: "Commit your works to the Lord, and your thoughts shall be established (וְיִכֹּנוּ)" (ibid. 16:3).

— Po'el, כּוֹנֵן, כּוֹנְנָה, כּוֹנַנְתָּ, כּוֹנַנְתָּה, כּוֹנַנְתִּי, כּוֹנְנוּ, כּוֹנֵן, כּוֹנְנָה, תְּכוֹנֵן, יְכוֹנֵן, כּוֹנַנְתָּהּ, תְּכוֹנְנֵהוּ, יְכוֹנְנֶךָּ, יְכוֹנְנֶהָ, יְכוֹנֲנוּנִי, כּוֹנַנְנוּ [Note: This and the rest: Radak.] or כּוֹנַנּוּ with dagesh, מְכוֹנֵן, מְכוֹנְנִים, מְכוֹנְנָה, מְכוֹנֶנֶת, מְכוֹנְנוֹת, אֲכוֹנֵן etc., תְּכוֹנֲנְנָה, or תְּכוֹנֶנָּה, — a) set it up and founded and strengthened it, German aufstellen, gründen, French établir, fonder, English establish, ground: "The place, O Lord, which You have made for You to dwell in, the sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have established (כּוֹנְנוּ)" (Exodus 15:17). "He shall build a house for My name, and I will establish (וְכֹנַנְתִּי) the throne of his kingdom forever" (2 Samuel 7:13). "Woe to him who builds a town with blood, and establishes (וְכוֹנֵן) a city by iniquity" (Habakkuk 2:12). "And give Him no rest, till He establish (יְכוֹנֵן), and till He make Jerusalem a praise in the earth" (Isaiah 62:7). "He turns a wilderness into a pool of water, and a dry land into watersprings; and there He makes the hungry to dwell, and they establish (וַיְכוֹנְנוּ) a city of habitation, and sow fields, and plant vineyards, which yield fruits of increase" (Psalms 107:35-37). "As we have heard, so have we seen in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God; God establish (יְכוֹנְנֶהָ) it forever" (ibid. 48:9). "But of Zion it shall be said, This man and that was born in her; and the Most High Himself shall establish (יְכוֹנְנֶהָ) her" (ibid. 87:5). — And the earth: "He is God, who formed the earth and made it, He established (כוֹנְנָהּ) it, He created it not a waste" (Isaiah 45:18). "The earth is the Lord's, and the fullness thereof, the world and they who dwell therein; for He has founded it upon the seas, and established (יְכוֹנְנֶהָ) it upon the floods" (Psalms 24:1-2). "A bounteous rain did You pour down, O God; when Your inheritance was weary, You did establish (כוֹנַנְתָּהּ) it" (ibid. 68:10). "You have established (כּוֹנַנְתָּ) the earth, and it stands" (ibid. 119:90). — And the heavens and their host: "The Lord by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding He established (כּוֹנֵן) the heavens" (Proverbs 3:19). "When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars, which You have established (כּוֹנַנְתָּה)" (Psalms 8:4). — And in the Midrash: "At first the Omnipresent sought to establish (לכונן) the world and did not find a way, until the Patriarchs arose" (Exodus Rabbah 15). "At first the world was water within water, and God sought to establish (לכונן) worlds, and the wicked would not let Him, etc.; once the Patriarchs came and were found worthy, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: On these I establish (מכונן) the world" (ibid.). — And the liturgical poet said: "You established (כוננת) the world from the beginning, You founded the earth, and You made all" (Yose ben Yose, Avodah). "And by Your word You established (כוננת) the circle of the heavens to be ever revolving" (R. Bachya, Bakkashah, Adonai Sefatai). "You established (כוננת) canopies for them in Eden, every precious stone was their covering to canopy" (Meshullam ben Kalonymus, Avodah, J. Elbogen, GJG 126). "City of the kingdom for David and Solomon his son, you were built, and they of old were your establishers (מכונניך)" (Kinot for Tisha B'Av, Tziyon Ateret). — And a people and a man and the like: "And You established (וַתְּכוֹנֵן) for Yourself Your people Israel to be a people to You forever" (2 Samuel 7:24). "Do you thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise? Is not He your father who acquired you? He made you and established (וַיְכֹנְנֶךָ) you" (Deuteronomy 32:6). "Oh let the evil of the wicked come to an end, but establish (וּתְכוֹנֵן) the righteous" (Psalms 7:10). "Your hands have made me and fashioned (וַיְכוֹנְנוּנִי) [Note: In some books the first nun has a chataf.] me" (ibid. 119:73). — And the feet and the like: "And He set my feet upon a rock; He established (כּוֹנֵן) my steps" (Psalms 40:3). — And abstract things: "You have established (כּוֹנַנְתָּ) equity; You have executed justice and righteousness in Jacob" (Psalms 99:4). — כּוֹנֵן דָּבָר לדָבָר, for the sake of that thing: "But the Lord is enthroned forever; He has established (כּוֹנֵן) His throne for judgment" (Psalms 9:8). — b) כּוֹנֵן חֵץ and the like, caused it to go to the desired place, German richten, French diriger, English direct: "For behold, the wicked bend the bow, they have aimed (כּוֹנְנוּ) their arrow upon the string" (Psalms 11:2). — And the bow: "He will whet his sword; he has bent his bow and made it ready (וַיְכוֹנְנֶהָ)" (ibid. 7:13). "You shall aim (תְּכוֹנֵן) with Your bowstrings against their faces" (ibid. 21:13). — כּוֹנֵן מחשבותיו או מעשיו לדָבָר, made his thoughts or his deeds turn toward what he wished to attain: "And you fear continually all the day because of the fury of the oppressor, when he aims (כּוֹנֵן) to destroy" (Isaiah 51:13). "For inquire, I pray you, of the former generation, and apply yourself (וְכוֹנֵן) [Note: Some emend to בונן, with a bet.] to that which their fathers have searched out" (Job 8:8). — c) כּוֹנֵן מעשה, caused the work to go properly and to succeed well: "And let the graciousness of the Lord our God be upon us; establish (כּוֹנְנָה) the work of our hands upon us; yes, the work of our hands, establish (כּוֹנְנֵהוּ) it" (Psalms 90:17).

— Polel, כּוֹנֵן, כּוֹנָנוּ, — that they established it: "The workmanship of your settings and of your sockets was in you; in the day that you were created they were prepared (כּוֹנָנוּ)" (Ezekiel 28:13). — And the steps, to go in the desired way: "It is of the Lord that a man's goings are established (כּוֹנָנוּ), and He delights in his way" (Psalms 37:23).

— Hif'il, הֵכִין, הֲכִינוֹתָ, הֲכִינֹתָה, הֲכִינוֹתִי, הֵכִינוּ, הֱכִינוֹנוּ, הֵכַנּוּ, מֵכִין, הָכִין, הָכֵן, הָכִינוּ, אָכִין, אָכִינָה, תָּכִין, תָּכִן, יָכִין, וַיָּכֶן, יָכִינוּ, הֲכִינַנִי, הֲכִינוֹ, הֲכִינָהּ, תְּכִינֶהָ, — a) הֵכִין דבר, did to it all that was needed so that it could already be used for the desired purpose, so that there would be no need to wait any longer, and that nothing would be lacking in it, German bereiten, vorberetein, French préparer, English make ready, — a meal and the like: "Bring the men into the house, and kill the beasts, and make ready (וְהָכֵן); for the men shall dine with me at noon" (Genesis 43:16). "Hold your peace at the presence of the Lord God, for the day of the Lord is at hand; for the Lord has prepared (הֵכִין) a sacrifice, He has consecrated His guests" (Zephaniah 1:7). — And provisions: "And command the people, saying, Prepare (הָכִינוּ) for yourselves provisions [Note: The original printed 'צדה'.], for within three days you are to pass over this Jordan" (Joshua 1:11). "Who provides (יָכִין) for the raven his prey?" (Job 38:41). "Behold, He smote the rock, that waters gushed out, and streams overflowed; can He give bread also? Or will He provide (יָכִין) flesh for His people?" (Psalms 78:20). "Go to the ant, you sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise; which, having no chief, overseer or ruler, provides (תָּכִין) her bread in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest" (Proverbs 6:6-8). "The ants are a people not strong, yet they provide (וַיָּכִינוּ) their food in the summer" (ibid. 30:25). — And a gift: "And they made ready (וַיָּכִינוּ) the present against Joseph's coming at noon" (Genesis 43:25). — And food, clothing and the like: "And there they were with David three days, eating and drinking, for their brethren had prepared (הֵכִינוּ) for them" (1 Chronicles 12:39). "Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare (יָכִין) raiment as the clay" (Job 27:16). "You have remembered the earth, and watered her, etc.; You prepare (תָּכִין) them grain, for so You prepare (תְּכִינֶהָ) her" (Psalms 65:10). "Your flock settled therein; You prepare (תָּכִין) in Your goodness for the poor, O God" (ibid. 68:11). "Then Hezekiah commanded to prepare (לְהָכִין) chambers in the house of the Lord, and they prepared (וַיָּכִינוּ) them, and brought in the offering and the tithes and the dedicated things faithfully" (2 Chronicles 31:11-12). — And an altar, offerings and the like: "And Balaam said to Balak, Build me here seven altars, and prepare (וְהָכֵן) me here seven bullocks and seven rams" (Numbers 23:1). — And the showbread: "And some of their brethren, of the sons of the Kohathites, were over the showbread, to prepare (לְהָכִין) it every Sabbath" (1 Chronicles 9:32). — And what was needed for building: "And Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders and the Gebalites did fashion them, and prepared (וַיָּכִינוּ) the timber and the stones to build the house" (1 Kings 5:32). "And David prepared (הֵכִין) iron in abundance for the nails for the doors of the gates, and for the couplings" (1 Chronicles 22:3). "And David said, Solomon my son is young and tender, and the house that is to be built for the Lord must be exceedingly magnificent, etc.; I will therefore make preparation (אָכִינָה) for it. So David prepared (וַיָּכֶן) abundantly before his death" (ibid. 5). "Now behold, in my affliction I have prepared (הֲכִינוֹתִי) for the house of the Lord a hundred thousand talents of gold, etc.; timber also and stone have I prepared (הֲכִינוֹתִי), and you may add thereto" (ibid. 14). "Send me also cedar trees, etc., even to prepare (וּלְהָכִין) me timber in abundance, for the house which I am about to build shall be great and wonderful" (2 Chronicles 2:7-8). "O Lord our God, all this store that we have prepared (הֱכִינוֹנוּ) [Note: In some books the he has a chataf segol.] to build You a house for Your holy name comes from Your hand, and is all Your own" (1 Chronicles 29:16). "Moreover all the vessels which King Ahaz in his reign cast away when he acted treacherously have we prepared (הֵכַנּוּ) and sanctified, and behold, they are before the altar of the Lord" (2 Chronicles 29:19). — And weapons and the like: "And Uzziah prepared (וַיָּכֶן) for them, even for all the host, shields and spears and helmets and coats of mail and bows and stones for slinging" (2 Chronicles 26:14). "They have blown the horn, and have made all ready (וְהָכִין), but none goes to the battle" (Ezekiel 7:14). "He will whet his sword; he has bent his bow and made it ready; he has also prepared (הֵכִין) for him the weapons of death" (Psalms 7:13-14). "The chariots are fire of steel in the day of his preparation (הֲכִינוֹ), and the cypress spears are made to quiver" (Nahum 2:4). "Now Haman had come into the outer court of the king's house, to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared (הֵכִין) for him" (Esther 6:4). "So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared (הֵכִין) for Mordecai" (ibid. 7:10). — And slaughter and the like: "Prepare (הָכִינוּ) slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers" (Isaiah 14:21). — A net: "They have prepared (הֵכִינוּ) a net for my steps" (Psalms 57:7). — Rain: "Who covers the heaven with clouds, who prepares (הַמֵּכִין) rain for the earth" (Psalms 147:8). — And an abstract thing: "They conceive mischief and bring forth iniquity, and their belly prepares (תָּכִין) deceit" (Job 15:35). — The service: "And kill the passover lamb, and sanctify yourselves, and prepare (וְהָכִינוּ) for your brethren, to do" (2 Chronicles 35:6). "And afterward they prepared (הֵכִינוּ) (the offerings) for themselves and for the priests, etc., and the Levites prepared (הֵכִינוּ) for themselves and for the priests the sons of Aaron" (ibid. 14). "They need not depart from their service, for their brethren the Levites prepared (הֵכִינוּ) for them" (ibid. 15). — And in the sense of completed all that was needed: "After all this, when Josiah had prepared (הֵכִין) the house, Necho king of Egypt went up to fight at Carchemish" (2 Chronicles 35:20). — And in the sense of made the necessary preparations: "I had it in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and for the footstool of our God, and I had made ready (וַהֲכִינוֹתִי) to build; but God said to me, You shall not build" (1 Chronicles 28:2-3). — הֵכִין לו, prepared himself, for war and the like: "Declare in Egypt, and announce in Migdol, etc.; say, Stand forth, and prepare (וְהָכֵן) yourself, for the sword has devoured round about you" (Jeremiah 46:14). "Be prepared, and prepare (וְהָכֵן) for yourself, you and all your company that are assembled to you, and be a guard to them" (Ezekiel 38:7). — And this past verb occurs with the definite article, הַהֵכִין: "And Hezekiah rejoiced, and all the people, because of that which God had prepared (הַהֵכִין) for the people, for the thing was done suddenly" (2 Chronicles 29:36). — And in the Talmud and Midrash: "Whether she prepared it (the rag) to patch it or did not prepare it to patch it" (Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2, 4d). "A weekday prepares (מכין) for the Sabbath, and a weekday prepares for a festival, but a festival does not prepare for the Sabbath, and the Sabbath does not prepare for a festival" (Beitzah 2b). "Did they prepare (הכינו) a table before You?" (Megillah 12b). "Who prepares (מכין) the altar before You?" (Esther Rabbah, on והקרוב אליו). "He prepared (הכין) all that was needed for the meal, and baked his bread and slaughtered his meat, before they entered upon the celebration" (Rambam, Avel 11:8). — b) הֵכִין אנשים, appointed them for some matter, German bestellen, bestimmen, French désigner, English appoint: "Then Joshua called the twelve men whom he had appointed (הֵכִין) of the children of Israel" (Joshua 4:4). "Set up a standard against the walls of Babylon, make the watch strong, set the watchmen, prepare (הָכִינוּ) the ambushes; for the Lord has both purposed and done" (Jeremiah 51:12). "The skilled men who are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father provided (הֵכִין)" (2 Chronicles 2:6). — הֱכִינוֹ למלך, designated and decided upon him: "And David perceived that the Lord had established (הֱכִינוֹ) him king over Israel" (2 Samuel 5:12). — And a place: "Behold, I send an angel before you, to keep you by the way, and to bring you into the place which I have prepared (הֲכִנֹתִי)" (Exodus 23:20). "And David assembled all Israel to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the Lord to its place, which he had prepared (הֵכִין) for it" (1 Chronicles 15:3). "And he prepared (וַיָּכֶן) a place for the ark of God" (ibid. 1). "But the ark of God had David brought up from Kiriath-jearim to the place that David had prepared (בַּהֵכִין) for it" (2 Chronicles 1:4), in place of במקום אשר הכין לו. — And in the sense of arranged: "You shall separate three cities for yourself in the midst of your land, etc.; you shall prepare (תָּכִין) for yourself the way, etc., that every manslayer may flee there" (Deuteronomy 19:2-3). "Prepare (הָכֵן) your work outside, and make it ready for yourself in the field, and afterward build your house" (Proverbs 24:27). — c) הֵכִין ממלכה, כסא מלכות and the like, like כּוֹנֵן, made it strong and enduring and lasting: "For now would the Lord have established (הֵכִין) your kingdom upon Israel forever" (1 Samuel 13:13). "I will set up your seed after you, who shall proceed out of your body, and I will establish (וַהֲכִינֹתִי) his kingdom" (2 Samuel 7:12). "Upon the throne of David and upon his kingdom, to establish (לְהָכִין) it and to uphold it through justice and through righteousness from henceforth even forever" (Isaiah 9:6). "And it came to pass, when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established (כְּהָכִין), and he was strong, that he forsook the law of the Lord" (2 Chronicles 12:1). "Therefore the Lord established (וַיָּכֶן) the kingdom in his hand" (ibid. 17:5). "And I will establish (וַהֲכִינוֹתִי) the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever" (1 Chronicles 22:10). "The Lord has established (הֵכִין) His throne in the heavens" (Psalms 103:19). — And the king on his throne: "Now therefore, as the Lord lives, who has established (הֱכִינַנִי) me and set me on the throne of David my father, etc., Adonijah shall be put to death this day" (1 Kings 2:24). — And his seed: "I have made a covenant with My chosen, I have sworn to David My servant: Your seed will I establish (אָכִין) forever, and build up your throne to all generations" (Psalms 89:4-5). — And an altar: "And they set (וַיָּכִינוּ) the altar upon its base" (Ezra 3:3). — And one's seat in a place, set, fixed: "When I went forth to the gate unto the city, when I prepared (אָכִין) my seat in the broad place, the young men saw me and hid themselves" (Job 29:7-8). — And his heart, made it strong and steadfast in one thing: "And might not be as their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation that did not set (הֵכִין) their heart aright, and whose spirit was not steadfast with God" (Psalms 78:8). — And an abstract thing: "For I have said, Forever is mercy built; in the very heavens You establish (תָּכִן) Your faithfulness" (ibid. 89:3). — הָכִין, הָכֵן, like an adverb: "Take up for yourselves from here, out of the midst of the Jordan, from the place where the priests' feet stood firm (הָכִין), twelve stones" (Joshua 4:3). "And the priests who bore the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood firm (הָכֵן) on dry ground in the midst of the Jordan, while all Israel passed over on dry ground" (ibid. 3:17). — d) הֵכִין, made, arranged and set in order: "And he prepared (הֵכִין) a sanctuary in the midst of the house within, to set there the ark of the covenant of the Lord" (1 Kings 6:19). "He chooses a tree that will not rot; he seeks for himself a skillful craftsman to prepare (לְהָכִין) a graven image that shall not be moved" (Isaiah 40:20). — And in poetic language, הֵכִין תבל and the like, created, established: "He has made the earth by His power, He has established (מֵכִין) the world by His wisdom, and by His understanding has He stretched out the heavens" (Jeremiah 10:12). "Thus says the Lord who does it, the Lord who forms it to establish (לַהֲכִינָהּ) it, the Lord is His name" (ibid. 33:2). "Who by His strength sets fast (מֵכִין) the mountains, who is girded about with might" (Psalms 65:7). "While as yet He had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world. When He established (בַּהֲכִינוֹ) the heavens, I was there; when He set a circle upon the face of the deep" (Proverbs 8:26-27). "Yours is the day, Yours also the night; You have established (הֲכִינוֹתָ) the luminary and the sun" (Psalms 74:16). — e) הֵכִין את לבו לפלוני, turned it, inclined it toward someone, German richten, French diriger, English direct: "Put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you, and direct (וְהָכִינוּ) your hearts to the Lord, and serve Him only" (1 Samuel 7:3). "For Ezra had set (הֵכִין) his heart to seek the law of the Lord" (Ezra 7:10). "And he (Rehoboam) did evil, because he did not set (הֵכִין) his heart to seek the Lord" (2 Chronicles 12:14). "Who sets (הֵכִין) his whole heart to seek God" (ibid. 30:19). "Keep this forever in the imagination of the thoughts of the heart of Your people, and direct (וְהָכֵן) their heart to You" (1 Chronicles 29:18). "For you have put away the Asheroth out of the land, and have set (וַהֲכִינוֹתָ) your heart to seek God" (2 Chronicles 19:3). "However, the high places were not taken away, neither as yet had the people directed (הֵכִינוּ) their hearts to the God of their fathers" (ibid. 20:33). "If you set (הֲכִינוֹתָ) your heart aright, and stretch out your hands toward Him" (Job 11:13). — And the poet said: "And You will make my tongue clear and direct (תכין) my heart, and awaken my soul and make my meditation straight" (Bakkashah of R. Bachya, Adonai Sefatai Tiftach). — And his steps, his paces: "O Lord, I know that a man's way is not his own; it is not in man as he walks to direct (וְהָכִין) his steps" (Jeremiah 10:23). "A man's heart devises his way, but the Lord directs (יָכִין) his steps" (Proverbs 16:9). "Order (הָכֵן) my steps by Your word, and let not any iniquity have dominion over me" (Psalms 119:133). — And his ways: "So Jotham became mighty, because he ordered (הֵכִין) his ways before the Lord his God" (2 Chronicles 27:6). — And his face: "And you, take for yourself an iron griddle, and set it for a wall of iron between you and the city, and set (וַהֲכִינֹתָה) your face toward it" (Ezekiel 4:3). "And you shall set (תָּכִין) your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, with your arm uncovered" (ibid. 7). — f) הֵכִין דבר, considered whether it was right, examined it, German betrachten, French considérer, English -der: "And they shall gather it (the manna), a day's portion every day, etc.; and it shall come to pass on the sixth day that they shall prepare (וְהֵכִינוּ) that which they bring in, and it shall be twice as much as they gather daily" (Exodus 16:4-5). "Then the Ziphites came up to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Does not David hide himself with us in the strongholds in the wood, etc.? Now therefore, O king, come down, according to all the desire of your soul to come down; and our part shall be to deliver him into the king's hand. And Saul said, Blessed be you of the Lord, for you have had compassion on me. Go, I pray you, make yet more sure (הָכִינוּ), and know and see his place where his haunt is, and who has seen him there" (1 Samuel 23:19-22). "Lord, You have heard the desire of the humble; You will direct (תָּכִין) their heart, You will cause Your ear to attend" (Psalms 10:17). "Then did He see it (wisdom) and declare it; He established (הֱכִינָהּ) it, yes, and searched it out" (Job 28:27). "A wicked man hardens his face, but as for the upright, he considers (יָכִין) [Note: So the ketiv, and the qere is יבין. And it is recorded by the Masorah that it is one of three words written with kaf and read with bet (Okhlah ve-Okhlah, § 158). And in some books the qere is also יכין, and in some also the ketiv is יבין; and this too testifies that according to the context the sense of consideration is fitting here.] his ways" (Proverbs 21:29). — g) intransitive verb, הֵכִין, was ready and prepared, able, German fähig s., French être capable, English be able: "Then they (the men of Gilead) said to him (the Ephraimite), Say now Shibboleth; and he said Sibboleth, for he could not (ולא יָכִין) frame to pronounce it right" (Judges 12:6).

— Huf'al, הוּכַן, הֻכַן, מוּכָן, מוּכָנִים, — that they prepared it, a) that they made it ready: "For a hearth is ordered of old; yes, for the king it is prepared (הוּכַן), deep and large" (Isaiah 30:33). "The horse is prepared (מוּכָן) for the day of battle, but victory is of the Lord" (Proverbs 21:31). — And in the Talmud and Midrash: "If it was not a carcass from the eve of the Sabbath, it is forbidden, because it is not of what was prepared (המוכן)" (Shabbat 24:4). "Any whose blemish was not recognizable while it was still day, this is not of what was prepared (המוכן)" (Beitzah 3:4). "Less than three by three that he set aside for wiping the bathhouse with, etc., for wiping the millstones with, whether prepared (מוכן) or not prepared" (Kelim 28:2). "If it (the hen) was prepared (מוכנה) for slaughter, it is permitted, etc.; and not all hens are prepared (מוכנין) for slaughter; therefore it is needed even if it is not prepared (מוכנת)" (Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah 1, 60d). "Ben Azzai said: By your name they will call you, and in your place they will seat you, and of your own they will give you; no man touches what is prepared (במוכן) for his fellow" (Yoma 38b). "Prepared (מוכן) for a person, prepared (מוכן) for the dogs" (Chullin 14a). "And at the ninth hour of the day Israel returned to their tents, and the manna was prepared (מוכן) for them for two days" (Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer 46). — b) that they made and strengthened it and fixed it: "The spoiler ceases, the extortioner is at an end, they that trampled are consumed out of the land; and a throne is established (וְהוּכַן) in mercy, and there sits thereon in truth, in the tent of David, one who judges, and seeks justice, and is swift in righteousness" (Isaiah 16:4-5). "They make haste to its wall, and the mantelet is prepared (וְהֻכַן)" (Nahum 2:6). "To build her a house in the land of Shinar; and when it is prepared (וְהוּכַן), she shall be set there in her own place" (Zechariah 5:11). "And the hooks, etc., were fastened (מוּכָנִים) within, round about" (Ezekiel 40:43).

— Hitpa'el, with the tav assimilated, הִכּוֹנֵן [Note: Because of the closeness in sound between כ and ת; see the entry כ.], and with the tav, הִתְכּוֹנֵן, — became strong and enduring: "Let the city of Sihon be built and established (וְתִכּוֹנֵן)" (Numbers 21:27). "In righteousness shall you be established (תִּכּוֹנָנִי)" (Isaiah 54:14). "Through wisdom is a house built, and by understanding it is established (יִתְכּוֹנָן)" (Proverbs 24:3). — הִכּוֹנְנוּ אנשים, gathered and were joined together with one intent: "Without my fault they run and prepare themselves (וְיִכּוֹנָנוּ); awake to meet me, and behold" (Psalms 59:5).

— Pi'el, *כִּוֵּן [Note: In Jewish Aramaic כִּוֵּן is like פָּנָה: "And the men turned from there" (Genesis 18:22), Targum Jonathan: וכוינו מתמן גבריא. "Turn you" (Deuteronomy 1:7): כוינו לכון (Arukh, entry כוון II). "You shall prepare for yourself the way" (Deuteronomy 19:3), Targum Jonathan: תכוונון לכון ארחא.], יְכַוֵּן, — a) transitive verb, כִּוֵּן שני דברים זה נגד זה, so that they stand exactly opposite one another, German gerade machen, French faire droit, English straighthen: "A vineyard that is planted in disorder, if it is possible to line up (לכוין) two opposite three, this is a vineyard" (Kilayim 5:1). "One may align (מכוונין) the saplings until Rosh Hashanah" (Tosefta Shevi'it 1:6). "And they align (ומכוונין) [Note: So in the manuscript (Dikdukei Soferim); in the printed editions מכוונות.] roads for them (for the cities of refuge) from one to another" (Makkot 2:5). "'You shall prepare for yourself the way,' so that they will not go astray" (Numbers Rabbah 22). — And the liturgical poet said: "He engraved them (the Ten Commandments) one opposite the other for exposition; He aligned them (כוונם) and sealed them, five opposite five" (Yotzer for the second day of Sukkot, Shevuyat Marom). — כִּוֵּן מַקֵּל and the like, so that it would not be crooked: "Like one who had a crooked staff in his hand and gave it to a craftsman to repair; he repairs it with fire, and if not, he straightens it (מכוונו) with a roller, and if not, he twists it with an adze" (Sifre Deuteronomy 308). — And a hem in a shirt, so that it would not be crooked: "Anyone who cannot sew a straight (לכוין) hem in the opening of his shirt" (Moed Katan 10a). — And an ox and the like, caused it to go in the needed way: "This goad directs (מכוון) the cow to its furrows, to bring life to the world" (Sifre Deuteronomy 41). — *כִּוֵּן את לבו לדָבָר, turned himself so as to face one of the points: "Those standing outside the Land direct (מכוונין) their hearts toward the Land of Israel and pray, etc.; those standing in the Land of Israel direct (מכוונין) their hearts toward Jerusalem and pray, etc.; those standing in Jerusalem direct (מכוונין) their hearts toward the Temple and pray" (Tosefta Berakhot 3:15-16). "All Israel direct (מכוונין) their hearts to one place" (Gemara ibid. 30a). "Thus our Rabbis taught: A person should direct (יכוין) his heart (when he prays) toward the House of the Holy of Holies" (Pesikta Rabbati 33). — And figuratively, turned his thought to a thing: "The early pious ones would wait one hour and then pray, so that they might direct (שיכוונו) their hearts to their Father in heaven" (Berakhot 5:1). "One who does much and one who does little are alike, provided that he directs (שיכוין) his heart to Heaven" (Gemara ibid. 5b). — כִּוֵּן את פלוני כנגד דבר, set him exactly facing the thing: "They set him (כיוונו) (the man who was afterward killed) facing the horse, they set him facing the arrow, they set him facing the spear, they stood him in the cold, he gave him bad water to drink" (Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 9, 27a). — °כִּוֵּן את עצמו לפלוני, acted so that someone would see him: "It is not fitting for a sage to trouble the people and to put himself in their way (ויכוין עצמו להן) so that they will rise before him" (Rambam, Talmud Torah 6:3). — *כִּוֵּן לבו על דבר, thought about it: "One who separates terumah from the threshing floor must direct (שיכוין) his heart to what is in the corners and to what is at the sides" (Tosefta Terumot 3:6). — And simply כִּוֵּן לבו, set his mind and thought about what he was doing: "If he was reading in the Torah and the time for the recitation arrived, if he directed (כיון) his heart, he has fulfilled his obligation" (Berakhot 2:1). "If he was writing it (the Megillah), expounding it or correcting it, if he directed (כיון) his heart, he has fulfilled his obligation" (Megillah 2:2). "One who recites the Shema must direct (שיכוין) his heart. R. Achai says in the name of R. Yehudah: If he directed (כיון) his heart in the first section, even though he did not direct (כיון) his heart in the last section, he has fulfilled his obligation" (Tosefta Berakhot 2:2). "If he blessed, he must direct (שיכוין) his heart in all of them" (Jerusalem Talmud ibid. 2, 4a). "If he prayed and did not direct (כוין) his heart, if he knows that he will go back and direct (ומכוין) his heart, let him pray, and if not, let him not pray" (ibid. 2, 5a). "If you have directed (כוונתה) your heart in prayer, be assured that your prayer has been heard" (ibid. 5, 9d). "And this one directs (מכוון) his heart and that one directs (מכוון) his heart, and they repent" (Exodus Rabbah 1). — כִּוֵּן לבו לדָבָר, prepared himself for the thing: "Anyone who goes out on the road and does not set (מכוין) his heart for war will in the end fall in war" (Leviticus Rabbah 25). — And כִוֵּן דבר, in the sense of thought and decided in his mind about the thing: "And a lock and a key that broke may be repaired on the intermediate days of the festival, provided that he does not deliberately schedule (יכוין) [Note: So in the Mishnah of the Mishnah editions, and so in the Jerusalem Talmud, Rif and Rosh, and so in the manuscript (Dikdukei Soferim); and in the Mishnah in the Babylonian Talmud: שלא יתכוין לעשות מלאכתו. And Rashi explained: When he could repair all these on the other days of the year and leaves it until the festival. End quote. And so Rambam: That he should not be lazy in his work before the festival and intend to do it on the festival.] his work for the festival" (Moed Katan 1:10). "A person may bring in his produce because of thieves, and draw his flax out of the steeping pool so that it will not be lost, provided that he does not deliberately schedule (יכוין) his work for the festival; and all of them, if they deliberately scheduled (כיונו) their work for the festival, it shall be destroyed" (ibid. 2:3). — כִּוֵּן שמועתו, took care that it be exactly as it was said: "One who makes his teacher wise, and one who gets his tradition exact (והמכוין), and one who says a thing in the name of the one who said it" (Avot 6:6). "It seems to me that we have not had our tradition exact (כיווננו) until now" (Menachot 18a). "Whoever humbles himself gets his tradition exact (מכוין)" (Derekh Eretz Zuta 8). "For he did not render (מכוין) the words exactly in their truth" (Numbers Rabbah 20). — °כִּוְנוּ שנים דבריהם, the two of them spoke alike: "If the witnesses were many, and two of them agreed (כיוונו) in their testimony in the examinations and inquiries, and the third said, 'I do not know,' the testimony stands with two" (Rambam, Edut 2:3). "Behold, if they testified about him that he killed and they were examined with the seven examinations, etc., and they agreed (וכוונו) about the deed and agreed (וכוונו) about the weapon with which he killed him" (ibid. 1:6). "That they should agree (מכוונים) between them on one number, ten or twenty, etc., and they would not tell him the number they had agreed (שכיוונו) between them" (Tosafot Yeshanim, Yoma 22a). — And in the sense of °stated exactly as it is: "This one gave the measure of its length and breadth, and that one stated exactly (כיון) its weights; it is given to the one who stated its weight exactly (שכיון)" (Rambam, Gezelah va-Avedah 13:7). "One who states exactly (המכוין) the weight of the thing, or its measure, or its knots, or its number, etc., it is a sign" (Tur Choshen Mishpat, Avedah 262:15). — *כִּוֵּן את הרוחות, knew on which side the directions of the world are, east, west, etc.: "A blind person and one who cannot determine (לכוין) the directions direct (מכונין) their hearts before the Omnipresent and pray" (Tosefta Berakhot 3:16). "R. Yose said: If one does not know how to determine (לכוין) the directions, go out and learn from the solstice: from the place where the sun rises, etc., this is the east side, etc.; from the place where the sun sets, etc., this is the west side, and the rest are north and south, etc. And in the wilderness, who determined (מכוין) the directions for them? R. Acha said: The ark determined (מכוין) the directions for them" (Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 5, 22c). "And one who cannot determine (לכוין) the directions should direct (יכוין) his heart toward his Father in heaven" (Berakhot 30a). — כִּוֵּן רוחותיה של הנטיעה, where its roots would spread and the like: "Before it (the sapling) has been formed from its mother's womb, a person must determine (לכוין) its directions" (Genesis Rabbah 15). — כִּוֵּן את השעה, knew exactly when it is: "'And God is angry every day.' And how long is His anger? A moment, etc. And no creature can pinpoint (לכוין) that moment except Balaam the wicked, etc., who knew how to pinpoint (לכוין) that moment when the Holy One, blessed be He, is angry" (Berakhot 7a). — b) like an intransitive verb, כִּוֵּן absolutely, his mind and thought were directed to a thing, German beabsichtigen, French avoir L`intention, English intend: "Like a king of flesh and blood who had two sons, one older and one younger. He went into his chamber at night and said to the younger, 'Wake me at sunrise,' and he said to the older, 'Wake me at the third hour.' The younger came to wake him at sunrise, and the older would not let him, etc. While they stood shouting, their father woke and said to them, 'My sons, both of you intended (כוונתם) only my honor; I too will not withhold your reward'" (Mekhilta Beshallach 2:5). "An old woman who skipped three periods, her time suffices; if she again skipped three periods and afterward saw blood, her time suffices, when she did not coincide (כיוונה) because of the cycle, in her decreasing or in her increasing; for if she had coincided (כיוונה), her cycle would have been fixed" (Jerusalem Talmud Niddah 1, 49c). — And in this sense it is common in medieval literature: "And the makers of the first calf, and the company of Jeroboam, and the worshipers at the high places, and the image of Micah, did not direct (מכוונים) their hearts except to the God of Israel" (Kuzari 4:14). "And he gave them praise for what they argued from the abstraction of their syllogisms, and they intended (וכוונו) the good" (ibid. 5:14). "The Creator, may He be exalted, whom we have sought and whom we have aimed (כווננו) [Note: And possibly also כִּוַּנּוּ.] to find in our thoughts and our intellect" (Chovot HaLevavot, Sha'ar HaYichud 6). "Provided that he does not intend (יכוין) to delay it until the festival" (Tur Orach Chayim 538). "And he should take care (ויכוין) that the knot comes in that same place" (ibid., Even HaEzer 169). — And the liturgical poet said: "How have You aimed (כוונת) in Your anger to destroy Your vineyard by the hand of those who stumble" (Kinot for Tisha B'Av, Eikhah Atzta). "How will you purify your heart from your transgressions, or find in this freedom for your soul? Direct yourself (כַּוֵּין) with all your strength to bless your Rock; then your fragrance will rise like the fragrance of pure myrrh" (Moses ibn Habib, Darkhei Noam 17). — °וכִוֵּן מחשבות, plotted, devised counsels: "We laid plans what to do, there is no counselor among us; we devised (כִּוַּנּוּ) thoughts in the heart, to bring knowledge from afar" (Selichot for the Monday fast, Afafunu Mayim). — And כִוֵּן in the sense of had in mind a thing: "If he recited (the Shema) and found himself at למען, it is presumed that he had intention (כוין), etc.; if he prayed and found himself at 'Who hears prayer,' it is presumed that he had intention (כוין)" (Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2, 5a). "R. Zeira said to his disciple: Intend (כוין) and sound the shofar for me; he thought that we require the intention of the one who sounds it" (Halakhot Pesukot, Rosh Hashanah). — And כִוֵּן בדבריו לדָבָר, in what he said his intention was such-and-such: "It seems to me that it is this that the sage who arranged the bridegroom's blessing intended (כיון) when he said, 'and prepared for him from it an everlasting building'" (Ruach Chen 3). — And in the sense of checked and examined: "Yochanan the High Priest heard from the House of the Holy of Holies: The young men who went to wage war at Antioch have been victorious. And they noted (וכיונו) that hour, and they verified (וכיונו) that they were victorious at that hour" (Tosefta Sotah 13:5). — And in the sense of recorded the hour exactly: "It happened that the son of Rabban Gamliel fell ill; he sent two disciples of the sages to R. Chanina ben Dosa to ask for mercy on him, etc. He said to them: Go, for the fever has left him, etc. They sat and wrote, and noted (וכיונו) that hour; and when they came to Rabban Gamliel, he said to them: By the Temple service! You have neither subtracted nor added, but so it happened: at that hour the fever left him" (Berakhot 34b). — And fixed exactly; and the liturgical poet said: "He gathered all the waters, He made them wise to make the dry land appear; He fixed (כון) in His palm the measure of their weight" (Second Sabbath after Passover, Aranen). — And in the sense of °made exactly like another: "It happened that a document came before Rava on which Rava and Rav Acha bar Adda were signed. Rava said to him: Certainly this is my handwriting, but I do not sign before Rav Acha bar Adda. He compelled him, and he confessed. He said to him: Granted you forged mine, but that of Rav Acha bar Adda (whose hand trembled), how did you reproduce it exactly (כיונתה)? He said to him: I put my hand on a rope" (Halakhot Pesukot, Mamonot).

— Pu'al, *כֻּוַּן, מְכֻוָּן, מכוון, מְכֻוָּנִים, מכוונים, מְכֻוָּנוֹת, מכוונות, — that they aligned it, in all the senses of the active, a) exact, German genau, French exact, English -tly: "If (the slain man) was found exactly (מכוון) between two towns, both of them bring two heifers" (Sotah 9:2). — And a measure מכֻונת, in which nothing is lacking: "A mikveh that has in it exactly (מכוונות) forty se'ah" (Mikvaot 7:6). "The three by three that they spoke of is apart from the hem, these are the words of R. Shimon; and the Sages say: Exactly (מכוונות) three by three" (Kelim 28:7). "R. Pedat said: All agree that if we had need of the date of the document, and its date was found to fall exactly (מכוונת) on the Sabbath or on the tenth of Tishrei, the document is postdated and valid" (Bava Batra 171a). — And like an adverb in this sense, also with the feminine: "And a clump of olives that fell into an oven and was heated: exactly (מכוון) an egg's bulk, it is clean; more than an egg's bulk, it is unclean" (Kelim 3:2). "One unclean by the dead who pressed olives and grapes, exactly (מכוון) an egg's bulk, it is clean" (ibid. 3). — b) מכֻון כנגד דבר, stood opposite it: "Beams of the house and of the upper story that have no plaster on them, and they are aligned (מכוונות) (the upper ones over the lower ones): if there is impurity under one of them, what is beneath it is unclean" (Oholot 12:5). "A basilica whose two entrances are aligned (מכוונין) opposite each other" (Tosefta Tohorot 7:13). "He planted three opposite three, and one aligned (מכוונת) opposite the middle one" (Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 4, 29c). "The Holy of Holies below is aligned (מכוון) opposite the Holy of Holies above" (ibid. Berakhot 4, 8c). — And that which stands in a straight row: "If the stock is aligned (מכוון) and the foliage is not aligned, this is a vineyard; if the foliage is aligned (מכוון) and the stock is not aligned, this is not a vineyard. How is it known whether it is aligned (מכוון) or not? He stretches the cord over the vines; if they all touch it as one, this is a vineyard; if one goes in and one comes out, it is not a vineyard" (Tosefta Kilayim 3:4). "A skylight in the ceiling of a house, and a pot set on the ground and aligned (ומכוונת) opposite the skylight, so that if it were raised it would come out exactly through the skylight" (Rambam, Tum'at Met 16:5). — And like an adverb: "For he would put his hand down to his armpit and afterward open it, and one would open opposite him exactly (מכוון), and he would not need to put his hand down" (Rif, Bava Metzia 18a). — And in the sense of inclined toward: "A person's eyes and heart and ears must be directed (מכוונים) to the words of Torah" (Sifre Deuteronomy 334). "A south wind comes out and bends it (the rose) toward the north, and the thorn pricks it, and even so its heart is directed (מכוון) upward" (Leviticus Rabbah 23). "As this palm tree, its heart is directed (מכוון) upward, so Israel, their heart is directed (מכוון) to their Father in heaven" (Numbers Rabbah 3). — And the mind: "Because the minds of most women are not directed (מכוונת) to being taught, but they turn words of Torah into words of nonsense according to the poverty of their understanding" (Rambam, Talmud Torah 1:13). — °דברים מכֻונים, as they should be, with understanding: "And we found him sick, lying in bed, and his mind was settled upon him, and his tongue and speech were in order (מכוונים) in his mouth, knowing how to speak and to listen, to ask and to answer" (Responsa of the Geonim, Harkavy 370). "An individual who writes a bill of divorce in another language requires investigation and is not presumed competent in it; and when he is investigated and found to be properly accurate (מכוון), it is valid" (ibid. 255). "It is fitting not to do so (to write a bill of divorce) in another language from the outset, lest he be unable to speak in that language words that are accurate (מכוונים) for these formulas, and lest, if they come under investigation, a defect be found in them" (ibid.). — *דברים מכונים זה לזה, agreed, the one like the other: "And they examine him (the second witness); if their words are found to agree (מכוונין), they discuss the matter" (Sanhedrin 3:6). — c) °דבר מְכֻוָּן, that has a purpose in it: "And the knowledge that is intended (המכוונת) in the being of man" (Solomon ibn Gabirol, Mekor Chayyim 1:5). "The combinations and separations that are needed for the completion of study in the intended (המכוונת) counsel" (Kuzari 5:12). — d) °made in equal proportion: "For he (man) is equal and balanced (ומכוון) in his temperament more than all living creatures" (Tikkun Middot HaNefesh 8).

— Nitpa'el, *נִתְכַּוֵּן, — a) placed himself opposite a thing: "He stands on the top of the Mount of Olives and aligns himself (ומתכוין) and sees into the entrance of the Sanctuary" (Middot 2:4). "One of the house of Rabban Gamliel would enter with his shekel between his fingers and throw it before the one taking up the offering, and the one taking up the offering would aim (מתכוין) and push it into the chest" (Shekalim 3:3). — b) set his mind and thought on such-and-such, German beabsichtigen, French avoir L`intention, English intend: "One who intends (המתכוין) to carry something out in front of him, and it came around behind him" (Shabbat 10:4). "Provided that he does not intend (יתכוון) to make a large portion against a small one" (ibid. 23:2). "A person may break open a jar to eat dried figs from it, provided that he does not intend (יתכוון) to make a vessel" (ibid. 22:3). "Clothes-sewers sew in their usual way, provided that they do not intend (יתכוונו) it in the sun because of the sun, or in the rain because of the rain" (Kilayim 9:6). "And both this one and that one intend (מתכוונין) to be lenient" (Eruvin 8:2).
