בן יוסף) בדרך אמר לי רבי למדני  בנטיעת קשואין אמרתי דבר אחד נתמלאה כל השדה קשואין אמר לי רבי למדתני נטיעתן למדני עקירתן (שם).  אמר רבי דבר זה למדני אנטונינוס ומקרא מסייעו (שם צא:).  וכי חזקיה מלך יהודה לכל העולם כולו לימד תורה ולמנשה בנו לא לימד תורה (שם קא:).  בשעה שהתלמיד הולך אצל רבו ואומר לו למדני תורה אם מלמדו מאיר עיני שניהם ה' (תמור' טז.).   למד ולא לימד אין לך הבל גדול מזה (מד"ר ויקר' כב).  שהרב רוצה ללמד ותלמיד אינו רוצה ללמוד (פסיק' רבתי לא).  בשעת פטירתו של ראב"ע נכנסו תלמידים לבקרו וישבו לפניו ואמרו לו ר' למדנו דבר אחד בלבד א"ל בניי מה אלמד אתכם צאו והזהרו כל אחד איש בכבוד חברו (דא"ר ג).  אתה חונן לאדם דעת ומלמד לאנוש בינה (תפלת י"ח, אתה חונן). — לִמֵּד אומנות: ר"מ אומר לעולם ילמד אדם את בנו אומנות נקיה וקלה (קדוש' ד יד).  כל שאינו מלמד את בנו אומנות מלמדו ליסטות (גמ' שם כט.).  מעשה באשה אחת בקיסרין שהוליכה את בנה אצל נחתום אחד אמרה לו למד את בני אומנות אמר לה ימתין אצלי חמש שנים ואני מלמדו חמש מאות מינין בחטה (מד"ר איכה, ויגרס).  האב חייב בבנו למולו ולפדותו וכו' וללמדו אומנות ולהשיאו אשה (שם קהל', ראה חיים). — לִמְּדוֹ לעשות דבר, אמר לו ויעץ לו לעשות כך וכך: מוליכין את לולביהם להר הבית והחזנים מקבלין מהן וסודרין אותן על גב האיצטבא והזקנים מניחין את שלהן בלשכה ומלמדים אותם לומר כל מי שמגיע לולבי בידו הרי הוא לו במתנה (סוכ' ד ד).  בא יבם על הקטנה וחזר ובא על הגדולה או שבא אחיו על הגדולה פסל את הקטנה ר' אליעזר אומר מלמדים את הקטנה שתמאן בו (יבמ' יג יא).  מי שזכה בקטורת היה נוטל את הבזך מתוך הכף ונותנו לאוהבו או לקרובו נתפזר ממנו לתוכו נותנו לו בחפניו ומלמדים אותו הוי זהיר שמא תתחיל לפניך שלא תכוה (תמיד ו ג).  השוחה על כל ברכה וברכה מלמדין אותו שלא ישוח (ירוש' ברכ' א ג ג). — לִמֵּד, הוכיח והורה הלכה, הראה שכך הוא הדין: בראשונה היו שולחין אצל בעלי בתים שבמדינות מהרו והתקינו את פירותיכם עד שלא תגיע שעת הביעור עד שבא ר"ע ולימד שכל הפירות שלא באו לעונת המעשרות פטורים מן הביעור (מע"ש ה ח).  שלח לו ר"ג (לר' יהושע) גוזרני עליך שתבא אצלי במקלך ובמעותיך ביוה"כ שחל להיות בחשבונך הלך ומצאו ר' עקיבא מיצר אמר לו (ר"ע) יש לי ללמד שכל מה שעשה רבן גמליאל עשוי שנאמר אלה מועדי יי' וכו' (ר"ה ב ט).  אמר רבי יהושע מי יגלה עפר מעיניך ריב"ז שהיית דורש כל ימיך שלא עבד איוב את המקום אלא מיראה וכו' והלא יהושע תלמיד תלמידך לימד שמאהבה עשה (סוט' ה ה).  שבא ר' עקיבא ולימד שהנדר שהותר מקצתו הותר כולו (נדר' ט ו).  אמר לו ר' ישמעאל אלעזר בן עזריה עליך ראיה ללמד שאתה מחמיר שכל המחמיר עליו ראיה ללמד (ידים ד ג).  נכנס (רשב"ג) לבית דין ולימד האשה שהיו עליה חמש לידות וודאות חמש זיבות וודאות מביאה קרבן אחד (ב"ב קסו.). — והתורה לִמְּדָה, במה שכתוב בה כך וכך הורת לנו כך וכך: לימדה תורה דרך ארץ נתמנה לאדם פרנסה יקח בית ואח"כ שדה ואח"כ אשה שנאמר אשר בנה אשר נטע אשר ארש אשה (תופסתא סוט' ז כ).  מכאן (ממה שנאמר בכתוב ויביאה אל האדם) לימדה תורה ד"א שיחזור גדול עם קטן בשושבינות ואל ירע לו (ברכ' סא.).  (כתוב) ויקרא אל משה וידבר למה הקדים קריאה לדיבור לימדה תורה דרך ארץ שלא יאמר אדם דבר לחבירו אלא א"כ קוראהו (יומ' ד:).  מיכן (ממה שנאמר בכתוב תן חיים לנערותך) לימדה תורה דרך ארץ שלא ילמד אדם את בנו בשר ויין (חול' פד.).  כאן (שאמר הכתוב אם במחתרת ימצא הגנב והכהו ומת אין לו דמים) למדתך תורה אם בא להרגך השכם להרגו (רש"י שמות כב א). — לִמְּדַתְךָ לָשׁוֹן, בלשון שהשתמשה התכונה ללמדך דבר: ראה לשון שלימדתך התורה מולך כל שתמליכהו עליך (ירוש' סנה' ז כה ג). — לְלַמֵּד, לְלַמֶּדְךָ, מה שנאמר בכתוב כך וכך הוא כדי להורות כך וכך: (כתוב) ויעל משה ואהרן נדב ואביהוא ושבעים מזקני ישראל ולמה לא נתפרשו שמותן של זקנים אלא ללמד שכל שלשה ושלשה שעמדו בית דין על ישראל הרי הוא כבית דינו של משה (ר"ה ב ט).  ר' נתן אומר בקיפוסולין של מצרים היה קבור יוסף ללמדך שבמדה שאדם מודד בה מודדים לו וכו' (מכי' בשלח ב, פתיח').  ר"י אומר בא הכתוב (שאמר וכל תרומה לכל קדשי בני ישראל) ללמדך על מקדיש ערימתו עד שלא מירח שהוא פטור מן התרומה (ספרי במד' ה).  מפני מה התקינו גואל ישראל ברכה שביעית ללמדך שאין ישראל נגאלין אלא בשביעית (ירוש' ברכ' ב ד ד).  כך היתה הלכה בידם ושכחוה ועמדו השניים והסכימו על דעת הראשונים ללמדך שכל דבר שבית דין נותנין נפשם עליו סופו להתקיים בידם (שם שבי' א לג:).  (כתוב) כי יתן איש אל רעהו וכו' ללמד שאין ב"ד נזקקין לפחות משוה פרוטה (שם שבו' ו לו ד).  (כתוב) וישכם אברהם בבקר ויקח לחם וחמת מים ללמדך שהיה שונא לישמעאל על שיצא לתרבות רעה ושלחו הוא ואמו הגר ריקם וטרדו מביתו על כך וכי תעלה על דעתך שאברהם שכתוב בו ואברם כבד מאד במקנה וגומר משלח אשתו ובנו מביתו ריקם בלא כסות ובלא מחיה אלא ללמדך כיון שיצא לתרבות רעה לא נפנה עליו (מד"ר שמות א). —  ומְלַמֵּד: ההלל והשמחה שמנה כיצד מלמד שחייב אדם בהלל ובשמחה ובכבוד יו"ט האחרון של חג כשאר כל ימות החג (סוכ' ד ח).  לא עבד איוב את הקב"ה אלא מאהבה שנאמר הן יקטלני לו אייחל ועדין הדבר שקול לו אני מצפה או איני מצפה ת"ל עד אגוע לא אסיר תומתי ממני מלמד שמאהבה עשה (סוט' ה ה).  (כתוב) לעיני כל העם מלמד שלא היה בהם סומים דבר אחר לעיני כל העם מלמד שראו באותה שעה מה שלא ראה יחזקאל וישעיה (מכי' יתרו ג).  (כתוב) אם לא שכב איש אותך מלמד שפותח לה (הכהן להסוטה) בזכות (ספרי במד' יב).  הרי הוא אומר חי אל הסיר משפטי ושדי המר נפשי מלמד שאין אדם נודר בחיי המלך אלא א"כ אוהב את המלך (תוספתא סוט' ו א).  (כתוב) הנה אנכי והילדים אשר נתן לי יי' וכי ילדים היו והלא תלמידיו היו אלא מלמד שהיו חביבין עליו והיה קורא אותם בני (ירוש' סנה' י כח:).  (כתוב בבלעם) ויודע דעת עליון (והלא דעת בהמתו לא היה יודע דעת עליון היה יודע) אלא מלמד שהיה יודע לכוין אותה שעה שהקב"ה כועס בה (ברכ' ז.).  (כתוב) ושחטו אותו כל קהל עדת ישראל בין הערבים וכי כל הקהל שוחטין והלא אין שוחט אלא אחד אלא מלמד שכל ישראל יוצאין בפסח אחד (פסח' עח:).  (כתוב) ולהג הרבה יגיעת בשר וכו' מלמד שכל המלעיג על דברי חכמים נידון בצואה רותחת (ערוב' כא:).  (כתוב) וקראו לו זקני עירו הן ולא שלוחן ודברו אליו מלמד שמשיאין לו עצה הוגנת לו (יבמ' מד.).  (כתוב) אם יקום והתהלך בחוץ על משענתו ונקה במקור נדפס "ונכה" המכה וכי תעלה על דעתך שזה מהלך בשוק וזה נהרג אלא מלמד שחובשין אותו (כתוב' לג:).  ובקלקלה מתחילים מן הקטן שנאמר ויאמר יי' אלהים אל הנחש ואל האשה אמר וכו' ולאדם אמר וכו' מלמד שמתחלה נתקלל נחש ואח"כ נתקללה חוה ואח"כ נתקלל אדם (מד"ר בראש' כ). — לִמֵּד הַדָּבָר עַל דָּבָר, הורה לנו בדבר ההוא כך וכך: כל דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא מן הכלל ללמד לא ללמד על עצמו יצא אלא ללמד על הכלל כלו יצא (י"ג מדות של ר' ישמעאל).  דרש ר"ע כל כלי חרש וכו' יטמא אינו אומר טמא אלא יטמא לטמא אחרים לימד על ככר שני שמטמא את השלישי (סוט' ה ב).  הבערה לימדה על כל המלאכות שבתורה כולהן לצורך והיא שלא לצורך (ירוש' שבת ב ה.).  (כתוב) ונתנו בני אהרן הכהן אש על המזבח לימד על הצתת אליתא שלא תהא אלא בכהן כשר ובכלי שרת (יומ' מה.).  (כתוב) לבד מנדריכם ונדבותיכם לימד על נדרים ונדבות שקרבין בחולו של מועד (תמור' יד:). (כתוב) ופרע את ראש האשה וכו' לימד על בנות ישראל שיהיו מכסות ראשיהן (מד"ר במד' ט).  — בא לְלַמֵּד ונמצא לָמֵד: רבי אומר (כתוב בנערה המאורסה) כי כאשר יקום איש על רעהו ורצחו נפש כן הדבר הזה וכי מה ענין רוצח אצל נערה המאורסה הרי זה בא ללמד ונמצא למד מקיש רוצח לנערה המאורסה וכו' (פסח' כה:), ומצוי הדבור הרבה.  — לִמֵּד על פלוני זכות או חובה, דבּר והוכיח בראיות וכדומה שפלוני זכאי או חיב: דיני ממונות הכל מלמדין זכות וחובה דיני נפשות הכל מלמדין זכות ואין הכל מלמדין חובה דיני ממונות המלמד חובה מלמד זכות והמלמד זכות מלמד חובה דיני נפשות המלמד חובה מלמד זכות אבל המלמד זכות אינו יכול לחזור וללמד חובה (סנה' ד א).  נגמר הדין מוציאין אותו לסקלו וכו' אמר אחד יש לי ללמד עליו זכות וכו' ואפי' הוא אומר יש לי ללמד על עצמי זכות מחזירין אותו וכו' וכרוז יוצא לפניו איש פלוני בן פלוני יוצא ליסקל על שעבר עברה פלונית ופלוני ופלוני עדיו כל מי שיודע לו זכות יבא וילמד עליו (שם ו א).  יה"ר מלפניך יי' אלהי שבשעה שיהיו בניו של יצחק בני נכנסים לידי צרה ואין להם מי ילמד עליהם סניגוריא אתה תהא מלמד עליהם סניגוריא (ירוש' תענ' ב סה ד).  אפילו תשע מאות ותשעים ותשעה מלאכים מלמדין עליו חובה ומלאך אחד מלמד עליו זכות הקב"ה מכריעו לכף זכות (שם קדוש' א סא ד).  מדת בשר ודם שנים עומדים בפני המלך אחד מלמד קטיגוריא שלו ואחד סניגוריא שלו לא כל המלמד קטיגוריא מלמד סניגוריא ולא המלמד סניגוריא מלמד קטיגוריא אבל הקב"ה אינו כן הוא מלמד סניגוריא הוא מלמד קטיגוריא (מד"ר שמות יה).  אמר משה אם מניח אני את ישראל וארד אין להם תקומה לעולם איני זז מכאן עד שאבקש עליהם רחמים מיד התחיל מלמד עליהם סנגורי' אמר להקב"ה יש לי זכות ללמד עליהם (שם מב).  כל אותה הלילה היה לוט עומד ומדבר עליהם סנגורי' כיון שבאו ואמרו לו איה האנשים ונדעה אותם בתשמיש מיד ויאמרו האנשים אל לוט עוד מי לך פה עד כאן היה לך פתחון פה ללמד עליהן סניגוריא (שם ויקר' כג).  למלך שעשה סעודה וזימן האורחין מהם אוכלים ושותים ומברכים למלך ומהן אוכלים ושותים ומקללין למלך הרגיש המלך ובקש להכניס בהם מהומה בסעודתו ולערבבה נכנסה מטרונה ולימדה עליהם סניגוריא אמרה לו אדוני המלך וכו' הביטה באלו שאוכלים ושותים ומברכים אותך ומשבחים לשמך (שם שה"ש, ברח דודי).  אמר לו הקב"ה נשתתקת ואין אתה מלמד סניגוריא על בני (שם, רות א). — ג) בהשאלה, לִמֵּדבאשור' בספר המשפט' של חמורבי משמש בנין למד ביחס לאשה כמו בעבר' ידע אשה. ולא נתברר אם זה פעל מיוחד, או באמת נסתעף מן המשמ' העקרית של למד. אִשָּׁה, התחבר אליה, דבק בה:   מי יתנך כאח לי יונק שדי אמי אמצאך בחוץ אשקך גם לא יבזו לי אנהגך אביאך אל בית אמי תְּלַמְּדֵנִי אשקך מיין הרקח מעסיס רמני (שה"ש ח א-ב). ד) *לִמֵּד אבנים וכדומה, ערך אותן וסדר אותן לפי הצרך: פעם א' הלך רבי למקום אחד ומצא נדבך של אבנים ואמר לתלמידיו צאו וחשבו כדי שנשב עליהן למחר וכו' רבי אמי אמר (לא אמר להם אלא) צאו ולמדום (שבת קכה:).  נדבך של אבנים שחשב עליו מבעוד יום אם למדום מותר לישב עליהם למחר (רמב"ם, שבת כה כא).

— פֻע', לֻמַּד, מְלֻמָּד, מְלֻמָּדָה, מְלֻמְּדֵי, — שלִמְּדוּהוּ, שהרגילוהו בדבר, geübt; exercé; trained: יסרתני ואוסר כעגל לא לֻמָּד (ירמ' לא יז).  עגלה מְלֻמָּדָהּ אהבתי לדוש ואני עברתי על טוב צוארה (הוש' י יא).  הנה מטתו שלשלמה ששים גברים סביב לה מגברי ישראל כלם אחזי חרב מְלֻמְּדֵי מלחמה איש חרבו על ירכו מפחד בלילות (שה"ש ג ז-ח). — ושיר וכדומ': ויהי מספרם עם אחיהם מְלֻמְּדֵי שיר ליי' כל המבין מאתים שמונים ושמנה (דהי"א כה ז). — ובתו"מ, מְלֻמַּד בדבר, רגיל בו: אמרו מי ילך ויבטל הגזירות ילך ר' שמעון בן יוחאי שהוא מלומד בנסים (מעי' יז:).  כל זמן שמאורות לוקין סימן רע לשונאיהם של ישראל מפני שמלומדים במכותיהן (סוכ' כט.). — ומצוי בסהמ"א: שלא היו מלומדין לשתות תמיד לפני המועד (רש"י מו"ק ו:).  אמר להם הריני מוחל לו על תנאי שלא יהיה מלומד לעשות כן (פרקי רבנו הקדוש יא). — ב) °אדם שלמד הרבה, Gelehrter; savant: והסכימו ביניהם שלא יהיה ענינם כמדת היהודים המלומדים בישיבותיהם ליכנס כל אחד בדברי חבירו (שבט יהודה מ).

— הִתפ', *הִתְלַמֵּד, — א) התרגל בדבר: אחר הכל עונין אמן חוץ מתינוקות של בית רבן הואיל ולהתלמד עשויין (ברכ' נג:).  כותבין מגילה לתינוק להתלמד בה (יומ' לז:).  אמר ר' חנינא קרא צער גדול היה לי אצל ר"ח הגדול ולא התיר לי לפסוק (את הפסוק לשנים) אלא לתינוקות של בית רבן הואיל ולהתלמד עשויין (תענ' כז:).  כתב לגרש את אשתו ונמלך וכו' א"ר פפא בסופרים העשויין  להתלמד (גיט' כד:).  שמע קול התינוק' מתלמדין ואומרי' איש פלוני גירש את פלונית ממקום פלוני ואמר זה שמי וזה שם אשתי (מדר' תנא' כד א).  מכניסין את התינוקות להתלמד  כבן שש כבן שבע לפי כח הבן ובנין גופו (רמב"ם, ת"ת ב ב). — ב) נתלמד הדבר, למדו אותו: התורה היום לומד מעט ולמחר הרבה לפי שאינה מתלמדת לא בשנה ולא בשתים (מד"ר במד' יב). — ואמר הפיטן: חביון עז שכנתי במחמד, לארץ לא ירדתי להתלמד, ועמד איש תם ותאותי חמד (רשב"י, ג' שבוע', בשורי מעשהו). — ג) °כמו לְמַד, התלמד מפלוני: הרב שאינו הולך בדרך טובה אע"פ שחכם גדול הוא וכל העם צריכין לו אין מתלמדין ממנו עד שובו למוטב (רמב"ם, ת"ת ד א).  ושל צורות שעושין אותו כדי שיתלמד ממנו הרוקם (הוא, כלים כז יב).  וכן המלמד והמתלמד כי החכמה נמצאת למלמד בפועל ולמתלמד בכח (אמונה רמה א ה).
en: Intransitive verb, לָמַדְתִּי, אֶלְמַד, אֶלְמְדָה, תִּלְמַד, יִלְמַד, לָמְדוּ, לְמַדְתֶּם, יִלְמְדוּ, יִלְמְדוּן, תִּלְמָדוּ, לָמֹד, לָמְדִי, לִמְדוּ, לְמוּדֵי, — לָמַד to do a thing: to exert oneself to do it many times, one after another, and to study it closely, so as to know how to do it well, German lernen; French apprendre; English learn: "And he (the king) shall write him a copy of this law in a book, out of that which is before the priests the Levites; and it shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life, that he may learn (יִלְמַד) to fear the LORD his God" (Deuteronomy 17:18-19). "And that their children, which have not known, may hear, and learn (וְלָמְדוּ) to fear the LORD your God" (ibid. 31:13). "Gather the people together, men and women and children, and thy stranger that is within thy gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn (יִלְמְדוּ), and fear the LORD your God" (ibid. 12). "Gather me the people together, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn (יִלְמְדוּן) to fear me" (ibid. 4:10). "Cease to do evil; learn (לִמְדוּ) to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed" (Isaiah 1:16-17). "And she (the lioness) brought up one of her whelps: it became a young lion, and it learned (וַיִּלְמַד) to catch the prey; it devoured men" (Ezekiel 19:3). — And war: "Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn (יִלְמְדוּ) [Note: In Micah 4:3 יִלְמְדוּן.] war any more" (Isaiah 2:4). "Men able to bear buckler and sword, and to shoot with bow, and skilful (וּלְמוּדֵי) in war" (1 Chronicles 5:18). — And in the sense of: to take one of the things as a model for oneself and exert oneself to do likewise: "When thou art come into the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee, thou shalt not learn (תִלְמַד) to do after the abominations of those nations" (Deuteronomy 18:9). — And וְלָמַד אל a thing, in this sense: "Thus saith the LORD, Learn not (אל תִּלְמָדוּ) the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven" (Jeremiah 10:2). — And also לָמַד a thing, in this sense: "If they will diligently learn (לָמֹד יִלְמְדוּ) the ways of my people, to swear by my name" (Jeremiah 12:6). "But were mingled among the heathen, and learned (וַיִּלְמְדוּ) their works. And they served their idols" (Psalms 106:35-36). — And וְלָמַד a thing: to study it, to investigate it in order to know it: "And Moses called all Israel, and said unto them, Hear, O Israel, the statutes and judgments which I speak in your ears this day, that ye may learn (וּלְמַדְתֶּם) them, and keep, and do them" (Deuteronomy 5:1). "They also that erred in spirit shall come to understanding, and they that murmured shall learn (יִלְמְדוּ) doctrine" (Isaiah 29:24). — And in the sense of: to see and become convinced that a thing is so, or that the thing must be done: "For when thy judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn (לָמְדוּ) righteousness. Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn (לָמַד) righteousness: in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly" (Isaiah 26:9-10). — And in particular לָמַד wisdom: to occupy oneself with it and exert oneself to attain knowledge of it: "Surely I am more brutish than any man, and have not the understanding of a man. I neither learned (לָמַדְתִי) wisdom, nor have the knowledge of the holy" (Proverbs 30:2-3). — And statutes and the like: "I will praise thee with uprightness of heart, when I shall have learned (בְּלָמְדִי) thy righteous judgments" (Psalms 119:7). — And in the Talmud and Midrash, in the sense of: to become accustomed to a thing, and especially the passive participle, to be לָמוּד, לְמוּדָה, לְמוּדִים, לְמוּדוֹת, to be accustomed, German gewöhnt s.; French être habitué; English be accustomed: "If one in sixty-one came up in his hand as terumah, he should go back and separate terumah as he is accustomed (למוד) to, by measure, by weight or by number" (Terumot 4:3). "An Israelite's daughter who married a priest and is accustomed (למודה) (to come) to her father's house" (ibid. 11:10). "If she was accustomed (למודה) to see at the beginning of her periods etc. If she was accustomed to see it at sunrise" Niddah 9:9. "If she was accustomed to see it on the fifteenth day and changed to seeing it on the twentieth day" (ibid. 10). "If a priest or a poor man was accustomed (למודים) to eat with him, let them come and eat" (Demai 4:4). "Israel were accustomed (למודין) to speak words of complaint against Moses" (Mekhilta Beshalach 4:1). "Three hours he has fasted: if he was accustomed to eat at the third hour and ate at the sixth, if accustomed to eat at the sixth and ate at the ninth" (Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10, 28b). "Like the friend of a king who was dwelling in a province, and for his sake the king attended to the province; and when they came to words to attend to him, they said, Woe to us, for the king does not attend to the province as he is accustomed (למוד) if we kill his friend" (Genesis Rabbah 42). "R. Yose bar Halafta and his disciples were accustomed (למודים) to rise early and sit and study under one fig tree" (ibid. 62). "If he was accustomed to read one page, he reads two pages; and if he was accustomed to study one chapter, let him study two" (ibid., Leviticus Rabbah 25). "R. Judah the Levite son of R. Shalom said: The Holy One, blessed be He, is accustomed (למוד) to count this tribe in every place" (ibid., Numbers Rabbah 3). "He (Balaam) said to him (to the angel): I did not go until the Holy One, blessed be He, said to me, Rise, go with them; and you say that I should go back? Such is his craft etc. He is accustomed (למוד) to say a thing and an angel reverses it" (ibid. 20). "Merodach was a worshipper of the sun, and he was accustomed to eat at the sixth hour and sleep until the ninth hour" (ibid., Song of Songs Rabbah, מצאוני). "Rabban Gamaliel had a member of his household who was accustomed to take a basket of forty seahs and carry it to the baker" (ibid., ידיו). "So R. Tanhum used to do: if he was accustomed to buy a litra of meat, he would buy two, one for himself and one for the poor" (ibid., Ecclesiastes Rabbah, ביום טוב). "Like one who was accustomed to have marital relations at sunrise, and forgot and had relations before sunrise" (ibid., כי את כל). "While they were still in Egypt they mocked me etc.; they are accustomed (למודים) to this" (Tanhuma Shelach 8). "Be accustomed (למוד) to accept suffering, and forgive your insult" (Avot de-Rabbi Natan 41). — And also of things that are not living creatures: "For example, those of which they say, they are accustomed (למודות) in the eves of the Sabbatical year to produce fine wheat" (Sifra Kedoshim 11). — °לָמוּד at so-and-so's: to be accustomed to be at his place: "The son or slave of a haver who were accustomed (למודין) to be with an am ha-aretz must undertake; the son or slave of an am ha-aretz who were accustomed (למודים) to be with a haver, as long as they are with him they are like a haver" (Rambam, Ma'aser 10:3). — And the active past, לָמַד a meal: to be accustomed to it: "For they were not accustomed (למדו) to the meals of kings" (Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6, 10d). — And in the sense of: to learn to know how to do a thing: "Children are not prevented from blowing the shofar, but one occupies oneself with them until they learn (שילמדו)" (Rosh Hashanah 4:8). "A Torah scholar must learn (שילמוד) three things: writing, slaughtering and circumcision" (Chullin 9a). And in particular לָמַד Torah, wisdom and the like: "If you have learned (למדת) much Torah, do not take credit for yourself, for to this end you were created" (Avot 2:8). "Be diligent to learn (ללמוד) Torah, and know what to answer the Epicurean" (ibid. 14). "If you have learned Torah, they give you much reward" (ibid. 16). "(A man who has) to learn Torah and to marry a wife: he learns (לומד) Torah and afterwards marries a wife etc. He to learn Torah and his son to learn Torah etc.: he comes before his son" (Tosefta Bekhorot 6:10). "When Hanina, the nephew of R. Joshua, went down to the Diaspora etc., they sent two Torah scholars after him, R. Yose ben Kipper and the grandson of Zechariah ben Kevutal. When he saw them he said to them, Why have you come? They said to him, We have come to learn Torah" (Berakhot 63a). "R. Yohanan said: When we were learning (לומדין) Torah with R. Oshaya, we would sit four by four in a cubit" (Eruvin 53a). "Torah scholars who go from city to city and from province to province to learn Torah" (ibid. 54b). "What was the order of teaching the Mishnah? Moses learned (למד) from the mouth of the Almighty; Aaron came in and Moses taught him his chapter etc." (ibid.). "R. Hiyya bar Abba said: It (the Torah) is trustworthy to bear witness for those who learn it (בלומדיה)" (Yoma 72b). "The men come to learn, the women come to hear" (Chagigah 6a). "R. Eleazar son of R. Zadok said: When I was learning Torah with R. Yohanan ha-Horani, I saw that he ate dry bread with salt in years of drought" (Yevamot 15b). "R. Akiva says: If he learned (למד) Torah in his youth, let him learn Torah in his old age" (ibid. 62b). "Here it (the Torah) is rolled up and lying in a corner; whoever wishes to learn, let him come and learn" (Kiddushin 66a). "Much Torah have I learned (למדתי), and I did not take from my teachers even as much as a dog lapping from the sea" (Sanhedrin 68a). "For in his youth he made himself small before one greater than him in order to learn Torah" (Sotah 10b). "Rav Huna said: Learn (למוד) Torah even if not for its own sake, for out of not for its own sake comes for its own sake" (Lamentations Rabbah, Petichta). "If you wish to learn, do not say of what you have not heard, I have heard" (Kallah Rabbati 4). "The student should not be ashamed before his fellows who learned the first or second time while he learned only after several times" (Rambam, Talmud Torah 4:5). — And the participle לָמֵד, לְמֵדִים: "One who learns (הלמד) [Note: So, without ו between ל and מ, in the Mishnah with the Arabic text of Maimonides' commentary, and so in other manuscripts; and R. Simeon ben Zemah Duran already testified to this: "and it is a precise reading in old books" (Magen Avot 4:5).] as a child, what is he like? Like ink written on new paper. And one who learns (והלמד) [Note: So, without ו between ל and מ, in the Mishnah with the Arabic text of Maimonides' commentary, and so in other manuscripts; and R. Simeon ben Zemah Duran already testified to this: "and it is a precise reading in old books" (Magen Avot 4:5).] when old, what is he like? Like ink written on erased paper" (Avot 4:20). "Just as I learned it in pain, so shall you learn (למדים) it in pain" (Sifre Deuteronomy 306). "R. Joshua says: One who studies and does not toil is like a man who sows and does not reap; one who learns (הלמד) Torah and forgets is like a woman who gives birth and buries" (Tosefta Parah 4:7). "One who learns in order to do, and not one who learns in order not to do; for one who learns in order not to do, it would have been better for him not to have been created" (Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1, 3b). "One who learns aggadah from a book does not quickly forget it" (ibid. 5, 9a). "R. Meir said: All the days that we were learning (למידין) with R. Ishmael we did not put vitriol in the ink" (ibid. Sotah 2, 18a). "Rabbi said: When we were learning Torah with R. Simeon in Tekoa, we used to carry oil and a towel from courtyard to roof" (Babylonian Talmud Shabbat 147b). "Remember that man for good, and Joshua ben Gamla is his name; for were it not for him the Torah would have been forgotten from Israel. For at first, whoever had a father, his father taught him Torah; whoever had no father did not learn (למד) Torah etc. They ordained that teachers of children be set up in Jerusalem etc. And still, whoever had a father, his father would bring him up and teach him; whoever had no father would not go up and learn. They ordained that they be set up in every district" (Bava Batra 21a). "At the moment when Israel heard 'I am the LORD thy God', the study of Torah was fixed in their heart, and they would learn (למדים) and not forget" (Song of Songs Rabbah, ישקני). "Torah: a man learns (למד) two laws today and two tomorrow, until he becomes like a flowing stream" (ibid., כי טובים). "Although it is a commandment to learn by day and by night, a man learns (למד) most of his wisdom only at night" (Rambam, Talmud Torah 3:13). "Twenty-five children learning (למדים) with one teacher" (ibid. 2:5). — לָמַד from so-and-so: so-and-so taught him: "Who is wise? He who learns (הלומד) from every man" (Avot 4:1). "One who learns (הלמד) [Note: See the previous note.] (Torah) from the young, what is he like? Like one who eats unripe grapes and drinks wine from his vat. And one who learns (והלמד) [Note: See the previous note.] from the old, what is he like? Like one who eats ripe grapes and drinks old wine" (ibid. 20). "One who learns from his fellow one chapter or one law etc. must treat him with honour; for so we find with David king of Israel, who learned from Ahithophel only two things, and called him his master" (ibid. 6:3). "One who learns by himself is not like one who learns from his master" (Ketubot 111a). "A parable of two men, one learned from his master and one learned by himself etc." (Commentary on Sefer Yetzirah by R. Judah of Barcelona 2, in the name of the Midrash). — לָמַד a thing from so-and-so, from so-and-so's words, or from his deeds, his custom: to understand and know what such-and-such a thing is, or how to conduct oneself in it: "And it happened in the days of the father of R. Zadok and in the days of Abba Saul ben Botnit that they stopped up the window with a jug etc., and from their words we learned (למדנו) that one may stop up, measure and tie on the Sabbath" (Shabbat 24:5). "(An Arab said to a Jew that on the day the Temple was destroyed the Messiah was born.) R. Bun said: Why do we need to learn from this Arab? Is it not an explicit verse: 'And Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one', (and what is written after it?) 'And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse'" (Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2, 5a). "At that time I learned (למדתי) three things from him (from Elijah): I learned that one does not enter a ruin, and I learned that one may pray on the road, and I learned that one who prays on the road prays a short prayer" (Babylonian Talmud ibid. 3a). "R. Akiva said: Once I went in after R. Joshua to the privy, and I learned three things from him: I learned that one does not relieve oneself facing east and west but north and south; and I learned that one does not uncover oneself standing but sitting; and I learned that one does not wipe with the right hand but with the left. Ben Azzai said to him: So far you were brazen toward your master? He said to him: It is Torah, and I need to learn" (ibid. 62a). "R. Yohanan said: Eighteen days I grew up with R. Oshaya the Great, and I learned from him only one thing" (Eruvin 53a). "Rav Joseph said: A man should always learn (ילמד) (humility) from the mind of his Maker, for the Holy One, blessed be He, passed over all the mountains and hills and caused His Presence to rest on Mount Sinai" (Sotah 5a). "One who takes leave of his fellow, whether great or small, must take leave of him. From whom do you learn this (למד)? From Abraham. Once Abraham was speaking with the Holy One, blessed be He; the ministering angels came to speak with him. He said to them: I will take leave of the Shekhinah, which is greater than you etc." (Genesis Rabbah 47). "Five things we learned (למדנו) from R. Eliezer at the hour of his death, and we rejoiced in them with great joy" (Derekh Eretz Rabbah 3). — לָמַד a thing: the thing became clear to him: "(It is written) 'And if it be from sixty years old and above, if it be a male': behold, we learn (למדים) for all of them from the sixtieth year: just as the sixtieth year is like what is below it, so the fifth year and the twentieth year are like what is below them" (Arakhin 4:4). "(It is written) 'And if a man sell': we have learned (למדנו) that he is permitted to sell her" (Mekhilta Mishpatim 3). "R. Eleazar of Modiin says: He (Moses) gave him (Jethro) many gifts, for from the answer he gave him you learn (למד)" (ibid. Yitro 2). "And according to our way we have learned (למדנו) that a dwelling outside the Land is not counted for them in the number" (Tosefta Yevamot 8:4). "For they also asked Sarah, 'Where is Abraham?' We have learned (למדנו) that a man should ask at his lodging the man about the wife and the wife about the man" (Rashi Genesis 18:9). "You have learned (למדת) that a season never falls at the beginning of the night except at the end of four years" (the same, Berakhot 59b). הא לָמַדְתָּ, behold you have seen, behold it has become clear to you: "R. Zadok says: Do not make them (the Torah and the commandments) a crown to magnify yourself with them, nor a spade to dig with them etc. Hence you learn (הא למדת): whoever derives benefit from words of Torah removes his life from the world" (Avot 4:5). "For sufferings appease more than sacrifices etc. Hence you learn that sufferings are precious" (Mekhilta Yitro 10). "She went and married one from the market and had children by him; if she married this one, the children of the first are not found to be mamzerim. Hence you learn that this is not a bill of divorce" (Sifre Deuteronomy 269). "(It is written) 'And he shall wash his flesh in water, and so put them on': hence you learn that whoever changes from one service to another requires immersion" (Yoma 32a). — נמצאנו לְמֵדִים, we are found to learn: "It tells that Nisan is the first of the months; and whence also for kings? Scripture says, 'in the second month of Solomon's reign over Israel'; and whence also for the festivals? Scripture says, 'the feast of unleavened bread, and the feast of weeks, and the feast of tabernacles'. We are found to learn (נמצינו למדין) that Nisan is the head of the months, for kings and for the festivals" (Mekhilta Bo 1). "We find that none of the priests was permitted to enter and serve in the Tent of Meeting unless he was thirty years old, as it is said, 'From thirty years old and upward even until fifty years old' etc. Behold, we are found to learn (נמצאנו למדים) that Eleazar, before the decree was decreed, was thirty years old or more" (Numbers Rabbah 3). "Thirty days in the year count as a year, provided the planting takes root before thirty days; and how long is ordinary rooting for all trees? Two weeks. You are found to learn (נמצאת למד) that one who plants forty-four days before Rosh Hashanah, it counts for him as a year" (Rambam, Ma'aser Sheni 9:8-9). — מכאן אתה לָמֵד, from here you learn: "When a man comes to you to convert, he comes only for the sake of Heaven; you too, bring him near and do not push him away. From here you learn that a man should push away with the left hand and bring near with the right" (Mekhilta Yitro 1). "Behold it says, 'which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart'; from here you learn that the whole section requires intention" (Berakhot 13b). "He (Joshua) cut off the heads of his (Amalek's) mighty men and left only the weak among them, and did not kill them all; from here we learn (למדים) that they acted according to the word of the Shekhinah" (Rashi Exodus 17:13). "We have already explained in the laws of the Nazirite that if the Nazirite and an olive's bulk of a corpse were under a camel or under a bed etc., he does not shave; and from there you learn that all these laws stated concerning the impurity of tents etc. are all from the words of the Scribes" (Rambam, Tum'at Met 19:6). — And kingdoms לְמֵדָה: "It is not written 'journeying' (נוסעים) here but 'journeyed' (נוסע): it tells that they all became troops upon troops like one man; from here kingdoms learn (למדין) to lead in troops upon troops" (Mekhilta Beshalach 2). — לָמֵד מִדָּבָר, to learn from a thing: "One does not learn (למדין) neither from the halakhot nor from the aggadot nor from the additions, but only from the Talmud" (Jerusalem Talmud Pe'ah 2, 17a). "Because we learn (למידין) from the halakhah, we do it" (ibid. Shevi'it 10, 39b). "One learns the possible from the impossible" (ibid. Terumot 2, 41b). "One learns a gezerah shavah even if it is free on one side" (ibid. Yoma 8, 45a). — And a thing from a thing: "A matter learned (הלמד) from its context: of what is Scripture speaking? Of money; so here too of money. A matter learned from its end: that the house does not become impure until it has in it stones, wood and earth" (Baraita of R. Ishmael). "R. Simeon said: And the thanksgiving offering, whence was it learned (למדה)? Was it not from the peace offerings? And a thing learned from another place, you come to teach from it? Learning from what is learned" (Sifre Numbers 118). "And the sin offering of the leper, whence is it learned (למידה) that it is invalid when not for its own sake?" (Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 5, 31d). "To say that they (the laws of the intermediate days of the festival) are uprooted and are not learned (למידות) one from another" (Mo'ed Katan 12a). "In the whole Torah one learns (למידין) what is learned from what is learned, except for holy things, where one does not learn what is learned from what is learned" (Shevuot 10a). — לָמַד לְדָבָר, to teach concerning this matter: "If I have learned for the leper that he shaves all his hair, so too the Nazirite shall shave all his hair" (Sifre Numbers 28). "If I have learned for impurity that it cancels everything, so too shaving shall cancel everything" (ibid. 31). — לָמַד בְּדָבָר: to discuss it, to show reasons in it: "A summer garment that has stripes dyed and white, plague spreads from one to the other. They asked R. Eliezer, But it is a single stripe? He said to them, I have not heard. R. Judah ben Bathyra said to him, Shall I reason (אלמד) about it? He said to him, If to uphold the words of the Sages, yes" (Nega'im 11:7). — לָמַד the heart of so-and-so and the like: his nature and quality became clear to him: "R. Yohanan said: R. Oshaya the Great had twelve disciples, and eighteen days I grew up among them, and I learned (ולמדתי) the heart of each one and the wisdom of each one" (Eruvin 53a). — לָמַד his words: to study them, to examine and test them: "(The witness who said) I was declaring guilty and now I declare innocent, they accept him; (and if he said) I was declaring innocent and now I declare guilty, they say to him, Study (למוד) your words. If at first one of those declaring innocent erred in his words, the scribes of the judges remind him; (and if one) of those declaring guilty (erred), the scribes of the judges do not remind him, but say to him, Study your words as at first" (Tosefta Sanhedrin 9:1). — And also in the sense of a transitive verb with a person: לָמַד him, to teach him and explain to him so that he may know it: "A minor who knows how to shake is obligated in the lulav; to wrap himself, he is obligated in tzitzit etc.; if he knows how to speak, his father teaches him (לומדו) Torah and the reading of the Shema" (Sukkah 42a).

— Pi'el, לִמַּד, לִמַּדְתִּי, לִמַּדְתְּ, לִמְּדוּ, לִמַּדְתֶּם, אֲלַמֵּד, אֲלַמְּדָה, יְלַמֵּד, יְלַמְּדוּ, יְלַמֵּדוּן, מְלַמֵּד, לַמֵּד, לְלַמֵּד, לִמַּדְתַּנִי, לַמְּדֵּנִי, לַמֵּדְנָה, לַמְּדָהּ, אֲלַמֶּדְכֶם, אֲלַמְּדֵם, תְּלַמְּדֵנִי, תְּלַמְּדֵנוּ, תְּלַמְּדֵם, יְלַמְּדֵהוּ, יְלַמְּדָהּ, מְלַמֶּדְךָ, לְלַמְּדָם, — a) לִמַּד so-and-so a thing, war and the like: to accustom him to it, to cause him to learn it, to do it many times so that he knows how to do it well, German einüben; French exercer; English to train: "Now these are the nations which the LORD left, to prove Israel by them etc.; only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them (לְלַמְּדָם) war" (Judges 3:1-2). "He teacheth (מְלַמֵּד) my hands to war; so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms" (2 Samuel 22:35). "Blessed be the LORD my strength, which teacheth (הַמְלַמֵּד) my hands to war, and my fingers to fight" (Psalms 144:1). — לִמְּדוֹ the bow and the like: "And he (David) bade them teach (לְלַמֵּד) the children of Judah the use of the bow" (2 Samuel 1:18). — And his tongue and the like: "And will not speak the truth: they have taught (לִמְּדוּ) their tongue to speak lies" (Jeremiah 9:4). — לִמְּדוֹ a way: to lead him and show him the way in which he should go, German lenken; French diriger; English to direct, and figuratively in moral matters: "Shew me thy ways, O LORD; teach me (לַמְּדֵנִי) thy paths" (Psalms 25:4). "The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach (וִילַמֵּד) his way" (ibid. 9). "Then will I teach (אֲלַמְּדָה) transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee" (ibid. 51:15). — לִמְּדוֹ to do a thing: to be by his deeds a model for him, so that he too does likewise: "That they (the nations) teach you not (לא יְלַמְּדוּ) to do after all their abominations" (Deuteronomy 20:18). — לִמְּדוֹ over so-and-so: to accustom him to be ruler over him: "For thou hast taught them (לִמַּדְתְּ) to be captains, and as chief over thee" (Jeremiah 13:21). b) In particular לִמְּדוֹ Torah, wisdom, knowledge: to instruct him and explain to him so that he understands and knows, German lehren; French enseigner; English to teach: "Now therefore hearken, O Israel, unto the statutes and unto the judgments, which I teach (מְלַמֵּד) you, for to do them" (Deuteronomy 4:1). "Behold, I have taught (לִמַּדְתִּי) you statutes and judgments, even as the LORD my God commanded me" (ibid. 5). "That they may learn to fear me all the days that they shall live upon the earth, and that they may teach (יְלַמֵּדוּן) their children" (ibid. 10). "And the LORD commanded me at that time to teach (לְלַמֵּד) you statutes and judgments" (ibid. 14). "But as for thee, stand thou here by me, and I will speak unto thee all the commandments, and the statutes, and the judgments, which thou shalt teach them (תְּלַמְּדֵם)" (ibid. 5:28). "And ye shall teach them (וְלִמַּדְתֶּם) your children, speaking of them" (ibid. 11:19). "Now therefore write ye this song for you, and teach it (וְלַמְּדָהּ) the children of Israel: put it in their mouths" (ibid. 31:19). "Moses therefore wrote this song the same day, and taught it (וַיְלַמְּדָהּ) the children of Israel" (ibid. 22). "Yet hear the word of the LORD, O ye women, and let your ear receive the word of his mouth, and teach (וְלַמֵּדְנָה) your daughters wailing, and every one her neighbour lamentation" Jeremiah 9:19. "And they shall teach (יְלַמְּדוּ) no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the LORD: for they shall all know me" ibid. 31:33. "And they have turned unto me the back, and not the face: though I taught (וְלַמֵּד) them, rising up early and teaching (וְלַמֵּד) them, yet they have not hearkened to receive instruction" ibid. 32:33. "With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him (וַיְלַמְּדֵהוּ) in the path of judgment, and taught him (וַיְלַמְּדֵהוּ) knowledge, and shewed to him the way of understanding?" Isaiah 40:14. "Thus saith the LORD, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the LORD thy God which teacheth thee (מְלַמֶּדְךָ) to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go" ibid. 48:17. "Come, ye children, hearken unto me: I will teach you (אֲלַמֶּדְכֶם) the fear of the LORD" Psalms 34:12. "O God, thou hast taught me (לִמַּדְתַּנִי) from my youth: and hitherto have I declared thy wondrous works" ibid. 71:17. "He that chastiseth the heathen, shall not he correct? he that teacheth (הַמְלַמֵּד) man knowledge?" ibid. 94:10. "Blessed is the man whom thou chastenest, O LORD, and teachest him (תְלַמְּדֶנּוּ) out of thy law" (ibid. 12). "Blessed art thou, O LORD: teach me (לַמְּדֵנִי) thy statutes" (ibid. 119:2). "Teach me (לַמְּדֵנִי) good judgment and knowledge: for I have believed thy commandments" (ibid. 66). "Accept, I beseech thee, the freewill offerings of my mouth, O LORD, and teach me (לַמְּדֵנִי) thy judgments" (ibid. 108). "My lips shall utter praise, when thou hast taught me (תְלַמְּדֵנִי) thy statutes" (ibid. 171). "If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony that I shall teach them (אֲלַמְּדֵם), their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore" (ibid. 132:12). "Shall any teach (יְלַמֶּד) God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high" (Job 21:22). "For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach (וּלְלַמֵּד) in Israel statutes and judgments" (Ezra 7:10). "Also in the third year of his reign he sent to his princes, even to Ben-hail, and to Obadiah etc., to teach (לְלַמֵּד) in the cities of Judah etc. And they taught (וַיְלַמְּדוּ) in Judah, and had the book of the law of the LORD with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught (וַיְלַמְּדוּ) the people" (2 Chronicles 17:7-10). "And the king spake unto Ashpenaz the master of his eunuchs, that he should bring certain of the children of Israel, and of the king's seed, and of the princes; children in whom was no blemish etc., and whom they might teach (וְלְלַמְּדָם) the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans" (Daniel 1:3-4). "And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught (לִמַּד) the people knowledge" (Ecclesiastes 12:9). — And in the Talmud and Midrash, as in Scripture, in the sense of: to accustom: "One trains (מלמדין) the heifer only in loose soil" (Tosefta Shevi'it 3:20). "Melammad (מלמַד) (is so called) because it teaches (מלמד) the cow to plough in order to give life to its owners" (Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10, 28a). "Teach (למד) your tongue to say 'I do not know', lest you be caught in a falsehood and be seized" (Berakhot 4a). "A man should always accustom (ילמד) himself to rise early and to stay late" (Horayot 13b). "That a man should not accustom (ילמד) his son to meat and wine" (Chullin 84a). — And לִמְּדוֹ a way: "When R. Eliezer fell ill, his disciples went in to visit him. They said to him: Our master, teach us (למדנו) the paths of life, that we may merit through them the life of the world to come" (ibid. 28b). — And in particular לִמְּדוֹ Torah and the like: "An unmarried man shall not teach (ילמד) children, and a woman shall not teach children" (Kiddushin 4:13). "I set aside all the crafts in the world and teach (מלמד) my son only Torah" (ibid. 14). "A man is obligated to teach his daughter Torah" (Sotah 3:4). "Whoever teaches his daughter Torah, it is as though he teaches her frivolity" (ibid.). "One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from his fellow may pay his shekel for him etc., and may teach him midrash, halakhot and aggadot, but he shall not teach him Scripture" (Nedarim 4:2-3). "Hygros ben Levi knew a skill in song and did not wish to teach it; Ben Kamtzar did not wish to teach concerning the craft of writing" (Yoma 3:11). "For if his father did not teach him (Torah), he teaches himself" (Mekhilta Bo 18). "Just as you learn it in pain, so shall you teach (מלמדים) it in pain" (Sifre Deuteronomy 306). "He (R. Simeon bar Yohai) said to him (to R. Akiva): Master, teach me (למדני) Torah. He said: I will not teach you. He said to him: If you do not teach me, I will tell Yohai my father and he will hand you over to the government etc. He said to him: If you seek to be strangled, hang yourself on a great tree; and when you teach your son, teach him from a corrected book" (Pesachim 112a). "Whoever learns Torah and does not teach it is like a myrtle in the wilderness" (Rosh Hashanah 23a). "A man is forbidden to teach his slave Torah" (Ketubot 28a). "Samuel said: The Torah scholars who teach the laws of slaughtering to the priests would take their wages from the terumah of the Chamber" (ibid. 106a). "R. Akiva said to him: Master, permit me to say one thing of what you taught me (שלימדתני). He said to him: Say it" (Avodah Zarah 16b). "R. Jonathan said: Whoever teaches his fellow's son Torah, Scripture regards him as though he had begotten him" (Sanhedrin 19b). "Much Torah have I taught (לימדתי), and my disciples did not take from me except as a brush in a tube" (ibid. 68a). "We were walking (with Akiva ben Joseph) on the road. He said to me: Master, teach me (למדני) about the planting of cucumbers. I said one thing, and the whole field was filled with cucumbers. He said to me: Master, you have taught me (למדתני) their planting; teach me their uprooting" (ibid.). "Rabbi said: This thing Antoninus taught me (למדני), and a verse supports him" (ibid. 91b). "And did Hezekiah king of Judah teach Torah to the whole world, and to Manasseh his son he did not teach Torah?" (ibid. 101b). "When the student goes to his master and says to him, Teach me Torah: if he teaches him, the LORD lightens the eyes of them both" (Temurah 16a). "He learned and did not teach: there is no greater vanity than this" (Leviticus Rabbah 22). "For the master wishes to teach and the student does not wish to learn" (Pesikta Rabbati 31). "At the time of the passing of R. Eleazar ben Azariah, the disciples went in to visit him and sat before him and said to him: Master, teach us just one thing. He said to them: My sons, what shall I teach you? Go and be careful, each one, of the honour of his fellow" (Derekh Eretz Rabbah 3). "You graciously give man knowledge and teach (ומלמד) mortals understanding" (Prayer of the Eighteen Benedictions, אתה חונן). — לִמֵּד a craft: "R. Meir says: A man should always teach (ילמד) his son a clean and easy craft" (Kiddushin 4:14). "Whoever does not teach his son a craft teaches him robbery" (Gemara ibid. 29a). "It happened that a woman in Caesarea took her son to a baker. She said to him: Teach my son a craft. He said to her: Let him wait with me five years and I will teach him five hundred kinds of things from wheat" (Lamentations Rabbah, ויגרס). "The father is obligated toward his son to circumcise him and to redeem him etc., and to teach him a craft and to marry him to a wife" (ibid., Ecclesiastes Rabbah, ראה חיים). — לִמְּדוֹ to do a thing: to tell him and advise him to do thus and thus: "They bring their lulavs to the Temple Mount, and the attendants receive them from them and arrange them on the roof of the portico, and the elders put theirs in the chamber; and they teach (ומלמדים) them to say: Whoever my lulav comes into his hand, behold it is his as a gift" (Sukkah 4:4). "If the levir had relations with the minor and then had relations with the adult, or his brother had relations with the adult, he disqualified the minor. R. Eliezer says: They teach (מלמדים) the minor to refuse him" (Yevamot 13:11). "Whoever won the incense would take the ladle from the spoon and give it to his friend or his relative; if some was scattered from it into it, he gives it to him in his hands; and they teach (ומלמדים) him: Be careful lest you begin in front of you, lest you be burned" (Tamid 6:3). "One who bows at every blessing, they teach (מלמדין) him not to bow" (Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1, 3c). — לִמֵּד: to prove and instruct a halakhah, to show that such is the law: "At first they would send to the householders in the provinces: Hasten and prepare your produce before the time of removal arrives; until R. Akiva came and taught (ולימד) that all produce that has not reached the season of tithes is exempt from removal" (Ma'aser Sheni 5:8). "Rabban Gamaliel sent to him (to R. Joshua): I decree upon you that you come to me with your staff and your money on the Day of Atonement that falls according to your reckoning. R. Akiva went and found him distressed. He (R. Akiva) said to him: I can teach (ללמד) that whatever Rabban Gamaliel has done is done, for it is said, 'These are the feasts of the LORD' etc." (Rosh Hashanah 2:9). "R. Joshua said: Who will remove the dust from your eyes, Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai, for you used to expound all your days that Job served the Omnipresent only out of fear etc.; and did not Joshua, your disciple's disciple, teach (לימד) that he acted out of love?" (Sotah 5:5). "For R. Akiva came and taught that a vow part of which has been released is wholly released" (Nedarim 9:6). "R. Ishmael said to him: Eleazar ben Azariah, the proof is upon you to teach, since you are the one who is stringent; for whoever is stringent, the proof is upon him to teach" (Yadayim 4:3). "He (Rabban Simeon ben Gamaliel) entered the court and taught (ולימד) that a woman who had five certain births and five certain fluxes brings one offering" (Bava Batra 166a). — And the Torah לִמְּדָה, by what is written in it thus and thus it has taught us thus and thus: "The Torah has taught (לימדה) proper conduct: when a man has been appointed a livelihood, let him take a house, and afterwards a field, and afterwards a wife, as it is said, 'that hath built', 'that hath planted', 'that hath betrothed a wife'" (Tosefta Sotah 7:20). "From here (from what is said in Scripture, 'and brought her unto the man') the Torah has taught proper conduct, that a great man should go about with a small one as groomsman and not take it ill" (Berakhot 61a). "(It is written) 'And called unto Moses, and spake'. Why did calling precede speaking? The Torah has taught proper conduct, that a man should not say a thing to his fellow unless he calls him" (Yoma 4b). "From here (from what is said in Scripture, 'and for the maintenance for thy maidens') the Torah has taught proper conduct, that a man should not accustom his son to meat and wine" (Chullin 84a). "Here (where Scripture said, 'If a thief be found breaking up, and be smitten that he die, there shall no blood be shed for him') the Torah has taught you (למדתך): if he comes to kill you, rise early to kill him" (Rashi Exodus 22:1). — לִמְּדַתְךָ a language, in the language that the Torah used, to teach you a thing: "See the language that the Torah taught you: מולך, whatever you make king (שתמליכהו) over you" (Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 7, 25c). — לְלַמֵּד, לְלַמֶּדְךָ: what is said in Scripture thus and thus is in order to teach thus and thus: "(It is written) 'Then went up Moses, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel.' And why were the names of the elders not specified? Only to teach (ללמד) that every three and three who stood as a court over Israel, behold it is like the court of Moses" (Rosh Hashanah 2:9). "R. Nathan says: Joseph was buried in the capitolium of Egypt, to teach you (ללמדך) that with the measure with which a man measures, they measure to him etc." (Mekhilta Beshalach 2, Petichta). "R. Ishmael says: Scripture comes (which said, 'And every offering of all the holy things of the children of Israel') to teach you about one who consecrates his heap before it was smoothed, that he is exempt from terumah" (Sifre Numbers 5). "Why did they institute 'Redeemer of Israel' as the seventh blessing? To teach you that Israel will be redeemed only in the seventh" (Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2, 4d). "So the halakhah was in their hands and they forgot it, and the second ones arose and agreed with the opinion of the first, to teach you that every matter to which a court devotes itself will in the end be established in their hands" (ibid. Shevi'it 1, 33b). "(It is written) 'If a man shall deliver unto his neighbour' etc., to teach that the court does not attend to less than a perutah's worth" (ibid. Shevuot 6, 36d). "(It is written) 'And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread, and a bottle of water': to teach you that he hated Ishmael because he had gone out to evil ways, and he sent him and his mother Hagar away empty-handed and drove him from his house for this. And would it enter your mind that Abraham, of whom it is written, 'And Abram was very rich in cattle' etc., would send his wife and his son away from his house empty-handed, without clothing and without sustenance? Rather, to teach you that since he had gone out to evil ways, he paid no attention to him" (Exodus Rabbah 1). — And מְלַמֵּד, it teaches: "The Hallel and the rejoicing eight days: how so? It teaches (מלמד) that a man is obligated in Hallel and in rejoicing and in honouring the last festival day of the Feast like all the other days of the Feast" (Sukkah 4:8). "Job served the Holy One, blessed be He, only out of love, as it is said, 'Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him'. And still the matter is in the balance: 'for him' (לו) I hope, or 'not' (לא) I hope? Scripture says, 'Till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me': it teaches that he acted out of love" (Sotah 5:5). "(It is written) 'In the sight of all the people': it teaches that there were no blind among them. Another explanation: 'in the sight of all the people': it teaches that they saw at that moment what Ezekiel and Isaiah did not see" (Mekhilta Yitro 3). "(It is written) 'If no man have lain with thee': it teaches that he (the priest) opens for her (the suspected wife) with a plea of merit" (Sifre Numbers 12). "Behold it says, 'As God liveth, who hath taken away my judgment; and the Almighty, who hath vexed my soul': it teaches that a man does not vow by the life of the king unless he loves the king" (Tosefta Sotah 6:1). "(It is written) 'Behold, I and the children whom the LORD hath given me'. And were they children? Were they not his disciples? Rather, it teaches that they were dear to him and he called them 'my sons'" (Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10, 28b). "(It is written of Balaam) 'And knew the knowledge of the most High' (and did he not know the mind of his beast, yet knew the mind of the Most High?) Rather, it teaches that he knew how to pinpoint the moment in which the Holy One, blessed be He, is angry" (Berakhot 7a). "(It is written) 'And the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it in the evening'. And does the whole assembly slaughter? Does not only one slaughter? Rather, it teaches that all Israel fulfil their obligation with one Passover offering" (Pesachim 78b). "(It is written) 'And much study is a weariness of the flesh' etc.: it teaches that whoever mocks the words of the Sages is judged with boiling excrement" (Eruvin 21b). "(It is written) 'Then the elders of his city shall call him': they, and not their agents; 'and speak unto him': it teaches that they give him advice fitting for him" (Yevamot 44a). "(It is written) 'If he rise again, and walk abroad upon his staff, then shall he that smote him be quit (ונקה) [Note: In the original printed "ונכה".]'. Would it enter your mind that this one walks in the market and that one is killed? Rather, it teaches that they imprison him" (Ketubot 33b). "And in cursing one begins from the least, as it is said, 'And the LORD God said unto the serpent'; 'Unto the woman he said' etc.; 'And unto Adam he said' etc.: it teaches that first the serpent was cursed, and afterwards Eve was cursed, and afterwards Adam was cursed" (Genesis Rabbah 20). — לִמֵּד הַדָּבָר עַל דָּבָר, the thing taught us thus and thus concerning that thing: "Any matter that was included in a general rule and went out of the general rule to teach, it did not go out to teach about itself but went out to teach about the whole general rule" (The Thirteen Principles of R. Ishmael). "R. Akiva expounded: 'And every earthen vessel' etc. 'shall be unclean' (יטמא): it does not say 'unclean' (טמא) but 'shall be unclean' (יטמא), to make others unclean; it taught (לימד) concerning a second-degree loaf that it makes the third unclean" (Sotah 5:2). "Kindling taught concerning all the labours in the Torah, all of which are for a need, while it is not for a need" (Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2, 5a). "(It is written) 'And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire upon the altar': it taught concerning the kindling of the flame, that it should be only by a fit priest and with a service vessel" (Yoma 45a). "(It is written) 'Beside your vows, and your freewill offerings': it taught concerning vows and freewill offerings that they are offered on the intermediate days of the festival" (Temurah 14b). "(It is written) 'And uncover the woman's head' etc.: it taught concerning the daughters of Israel that they should have their heads covered" (Numbers Rabbah 9). — בא לְלַמֵּד ונמצא לָמֵד, it came to teach and is found to learn: "Rabbi says (it is written concerning the betrothed maiden): 'For as when a man riseth against his neighbour, and slayeth him, even so is this matter'. And what has a murderer to do with a betrothed maiden? Behold, this came to teach and is found to learn: it compares the murderer to the betrothed maiden etc." (Pesachim 25b), and the expression is very common. — לִמֵּד on so-and-so merit or guilt: to speak and prove by evidence and the like that so-and-so is innocent or guilty: "In monetary cases all may argue (מלמדין) for acquittal or for conviction; in capital cases all may argue for acquittal, but not all may argue for conviction. In monetary cases one who argued for conviction may argue for acquittal, and one who argued for acquittal may argue for conviction; in capital cases one who argued for conviction may argue for acquittal, but one who argued for acquittal cannot go back and argue for conviction" (Sanhedrin 4:1). "The verdict was concluded; they take him out to stone him etc. One said, I have something to argue (ללמד) in his favour etc. And even if he himself says, I have something to argue in my own favour, they bring him back etc. And a herald goes out before him: So-and-so son of so-and-so is going out to be stoned because he committed such-and-such a transgression, and so-and-so and so-and-so are his witnesses; whoever knows anything in his favour, let him come and argue (וילמד) for him" (ibid. 6:1). "May it be Your will, LORD my God, that when the children of Isaac my son come into trouble and have none to plead (ילמד) defence for them, You shall plead (מלמד) defence for them" (Jerusalem Talmud Ta'anit 2, 65d). "Even if nine hundred and ninety-nine angels argue (מלמדין) guilt against him and one angel argues merit for him, the Holy One, blessed be He, tips him to the scale of merit" (ibid. Kiddushin 1, 61d). "The way of flesh and blood: two stand before the king, one pleads (מלמד) his prosecution and one his defence; not the one who pleads prosecution pleads defence, nor the one who pleads defence pleads prosecution. But the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so: He pleads defence, He pleads prosecution" (Exodus Rabbah 15). "Moses said: If I leave Israel and go down, they will never have a recovery; I will not move from here until I ask mercy for them. At once he began to plead (מלמד) defence for them. He said to the Holy One, blessed be He: I have merit to plead (ללמד) for them" (ibid. 42). "All that night Lot stood and spoke in their defence. When they came and said to him, 'Where are the men? that we may know them' in the sense of intercourse, at once 'the men said unto Lot, Hast thou here any besides?' Until now you had an opening of the mouth to plead (ללמד) defence for them" (ibid., Leviticus Rabbah 23). "Like a king who made a feast and invited guests; some of them eat and drink and bless the king, and some of them eat and drink and curse the king. The king perceived it and wished to bring confusion upon his feast and upset it. The matron came in and pleaded (ולימדה) defence for them. She said to him: My lord the king etc., look at these who eat and drink and bless you and praise your name" (ibid., Song of Songs Rabbah, ברח דודי). "The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: You have fallen silent and do not plead (מלמד) defence for My children" (ibid., Ruth 1). — c) Figuratively, לִמֵּד [Note: In Akkadian, in the code of laws of Hammurabi, the stem למד is used in relation to a woman like ידע אשה in Hebrew. And it has not been clarified whether this is a separate verb, or whether it truly branched off from the principal meaning of למד.] a woman: to join with her, to cleave to her: "O that thou wert as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother! when I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; yea, I should not be despised. I would lead thee, and bring thee into my mother's house, who would instruct me (תְּלַמְּדֵנִי): I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate" (Song of Songs 8:1-2). d) *לִמֵּד stones and the like: to arrange them and set them in order as needed: "Once Rabbi went to a certain place and found a row of stones, and he said to his disciples: Go out and intend them, so that we may sit on them tomorrow etc. R. Ammi said (he said to them only): Go out and arrange them (ולמדום)" (Shabbat 125b). "A row of stones which one intended for use while it was still day: if he arranged them (למדום), it is permitted to sit on them the next day" (Rambam, Shabbat 25:21).

— Pu'al, לֻמַּד, מְלֻמָּד, מְלֻמָּדָה, מְלֻמְּדֵי, — that he was taught, that he was accustomed to a thing, German geübt; French exercé; English trained: "Thou hast chastised me, and I was chastised, as a bullock unaccustomed (לא לֻמָּד) to the yoke" (Jeremiah 31:17). "And Ephraim is as an heifer that is taught (מְלֻמָּדָהּ), and loveth to tread out the corn; but I passed over upon her fair neck" (Hosea 10:11). "Behold his bed, which is Solomon's; threescore valiant men are about it, of the valiant of Israel. They all hold swords, being expert (מְלֻמְּדֵי) in war: every man hath his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night" (Song of Songs 3:7-8). — And song and the like: "So the number of them, with their brethren that were instructed (מְלֻמְּדֵי) in the songs of the LORD, even all that were cunning, was two hundred fourscore and eight" (1 Chronicles 25:7). — And in the Talmud and Midrash, מְלֻמַּד in a thing: accustomed to it: "They said: Who will go and annul the decrees? Let R. Simeon ben Yohai go, for he is accustomed (מלומד) to miracles" (Me'ilah 17b). "Whenever the luminaries are eclipsed it is a bad sign for the enemies of Israel, because they are accustomed (שמלומדים) to their blows" (Sukkah 29a). — And common in medieval literature: "For they were not accustomed (מלומדין) to drink constantly before the festival" (Rashi Mo'ed Katan 6b). "He said to them: Behold, I forgive him on condition that he not be accustomed (מלומד) to do so" (Pirkei Rabbenu ha-Kadosh 11). — b) °A person who has learned much, German Gelehrter; French savant: "And they agreed among themselves that their manner should not be like the way of the learned (המלומדים) Jews in their academies, each one breaking into the words of his fellow" (Shevet Yehudah 40).

— Hitpa'el, *הִתְלַמֵּד, — a) To become practised in a thing: "After everyone one answers Amen, except for schoolchildren, since they are made to practise (להתלמד)" (Berakhot 53b). "One may write a scroll for a child to practise (להתלמד) with it" (Yoma 37b). "R. Hanina the Bible teacher said: I had great distress with R. Hanina the Great, and he did not permit me to divide (the verse in two) except for schoolchildren, since they are made to practise" (Ta'anit 27b). "He wrote in order to divorce his wife and changed his mind etc. Rav Papa said: With scribes who are accustomed to practise (להתלמד)" (Gittin 24b). "He heard the voice of children practising (מתלמדין) and saying: So-and-so divorced so-and-so from such-and-such a place; and he said, This is my name and this is my wife's name" (Midrash Tannaim 24:1). "They bring in children to practise (להתלמד) at about six or seven, according to the child's strength and the build of his body" (Rambam, Talmud Torah 2:2). — b) נתלמד the thing: they learned it: "The Torah: today one learns a little and tomorrow much, because it is not learned (מתלמדת) in one year or in two" (Numbers Rabbah 12). — And the liturgical poet said: "A hidden mighty one, I dwelt in delight; to earth I did not descend to be taught (להתלמד); and a perfect man arose and desired my longing" (רשב"י, third day of Shavuot, בשורי מעשהו). — c) °Like לְמַד, הִתְלַמֵּד from so-and-so: "A master who does not walk in a good way, even though he is a great sage and all the people need him, one does not learn (מתלמדין) from him until he returns to good" (Rambam, Talmud Torah 4:1). "And of forms which they make so that the embroiderer may learn (שיתלמד) from it" (the same, Kelim 27:12). "And so the teacher and the learner (והמתלמד), for wisdom is found in the teacher in actuality and in the learner in potentiality" (Emunah Ramah 1:5).

he: *, ש"נ, — כְּלוּם, Nichts; rien; nothing: והארץ היתה תהו ובהו זה אדם הראשון שהיה ללמה ולא כלום (מד"ר בראש' ב).   אמר להם (פרעה למשה ולאהרן) אתם למה ודבריכם למה לכו לסבלותיכם (שם שמות ה).  שלא אעשה למה בעיני חבריך על עדריהן (שם שה"ש, הגידה לי).
en: *, feminine noun, — nothing, German Nichts, French rien, English nothing: "'And the earth was formless and void' — this is the first man, who became למה and nothing at all" (Genesis Rabbah 2). "He (Pharaoh) said to them (to Moses and Aaron): You are למה and your words are למה; go to your burdens" (ibid. Exodus 5). "That I should not be made למה in the eyes of your companions over their flocks" (ibid. Song of Songs, הגידה לי).

he: — קל לא נמצא.

— נִפע', נִלְעַג, — נִלְעַג לָשׁוֹן, שמדבר בלשון שקשה להבין, בלשון נכריה: את עם נועז לא תראה עם עמקי שפה משמוע נִלְעַג לשון אין בינה (ישע' לג יט). — והשתמשו בסהמ"א במשמ' אדם שאינו יודע לשון מהלשונו': והמגיד לו (לר' נתן בעל הערוך) לא ידע לשון ערבי כי נלעג היה (ראב"ע שמות כה כט). — ואמר המשורר: לא עוד כאתון בלעם ובהרבה להג נלעג היהודי ויהי גם ללעג כי בלשון עם ועם צחות ישיח (יל"ג, דרך בת עמי).
— פָעו', °לָעוּג, לְעוּגָה, — לשון לְעוּגָה, לשון נכריה, לא עברית: והנה העתקתי את ספר המוסיקה משפה לעוגה אל לשון הקדש (יהודה בן הק"ר יצחק, כ"י פריז).
— הִתפ', °הִתְלַעֵג, — היה נלעג לשון: יצחצח מליו ולא יתלעג במו כי אמנם הנלעג לשון לא יפל עליו שם לשון צחות (מנחם, פתיחה).
en: — Qal is not found.

— Nif'al, נִלְעַג, — נִלְעַג לָשׁוֹן, one who speaks in a language that is hard to understand, in a foreign language: "You shall not see the fierce people, a people of a speech too deep to perceive, of a stammering tongue (נִלְעַג לשון) without understanding" (Isaiah 33:19). — And in the literature of the Middle Ages it was used in the sense of a person who does not know one of the languages: "And the one who told him (R. Nathan, author of the Arukh) did not know the Arabic language, for he was נלעג" (Ibn Ezra, Exodus 25:29). — And the poet said: "No longer, like Balaam's she-ass and with much babble, is the Jew נלעג and become also a mockery, for in the language of each and every people he speaks fluently" (Yalag, דרך בת עמי).

— Pa'ul, °לָעוּג, לְעוּגָה, — לשון לְעוּגָה, a foreign language, not Hebrew: "And behold, I have translated the book of music from a foreign tongue (שפה לעוגה) into the holy tongue" (Judah son of the honored R. Isaac, Paris manuscript).

— Hitpa'el, °הִתְלַעֵג, — was נלעג לשון: "He polishes his words and does not stammer (יתלעג) in them, for indeed the name 'fluent of tongue' does not apply to one who is נלעג לשון" (Menahem, Introduction).

he: פ"ע, לָעֲגָה, עתי' אֶלְעַג, תִּלְעַג, יִלְעַג, יִלְעָג, יִלְעֲגוּ, לֹעֵג, — לָעַג, ולָעַג לפלוני, צחק עליו, דבּר עליו בצחוק ובוז, spotten; railler; to deride: זה הדבר אשר דבר יי' עליו (על סנחריב מלך אשור) בזה לך לָעֲגָה לך בתולת בת ציון אחריך ראש הניעה בת ירושלם ישע' לז כב.  הייתי לשחוק כל היום כלה לֹעֵג לי ירמ' כ ז.  יושב בשמים ישחק אדני יִלְעַג למו תהל' ב ד.  ואתה יי' תשחק למו תִּלְעַג לכל גוים שם נט ט.  תשימנו מדון לשכנינו ואיבינו יִלְעֲגוּ למו שם פ ז.  גם אני באידכם אשחק אֶלְעַג בבא פחדכם משלי א כא.  לֹעֵג לרש חרף עשהו שמח לאיד לא ינקה שם יז ה.  עין תִּלְעַג לאב ותבז ליקהת אם יקרוה ערבי נחל ויאכלוה בני נשר שם ל יז.  אם שוט ימית פתאם למסת נקים יִלְעַג איוב ט כג.  בדיך מתים יחרישו וַתִּלְעַג ואין מכלם שם יא ג.  יראו צדיקים וישמחו ונקי יִלְעַג למו שם כב יט. — ואמר בן סירא: בני אל תלעג לחיי עני ואל תדאיב עיני מר רוח ב"ס גני' ד א. — ובתו"מ וסהמ"א: שעשה הקב"ה על עולמו מלאכי חבלה ומחבלים והולכים כל ימות הגאולה ואבילי ציון עמהם נכנסים ועמהם יוצאים כאדם שנכנס אצל חבירו ויוצא ואין מזיקים אותו והרואה אותם יושב ואומר לשוא לעגנו על דבריהם פסיק' רבתי לד.  והגאוה והגובה והגאון ובזות בני אדם ולעוֹג לנביאים ולדברים הבאים מאלהים חו"ה, עבוד' ה' ד. — ואמר הפיטן: גמול תשיב ולה תושיב ותקשיב לשועתה ודמעתה ברדתה, לעג שדי לצרים לעגו לה נקום נקמת כלמתה ובשתה רשב"ג, בקשה, לך נפשי.  דברה על לבב מיחליך מדברי רחמים, שבחם בהדר פעליך לועגים זועמים, המחכים שנת גאוליך אל נאם נאמים ר"י הלוי, יזכרו פלאך.

— הִפע', הִלְעִיג, תַּלְעִיג, יַלְעֵג, יַלְעִיגוּ, מַלְעִיגִים, — הִלְעִיג, והִלְעִיג לפלוני, כמו לָעַג: שאוני ואנכי אדבר ואחר דברי תַלְעִיג איוב כא ג.  כל ראי יַלְעִיגוּכך בדפוס' הקדומים, אך בהרבה ספרי דפוס חסר, והעיד ע"ז גם מנחת שי: בספרים מדוייקים חסר יוד והגימל רפה. לי יפטירו בשפה יניעו ראש תהל' כב ח.  וישמע סנבלט החרני וטביה העבד העמוני וגשם הערבי וַיַּלְעִגוּבכל הספרים חסר, ולפי זה אפשר שיהיה קל, אך הקריאה המסורה היא בהפעיל. לנו ויבזו עלינו ויאמרו מה הדבר הזה אשר אתם עשים נחמ' ב יט. — וְהִלְעִיג על פלוני: ויהי כאשר שמע סנבלט כי אנחנו בונים את החומה ויחר לו ויכעס הרבה וַיַּלְעֵג על היהודים וכו' ויאמר מה היהודים האמללים עשים וכו' היחיו את האבנים מערמות העפר והמה שרופות נחמ' ג כג-כד. — והִלְעִיג בפלוני: ויהיו הרצים (של המלך יחזקיהו) עברים מעיר לעיר בארץ אפרים ומנשה ועד זבלון ויהיו משחיקים עליהם וּמַלְעִגִים בם דהי"ב ל י. — ובתו"מ: מעשה בתלמיד אחד שעבר לפני ר"א וקצר בברכותיו והיו מלעיגין עליו ואומרים עליו תלמיד חכם קצרן הוא זה מכי' בשלח ד א.  עין שהלעיגה על כיבוד אב ואם וכו' יבוא עורב שהוא אכזרי ויקרנה ירוש' פאה א יה ד.  שכל המלעיג על דברי חכמים נידון בצואה רותחת ערוב' כא:.  שהיה (פרעה) מלעיג על הקב"ה שהיה סבור שמעשה כשפים הן מה שעשו משה ואהרן וקרא לכל בני ביתו לעשות כמותם מד"ר שמות ט.  כעין זה (הוא) מלעיג על המוכה שם בראש' פד.  מאחר שהן יושבין ואוכלין ושותין ומשתכרין הן יושבין משיחין בי ומלעיגים בי שם איכ', פתיח'.  ועדיין לא שנו מעשיהם המכוערין ואעפ"י שהם בגלות בינינו מלעיגין אותנו ואת אמונת אלהינו שם אסת', אם על המלך טוב.  ענה ירמיה ואמר לפני הקב"ה רבש"ע איני יכול להתנבאות עליהם איזה נביא יצא להם ולא בקשו להורגו וכו' העמדת להם אליהו בעל קווצות והיו מלעיגים  ומשחקים עליו הרי מסלסל קווצותיו פסיק' רבתי כו. אילו אבלים שחמדו את הישועה ערב ובקר וצהרים והיתה צרה גדולה לישראל שמבזין אותם ומלעיגין עליהן שם לד.  עד שהיו במצרים הלעיגו לי וכו' למודים הם בכך תנחומא שלח ח.  צוה יוסף ובנו את האוצרות בכל עיר ועיר וקבץ את תבואת הארצות לאוצרות והיו המצרים מלעיגים  עליו ואומרים עכשיו התולעת אוכלת כל אוצרות יוסף פדר"א לט. — ובסהמ"א: ולא ראוי לבן אדם להלעיג במעשה האב א"ב של ב"ס כד.  וחזרה מלעגת ואומרת קח אתה שלמה האלף שלך וירויחו הנוטרים השוכרים מאתים ראב"ע שה"ש ח יב.  לא עבדו אלהים אחרים ולא הושיבו נשים נכריות ולא הלעיגו על המצות והתקינו שיהו קורין בתורה בשני ובחמשי ובשבת ספ' הקבלה לראב"ד.  כי השחוק ימשך לאדם על צד הלעג ממה שראוי להלעיג עליו העקרים ב טז.  וכבר הלעיג על זה המשורר באמרו בינו בוערים בעם רי"א, נחל' אבות ג.  אם אדם שומע דבר תורה מאדם טוב ויודע שאינו מתקבל על הלב אם אמרו והלעיגו בו אל יאמר בשם אומרו אלא יאמר טעיתי אני ספ' חסיד' תתתתשסג. — ואמר הפיטן: חטא חטאה ואמרה לאליל זה אל, והלעיגה ותעתעה בחוזי אל ר"א קליר, איכה ישבה חבצלת.   וירד לראות העיר והמגדל ופץ לא יבצר, להם הלעיג  יושב שחק ונבללה שפתם ונבקה עצתם, לכל רוח פוזרו וכמוץ הונשפו קטע כ"י גני' J. Elbog. 168. — והִלְעִיגוֹ: רציתי לילך אחריו להלעיגו  ולהכלימו מכת' מזמן הגאו', Monats. 1906. 596.
— פִע', °לִעֵג, — כמו קל והִפע': כלומר שליעג עליו שהיה מת וחיה רש"י ב"ק קיו:.
en: intransitive verb, לָעֲגָה, future אֶלְעַג, תִּלְעַג, יִלְעַג, יִלְעָג, יִלְעֲגוּ, לֹעֵג, — לָעַג, and לָעַג לפלוני, laughed at him, spoke of him with mockery and contempt, German spotten, French railler, English to deride: "This is the word which the Lord hath spoken concerning him (concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria): The virgin daughter of Zion hath despised thee and laughed thee to scorn (לָעֲגָה); the daughter of Jerusalem hath shaken her head at thee" (Isaiah 37:22). "I am become a laughing-stock all the day, every one mocketh (לֹעֵג) me" (Jeremiah 20:7). "He that sitteth in heaven laugheth, the Lord hath them in derision (יִלְעַג)" (Psalms 2:4). "But Thou, O Lord, shalt laugh at them; Thou shalt have all the nations in derision (תִּלְעַג)" (ibid. 59:9). "Thou makest us a strife unto our neighbours; and our enemies mock (יִלְעֲגוּ) as they please" (ibid. 80:7). "I also will laugh in your calamity; I will mock (אֶלְעַג) when your dread cometh" (Proverbs 1:21). "Whoso mocketh (לֹעֵג) the poor blasphemeth his Maker; and he that is glad at calamity shall not be unpunished" (ibid. 17:5). "The eye that mocketh (תִּלְעַג) at his father, and despiseth to obey his mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young vultures shall eat it" (ibid. 30:17). "If the scourge slay suddenly, He mocketh (יִלְעַג) at the calamity of the guiltless" (Job 9:23). "Thy boastings have made men hold their peace, and thou mockest (וַתִּלְעַג), and no man maketh thee ashamed" (ibid. 11:3). "The righteous saw it, and were glad; and the innocent laugh them to scorn (יִלְעַג)" (ibid. 22:19). — And Ben Sira said: "My son, do not mock (תלעג) the life of the poor, and do not grieve the eyes of the bitter in spirit" (Ben Sira, Genizah 4:1). — And in Talmud and Midrash and post-biblical literature: "For the Holy One, blessed be He, made over His world angels of destruction and destroyers, and they go on all the days of the redemption, and the mourners of Zion go in with them and go out with them, like a man who goes in and out with his fellow and they do not harm him; and whoever sees them sits and says: In vain did we mock (לעגנו) their words" (Pesikta Rabbati 34). "And pride, haughtiness and arrogance, and contempt of people, and mocking (ולעוֹג) the prophets and the words that come from God" (Duties of the Hearts, Service of God 4). — And the paytan said: "Requite with recompense and settle her, and hearken to her cry and her tear in her descent; Shaddai, mock (לעג) the foes who mocked (לעגו) her, avenge the vengeance of her disgrace and her shame" (R. Solomon ibn Gabirol, Bakkashah, לך נפשי). "Speak to the heart of those who hope in You words of mercy; their praise is in the splendor of Your deeds, mocking (לועגים), indignant, those who await the year of Your redeemed, O God, Speaker of speeches" (R. Judah Halevi, יזכרו פלאך).

— Hif'il, הִלְעִיג, תַּלְעִיג, יַלְעֵג, יַלְעִיגוּ, מַלְעִיגִים, — הִלְעִיג, and הִלְעִיג לפלוני, like לָעַג: "Suffer me, and I also will speak; and after that I have spoken, mock on (תַלְעִיג)" (Job 21:3). "All they that see me laugh me to scorn (יַלְעִיגוּ) [Note: So in the early printed editions, but in many printed books it is written defectively, and Minhat Shai also testified to this: "In accurate books the yod is missing and the gimel is rafe."]; they shoot out the lip, they shake the head" (Psalms 22:8). "But when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian, heard it, they laughed us to scorn (וַיַּלְעִגוּ) [Note: In all the books it is written defectively, and accordingly it could be Qal, but the Masoretic reading is in Hif'il.], and despised us, and said: What is this thing that ye do?" (Nehemiah 2:19). — And הִלְעִיג על פלוני: "But it came to pass that, when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he was wroth, and took great indignation, and mocked (וַיַּלְעֵג) the Jews etc. And he said: What do these feeble Jews etc.? Will they revive the stones out of the heaps of rubbish, seeing they are burned?" (Nehemiah 3:23-24). — And הִלְעִיג בפלוני: "So the posts (of King Hezekiah) passed from city to city through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh, even unto Zebulun; but they laughed them to scorn, and mocked them (וּמַלְעִגִים בם)" (2 Chronicles 30:10). — And in Talmud and Midrash: "It happened that a certain student passed before (the ark) in the presence of Rabbi Eliezer and shortened his blessings, and they mocked him (מלעיגין עליו) and said of him: This disciple of the wise is a shortener" (Mekhilta Beshalach 4:1). "An eye that mocked (שהלעיגה) the honoring of father and mother etc. — let the raven, which is cruel, come and pick it out" (Jerusalem Talmud Pe'ah 1:15d). "For whoever mocks (המלעיג) the words of the Sages is punished with boiling excrement" (Eruvin 21b). "For he (Pharaoh) mocked (מלעיג) the Holy One, blessed be He, for he thought that what Moses and Aaron did were acts of sorcery, and he called all the members of his household to do likewise" (Exodus Rabbah 9). "Like this, (he) mocks (מלעיג) the one who is smitten" (ibid., Genesis 84). "After they sit and eat and drink and become drunk, they sit and talk about me and mock me (ומלעיגים בי)" (ibid., Lamentations, Introduction). "And still they have not changed their ugly deeds, and although they are in exile among us, they mock (מלעיגין) us and the faith of our God" (ibid., Esther, אם על המלך טוב). "Jeremiah answered and said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, I cannot prophesy to them; what prophet went out to them and they did not seek to kill him? etc. You raised up for them Elijah, the hairy one, and they mocked (מלעיגים) and laughed at him: Look, he is curling his locks" (Pesikta Rabbati 26). "These are mourners who longed for the salvation evening, morning and noon, and there was great trouble for Israel, for they despise them and mock them (ומלעיגין עליהן)" (ibid. 34). "While they were in Egypt they mocked Me (הלעיגו לי) etc. — they are accustomed to it" (Tanhuma Shelach 8). "Joseph commanded and they built the storehouses in every city, and he gathered the produce of the lands into storehouses, and the Egyptians mocked (מלעיגים) him and said: Now the worm is eating all of Joseph's storehouses" (Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer 39). — And in post-biblical literature: "And it is not fitting for a person to mock (להלעיג) the deed of the father" (Alphabet of Ben Sira 24). "And she again mocked (מלעגת) and said: Take, you, Solomon, your thousand, and let the keepers, the hired men, gain two hundred" (Ibn Ezra, Song of Songs 8:12). "They did not worship other gods, nor did they take foreign wives, nor did they mock (הלעיגו) the commandments; and they instituted that the Torah be read on Monday and on Thursday and on the Sabbath" (Sefer ha-Kabbalah of the Rabad). "For laughter comes to a person by way of mockery of what is fit to be mocked (להלעיג עליו)" (Ikkarim 2:16). "And the poet already mocked (הלעיג) this, saying: Understand, ye brutish among the people" (R. Isaac Abravanel, Nahalat Avot 3). "If a person hears a word of Torah from a good person and knows that it is not acceptable to the mind, if he said it and they mocked him (והלעיגו בו), he should not say it in the name of the one who said it, but should say: I erred" (Sefer Hasidim תתתתשסג). — And the paytan said: "She sinned a sin and said to an idol: This is God; and she mocked (והלעיגה) and deceived the seers of God" (R. Eleazar Kallir, איכה ישבה חבצלת). "And He came down to see the city and the tower, and burst what was not to be withheld; He who sits in the heavens mocked them (הלעיג), and their language was confounded and their counsel made void; they were scattered to every wind and blown away like chaff" (Genizah manuscript fragment, J. Elbog. 168). — And הִלְעִיגוֹ: "I wanted to go after him to mock him (להלעיגו) and to shame him" (a letter from the time of the Geonim, Monats. 1906. 596).
— Pi'el, °לִעֵג, — like Qal and Hif'il: "That is to say, that he mocked (שליעג) him, that he had been dead and come back to life" (Rashi, Bava Kamma 117b).

he: *, פ"ע, —  הוציא לַעַז, דבּר עליו רעות:  ומעשה ביהודה והלל בניו של רבן גמליאל שרחצו שניהן כאחד בכבול ולעזה עליהן כל המדינה אמרו מימינו לא ראינו כך (פסח' נא.).  ומעשה ברבי שמעון ב"ג שישב על ספסל נכרים בשבת בעכו ולעזה עליו כל המדינה (שם).

— הִפע', * הִלְעִיז, —  כמו לָעַז: רבי זכריה (חתנו של ) ר' לוי היו מלעיזין כך בנוסח' שבדפ' ש"ס בבלי, ובנוסח' הירוש': הכל מליזין. עליו ואומרים (שלא היה צריך לקבל צדקה מלשכת חשאים והוא היה מקבל) (ירוש'שקל' ה מט.).  —  והִלְעִיז בו: אמר לו הקב"ה למשה משה החייתני בדבריך זה הדבר קשה היה בפני התלמידים והיו מלעיזים בו עלינו החולקין על דברי רבותינו ז"ל (ר"נ גאון, ברכ' לב.). —  ואמר הפיטן: וירא משיסת מסתולל בו להלעז, ממושך מפרך ביד רמה להעז, בית יעקב מעם לועז (רשב"י, ז' פסח, ויושע).
en: *, intransitive verb, — spread לַעַז, spoke ill of him: "And it happened that Judah and Hillel, the sons of Rabban Gamaliel, bathed together in Kabul, and the whole region spoke ill of them (ולעזה עליהן), saying: In all our days we have never seen such a thing" (Pesachim 51a). "And it happened that Rabban Simeon ben Gamaliel sat on a bench of gentiles on the Sabbath in Acre, and the whole region spoke ill of him (ולעזה עליו)" (ibid.).

— Hif'il, * הִלְעִיז, — like לָעַז: "R. Zechariah (son-in-law of ) R. Levi — they used to speak ill (מלעיזין) [Note: So in the version in the printed editions of the Babylonian Talmud; and in the version of the Jerusalem Talmud: הכל מליזין.] of him and say (that he did not need to accept charity from the Chamber of Secret Gifts, and he did accept)" (Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 5, 49a). — And הִלְעִיז בו: "The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: Moses, you have revived Me with your words.
